《字林西报》，1928年12月10日，星期一

阿尔伯特·托马斯先生在东京演讲中解释
国际联盟劳工局的职能

回应有关其日内瓦组织
侵犯各强国主权权利的论点

（东邦通讯社）
东京，12月9日。— 国际联盟国际劳工局局长阿尔伯特·托马斯先生在昨天于帝国学士院为他举行的讲座会议上向大量听众发表讲话时说。
“我听到一种论点，认为国际劳工局和国际联盟正在侵犯列强的主权权利，但必须记住，国际联盟和国际劳工局的职责在于努力在不侵犯联盟成员主权的情况下开展国际事业。
“在这些国际机构达成的条约都符合列强主权的动向，列强根据各自宪法规定的范围相互合作。因此，从前文可以清楚地看出，上述论点是一种偏见。
“国际劳工局和国际联盟的职能将根据凡尔赛和平条约的精神来发挥，联盟的所有成员都应在此基础上尽力而为。令人欣慰的是，日本是这一伟大原则的忠实执行者，已经批准了九项国际劳工协定，但令人深感遗憾的是，她迄今未能批准诸如禁止妇女和儿童夜间工作以及限制劳动时间等重要协定。
“我访问本国的目的是敦促日本迅速批准这些未批准的国际劳工协定，并全面调查这里的劳工状况细节。我真诚希望日本人民为世界社会正义的建立而奋起。”

December 8, 1928 THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW 51

Albert Thomas' Mission
in China

BY HARRY PAYTON HOWARD

"With us there are no unequal treaties. Every nation sending its representation to the International Labor Bureau of the League of Nations is recognized as on an equal basis, so far as the Bureau is concerned. Any nation can ratify or refuse to ratify the conventions adopted by the Bureau for the protection of labor. And China has utilized her sovereign power not to ratify."

Albert Thomas, Director of the International Labor Bureau of the League of Nations, at Geneva, made the foregoing response with regard to a suggestion regarding the unequal treaties here. Mr. Thomas has come to China as official representative of the International Labor Bureau, to visit the Government of China at Nanking and try to insure the full representation of China in the Bureau. Full representation would mean two delegates from the Government, one from Chinese labor, and one from Chinese capital.

Mr. Thomas' proposal met with a very favorable response from the Chinese Government, and he looks forward to seeing a full Chinese delegation, of four members, at the next meeting of the International Labor Bureau.

Short Stay in Shanghai

Mr. Thomas arrived in Shanghai on Saturday, December 1, from Nanking, having gone there from Peking and Hankow. He was accompanied by Mr. Edward Philan, his associate, and a Chinese interpreter, and came down from Nanking with Dr. H. H. Kung, Nationalist Minister of Industry, Commerce and Labor, and Dr. C. T. Wang, Nationalist Minister of Foreign Affairs.

It was originally intended that Mr. Thomas stay at Shanghai four days before going on to Japan, where he has important conferences both with Government and labor representatives. This was found impossible, however, so it was necessary to crowd the four-day program into two days, so far as possible. Many of Mr. Thomas' engagements, therefore, were filled by his associate Mr. Philan after their arrival on Saturday.

Mr. Thomas was the principal speaker the same day at a tiffin in his honor at the Astor House, given by the Pan-Pacific Association. He delivered a half-hour's speech in French, part of which was translated into English by Mr. Philan.

"Why Come To China?"

On every hand, Mr. Thomas said in his address, people have been asking "Why did you come to China?" It was impossible, he stated, to come to any definite conclusions regarding the country since he has been here a short time and has had no real opportunity to make a careful study of the situation. The speaker pointed out that it would be unwise to draw conclusions without having real facts upon which to base them.

Mr. Thomas stated that he had come to China to lay the foundation for closer relationship between this country and the League of Nations Labor Bureau.

In discussing the work of the Bureau he said it was necessary to refer to conditions when the Bureau first began to function in the interests of labor all over the world. In comparison with labor conditions before the war, the conditions are much improved now, due to co-operation and unity of labor itself, Mr. Thomas said. One important improvement was that child labor has generally been abolished and an age limit for children established. The 8-hour day had also been generally recognized, he stated, and women were no longer required to work all night in mills and other establishments of that nature. The 8-hour day, Mr. Thomas explained, gives the laborer more time for sleep and for intellectual and moral development. Another question of great importance to the laborer, and one that has been taken up in a serious manner, was that of industrial insurance, in addition to the securing of work for the unemployed, unemployment insurance, and insurance against old age. These matters were of vital importance to labor the world over.

The battle for these things was being waged, he said, in order to enable labor to live with at least a share of human dignity, and to improve not only material but moral conditions. In this manner the laborer is thus given a chance to look after his own interests. Mr. Thomas particularly urged an improvement in child labor conditions in China.

Crowded Program

Mr. Thomas' program was a very crowded one, including visits to several industrial plants, to the Footung model village, to the Yangtsepoo Social Center, to the National Labor University, a reception and dinner by local officials meetings with representatives of local labor unions and with some foreign labor men now in China, a tiffin with the Manufacturers' Association of China, a dinner with Chinese commercial bodies, interviews with newspapermen, and a lecture and discussion with social workers. In addition, he received a number of reports on labor unions in China, a report on slavery, a report on the position of destitute Russians here and a proposal for organized effort in assisting their migration elsewhere, and a report on the recent refusal of the French authorities in Shanghai to permit a Russian socialist paper (anti-Bolshevik) to be published in the French Concession here.

In his speech at the tiffin of the Manufacturers' Association on Sunday, Mr. Thomas stressed the economic value of improved labor conditions and greater protection for the workers, which he pointed out resulted in increase of output. "The more employers do for labor in the real improvement of conditions, the more labor is able and willing to do both for itself and for production as a whole." (See The Review for August 18, 1928, for an economic exposition of this principle as applied to China, by the present writer.)

Fundamental Problems

Mr. Thomas came to a discussion of fundamental problems in a private conversation with the writer last Saturday, and went into further comment on these in his speech and discussion with social workers on Sunday. With regard to labor legislation, he remarked upon Poland and Czechoslovakia having formulated their labor laws after consultation with the International Labor Bureau, and hoped that China might make use of the Bureau in similar fashion. He denied flatly the statements attributed to him by a certain agency, both at Peking and at Nanking, to the effect that he had questioned the existence of "socio-economic problems in China," had declared that "there was no room for class struggle in China" that owing to difference of conditions China must formulate her labor laws on different basis than in other countries, etc. In a short trip such as his, Mr. Thomas pointed out, it was impossible to become an expert on China and make absolute statements of this kind. There were very serious gaps in their information about China, and he would certainly make no pretense of omniscience on the subject. He was deeply impressed however by the terrible conditions of the workers here.

Protection Urgently Needed

From what he had been able to see and observe of China, however, many things were required here even more than in western countries. For example, legal protection of labor—particularly women and children—from inhuman conditions. As for the organization of labor unions,—not as political organizations but as real workers' economic bodies for improving their material condition,—this was clearly a most urgent need here.

In Peking, Hankow, and Nanking Mr. Thomas had met representatives of committees which were presented as organizers—or reorganizers—of trade unions,—but they did not impress him as real labor men. Their aims were predominantly political—opposition to imperialism. They were much more interested in unequal treaties than in unequal feeling. But here in Shanghai he had seen some unions which impressed him as being genuine labor organizations. And he wanted to see if he could not induce Government people and Kuomintang people to recognize the importance of such real unions in raising the material standards and the educational standards of the Chinese workers. Trade unions were one of the best possible schools for the education of the workers.

Danger in Lack of Unions

Mr. Thomas pointed out that with the development of industry here, serious conflicts could be expected if China does not take advantage of present conditions to protect labor and to create true trade unions. Trade unions were the best education,—developing a sense of responsibility, developing the conscience of the workers, and developing the spirit of self-help in the minds of the workers. He wanted to see a strong union movement in China.

Mr. Thomas, while here officially as Director of the International Labor Bureau, has some other important posts. An old member of the French Socialist Party, it will be recalled that he was Minister of Munitions during the war. At present he is a member of the Executive Committee of the International Co-Operative Alliance.

Great Importance of Co-operation

Mr. Thomas feels that the co-operative movement is of the greatest importance in countries of the present economic development of China. Here is the practical construction of a socialist order within the framework of the old order. Like the trade unions, the co-operatives were a school in social consciousness, in responsibility, and in self-help. At the same time, they were the practical realization of socialism in daily

(Continued on page 67)
page_data.zh:
1928年12月8日 《密勒氏评论报》 第51页

阿尔伯特·托马斯在华使命

作者：哈里·佩顿·霍华德

“对我们而言，不存在不平等条约。凡向国际联盟国际劳工局派遣代表的国家，就该局而言，均被视为处于平等地位。任何国家均可批准或拒绝批准该局通过的劳工保护公约。而中国已行使其主权权力，不予批准。”

位于日内瓦的国际联盟国际劳工局局长阿尔伯特·托马斯，就此处有关不平等条约的建议作出了上述回应。托马斯先生以国际劳工局官方代表身份来到中国，访问南京的中国政府，并试图确保中国在该局拥有充分代表权。充分代表权意味着由政府派出两名代表，由中国劳工界派出一名代表，由中国资本家派出一名代表。

托马斯先生的提议得到了中国政府的非常积极的响应，他期待在下一次国际劳工局会议上看到由四名成员组成的完整中国代表团。

短暂停留上海

托马斯先生于12月1日（星期六）从南京抵达上海，此前他曾前往北京和汉口。陪同他的有他的助手爱德华·菲兰（Edward Philan，音译）先生和一名中文翻译，他们与国民党工商部部长孔祥熙博士及国民党外交部部长王正廷博士一同从南京南下。

原计划托马斯先生在上海停留四天，随后前往日本，在那里他将与政府及劳工代表举行重要会议。然而，这一计划被发现不可行，因此有必要在可能的情况下将四天的日程压缩到两天内。因此，托马斯先生的许多应酬活动在他们周六抵达后由其助手菲兰先生代为出席。

同日，托马斯先生在泛太平洋协会于礼查饭店（Astor House）为他举行的午宴上担任主宾并发表演讲。他用法语发表了半小时的演讲，其中部分内容由菲兰先生翻译成英语。

“为何来华？”

托马斯先生在演讲中说，到处都有人问：“你为何来中国？”他表示，由于他在此停留时间短暂，且没有真正机会对局势进行仔细研究，因此不可能对这个国家得出任何确切的结论。演讲者指出，在没有掌握作为依据的确凿事实的情况下得出结论是不明智的。

托马斯先生表示，他来华是为了奠定中国与国联劳工局之间更紧密关系的基础。

在讨论该局的工作时，他说有必要回顾该局开始为全球劳工利益运作时的状况。托马斯先生说，与战前的劳工状况相比，由于劳工自身的合作与团结，目前的状况已大有改善。一项重要的改进是童工普遍被废除，并确立了儿童的年龄限制。他还指出，八小时工作制也已得到普遍认可，妇女不再需要在纱厂及其他类似性质的机构中通宵工作。托马斯先生解释说，八小时工作制让工人有更多的时间用于睡眠以及智力和道德的发展。对劳工而言另一个至关重要且已被认真处理的问题是工业保险，此外还包括为失业者提供就业机会、失业保险以及养老保险。这些事项对全世界的劳工都至关重要。

他说，争取这些目标的斗争正在进行，目的是使劳工至少能享有部分人类尊严地生活，并改善不仅物质条件，还有道德条件。通过这种方式，劳工从而获得了照顾自身利益的机会。托马斯先生特别敦促改善中国的童工状况。

紧凑的日程

托马斯先生的日程安排非常紧凑，包括参观几家工厂、访问沪东模范村、杨树浦社会中心、国立劳动大学，参加地方官员举办的招待会和晚宴，会见当地工会代表以及一些目前在中国的外国劳工人士，与中国制造商协会共进午餐，与中国商业团体共进晚餐，接受记者采访，以及与社会工作者进行讲座和讨论。此外，他还收到了一些关于中国工会的报告、一份关于奴隶制的报告、一份关于在华贫困俄国人处境及组织协助其迁往他处的提案的报告，以及一份关于上海法国当局最近拒绝允许一份俄国社会主义报纸（反布尔什维克）在法租界出版的报告。

在周日中国制造商协会的午宴演讲中，托马斯先生强调了改善劳工条件和加强对工人保护的经济价值，他指出这会导致产量的增加。“雇主在切实改善条件方面为劳工做得越多，劳工就越有能力且越愿意为其自身及整体生产做出贡献。”（关于这一原则应用于中国的经济学阐述，请参阅本刊1928年8月18日号，由本文作者撰写。）

根本问题

上周六，托马斯先生在与笔者的私人谈话中讨论了根本问题，并在周日的演讲及与社会工作者的讨论中对此作了进一步评论。关于劳工立法，他提到波兰和捷克斯洛伐克在与国际劳工局协商后制定了其劳工法律，并希望中国也能以类似方式利用该局。他断然否认了某机构在北京和南京归咎于他的说法，即他质疑中国存在“社会经济问题”，宣称“中国没有阶级斗争的空间”，由于条件不同，中国必须基于与其他国家不同的基础制定劳工法律等。托马斯先生指出，在他这样短暂的行程中，不可能成为中国的专家并做出此类绝对性的陈述。他们关于中国的信息存在非常严重的空白，他当然不会假装对该主题无所不知。然而，这里工人的可怕状况给他留下了深刻印象。

亟需保护

然而，根据他在中国所能看到和观察到的情况，这里有许多事情甚至比西方国家更需要。例如，对劳工——特别是妇女和儿童——免受非人道待遇的法律保护。至于工会的组织——不是作为政治组织，而是作为改善其物质条件的真正的工人经济实体——这显然是这里最迫切的需求。

在北京、汉口和南京，托马斯先生会见了被介绍为工会组织者——或重组者——的委员会代表，但他们给他的印象并非真正的劳工人士。他们的目标主要是政治性的——反对帝国主义。他们对不平等条约的兴趣远大于对不平等感受的兴趣。但在上海，他看到了一些给他留下深刻印象的真正劳工组织的工会。他希望看看能否促使政府人员和国民党人士认识到此类真正工会在提高中国工人物质标准和教育标准方面的重要性。工会是教育工人的最佳学校之一。

缺乏工会的危险

托马斯先生指出，随着这里工业的发展，如果中国不利用当前条件保护劳工并创建真正的工会，预计会出现严重的冲突。工会是最好的教育——培养责任感，培养工人的良知，并在工人心中培养自助精神。他希望看到中国出现强大的工会运动。

托马斯先生此次是以国际劳工局局长的官方身份来访，但他还担任其他一些重要职务。众所周知，他是法国社会党的老党员，曾在战争期间担任军需部长。目前，他是国际合作社联盟执行委员会的成员。

合作的重要性

托马斯先生认为，合作社运动对于目前处于中国经济发展水平的国家具有极其重要的意义。这是在旧秩序框架内构建社会主义秩序的实际做法。与工会一样，合作社也是培养社会意识、责任感和自助精神的学校。同时，它们是社会主义在日常生活中的实际体现

THE OSAKA MAINICHI & THE TOKYO NICHI NICHI, OSAKA, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 8, 1928

Tokyo Workers Greet
Mr. Thomas Warmly

After Round of Calls, Visitor
Explains Purpose of Visit;
Schedule May Change

Mr. Albert Thomas, director of the International Labour Office, who arrived at Tokyo on December 6, accompanied by Mr. Vipple, Chief of the director's secretariat, called at the Premier's office and other Cabinet offices to pay respects upon his arrival in Tokyo, beginning from early in the morning. Then at 10.20 a.m., he visited the Tokyo Nichi Nichi to call on Dr. Minoru Oka, Editor-in-chief of the Tokyo Nichi Nichi, with whom Mr. Thomas is personally acquainted. In the absence of Dr. Oka, he was met by Mr. Shinnosuke Abe, one of the editors of the journal.

Mr. Thomas said that he considered it a great honour to have the opportunity of visiting the office of such an influential journal as the Tokyo Nichi Nichi on the first day of his visits in Tokyo. He said that he was well-acquainted with Dr. Oka since the time of the first International Labour Conference in Washington in 1919. Before he left Geneva, Mr. Butler, assistant director of the International Labour Bureau, wrote a letter to me, especially advising me to meet Dr. Oka, he said, and he regretted that he could not meet him.

Rousing Welcome at Tokyo

Upon his arrival at Tokyo station at 8.20 p.m., December 6, Mr. Thomas and his party were given a rousing welcome by about 500 labour leaders, representing various organizations subsidiary to the Japan Federation of Labour, the Seamen's Union, and the Naval Workers' Union, etc., who shouted Banzai three times for Mr. Thomas.

There were some labour leaders, however, who were not friendly to him, who distributed hand-bills denouncing Mr. Thomas. Nineteen persons were arrested by the police.

He received a bouquet of flowers from Mrs. Yoshiko Sunazuka, representing the women's section of the Japan Federation of Labour. He shook hands with the French Ambassador, Mr. de Billey. Amidst the crowd of welcoming people he moved out of the station compound to put up at the Imperial Hotel.

Mr. Thomas agreed to deliver a message to the citizens of Tokyo through the J.O.A.K. broadcasting station at 7.25 p.m., December 7.

Ratification of Labour Facts

Interviewed by the pressmen, Mr. Thomas said:

"If it is necessary in order to observe the conditions of labour in Japan, I may change my program. But I want it to be clearly understood that in order to have the labour conventions and recommendation signed at the International Labour Conferences so far, I, because of my official duty, must first meet the Japanese Government authorities to consult about the rat
(Continued on Page 2)

(Continued from Page 1)
fication. That is my duty in accordance with the Versailles Treaty of Peace.

"Since it is my duty to see that labour conditions are improved internationally, by the co-operation of the governments, capital, and labour, I shall not forget by any means to come into close touch with the labourers. Consequently, I shall devote all of my time in Japan, excepting the time needed to meet the government authorities, to inspecting the labour conditions. If that is not enough, I shall change my program to suit that purpose."

Guest of Honour at Pan-Pacific Club

Mr. Albert Thomas, director of the International Labour Office, and Mr. Phelan, head of the Diplomatic Division of that office, were the chief guests of the Pan-Pacific Club of Tokyo at a luncheon given at the Imperial Hotel, Tokyo, on December 7. Prince Iesato Tokugawa, President of the House of Peers, Dr. Rentaro Mizuno, former Minister of Education, and others numbering in all about 70 were present as hosts. Mr. Thomas delivered an address to the following effect:

"The Versailles Treaty of Peace contains 700 or more pages, comprising political, military, naval, economic, labour and a hundred and one other matters. In consideration of the fact that the political peace depends very much upon the social peace brought about by international co-operation, the treaty contains articles providing for the protection of the interests of the labourers in order to promote their welfare. In accordance with these articles, the International Labour Office was created.

Two Major Currents

"There are two major currents today; one to make the world a single economic unit, and the other to make it organized by a number of political units, and it is easy to observe to what extent the world has tended to become a single economic unit. For instance, the coffee we drink in the morning is produced in Brazil, our tea comes from China, our butter from Denmark, and the raw material flour for our bread from Canada, America, and Rumania. These facts show that we live internationally and that we need international cooperation.

"Since the organization of the League of Nations, the international labour conferences were held 11 times in Geneva in nine years, as a result of which 25 labour treaties were adopted, and 332 conventions and recommendations were ratified by governments of the nations. The governments of the nations are now more cooperating to advance the welfare and interests of the labourers.

"We heard that the labour organizations in Japan are divided on account of differences of principles, and that Communism has also entered Japan. I am not surprised by any means, because this is the course which the western European nations have gone through, or are going through."

After the address by Mr. Thomas, Mr. Tamen Maeda, former Deputy Mayor of Tokyo, delivered an address regarding the international labour conferences.

《大阪每日新闻》与《东京日日新闻》，大阪，1928年12月8日，星期六

东京工人热烈欢迎
托马斯先生

在一系列拜访之后，访客阐述访问目的；日程可能变更

国际劳工局局长阿尔伯特·托马斯（Albert Thomas）先生于12月6日抵达东京，随行者包括局长秘书处处长维普尔（Vipple，音译）先生。自清晨起，他便前往首相办公室及其他内阁部门拜会，以抵京致意。随后，上午10时20分，他访问了《东京日日新闻》社，拜会该报总编辑冈实（Minoru Oka）博士，托马斯先生与冈博士私交甚笃。因冈博士不在，由该报编辑之一阿部信之介（Shinnosuke Abe，音译）先生接待。

托马斯先生表示，能在东京访问的第一天就有机会拜访像《东京日日新闻》这样具有影响力的报社，他深感荣幸。他说，自1919年华盛顿第一届国际劳工大会以来，他与冈博士便已熟识。他说，在离开日内瓦之前，国际劳工局助理局长巴特勒（Butler，音译）先生曾专门写信给我，特别建议我会见冈博士，他对未能与冈博士会面表示遗憾。

在东京受到热烈欢迎

12月6日晚8时20分抵达东京站时，托马斯先生及其随行人员受到了约500名劳工领袖的热烈欢迎，这些领袖代表隶属于日本劳动总同盟的各个组织、海员工会以及海军工人工会等，他们为托马斯先生高呼三声“万岁”。

然而，也有一些对他不友好的劳工领袖分发传单谴责托马斯先生。警方逮捕了十九人。

他从代表日本劳动总同盟妇女部的砂塚良子（Yoshiko Sunazuka，音译）女士手中接过一束鲜花。他与法国大使德比伊（de Billey，音译）先生握手。在欢迎人群的簇拥下，他走出车站区域，入住帝国酒店。

托马斯先生同意于12月7日晚7时25分通过J.O.A.K.广播电台向东京市民发表讲话。

批准劳工事实

在接受记者采访时，托马斯先生说：

“如果为了考察日本的劳工状况而有此必要，我可能会改变我的日程安排。但我希望明确一点，为了使迄今为止在国际劳工大会上签署的劳工公约和建议书获得批准，出于我的职务责任，我必须首先会见日本政府当局，就批
（续至第2页）

（接第1页）
准事宜进行磋商。这是根据《凡尔赛和约》我所承担的责任。

“既然我的职责是通过政府、资本和劳工的合作，确保劳工状况在国际范围内得到改善，我绝不会忘记与劳工阶层保持密切联系。因此，除了会见政府当局所需的时间外，我将把在日本的所有时间都用于视察劳工状况。如果这还不够，我将为此目的改变我的日程安排。”

泛太平洋俱乐部的贵宾

12月7日，在东京帝国酒店举行的午餐会上，国际劳工局局长阿尔伯特·托马斯先生及该局外交司司长费伦（Phelan，音译）先生是东京泛太平洋俱乐部的主要宾客。贵族院院长德川家达（Iesato Tokugawa）亲王、前文部大臣水野炼太郎（Rentaro Mizuno）博士等共约70人作为东道主出席。托马斯先生发表了演讲，大意如下：

“《凡尔赛和约》包含七百多页，涵盖政治、军事、海军、经济、劳工以及其他一百零一项事务。考虑到政治和平在很大程度上取决于通过国际合作带来的社会和平，该条约包含旨在保护劳工利益以促进其福祉的条款。根据这些条款，国际劳工局得以成立。

两大潮流

“当今有两大潮流；一是使世界成为一个单一的经济单位，二是使世界由许多政治单位组成。观察世界趋向于成为单一经济单位的程度并非难事。例如，我们早晨喝的咖啡产自巴西，我们的茶来自中国，黄油来自丹麦，制作面包的面粉原料来自加拿大、美国和罗马尼亚。这些事实表明，我们的生活是国际化的，我们需要国际合作。

“自从国际联盟成立以来，九年间在日内瓦举行了11次国际劳工大会，结果通过了25项劳工条约，各国政府批准了332项公约和建议书。各国政府现在正更多地合作，以推进劳工的福祉和利益。

“我们听说日本的劳工组织因原则分歧而分裂，共产主义也已进入日本。我对此毫不惊讶，因为这是西欧各国已经经历或正在经历的过程。”

托马斯先生演讲结束后，东京前副市长前田多门（Tamen Maeda，音译）先生就国际劳工大会发表了演讲。

THE OSAKA MAINICHI & THE TOKYO NICHI NICHI, OSAKA, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 7. 1928

TO THE PEOPLE OF JAPAN
Message of Albert Thomas

In the first moments of treading Japanese soil, my heart filled with joyful emotion, I hail the people of Japan in fraternal greeting.
For hours, as we floated on the Inland Sea, Japanese mountains came into view under the fitful movements of light, with their delicate lines, their green and yellow draperies. The land of Japan did not betray us. It was as beautiful as we had imagined. We are sure, too, that neither will the heart of man betray us.
Is there, in truth, a civilized being who can remain insensible to all the qualities of courage, politeness and honour, of love of nature and of national conscience which have been revealed to the world as dominant traits of the Japanese people? Is there a man, knows he ever so little of history, who can remain indifferent to the long evolution which created the unity of the country, to the resurrections or successive reorganizations, which distinguished it for centuries? Is there, finally, in these always troubled and agonizing post-war times, a statesman who does not appreciate the real value of the determination and the spirit of organization of the Japanese community? Organization is the basis of all modern civilization.
But there will doubtless be none too much off all these qualifications to permit Japan to surmount the economic difficulties created simultaneously by nature and its position in the world. It will have need of them to solve the social and moral problems which arise here as in all the great industrial states.
In the ten years that our international Labour Organization has existed we have followed with fervid sympathy all the attempts made to efface, here as elsewhere, the "misery, injustice and privation" which the working classes endure and which denounce the Treaty of Peace. We have affectionately followed the patient and heroic efforts of the workers' first organizers.
In so far as labour problems are international we will aid Japan's progress towards social justice with all our heart, in accordance with the equitable and conciliatory methods established by our constitution. We will put at Japan's disposition all the experience, all the science which our Bureau has been able to consolidate.
May the three weeks which we shall pass amongst our Japanese friends aid us better to understand the deep union of our hearts! May they strengthen our common determination loyally and courageously to promote justice among men! May they in the end contribute a modest part to the work of mutual comprehension and understanding amongst all peoples, which the League of Nations pursues.
"Universal peace," have we written in the Pact. "Enlightened Peace," say you here to designate the new era. Thus is expressed the profound unity of the modern aspirations of the human race.
What joy it will be to feel this unity, all living and real, in the intimacy of Japan!

ALBERT THOMAS

《大阪每日新闻》与《东京日日新闻》，大阪，1928年12月7日，星期五

致日本人民
阿尔伯特·托马斯的文告

在踏上日本国土的最初时刻，我心中充满喜悦之情，以兄弟般的问候向日本人民致意。
数小时来，当我们漂浮在内海上时，日本的山峦在光线的变幻运动中映入眼帘，线条柔和，披着绿黄相间的帷幔。日本这片土地没有让我们失望。它正如我们想象的那样美丽。我们也确信，人心也不会让我们失望。
的确，难道有任何文明人能对勇气、礼貌、荣誉、热爱自然以及民族良知这些品质无动于衷吗？这些品质作为日本人的主要特征已向世人展现。难道有任何稍知历史的人，能对造就国家统一的漫长演变，或对数个世纪以来使其与众不同的复兴或 successive 重组漠不关心吗？最后，在这始终动荡且痛苦的战后时期，难道有任何政治家不赏识日本社会的决心和组织精神的真正价值吗？组织是所有现代文明的基础。
但是，仅凭所有这些素质，恐怕还不足以让日本克服由自然及其在世界中的地位同时造成的经济困难。它将需要这些素质来解决这里以及所有大型工业国家中出现的社会和道德问题。
在我们国际劳工组织存在的十年里，我们怀着热烈的同情关注着在此地及 elsewhere 为消除工人阶级所遭受并谴责《和约》的“贫困、不公和匮乏”所做的一切尝试。我们亲切地关注着劳工首批组织者耐心而英勇的努力。
鉴于劳工问题的国际性，我们将按照我们章程所建立的公平和调和的方法，全心全意地协助日本迈向社会正义。我们将把本局所积累的所有经验和科学知识供日本使用。
愿我们在日本朋友中间度过的三周时间，能帮助我们更好地理解我们心灵的深层联结！愿它们加强我们忠诚且勇敢地促进人类正义的共同决心！愿它们最终为国际联盟所追求的全民族相互理解与谅解的事业贡献微薄之力。
“普遍和平”，我们在盟约中写道。“开明和平”，你们在此用以指代新纪元。这就表达了人类现代愿望的深刻统一。
在日本的亲密氛围中感受到这种鲜活而真实的统一，将是多么大的喜悦啊！

阿尔伯特·托马斯

THE OSAKA MAINICHI & THE TOKYO NICHI NICHI, OSAKA, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 6, 1928

Mr. Thomas Receives Hearty
Welcome Upon Arrival at Kobe

VISITOR MAKES FIRST ADDRESS TO SEAMEN

Director of International Labour Office Here to Meet
Friends And Promote Interests of Labour

“My first impression of Japan is simply charming,” said Monsieur Albert Thomas on his arrival at Kobe from Shanghai. His landing was the occasion of animated greeting by some 3,000 workingmen, representing more than 20 different trade unions and organisations. The Director of the International Labour Office addressed a brief salutation to these people from the deck of S.S. Shanghai Maru and immediately entered the Oriental Hotel from whence he was taken to the Kobe headquarters of the Japan Seamen’s Union. Here he addressed a great audience, giving assurances of his sincere desire always to collaborate with the workers of Japan.

Fully an hour before the arrival of S.S. Shanghai Maru carrying the celebrated Director, the pier was the scene of extraordinary excitement. A great crowd of people—mostly workingmen—impatiently awaited the wharfing of the ship. There were a goodly number of distinguished men among the crowd, men like Mr. Bunji Suzuki, the famous leader of the Japanese Federation of Labour; Mr. Inabata, president of the Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and Monsieur Hauchecorne, French consul at Kobe, besides officials of Osaka-fu and many others.

Threat of Radicals

In view of the rumour of possible attack on the visitor by radical elements, the pier was cautiously guarded by a large force of policemen; but as things turned out, this precaution was quite unnecessary.

As the ship slowly made its headway towards the pier and the crowd recognised the smiling face of the Director, formidable shouts of Banzai arose almost spontaneously.

Monsieur Thomas responded to the enthusiastic greetings by swinging his hat, eminently appreciative of the enthusiastic reception.

So soon as the gang-plank was fixed hundreds struggled to enter the ship and Monsieur Thomas was soon surrounded by friends and acquaintances, all so glad to see him setting ashore in Japan. After initial salutations were over, the Director bade the crowd to a corner in the ship’s saloon and delivered a short speech through the able interpretation of Mr. Iwao Ayusawa, the Japanese member of the Labour Office. He said he was mighty glad to have arrived safely in Japan, a country which he has always admired and loved. He cordially thanked all for the hearty welcome at the pier and wished to be excused for not being able to return the courtesy individually.

Man of Sober Appearance

Monsieur Thomas is a man of sober appearance with an expression obvious of keen intelligence. He is rather stout though not very tall, and his face carries the evidence of good health and dynamic energy. He was clad all in black from head to foot, carrying the suggestion of a socialistic professor. Intelligent observers, however, did not fail to perceive in him the qualities of congeniality and broad-minded statesmanship, toned by extensive experience in big affairs of the world.

Interviewed by pressmen at the Oriental Hotel, Monsieur Thomas spoke rather freely, avoiding nevertheless touching upon subjects which might embarrass the Japanese Government, or render his position in this country awkward. Interrogated about the purposes of his visit to this country, he replied with a large smile that he intended to meet the many friends he has in Japan, to discuss with the people as to the best means of promoting co-operation between Japan and the organisation of which he is the chief official, and, last but not the least, to coax the Japanese Government to do more by way of ratifying some of the important labour conventions adopted at Geneva.

Visit to Russia Explained

When asked what he did in Russia, the Director appeared slightly perplexed but replied that, contrary to the rumour that he was rather maltreated at Moscow, he was most warmly received by the Bolshevik authorities. He wished to remind the journalists, however, that Russia is not, like Japan, a member of the Labour Organisation and that accordingly his position in Russia was quite different from what it is in Japan where he feels more at home because it is one of the most ardent supporters of the Geneva organisation. What he evidently wanted to suggest was that there was no such sentiment of hostility between him and Bolshevik leaders as is often suspected, for if there was he would not have been able to pass pleasant days in Moscow as he did.

“The Soviet today,” continued Mr. Thomas, “is no longer a mystery to the outer world. She is at present struggling with her serious economic difficulties and her greatest desire is to reorganize her economic sys-

托马斯先生抵达神户受到热烈欢迎

访客首次向海员发表讲话

国际劳工局局长在此会见友人并促进劳工利益

“我对日本的第一印象简直迷人，”阿尔伯特·托马斯先生（Monsieur Albert Thomas）从上海抵达神户时说道。他的登陆场面热烈，约有3,000名工人前来问候，他们代表了20多个不同的工会和组织。这位国际劳工局局长在“上海丸”号（S.S. Shanghai Maru）的甲板上向这些人致以简短的问候，随即进入东方酒店（Oriental Hotel），并从那里被送往日本海员工会的神户总部。在这里，他向大批听众发表了讲话，保证他始终真诚地希望与日本工人合作。

在载着这位著名局长的“上海丸”号抵达前整整一个小时，码头上就出现了异常的激动场面。一大群人——主要是工人——焦急地等待船只靠岸。人群中不乏显赫人物，如日本劳工联合会著名领袖铃木文治先生（Mr. Bunji Suzuki）、大阪工商会议所会长稻畑胜太郎先生（Mr. Inabata）以及法国驻神户领事豪什科尔内先生（Monsieur Hauchecorne），此外还有大阪府官员及许多其他人。

激进分子的威胁

鉴于有谣言称激进分子可能袭击这位访客，码头由大量警察谨慎守卫；但事实证明，这种 precaution 完全是不必要的。

当船只缓缓向码头驶去，人群认出了局长微笑的面容时，几乎自发地爆发出雷鸣般的“万岁”欢呼声。

托马斯先生挥舞帽子回应热情的问候，对受到的热烈接待表示极为感激。

舷梯一搭好，数百人争着登船，托马斯先生很快就被朋友和熟人包围，大家都很高兴看到他在日本上岸。初步寒暄结束后，局长请人群到船舱休息室的一角，并通过劳工局的日本成员鮎川岩雄先生（Mr. Iwao Ayusawa）的出色翻译发表了简短演讲。他说，他很庆幸安全抵达日本，这是一个他一直钦佩和热爱的国家。他衷心感谢大家在码头的热情欢迎，并请求原谅他无法逐一回礼。

外表庄重之人

托马斯先生外表庄重，神情中明显流露出敏锐的智慧。他身材较胖，个子不高，面容显示出良好的健康状况和充沛的精力。他从头到脚一身黑衣，给人一种社会主义教授的印象。然而，敏锐的观察者不难在他身上看到随和的气质和开阔的政治家胸襟，这些特质因其在世界重大事务中的丰富经验而显得沉稳。

在东方酒店接受记者采访时，托马斯先生谈话相当自由，但仍避免触及可能使日本政府尴尬或使其在本国处境为难的话题。当被问及访问本国的目的时，他微笑着回答说，他打算会见他在日本的许多朋友，与人们讨论促进日本与他所领导的组织之间合作的最佳方式，最后但同样重要的是，劝说日本政府采取更多行动，批准在日内瓦通过的一些重要劳工公约。

解释访俄之行

当被问及他在俄罗斯做了什么时，局长显得有些困惑，但回答说，与他在莫斯科受到虐待的谣言相反，他受到了布尔什维克当局最热烈的接待。不过，他希望提醒记者们，俄罗斯不像日本那样是劳工组织的成员，因此他在俄罗斯的立场与在日本完全不同；在日本他感到更自在，因为日本是日内瓦组织最热情的支持者之一。他显然想暗示的是，他与布尔什维克领导人之间并不存在常被人怀疑的那种敌意，因为如果存在这种敌意，他就不可能在莫斯科度过愉快的日子。

“今天的苏维埃，”托马斯先生继续说，“对外部世界来说已不再神秘。她目前正在与严重的经济困难作斗争，她最大的愿望是在共产主义原则的基础上重组其经济系

Impressions China
When queried to what he
thought of China her present
situation, Monsieur Thomas shrug-
ged his shoulders in characteristic
manner and said he should like it
to be remembered that he was neither
an encyclopedia, nor a professional
diplomat capable of discoursing on
any question in the world. He gave
assurance that there was no other
intention in visiting China than to
meet some of the leaders of Kuo-
mintang and to talk over with them
the best means of further promot-
ing the collaboration always exist-
ing between China and the organi-
sation in matters of social and in-
dustrial legislation.
"Are we ready to co-operate with
the Kuomintang Government in
China? Yes, so far as the present
political conditions in China are
concerned, the Kuomintang Gov-
ernment that exists, and naturally
we are anxious to have China join,
through that Government, in our
movement for the establishment of
Socialistic, instead of Capitalistic
legislation for the welfare of the
people at large. That is the main
principle of the institution I rep-
resent. One of the principles of the
late Dr. Sun Yat-sen, founder of
the Kuomintang Party in China,
was to promote the welfare of the
common people, and I feel sure that
China, as governed by the Kuomin-
tung element, will find it possible to
co-operate with us for the accom-
plishment of our common object."
Perhaps the most timely ques-
tion asked of the Director was what
he thought of Japanese radicals.
Monsieur Thomas' reply was a
model of intelligence and tactful-
ness. He stated that he is not yet
in full acquaintance with them, but
that he believed it would be found
that there existed common ground
of understanding if he was given
the opportunity to meet them per-
sonally and exchange opinions.
He had heard that a cer-
tain faction was not quite pleased
to see him in Japan, but he is con-
fident that these radical people will
be satisfied with his visit by the
time they know more about the
ideals which have been prompting
him in his international effort for
social justice.

Visitor Admires The Scenery
The most pleasant question that
could be asked of him and which he
most wanted to answer was what
was his impression of Japan upon
landing at Kobe. "Why, it is simply
charming!" exclaimed the Director
with the heartiest smile. "The tem-
perature," said "is not quite as
warm as I should like it to be; but,
nevertheless I am perfectly happy."
The press interview had to be cut
short because Monsieur Thomas was
scheduled to attend the general
meeting of the Japan Seamen's
Union in Kobe. Mr. Kunitaro
Hamada, president of the Union,
extended cordial welcome to the na-
tional guest, expressing his Union's
gratitude for the Director's unfail-
ing support of the cause of Japa-
nese labour. Mr. Bunji Suzuki
spoke at length, dwelling upon the
difficult battles Japanese workers
have been and still are wag-
ing against the contrary forces
which are in operation. He said
that the workingmen of Japan are
not well versed in French and there-
fore are not able to express their
sentiments to the Director, but that
how grateful they are for the un-
tiring encouragement he has been
extending to them, was shown by
their presence at the pier so eager
to greet him and cry "Thomas Ban-
zai!" He added that the Japanese
working population shall forever re-
member Monsieur Thomas' friendly
support of their cause, and that
they will increasingly depend upon
his effort for the improvement of
their status in Japan.
The Director in cordial tone ex-
pressed his hearty thanks for the
enthusiasm with which the working
men greeted him on his arrival. He
said that he is usually greeted when
visiting different places by men re-
presenting governments, capitalists,
and workers. But he gave assur-
ance that nothing pleased him as
much as being warmly received by
workers. Monsieur Thomas, there-
fore, highly appreciated the op-
portunity to be the guest of
Seamen's Union immediately upon
landing on Japanese soil. He
declared that he was more
than willing to do his best toward
promoting the interest of Japanese
workers. This speech, so sincere
and tactful, was met with tremend-
ous applause and he seemed to be
perfectly happy.
Monsieur Thomas is accompanied
by Mr. Phelan the head of the
Diplomatic Division of the Labour
Office, Mr. Vipple the chief of the
Director's secretariat, Mr. Duboury
and Mr. Ayusawa, both acting as
Thomas' secretaries. The party,
after spending a night in Kobe, will
go to Tokyo on Thursday, after-
noon's train.

对中国的印象
当被问及对中国及其当前局势的看法时，托马斯先生以特有的方式耸了耸肩，并表示希望大家记住，他既不是百科全书，也不是能对世界上任何问题侃侃而谈的职业外交官。他保证，访问中国没有其他意图，只是为了会见国民党的一些领导人，并与他们商讨如何进一步促进中国与该组织在社会和工业立法方面一直存在的合作。
“我们准备与中国的国民党政府合作吗？是的，就中国目前的政治状况而言，现存的国民党政府，自然我们渴望中国通过该政府加入我们的运动，即为广大人民的福祉建立社会主义而非资本主义的立法。这是我代表的机构的主要原则。中国国民党创始人孙中山博士晚年的原则之一是促进普通民众的福祉，我确信，由国民党元素治理的中国将发现有可能与我们合作，以实现我们的共同目标。”
也许向局长提出的最及时的问题是他对日本激进分子的看法。托马斯先生的回答是智慧和 tactfulness 的典范。他表示，他尚未与他们充分熟悉，但他相信，如果有机会亲自会面并交换意见，就会发现存在共同的理解基础。
他听说某些派系不太乐意见到他在日本，但他确信，当这些激进人士更多地了解推动他为社会正义进行国际努力的理想时，会对他的访问感到满意。

访客赞赏风景
可以问他的最令人愉快的问题，也是他最想回答的问题，是他在神户登陆时对日本的印象。“哎呀，简直迷人！”局长带着最真诚的笑容惊呼道。“气温，”他说，“不如我希望的那样温暖；但尽管如此，我非常快乐。”
由于托马斯先生预定参加日本海员工会在神户举行的全体会议，新闻采访不得不缩短。工会会长滨田国太郎先生（Mr. Kunitaro Hamada）向这位国宾表示热烈欢迎，表达了工会对局长一贯支持日本劳工事业的感激之情。铃木文治先生作了长篇发言，详述了日本工人过去和现在一直在与各种不利势力进行的艰难斗争。他说，日本工人不精通法语，因此无法向局长表达他们的情感，但他们对他给予的不懈鼓励是多么感激，这从他们在码头急切迎接他并高呼“托马斯万岁！”的表现中可见一斑。他补充说，日本劳动人民将永远铭记托马斯先生对他们事业的友好支持，并将越来越依赖他的努力来改善他们在日本的地位。
局长以亲切的语气衷心感谢工人们在抵达时对他的热情问候。他说，他在访问不同地方时，通常会有代表政府、资本家和工人的人士向他致意。但他保证，没有什么比受到工人的热情接待更让他高兴的了。因此，托马斯先生非常感激刚踏上日本国土就成为海员工会客人的机会。他声明，他非常愿意为促进日本工人的利益尽最大努力。这篇真诚而得体的演讲赢得了巨大的掌声，他似乎非常快乐。
陪同托马斯先生的是劳工局外交司司长费伦先生（Mr. Phelan）、局长秘书处主任维普尔先生（Mr. Vipple）、以及担任托马斯秘书的杜布里先生（Mr. Duboury）和鮎川先生（Mr. Ayusawa）。一行人在神户过夜后，将于周四下午乘火车前往东京。

THE OSAKA MAINICHI & THE TOKYO NICHI NICHI, OSAKA, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 4, 1928

Monsieur Albert Thomas

Portrait by an Anonymous Writer Appearing in The
"Review des Jeunes", Paris

Translated From French Text

This article written with much style is an admirable portrait of Monsieur Albert Thomas, the celebrated Director of International Labour Organisation, who is to arrive in Kobe on December 4 to stay in Japan for about a month. The anonymous author, as far as the editor is aware, is a youthful writer closely associated with Monsieur Thomas. The editor might also add that this is the only one of many portraits of Albert Thomas which he himself recognised as excellent.

Must we confess it? It is not without some apprehension that, on this white sheet, we write the name of a politician. How can we depict faithfully an actor embodying various characters? More especially, how can we make the spectators, who have before their eyes a certain image of the subject, admit that this image is but an appearance and that the true face of the man will be discovered only after scraping the paint and withdrawing the artificial light?

Among the stars on the political stage, Mr. Albert Thomas is perhaps more difficult to appreciate than anyone else. That is why the most divergent judgements are being expressed on him in equally categorical tones.

For some, he may be characterized in a few traits borrowed from the successive roles he played: it is the socialist professor, the fiery disciple of Jaures, soon his emulator, the mayor of Champigny and Deputy of the Tarn;—the Minister of Armaments, providence of "comrades" which he placed in offices and arsenals in the rear, dispenser of good orders and high salaries;—then the diplomat who fails to see behind Kerensky the silhouette of Lenin;—and lastly the Director of the International Labour Office, comfortably seated in his chair in Geneva, in charge of the amelioration of the labourers' fate.

Two Views

"Mistake or calumny!" reply others (who are not necessarily his political fellow-believers). This man remained on all the paths in which destiny led him an apostle, generous-hearted, ardently faithful to his ideals, a man of a luminous and acute intelligence, of valiant and tenacious will. Should you have any doubt on this, listen to the orator. His clear, warm and stirring speech is a warrant of his soul.

Need we choose between such contradictory portraits? Let us rather try to disentangle from among these contrasts the essential lines of the subject.

When the name of Mr. Albert Thomas is brought into a conversation, it is seldom that a question does not spring forth naturally and artlessly: "Is he still a socialist or not?"

Yes, certainly, if you deem that convictions can find their just and complete expression in the manifestations of Leagues and Parties, Albert Thomas has remained, on the shores of the Leman, the militant socialist that he was among the miners of Carmaux, in the meetings of his youth, of which he keeps a tender souvenir. On several occasions, as if to defend himself against perfidious or benevolent insinuations, the Director of the International Labour Office has made it a point to prove, in participating in socialist ceremonies or congresses, that he had not changed his flag. And his intellectual pride, his independence as polemist, rebel when a touchy Governing Body pretends to remind him that an official—even an international one—must observe some moderation in his public life.

Growing by Experience

It is none the less certain that from 1914 to today, the political thoughts of Mr. Albert Thomas have become richer from precious experiences. Called to Parliament from professorship, and confined to the side of opposition, he became, by the grace of Mars, a powerful Minister and a man-handler. The mankind which he then became acquainted with was no more the same as that he was accustomed to meet in the offices of "L'Humanite" (although this paper did not fail to maintain his collaboration): he was intimately mixed with the creative efforts of these manufacturers and chiefs of enterprises whom perhaps before he only saw imperfectly in their attempts at resistance against claims which were dear to him. 阿尔贝·托马斯先生

刊登于巴黎《青年评论》（Review des Jeunes）的一篇匿名作者肖像描写

译自法文原文

这篇文笔优美的文章是对国际劳工组织著名主任阿尔贝·托马斯先生的精彩肖像描写，他将于12月4日抵达神户，在日本停留约一个月。据编辑所知，这位匿名作者是一位与托马斯先生关系密切的年轻作家。编辑还可以补充说，在众多关于阿尔贝·托马斯的肖像描写中，这是唯一一篇得到他本人认可为优秀的作品。

我们是否必须承认这一点？在这张白纸上写下一位政治家的名字时，我们不免有些忐忑。我们要如何忠实地描绘一个扮演各种角色的演员？更重要的是，我们要如何让那些眼前已有既定印象的观众承认，这种印象不过是表象，而只有刮去油彩、撤去人造灯光后，才能发现此人真实的面目？

在政治舞台的群星中，阿尔贝·托马斯先生或许比任何人都更难被赏识。正因如此，人们对他的评价两极分化，且语气同样斩钉截铁。

对一些人来说，可以用他从 successive 角色中借来的几个特征来刻画他：他是社会主义教授，是饶勒斯（Jaures）热情的弟子，不久成为其效仿者，尚皮尼（Champigny）市长和塔恩省（Tarn）议员；——他是军需部长，是“同志们”的守护神，他将这些人安置在后方的办公室和兵工厂里，分发优厚的命令和高薪；——然后他是那位未能透过克伦斯基看到列宁身影的外交家；——最后，他是国际劳工局局长，舒适地坐在日内瓦的椅子上，负责改善劳动者的命运。

两种观点

“错误还是诽谤！”其他人（他们不一定是他的政治同道）回答道。这个人在命运引领他的所有道路上始终是一位使徒，心胸宽广，热烈忠于自己的理想，拥有明亮而敏锐的智慧，以及勇敢而顽强的意志。如果你对此有任何怀疑，请听听这位演说家的言论。他那清晰、温暖且激动人心的演讲是他灵魂的保证。

我们需要在这些相互矛盾的肖像之间做出选择吗？不如让我们试着从这些对比中梳理出此人的主要脉络。

当阿尔贝·托马斯先生的名字出现在谈话中时，很少不会自然而然且天真地冒出一个问题：“他还是社会主义者吗？”

是的，当然，如果你认为信念可以在联盟和政党的表现中找到公正而完整的表达，那么阿尔贝·托马斯在莱芒湖（Leman）岸边，仍然像他在卡尔莫（Carmaux）矿工中、在他青年时代的集会上那样，是一名战斗的社会主义者，他对那些集会保持着温柔的回忆。有几次，仿佛是为了防御恶意或善意的暗示，国际劳工局局长特意通过参加社会主义仪式或代表大会来证明，他并没有改变旗帜。而他的知识分子的骄傲、作为论战者的独立性，在一个敏感的理事会试图提醒他官员——即使是国际官员——在公共生活中必须保持适度克制时，便会奋起反抗。

经验带来的成长

尽管如此，可以肯定的是，从1914年至今，阿尔贝·托马斯先生的政治思想因宝贵的经验而变得更加丰富。他从教授职位被召入议会，并局限于反对派席位，却因战争之神（Mars）的眷顾，成为一位权势显赫的部长和善于驾驭人物的人。那时他所结识的人类，已不再是他习惯于在《人道报》（L'Humanite）编辑部遇到的人（尽管该报并未停止与他的合作）：他与那些制造商和企业领袖的创造性努力紧密交织在一起，而此前他可能只是在不完美地观察他们抵抗那些对他而言珍贵的诉求时的尝试。仿佛战争并不满足于给予这位年轻的宠儿如此丰厚的赏赐，还想通过一种确凿的继承关系，使他在随后的疯狂岁月中免于挥霍这些所得的诱惑，《和平条约》的整整一章确立了 ob-

page_data.en:
servatory where Mr. Albert
Thomas would be able, in all
liberty, to perfect his political edu-
cation. Ministers, officials, em-
ployers and workers of all countries
would come to him there, and it was
going to be easy for him to observe
the reactions of their national or
social sensibilities upon the treat-
ment that he was going to inflict on
them.

No Idle Post

Do not imagine, however, that Mr.
Albert Thomas has seen in his di-
rectorial post of Geneva but a chair
to go to sleep on, or—to speak like
Mr. Ferdinand Brunot—a particu-
larly well-equipped laboratory of
political psychology. It has often
been recalled that Mr. Albert
Thomas had qualified himself as the
"Wandering Jew of Social Politics."
Whatever opinion one may have
on the value of the goods that he
offers in the capitals of the whole
world, the tribulations and the visits
of Mr. Albert Thomas are, for him
at least, of the greatest interest.
Before him the high international
official doors open which would have
remained closed to the Frenchman
or to the Socialist. And Mr. Al-
bert Thomas has so many friends
who are happy to help him in keep-
ing these doors ajar. . . . If the
former Minister of Armaments en-
tertains, as is believed in some quar-
ters, the secret ambition to be one
day installed in the Quai d'Orsay,
the peregrinations which one week
lead his steps to the Balkans and
the next month to London, Berlin
or Rome (Quirinal and Vatican),
and which will perhaps soon take
him to Latin America after having
led him but lately from Quebec to
Washington, are certainly for him
an exceptional preparation and the
best personal propaganda in ad-
vance. . . . No doubt also that such
diverse contacts will have effaced
in him certain prejudices (in the
better sense of the word), and that
in rubbing himself to the political
constructions of the most various
styles, his own doctrine will have
smoothened its angles.

Still a Socialist

No illusions! however. Whatever
the name given today to ornate
them, the political ideas of Mr. Al-
bert Thomas remain imbued with so-
cialism. Is he not himself impreg-
nated with the image of Jaures to
whose memory he keeps an almost
filial affection? Further, could he,
like a Barres, resign himself, even
if he wanted to, to break the con-
tinuous trait which runs through
his life? Remembrances of a youth
devoted with enthusiasm to a Cause,
signs ever present of a parliamen-
tary past which has remained dear
to the tribune, comradeships some-
times troublesome, but also rich in
common efforts, how powerful you
are on the souls for which you re-
present Tradition!

Setting aside all petty contention
of words, one can say of Mr. Albert
Thomas, without risking to be con-
tradicted, that he is above all a so-
cial spirit and a democrat. The
Director of the International La-
bour Office has nothing of the offi-
cial; he is really an apostle. With
a tenacity and a suppleness which
his opponents are bound to admire,
he endeavours since five years to
lift, with the yet fragile lever of
international labour conventions, the
heavy stones of routine or egoism,
and to remove the obstacles (sin-
gularly more solid) which are rais-
ed before the pioneers of social leg-
islation by the after-war economic
difficulties

It is not through sheer profes-
sional vanity that this rough artisan
persists in his work in spite of the
mediocrity of the results so far
obtained. No doubt he believes
sincerely in the value of his tools
and his methods; but he is above
all persuaded that through the In-
ternational Labour Conference, as
well as by his proceedings and
voluminous correspondence, he
beneficiates the interests of the
workers and of the weak.

Democrat, Mr. Albert Thomas is
so, deeply, proudly. He has never
thought of hiding his popular con-
nections. No doubt he appreciates
the advantages of his present
situation; few capitalists are
acquainted as he is with the most
diverse European personalities.
But neither his association with
sovereigns nor his official receptions
have succeeded in turning his head.
After divesting himself of his
frockcoat and top-hat, he becomes
again the simple-mannered, and
easy-of-approach son of the
"Poitevin" baker. No mistake
about it. Through the parliamentary
phraseology of Mr. Albert Thomas'
speeches there passes a great breath
of this democratic spirit which
animated Jaures and which, perhaps,
deep at heart, is but a form of
human charity of those intellectuals.

Here lies the evil, would hasten
to say those who have not forgotten
the pre-war old tracks and seriously
begin to fear their re-appearance.
Such enthusiasm for Peace and
Humanity will surely lead us to war
and social struggle. Do you not
see that Mr. Albert Thomas, little
by little, forgets in Geneva that he
ever was in France one of the chiefs
of the National Defence? Do you
not hear him in the League of In-
struction or in the League of the
Republic, associate himself with the
sectarian campaigns of division?

Patriot

It is a fact that the Director of
the International Labour Office has
furnished to his political opponents,
sometimes through imprudence,
often also through fault or
negligence of those about him, many
opportunities to throw suspicion on
his patriotism. He himself must
sometimes feel with a little anguish
similar cases of conscience. The
French people who have approached
him and seen him at work in his
international functions could hardly
believe, however, that he did not
remain the patriot that they had
known during the war. Even if one
did not take into account the tone
of his voice when he speaks
of his country, how could such
a clear mind forget what he
owes to the French intellectu-
al disciplines? And what a com-
forting impression for his country-
men to see, among the confusion
and mediocrity of certain interna-
tional palavers, a Frenchman clear
up the chaotic ideas, classifying,
grouping and appreciating the argu-
ments. As his demonstration goes
on, the light is made in the dark
bushes and straight and calm
avenues open on every side as in a
French park. At certain cross-
roads we have to abandon the
orator, but it is with regret. . . .
Why does not Mr. Albert Thomas
administrate men as he regulates
ideas?

Though a layman, Mr. Albert
Thomas is liberal and very respect-
ful of religion. Is it sheer policy
in order to reserve to his work of
today and to his future plans the
sympathy of the Catholics? An in-
fluent member of the French As-
sociation for the Legal Protection
of the Workers, Mr. Albert Thomas
is too well acquainted with the
feelings and the work of the Social
Christians, and is too much enlight-
ened as to the spirit of youth, not
to feel towards the Catholics, but an
interested politeness. I know that,
at times, in the heat of his speeches,
the apostle of international labour
legislation may have dropped menac-
ing words. He once said: "One
can expect big things only from
those who are ready to burn the old
temples in order to edify new ones."
An observer, less inclined to en-
thusiasm than to criticism, is some-
times shocked by the dogmatic tone
with which this unbeliever affirms
that one must believe in the benefits
of international labour legislation.
In the severe Geneva Conference,
smiles are not in fashion. It is per-
haps because at bottom, irony is
aristocratic.

Man of Action

We must respect the faith of Mr.
Albert Thomas, but this does not
prevent us, however, if we thinks
it useful to try to limit its overflow.
It is besides difficult to imagine
that such an ardent temperament
could cover the soul of a sceptic.
Mr. Albert Thomas is not a
businessman but a man of action.
It remains to be seen to what extent
the man has been modelled by the
actor. Often, in listening to the
orator, we hesitate in attributing
the part of play and that of sinceri-
ty. In a thousand tokens we re-
cognise the influence of the parlia-
mentary platform: in the progres-
sion of the voice and the abrupt
silences precursory of a storm, in
the gesture of the hands which
gallop from beard to hair and which
hammer the folders, even in the
movements of emotion, we have an
impression of "true", and we regret
it just as we regret the abuse of
vibrato on a good cello. Luckily,
under the artist, we soon find the
man again.

The International Labour Office
offers for the present to this man
of action the wish of his nature in
the occasion to devote himself by
means of eloquence and diplomacy,
to the service of a nobly ideological
cause. But every great work has its
time. . . . What will become of
Mr. Albert Thomas the day he
leaves Geneva? His absence from
Parliament has no doubt, in the
last years, spared him many dif-
ficulties, we might even say, many
blunders. On this chapter, besides,
he could not compete with Mr.
Herriot and still less (in spite of
his friendship with Mr. George
Scelle) with Mr. Francois Albert.
But still the fact remains that during
his absence the posts have been
occupied. We do not imagine Mr.
Albert Thomas returning to sit in
the socialist seats under the ferula
of Mr. Leon Blum. . . . But is he
not born under a good star? A lucky
turn of events will perhaps facilitate
his re-entrance into the French
political life. Who knows but that
he is not the man of a new Sacred
Union which is expected by the
warriors, disgusted with the sordid
pastimes of the pre-war sectarians?
. . . Mr. Albert Thomas has enough
political pliancy to know how to
profit by timely circumstances. We
also believe that he is too faithful
to his convictions that we need fear
him to be accessible to equivocal
party combinations.
page_data.zh:
在那里，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生（Mr. Albert Thomas）将能够自由地完善他的政治教育。各国的部长、官员、雇主和工人都会来到他面前，他将很容易观察到他们对他的对待方式所产生的民族或社会情感反应。

并非闲职

然而，不要以为阿尔伯特·托马斯先生把他在日内瓦的主任职位仅仅看作是一把可以睡觉的椅子，或者——借用费迪南德·布吕诺（Ferdinand Brunot）先生的话来说——是一个设备特别精良的政治心理学实验室。人们常常提起，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生曾自称为“社会政治中的流浪犹太人”。无论人们对他在世界各首都推销的货物价值持何种看法，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生的磨难和访问对他本人至少具有极大的意义。在他面前，那些对法国人或社会主义者原本紧闭的高级国际官方大门敞开了。而阿尔伯特·托马斯先生有许多朋友乐于帮助他让这些门保持微开……如果这位前军备部长像某些圈子所相信的那样，怀有朝一日入驻凯道赛（Quai d'Orsay，即法国外交部）的秘密野心，那么他这一周足迹踏遍巴尔干，下个月又前往伦敦、柏林或罗马（奎里纳莱宫和梵蒂冈），并且不久前刚从魁北克到华盛顿，或许很快又将前往拉丁美洲的奔波，无疑对他来说是一种非凡的准备和最好的个人预先宣传……毫无疑问，这样多样的接触也会消除他身上的某些偏见（取其褒义），并且在与各种风格的政治架构磨合中，他自己的学说也会磨去棱角。

仍是社会主义者

然而，不要抱有任何幻想！无论今天人们给这些政治思想贴上什么华丽的标签，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生的政治思想仍然浸透着社会主义色彩。难道他自己不是深受饶勒斯（Jaures）形象的影响，并对他的记忆保持着近乎子女般的 affection 吗？此外，他能否像巴雷斯（Barres）那样，即使愿意，也甘心切断贯穿其一生的连续线索？青年时期热情奉献给一项事业的回忆，议会生涯中始终存在且为这位演说家所珍视的痕迹，有时令人烦恼但也充满共同努力的战友情谊，对于你们所代表传统的灵魂来说，你们的力量是多么强大！

撇开所有琐碎的文字争执，我们可以毫不冒犯地说，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生首先是一个具有社会精神和民主精神的人。国际劳工局局长没有一点官僚气；他确实是一位使徒。五年来，他以对手也不得不钦佩的坚韧和灵活，试图用尚且脆弱的国际劳工公约杠杆，撬起惯例或自私的沉重石块，并清除战后经济困难为社会立法先驱们设置的（格外坚固的）障碍。

这位粗犷的工匠坚持工作，并非出于纯粹的职业虚荣心，尽管迄今为止取得的成果平平。毫无疑问，他真诚地相信他的工具和方法的价值；但他更坚信，通过国际劳工大会，以及通过他的程序和大量的通信，他正在造福工人和弱者的利益。

阿尔伯特·托马斯先生是一位民主主义者，深沉而自豪。他从未想过隐藏自己的平民渊源。毫无疑问，他欣赏当前处境的有利条件；很少有资本家像他那样熟悉如此多样的欧洲人物。但是，无论是与君主的交往还是官方的接待，都没能让他头脑发热。脱下礼服和高顶礼帽后，他又变回了那位“普瓦图”（Poitevin）面包师之子，举止简朴，平易近人。这一点毋庸置疑。透过阿尔伯特·托马斯先生演讲中的议会辞令，传递出一股强烈的民主气息，这种气息曾激励着饶勒斯，也许在内心深处，这只是那些知识分子的一种人道慈善形式。

那些没有忘记战前旧轨道并开始认真担心其重现的人会急忙说，祸根就在这里。这种对和平与人道的热情肯定会导致战争和社会斗争。难道你没看到阿尔伯特·托马斯先生在日内瓦逐渐忘记了他曾在法国担任国防领袖之一吗？难道你没听到他在教育联盟或共和国联盟中，将自己与宗派性的分裂运动联系在一起吗？

爱国者

事实上，国际劳工局局长由于有时不够谨慎，也常因身边人的过错或疏忽，给他的政治反对派提供了许多质疑他爱国心的机会。他自己有时也必定带着些许焦虑感受到类似的良心不安。然而，接近他并目睹他在国际职能中工作的法国人，几乎无法相信他没有保持他们在战争期间所认识的那位爱国者形象。即使不考虑他谈论祖国时的语气，这样一个头脑清晰的人怎么会忘记他欠法国智力训练的情分呢？看到一位法国人在某些国际空谈的混乱和平庸中理清混沌的思想，分类、归纳和评估论点，这对他的同胞来说是多么令人欣慰的印象。随着他的论证展开，黑暗灌木丛中的光亮显现，笔直平静的林荫道向四面八方敞开，就像在法国公园中一样。在某些十字路口，我们不得不离开这位演说家，但这令人遗憾……为什么阿尔伯特·托马斯先生不能像梳理思想那样管理人员呢？

虽然是个俗人，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生却是自由主义者，并且非常尊重宗教。这仅仅是为了为他今天的工作和未来的计划保留天主教徒的同感而采取的策略吗？作为法国工人法律保护协会（French Association for the Legal Protection of the Workers）中有影响力的成员，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生对社会基督徒（Social Christians）的感受和工作太熟悉了，对青年精神也太了解了，以至于他对天主教徒不仅仅表现出出于利益的礼貌。我知道，有时在演讲的热潮中，这位国际劳工立法的使徒可能会说出威胁性的话语。他曾经说过：“只有那些准备烧毁旧庙宇以建立新庙宇的人，才能期待伟大的成就。”一位观察家，比起热情更倾向于批评，有时会对这位不信教者以教条式的口吻断言必须相信国际劳工立法的益处感到震惊。在严肃的日内瓦会议上，微笑并不流行。这也许是因为在骨子里，讽刺是贵族式的。

行动之人

我们必须尊重阿尔伯特·托马斯先生的信仰，但如果我们认为有必要，这并不妨碍我们试图限制其泛滥。此外，很难想象如此热烈的性情会掩盖一个怀疑论者的灵魂。阿尔伯特·托马斯先生不是商人，而是行动之人。还有待观察的是，这个人被演员角色塑造到了什么程度。通常，在聆听这位演说家时，我们在归因表演成分和真诚成分之间犹豫不决。在成千上万的迹象中，我们认出了议会讲台的影响：在声音的推进和预示风暴的突然沉默中，在从胡须到头发飞舞并敲击文件夹的手势中，甚至在情感的举动中，我们都有一种“真实”的印象，正如我们惋惜一把好大提琴上揉弦技巧的滥用一样令人遗憾。幸运的是，在艺术家之下，我们很快又找到了那个人。

目前，国际劳工局为这位行动之人提供了顺应其天性的愿望，即通过雄辩和外交手段，投身于一项具有崇高意识形态的事业。但每项伟大的工作都有其时机……阿尔伯特·托马斯先生离开日内瓦的那一天会变成什么样？毫无疑问，在过去几年里，他缺席议会使他避免了许多困难，甚至可以说，许多失误。在这一方面，他无法与赫里欧先生（Mr. Herriot）竞争，更不用说（尽管他与乔治·斯塞尔先生 Mr. George Scelle 有友谊）与弗朗索瓦·阿尔伯特先生（Mr. Francois Albert）相比了。但事实仍然是，在他缺席期间，职位已被占据。我们不认为阿尔伯特·托马斯先生会在莱昂·布鲁姆先生（Mr. Leon Blum）的管束下回到社会主义席位就座……但他不是生来就有好运吗？局势的幸运转折或许会促进他重新进入法国政治生活。谁知道他会不会成为战士们所期待的新神圣联盟（Sacred Union）的人物，这些战士已对战前宗派分子的卑劣消遣感到厌恶？……阿尔伯特·托马斯先生有足够的政治灵活性，懂得如何利用适时的环境。我们也相信，他对自己的信念如此忠诚，以至于我们不必担心他会受到暧昧的党派组合的影响。

THE OSAKA MAINICHI & THE TOKYO NICHI NICHI. OSAKA, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 4, 1928

Monsieur Albert Thomas

A Portrait by an Anonymous Writer Appearing in The
"Review des Jeunes", Paris

Translated From French Text

The article written with much style is an admirable portrait of Monsieur Albert Thomas, the celebrated Director of International Labour Organisation, who is to arrive in Kobe on December 4 to stay in Japan for about a month. The anonymous author, as far as the editor is aware, is a youthful writer closely associated with Monsieur Thomas. The editor might also add that this is the only one of many portraits of Albert Thomas which he himself recognised as excellent.

Must we confess it? It is not without some apprehension that, on this white sheet, we write the name of a politician. How can we depict faithfully an actor embodying various characters? More especially, how can we make the spectators, who have before their eyes a certain image of the subject, admit that this image is but an appearance and that the true face of the man will be discovered only after scraping the paint and withdrawing the artificial light?

Among the stars on the political stage, Mr. Albert Thomas is perhaps more difficult to appreciate than anyone else. That is why the most divergent judgements are being expressed on him in equally categorical tones.

For some, he may be characterized in a few traits borrowed from the successive roles he played: it is the socialist professor, the fiery disciple of Jaures, soon his emulator, the mayor of Champigny and Deputy of the Tarn;—the Minister of Armaments, providence of "comrades" which he placed in offices and arsenals in the rear, dispenser of good orders and high salaries;—then the diplomat who fails to see behind Kerensky the silhouette of Lenin;—and lastly the Director of the International Labour Office, comfortably seated in his chair in Geneva, in charge of the amelioration of the labourers' fate.

Two Views

"Mistake or calumny!" reply others (who are not necessarily his political fellow-believers). This man remained on all the paths in which destiny led him an apostle, generous-hearted, ardently faithful to his ideals, a man of a luminous and acute intelligence, of valiant and tenacious will. Should you have any doubt on this, listen to the orator. His clear, warm and stirring speech is a warrant of his soul.

Need we choose between such contradictory portraits? Let us rather try to disentangle from among these contrasts the essential lines of the subject.

When the name of Mr. Albert Thomas is brought into a conversation, it is seldom that a question does not spring forth naturally and artlessly: "Is he still a socialist or not?"

Yes, certainly, if you deem that convictions can find their just and complete expression in the manifestations of Leagues and Parties, Albert Thomas has remained, on the shores of the Leman, the militant socialist that he was among the miners of Carmaux, in the meetings of his youth, of which he keeps a tender souvenir. On several occasions, as if to defend himself against perfidious or benevolent insinuations, the Director of the International Labour Office has made it a point to prove, in participating in socialist ceremonies or congresses, that he had not changed his flag. And his intellectual pride, his independence as polemist, rebel when a touchy Governing Body pretends to remind him that an official—even an international one—must observe some moderation in his public life.

Growing by Experience

It is none the less certain that from 1914 to today, the political thoughts of Mr. Albert Thomas have become richer from precious experiences. Called to Parliament from professorship, and confined to the side of opposition, he became, by the grace of Mars, a powerful Minister and a man-handler. The mankind which he then became acquainted with was no more the same as that he was accustomed to meet in the offices of "L'Humanite" (although this paper did not fail to maintain his collaboration): he was intimately mixed with the creative efforts of these manufacturers and chiefs of enterprises whom perhaps before he only saw imperfectly in their attempts at resistance against claims which were dear to him. As if the War, not content with bestowing such bounty upon his young favourite, wanted moreover by a sure inheritance to spare him the temptation to squander this acquirement in the years of madness that followed, a whole Chapter of the Treaty of Peace erected the ob-

《大阪每日新闻》与《东京日日新闻》。大阪，1928年12月4日，星期二

阿尔贝·托马斯先生

一幅由匿名作者撰写、刊登于巴黎《青年评论》上的肖像

译自法文原文

这篇文笔优美的文章是对国际劳工组织著名主任阿尔贝·托马斯先生的一幅令人钦佩的肖像描绘，他将于12月4日抵达神户，在日本停留约一个月。据编辑所知，这位匿名作者是一位与托马斯先生关系密切的年轻作家。编辑还可以补充说，在众多关于阿尔贝·托马斯的肖像描写中，这是唯一被他本人认可为出色的一篇。

我们是否必须承认这一点？在这张白纸上写下一位政治家的名字，并非毫无顾虑。我们如何忠实地描绘一个扮演各种角色的演员？尤其是，如何让那些眼前已有某种既定形象的观众承认，这形象仅仅是一种表象，而只有刮去油彩、撤去人造灯光后，才能发现此人真实的面目？

在政治舞台的群星中，阿尔贝·托马斯先生或许比任何人都更难被赏识。正因如此，人们对他的评价截然不同，但语气却同样斩钉截铁。

对一些人来说，可以用他从 successive 角色中借来的几个特征来刻画他：他是社会主义教授，是饶勒斯的热烈弟子，不久成为其效仿者，尚皮尼市长和塔恩省议员；——他是军需部长，是“同志们”的救星，他将他们安置在后方的办公室和兵工厂里，分发优厚的订单和高薪；——然后是一位外交家，未能透过克伦斯基看到列宁的轮廓；——最后是国际劳工局局长，舒适地坐在日内瓦的椅子上，负责改善劳动者的命运。

两种观点

“错误还是诽谤！”其他人（他们不一定是他的政治同信仰者）回答道。这个人在命运引领他的所有道路上始终是一位使徒，心胸宽广，热诚忠于自己的理想，拥有明亮而敏锐的智慧，以及勇敢而顽强的意志。如果你对此有任何怀疑，请听听这位演说家的言论。他那清晰、温暖且激动人心的演讲是他灵魂的保证。

我们需要在这些相互矛盾的肖像之间做出选择吗？不如让我们试着从这些对比中梳理出此人的主要脉络。

当阿尔贝·托马斯先生的名字出现在谈话中时，很少不会自然而然地、天真地冒出一个问题：“他还是社会主义者吗？”

是的，当然，如果你认为信念可以在联盟和政党的表现中找到公正而完整的表达，那么阿尔贝·托马斯在莱芒湖畔，仍然像他在卡尔莫矿工中、在他青年时代的集会上那样，是一名战斗的社会主义者，他对那些集会保持着温柔的回忆。有几次，仿佛是为了防御恶意或善意的暗示，国际劳工局局长特意通过参加社会主义仪式或代表大会来证明，他并没有改变旗帜。而他的知识分子的骄傲、作为论战者的独立性，在一个敏感的理事会试图提醒他官员——即使是国际官员——在公共生活中必须保持某种克制时，便会奋起反抗。

经验中的成长

尽管如此，可以肯定的是，从1914年至今，阿尔贝·托马斯先生的政治思想因宝贵的经验而变得更加丰富。他从教授职位被召入议会，并局限于反对派席位，却因战争之神马尔斯的眷顾，成为一位强有力的部长和善于驾驭人才的人。他当时所结识的人类，已不再是他习惯于在《人道报》办公室遇到的人（尽管该报并未停止与他的合作）：他与那些制造商和企业领袖的创造性努力紧密交织在一起，而此前他可能只是在不完美地观察他们抵抗他所珍视的要求时的尝试。仿佛战争并不满足于给予这位年轻的宠儿如此丰厚的赏赐，还想通过确凿的遗产，使他在随后的疯狂岁月中免于挥霍这一获得的诱惑，和平条约的一整章确立了 ob-

page_data.en:
servatory where Mr. Albert
Thomas would be able, in all
liberty, to perfect his political edu-
cation. Ministers, officials, em-
ployers and workers of all countries
would come to him there, and it was
going to be easy for him to observe
the reactions of their national or
social sensibilities upon the treat-
ment that he was going to inflict on
them.

No Idle Post

Do not imagine, however, that Mr.
Albert Thomas has seen in his di-
rectorial post of Geneva but a chair
to go to sleep on, or—to speak like
Mr. Ferdinand Brunot—a particu-
larly well-equipped laboratory of
political psychology. It has often
been recalled that Mr. Albert
Thomas had qualified himself as the
"Wandering Jew of Social Politics."
Whatever opinion one may have
on the value of the goods that he
offers in the capitals of the whole
world, the tribulations and the visits
of Mr. Albert Thomas are, for him
at least, of the greatest interest.
Before him the high international
official doors open which would have
remained closed to the Frenchman
or to the Socialist. And Mr. Al-
bert Thomas has so many friends
who are happy to help him in keep-
ing these doors ajar. . . . If the
former Minister of Armaments en-
tertains, as is believed in some quar-
ters, the secret ambition to be one
day installed in the Quai d'Orsay,
the peregrinations which one week
lead his steps to the Balkans and
the next month to London, Berlin
or Rome (Quirinal and Vatican),
and which will perhaps soon take
him to Latin America after having
led him but lately from Quebec to
Washington, are certainly for him
an exceptional preparation and the
best personal propaganda in ad-
vance. . . . No doubt also that such
diverse contacts will have effaced
in him certain prejudices (in the
better sense of the word), and that
in rubbing himself to the political
constructions of the most various
styles, his own doctrine will have
smoothened its angles.

Still a Socialist

No illusions! however. Whatever
the name given today to ornate
them, the political ideas of Mr. Al-
bert Thomas remain imbued with so-
cialism. Is he not himself impreg-
nated with the image of Jaures to
whose memory he keeps an almost
filial affection? Further, could he,
like a Barres, resign himself, even
if he wanted to, to break the con-
tinuous trait which runs through
his life? Remembrances of a youth
devoted with enthusiasm to a Cause,
signs ever present of a parliamen-
tary past which has remained dear
to the tribune, comradeships some-
times troublesome, but also rich in
common efforts, how powerful you
are on the souls for which you re-
present Tradition!

Setting aside all petty contention
of words, one can say of Mr. Albert
Thomas, without risking to be con-
tradicted, that he is above all a so-
cial spirit and a democrat. The
Director of the International La-
bour Office has nothing of the offi-
cial; he is really an apostle. With
a tenacity and a suppleness which
his opponents are bound to admire,
he endeavours since five years to
lift, with the yet fragile lever of
international labour conventions, the
heavy stones of routine or egoism,
and to remove the obstacles (sin-
gularly more solid) which are rais-
ed before the pioneers of social leg-
islation by the after-war economic
difficulties

It is not through sheer profes-
sional vanity that this rough artisan
persists in his work in spite of the
mediocrity of the results so far
obtained. No doubt he believes
sincerely in the value of his tools
and his methods; but he is above
all persuaded that through the In-
ternational Labour Conference, as
well as by his proceedings and
voluminous correspondence, he
beneficiates the interests of the
workers and of the weak.

Democrat, Mr. Albert Thomas is
so, deeply, proudly. He has never
thought of hiding his popular con-
nections. No doubt he appreciates
the advantages of his present
situation; few capitalists are
acquainted as he is with the most
diverse European personalities.
But neither his association with

sovereigns nor his official receptions
have succeeded in turning his head.
After divesting himself of his
frockcoat and top hat, he becomes
again the simple-mannered, and
easy-of-approach son of the
"Poitevin" baker. No mistake
about it. Through the parliamentary
phraseology of Mr. Albert Thomas'
speeches there passes a great breath
of this democratic spirit which
animated Jaures and which, perhaps,
deep at heart, is but a form of
human charity of those intellectuals.
Here lies the evil, would hasten
to say those who have not forgotten
the pre-war old tracks and seriously
begin to fear their re-appearance.
Such enthusiasm for Peace and
Humanity will surely lead us to war
and social struggle. Do you not
see that Mr. Albert Thomas, little
by little, forgets in Geneva that he
ever was in France one of the chiefs
of the National Defence? Do you
not hear him in the League of In-
struction or in the League of the
Republic, associate himself with the
sectarian campaigns of division?

Patriot

It is a fact that the Director of
the International Labour Office has
furnished to his political opponents,
sometimes through imprudence,
often also through fault or
negligence of those about him, many
opportunities to throw suspicion on
his patriotism. He himself must
sometimes feel with a little anguish
singular cases of conscience. The
French people who have approached
him and seen him at work in his
international functions could hardly
believe, however, that he did not
remain the patriot that they had
known during the war. Even if one
did not take into account the tone
of his voice when he speaks
of his country, how could such
a clear mind forget what he
owes to the French intellectu-
al disciplines? And what a com-
forting impression for his country-
men to see, among the confusion
and mediocrity of certain interna-
tional palavers, a Frenchman clear
up the chaotic ideas, classifying,
grouping and appreciating the argu-
ments. As his demonstration goes
on, the light is made in the dark
bushes and straight and calm
avenues open on every side as in a
French park. At certain cross-
roads we have to abandon the
orator, but it is with regret. . . .
Why does not Mr. Albert Thomas
administrate men as he regulates
ideas?

Though a layman, Mr. Albert
Thomas is liberal and very respect-
ful of religion. Is it sheer policy
in order to reserve to his work of
today and to his future plans the
sympathy of the Catholics? An in-
fluent member of the French As-
sociation for the Legal Protection
of the Workers, Mr. Albert Thomas
is too well acquainted with the
feelings and the work of the Social
Christians, and is too much enlight-

ened as to the spirit of youth, not
to feel towards the Catholics, but an
interested politeness. I know that,
at times, in the heat of his speeches,
the apostle of international labour
legislation may have dropped menac-
ing words. He once said: "One
can expect big things only from
those who are ready to burn the old
temples in order to edify new ones."
An observer, less inclined to en-
thusiasm than to criticism, is some-
times shocked by the dogmatic tone
with which this unbeliever affirms
that one must believe in the benefits
of international labour legislation.
In the severe Geneva Conference,
smiles are not in fashion. It is per-
haps because at bottom, irony is
aristocratic.

Man of Action

We must respect the faith of Mr.
Albert Thomas, but this does not
prevent us, however, if we thinks
it useful to try to limit its overflow.
It is besides difficult to imagine
that such an ardent temperament
could cover the soul of a sceptic.
Mr. Albert Thomas is not a
businessman but a man of action.
It remains to be seen to what extent
the man has been modelled by the
actor. Often, in listening to the
orator, we hesitate in attributing
the part of play and that of sinceri-
ty. In a thousand tokens we re-
cognise the influence of the parlia-
mentary platform: in the progres-
sion of the voice and the abrupt

silences precursory of a storm, in
the gesture of the hands which
gallop from beard to hair and which
hammer the folders, even in the
movements of emotion, we have an
impression of "true", and we regret
it just as we regret the abuse of
vibrato on a good cello. Luckily,
under the artist, we soon find the
man again.

The International Labour Office
offers for the present to this man
of action the wish of his nature in
the occasion to devote himself by
means of eloquence and diplomacy,
to the service of a nobly ideological
cause. But every great work has its
time. . . . What will become of
Mr. Albert Thomas the day he
leaves Geneva? His absence from
Parliament has no doubt, in the
last years, spared him many dif-
ficulties, we might even say, many
blunders. On this chapter, besides,
he could not compete with Mr.
Herriot and still less (in spite of
his friendship with Mr. George
Scelle) with Mr. Francois Albert.
But still the fact remains that during
his absence the posts have been
occupied. We do not imagine Mr.
Albert Thomas returning to sit in
the socialist seats under the ferula
of Mr. Leon Blum. But is he
not born under a good star? A lucky
turn of events will perhaps facilitate
his re-entrance into the French
political life. Who knows but that
he is not the man of a new Sacred
Union which is expected by the
warriors, disgusted with the sordid
pastimes of the pre-war sectarians?
Mr. Albert Thomas has enough
political pliancy to know how to
profit by timely circumstances. We
also believe that he is too faithful
to his convictions that we need fear
him to be accessible to equivocal
party combinations.
page_data.zh:
在那里，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生（Mr. Albert Thomas）将能够自由地完善他的政治教育。各国的部长、官员、雇主和工人都会来到他面前，他将很容易观察到他们因他所施加的对待而产生的民族或社会情感反应。

并非闲职

然而，不要以为阿尔伯特·托马斯先生在日内瓦的主任职位上看到的只是一把供人打瞌睡的椅子，或者——借用费迪南德·布吕诺（Ferdinand Brunot）先生的话来说——是一个设备特别精良的政治心理学实验室。人们常提起，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生曾自称为“社会政治领域的流浪犹太人”。无论人们对他在世界各首都兜售的货物价值持何种看法，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生的磨难与访问对他本人而言至少具有极大的意义。在他面前，那些原本会对法国人或社会主义者紧闭的高级国际官方大门敞开了。而阿尔伯特·托马斯先生有许多朋友乐于帮助他保持这些门半开……如果这位前军备部长正如某些方面所相信的那样，怀有朝一日入驻凯道赛（Quai d'Orsay，即法国外交部）的秘密野心，那么他这一周足迹踏遍巴尔干半岛，下个月又前往伦敦、柏林或罗马（奎里纳莱宫和梵蒂冈），并且不久前刚从魁北克到华盛顿，或许不久后将前往拉丁美洲的奔波，无疑为他提供了非凡的准备和最佳的提前个人宣传……毫无疑问，这样多样的接触也抹去了他身上的某些偏见（取其褒义），并且在与各种风格的政治架构磨合中，他自己的学说也磨平了棱角。

仍是社会主义者

然而，不要抱有任何幻想！无论今天给这些政治思想披上什么华丽的外衣，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生的政治思想仍然浸透着社会主义色彩。难道他自己不是深受饶勒斯（Jaures）形象的影响，并对这位逝者保持着近乎子女般的爱戴吗？此外，他能否像巴雷斯（Barres）那样，即使愿意，也甘心切断贯穿其一生的连续脉络？青年时期热情奉献给一项事业的回忆，那位演说家珍视的议会生涯中始终存在的迹象，有时令人烦恼但也富含共同奋斗成果的同志情谊，对于视你们为传统的灵魂来说，你们的力量是多么强大！

撇开所有琐碎的文字争执，我们可以毫不冒犯地说，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生首先是一位具有社会精神和民主精神的人。国际劳工局局长没有丝毫官僚气；他确实是一位使徒。五年来，他以对手也不得不钦佩的坚韧和灵活，试图用尚且脆弱的国际劳工公约杠杆，撬动惯例或自私的重石，并清除战后经济困难为社会立法先驱们设置的（格外坚固的）障碍。

这位粗犷的工匠坚持工作，并非出于纯粹的职业虚荣心，尽管迄今为止取得的成果平平。无疑，他真诚地相信他的工具和方法的价值；但他更坚信，通过国际劳工大会，以及通过他的程序和大量的通信，他增进了工人和弱势群体的利益。

阿尔伯特·托马斯先生是一位民主主义者，深沉而自豪。他从未想过隐藏自己的平民渊源。无疑，他欣赏当前处境的 advantages；很少有资本家像他那样熟悉如此多样的欧洲人物。但是，无论是与君主的交往还是官方的接待，都没能让他头脑发热。脱下礼服和高顶礼帽后，他又变回了那位“普瓦图”（Poitevin）面包师之子，举止简朴，平易近人。这一点毋庸置疑。透过阿尔伯特·托马斯先生演讲中的议会辞令，传递着一股强烈的民主气息，这种气息曾激励着饶勒斯，也许在内心深处，这只是那些知识分子式的人道慈善的一种形式。那些没有忘记战前旧轨并认真开始担心其重现的人会急忙说，祸根就在这里。这种对和平与人道的热情必将把我们引向战争和社会斗争。难道你没看到阿尔伯特·托马斯先生在日内瓦渐渐忘记了他曾在法国担任国防领袖之一吗？难道你没听到他在教育联盟或共和联盟中，将自己与宗派性的分裂运动联系在一起吗？

爱国者

事实是，国际劳工局局长由于自己的轻率，也常常由于身边人的过错或疏忽，给他的政治反对派提供了许多质疑他爱国心的机会。他自己有时也必定带着些许焦虑感受到良心的特殊困境。然而，接触过他并目睹他在国际职能中工作的法国人，几乎无法相信他没有保持他们在战争期间所认识的那位爱国者形象。即使不考虑他谈论祖国时的语气，这样一个清醒的头脑怎能忘记他欠法国智力训练的情分？看到一位法国人在某些国际空谈的混乱和平庸中理清混沌的思想，分类、归纳和评估论点，这对他的同胞来说是一种多么令人欣慰的印象。随着他的论证展开，黑暗灌木丛中被照亮，笔直平静的林荫道向四面八方展开，宛如在法国公园中。在某些十字路口，我们不得不离开这位演说家，但这令人遗憾……为什么阿尔伯特·托马斯先生不能像梳理思想那样管理人员呢？

虽然是一名俗人，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生却是自由主义者，并且非常尊重宗教。这仅仅是为了为其今日的工作和未来计划保留天主教徒的同情的策略吗？作为法国工人法律保护协会的有力成员，阿尔伯特·托马斯先生对社会基督徒的感受和工作太熟悉了，对青年精神也太了解了，以至于他对天主教徒不仅仅抱有出于利益的礼貌。我知道，有时在演讲的热潮中，这位国际劳工立法的使徒可能会吐出威胁性的话语。他曾说：“只有那些准备烧毁旧庙宇以建立新庙宇的人，才能期待伟大的成就。”一位较少倾向于热情而较多倾向于批评的观察者，有时会被这位无神论者以教条式的口吻肯定必须相信国际劳工立法的益处所震惊。在严肃的日内瓦会议上，微笑并不流行。也许这是因为讽刺本质上是贵族式的。

行动之人

我们必须尊重阿尔伯特·托马斯先生的信念，但如果我们认为有必要，这并不妨碍我们试图限制其溢出。此外，很难想象如此炽热的性格会掩盖一个怀疑论者的灵魂。阿尔伯特·托马斯先生不是商人，而是行动之人。仍有待观察的是，这个人被演员角色塑造到了什么程度。通常，在聆听这位演说家时，我们在归因表演成分和真诚成分之间犹豫不决。在成千上万的迹象中，我们认出了议会讲台的影响：在声音的推进和预示风暴的突然沉默中，在从胡须掠过头发并敲击文件夹的手势中，甚至在情感的举动中，我们都有一种“真实”的印象，就像我们惋惜一把好大提琴上揉弦过度一样。幸运的是，在艺术家之下，我们很快又找到了那个人。

目前，国际劳工局为这位行动之人提供了顺应其天性的愿望，即通过雄辩和外交手段，投身于一项崇高意识形态事业的服务。但每项伟大的工作都有其时机……阿尔伯特·托马斯先生离开日内瓦的那一天会怎样？毫无疑问，在过去几年里，他缺席议会使他避免了许多困难，甚至可以说，许多失误。在这一方面，此外，他无法与赫里欧（Herriot）先生竞争，更不用说（尽管他与乔治·斯塞尔（George Scelle）先生有友谊）与弗朗索瓦·阿尔伯特（Francois Albert）先生竞争了。但事实仍然是，在他缺席期间，职位已被占据。我们不认为阿尔伯特·托马斯先生会在莱昂·布鲁姆（Leon Blum）先生的戒尺下回到社会主义席位就座。但他不是生来就有吉星高照吗？局势的幸运转折或许会促进他重新进入法国政治生活。谁知道他会不会成为战士们所期待的新神圣联合（Sacred Union）的人选，这些战士已对战前宗派分子的卑劣消遣感到厌恶？阿尔伯特·托马斯先生有足够的政治灵活性，懂得如何利用适时的环境。我们也相信，他对信念如此忠诚，以至于我们无需担心他会受制于暧昧的党派组合。

THE OSAKA MAINICHI & THE TOKYO NICHI NICHI, OSAKA, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 4. 1928

Monsieur Albert Thomas

A Portrait by an Anonymous Writer Appearing in The
"Review des Jeunes", Paris

Translated From French Text

The article written with much style is an admirable portrait of Monsieur Albert Thomas, the celebrated Director of International Labour Organisation, who is to arrive in Kobe on December ' to stay in Japan for about a month. The anonymous author, as far as the editor is aware, is a youthful writer closely associated with Monsieur Thomas. The editor might also add that this is the only one of many portraits of Albert Thomas which he himself recognized as excellent.

Must we confess it? It is not without some apprehension that, on this white sheet, we write the name of a politician. How can we depict faithfully an actor embodying various characters? More especially, how can we make the spectators, who have before their eyes a certain image of the subject, admit that this image is but an appearance and that the true face of the man will be discovered only after scraping the paint and withdrawing the artificial light?

Among the stars on the political stage, Mr. Albert Thomas is perhaps more difficult to appreciate than anyone else. That is why the most divergent judgements are being expressed on him in equally categorical tones.

For some, he may be characterized in a few traits borrowed from the successive roles he played: it is the socialist professor, the fiery disciple of Jaures, soon his emulator, the mayor of Champigny and Deputy of the Tarn;—the Minister of Armaments, providence of "comrades" which he placed in offices and arsenals in the rear, dispenser of good orders and high salaries;—then the diplomat who fails to see behind Kerensky the silhouette of Lenin;—and lastly the Director of the International Labour Office, comfortably seated in his chair in Geneva, in charge of the amelioration of the labourers' fate.

Two Views

"Mistake or calumny!" reply others (who are not necessarily his political fellow-believers). This man remained on all the paths in which destiny led him an apostle, generous-hearted, ardently faithful to his ideals, a man of a luminous and acute intelligence, of valiant and tenacious will. Should you have any doubt on this, listen to the orator. His clear, warm and stirring speech is a warrant of his soul.

Need we choose between such contradictory portraits? Let us rather try to disentangle from among these contrasts the essential lines of the subject.

When the name of Mr. Albert Thomas is brought into a conversation, it is seldom that a question does not spring forth naturally and artlessly: "Is he still a socialist or not?"

Yes, certainly, if you deem that convictions can find their just and complete expression in the manifestations of Leagues and Parties, Albert Thomas has remained, on the shores of the Leman, the militant socialist that he was among the miners of Carmaux, in the meetings of his youth, of which he keeps a tender souvenir. On several occasions, as if to defend himself against perfidious or benevolent insinuations, the Director of the International Labour Office has made it a point to prove, in participating in socialist ceremonies or congresses, that he had not changed his flag. And his intellectual pride, his independence as polemist, rebel when a touchy Governing Body pretends to remind him that an official—even an international one—must observe some moderation in his public life.

Growing by Experience

It is none the less certain that from 1914 to today, the political thoughts of Mr. Albert Thomas have become richer from precious experiences. Called to Parliament from professorship, and confined to the side of opposition, he became, by the grace of Mars, a powerful Minister and a man-handler. The mankind which he then became acquainted with was no more the same as that he was accustomed to meet in the offices of "L'Humanite" (although this paper did not fail to maintain his collaboration): he was intimately mixed with the creative efforts of these manufacturers and chiefs of enterprises whom perhaps before he only saw imperfectly in their attempts at resistance against claims which were dear to him.
