《大阪每日新闻》与《东京日日新闻》，大阪，1928年12月4日，星期二

阿尔贝·托马斯先生

一幅由匿名作者撰写、刊登于巴黎《青年评论》上的肖像

译自法文原文

这篇文笔优美的文章是对国际劳工组织著名主任阿尔贝·托马斯先生的一幅令人钦佩的肖像描绘，他将于12月抵达神户，并在日本停留约一个月。据编辑所知，这位匿名作者是一位与托马斯先生关系密切的年轻作家。编辑还可以补充说，在众多关于阿尔贝·托马斯的肖像描写中，这是唯一被他本人认可为出色的一篇。

我们是否必须承认这一点？在这张白纸上写下一位政治家的名字，并非毫无顾虑。我们如何才能忠实地描绘一个 embodying 多种角色的演员？更特别是，我们如何让那些眼前已有某种既定形象的观众承认，这形象仅仅是一种表象，而只有刮去油彩、撤去人造灯光后，才能发现此人真实的面目？

在政治舞台的群星中，阿尔贝·托马斯先生或许比任何人都更难被赏识。正因如此，人们对他的评价截然不同，但语气却同样斩钉截铁。

在一些人看来，可以用他从 successive 角色中借来的几个特征来刻画他：他是社会主义教授，是饶勒斯的火热弟子，不久便成为其效仿者，尚皮尼市长和塔恩省议员；——他是军需部长，是“同志们”的救星，他将他们安置在后方的办公室和兵工厂里，分发优厚的命令和高薪；——然后是一位外交家，未能透过克伦斯基看到列宁的轮廓；——最后，他是国际劳工局局长，舒适地坐在日内瓦的椅子上，负责改善劳动者的命运。

两种观点

“错误还是诽谤！”其他人（他们不一定是他的政治同道）回答道。这个人在命运引领他的所有道路上始终是一位使徒，心胸宽广，热烈忠于自己的理想，拥有明亮而敏锐的智慧，以及勇敢而顽强的意志。如果你对此有任何怀疑，请听听这位演说家的言论。他那清晰、温暖且激动人心的演讲是他灵魂的保证。

我们需要在这些相互矛盾的肖像之间做出选择吗？让我们试着从这些对比中梳理出此人的主要脉络。

当阿尔贝·托马斯先生的名字出现在谈话中时，很少不会自然而然且天真地冒出一个问题：“他还是社会主义者吗？”

是的，当然，如果你认为信念可以在联盟和政党的表现中找到公正而完整的表达，那么阿尔贝·托马斯在莱芒湖畔，仍然像他在卡尔莫矿工中、在他青年时代的集会上那样，是一名战斗的社会主义者，他对那些集会保持着温柔的回忆。有几次，仿佛是为了防御恶意或善意的暗示，国际劳工局局长特意通过参加社会主义仪式或代表大会来证明，他并没有改变旗帜。而他的智力骄傲、作为论战者的独立性，在一个敏感的理事会试图提醒他，一位官员——即使是国际官员——必须在公共生活中保持某种克制时，便会奋起反抗。

因经验而成长

尽管如此，可以肯定的是，从1914年至今，阿尔贝·托马斯先生的政治思想因宝贵的经验而变得更加丰富。他从教授职位被召入议会，并局限于反对派席位，却因战争之神（Mars）的眷顾，成为一位权势显赫的部长和善于驾驭人物的人。那时他所结识的人类，已不再是他习惯于在《人道报》办公室遇到的人（尽管该报并未停止与他的合作）：他与那些制造商和企业领袖的创造性努力紧密交织在一起，而此前他可能只是在不完美地观察他们抵抗那些对他来说珍贵的诉求时的尝试。仿佛战争并不满足于给予这位年轻宠儿如此丰厚的赏赐，还想通过确凿的继承，使他在随后的疯狂岁月中免于挥霍这一获得的诱惑，《和平条约》的整整一章竖起了 ob-

page_data.en:
servatory where Mr. Albert
Thomas would be able, in all
liberty, to perfect his political edu-
cation.. Ministers, officials, em-
ployers and workers of all countries
would come to him there, and it was
going to be easy for him to observe
the reactions of their national or
social sensibilities upon the treat-
ment that he was going to inflict on
them.

No Idle Post

Do not imagine, however, that Mr.
Albert Thomas has seen in his di-
rectorial post of Geneva but a chair
to go to sleep on, or—to speak like
Mr. Ferdinand Brunot—a particu-
larly well-equipped laboratory of
political psychology. It has often
been recalled that Mr. Albert
Thomas had qualified himself as the
"Wandering Jew of Social Politics."
Whatever opinion one may have
on the value of the goods that he
offers in the capitals of the whole
world, the tribulations and the visits
of Mr. Albert Thomas are, for him
at least, of the greatest interest.
Before him the high international
official doors open which would have
remained closed to the Frenchman
or to the Socialist. And Mr. Al-
bert Thomas has so many friends
who are happy to help him in keep-
ing these doors ajar.... If the
former Minister of Armaments en-
tertains, as is believed in some quar-
ters, the secret ambition to be one
day installed in the Quai d'Orsay,
the peregrinations which one week
lead his steps to the Balkans and
the next month to London, Berlin
or Rome (Quirinal and Vatican),
and which will perhaps soon take
him to Latin America after having
led him but lately from Quebec to
Washington, are certainly for him
an exceptional preparation and the
best personal propaganda in ad-
vance.... No doubt also that such
diverse contacts will have effaced
in him certain prejudices (in the
better sense of the word), and that
in rubbing himself to the political
constructions of the most various
styles, his own doctrine will have
smoothened its angles.

Still a Socialist

No illusions! however. Whatever
the name given today to ornate
them, the political ideas of Mr. Al-
bert Thomas remain imbued with so-
cialism. Is he not himself impreg-
nated with the image of Jaures to
whose memory he keeps an almost
filial affection? Further, could he,
like a Barres, resign himself, even
if he wanted to, to break the con-
tinuous trait which runs through
his life? Remembrances of a youth
devoted with enthusiasm to a Cause,
signs ever present of a parliamen-
tary past which has remained dear
to the tribune, comradeships some-
times troublesome, but also rich in
common efforts, how powerful you
are on the souls for which you re-
present Tradition!

Setting aside all petty contention
of words, one can say of Mr. Albert
Thomas, without risking to be con-
tradicted, that he is above all a so-
cial spirit and a democrat. The
Director of the International La-
bour Office has nothing of the offi-
cial; he is really an apostle. With
a tenacity and a suppleness which
his opponents are bound to admire,
he endeavours since five years to
lift, with the yet fragile lever of
international labour conventions, the
heavy stones of routine or egoism,
and to remove the obstacles (sin-
gularly more solid) which are rais-
ed before the pioneers of social leg-
islation by the after-war economic
difficulties

It is not through sheer profes-
sional vanity that this rough artisan
persists in his work in spite of the
mediocrity of the results so far
obtained. No doubt he believes
sincerely in the value of his tools
and his methods; but he is above
all persuaded that through the In-
ternational Labour Conference, as
well as by his proceedings and
voluminous correspondence, he
beneficiates the interests of the
workers and of the weak.

Democrat, Mr. Albert Thomas is
so, deeply, proudly. He has never
thought of hiding his popular con-
nections. No doubt he appreciates
the advantages of his present
situation; few capitalists are
acquainted as he is with the most
diverse European personalities.
But neither his association with
sovereigns nor his official receptions
have succeeded in turning his head.
After divesting himself of his
frockcoat and top-hat, he becomes
again the simple-mannered, and
easy-of-approach son of the
"Poitevin" baker. No mistake
about it. Through the parliamentary
phraseology of Mr. Albert Thomas'
speeches there passes a great breath
of this democratic spirit which
animated Jaures and which, perhaps,
deep at heart, is but a form of
human charity of those intellectuals.
Here lies the evil, would hasten
to say those who have not forgotten
the pre-war old tricks and seriously
begin to fear their re-appearance.
Such enthusiasm for Peace and
Humanity will surely lead us to war
and social struggle. Do you not
see that Mr. Albert Thomas, little
by little, forgets in Geneva that he
ever was in France one of the chiefs
of the National Defence? Do you
not hear him in the League of In-
struction or in the League of the
Republic, associate himself with the
sectarian campaigns of division?

Patriot

It is a fact that the Director of
the International Labour Office has
furnished to his political opponents,
sometimes through imprudence,
often also through fault or
negligence of those about him, many
opportunities to throw suspicion on
his patriotism. He himself must
sometimes feel with a little anguish
singular cases of conscience. The
French people who have approached
him and seen him at work in his
international functions could hardly
believe, however, that he did not
remain the patriot that they had
known during the war. Even if one
did not take into account the tone
of his voice when he speaks
of his country, how could such
a clear mind forget what he
owes to the French intellectu-
al disciplines? And what a com-
forting impression for his country-
men to see, among the confusion
and mediocrity of certain interna-
tional palavers, a Frenchman clear
up the chaotic ideas, classifying,
grouping and appreciating the argu-
ments. As his demonstration goes
on, the light is made in the dark
bushes and straight and calm
avenues open on every side as in a
French park. At certain cross-
roads, we have to abandon the
orator, but it is with regret....
Why does not Mr. Albert Thomas
administrate men as he regulates
ideas?

Though a layman, Mr. Albert
Thomas is liberal and very respect-
ful of religion. Is it sheer policy
in order to reserve to his work of
today and to his future plans the
sympathy of the Catholics? An in-
fluent member of the French As-
sociation for the Legal Protection
of the Workers, Mr. Albert Thomas
is too well acquainted with the
feelings and the work of the Social
Christians, and is too much enlight-
ened as to the spirit of youth, not
to feel towards the Catholics, but an
interested politeness. I know that,
at times, in the heat of his speeches,
the apostle of international labour
legislation may have dropped menac-
ing words. He once said: "One
can expect big things only from
those who are ready to burn the old
temples in order to edify new ones."
An observer, less inclined to en-
thusiasm than to criticism, is some-
times shocked by the dogmatic tone
with which this unbeliever affirms
that one must believe in the benefits
of international labour legislation.
In the severe Geneva Conference,
smiles are not in fashion. It is per-
haps because at bottom, irony is
aristocratic.

Man of Action

We must respect the faith of Mr.
Albert Thomas, but this does not
prevent us, however, if we thinks
it useful to try to limit its overflow.
It is besides difficult to imagine
that such an ardent temperament
could cover the soul of a sceptic.
Mr. Albert Thomas is not a
businessman but a man of action.
It remains to be seen to what extent
the man has been modelled by the
actor. Often, in listening to the
orator, we hesitate in attributing
the part of play and that of sinceri-
ty. In a thousand tokens we re-
cognise the influence of the parlia-
mentary platform: in the progres-
sion of the voice and the abrupt
silences precursory of a storm, in
the gesture of the hands which
gallop from beard to hair and which
hammer the folders, even in the
movements of emotion, we have an
impression of "truc", and we regret
it just as we regret the abuse of
vibrato on a good cello. Luckily,
under the artist, we soon find the
man again.

The International Labour Office
offers for the present to this man
of action the wish of his nature in
the occasion to devote himself by
means of eloquence and diplomacy,
to the service of a nobly ideological
cause. But every great work has its
time.... What will become of
Mr. Albert Thomas the day he
leaves Geneva? His absence from
Parliament has no doubt, in the
last years, spared him many dif-
ficulties, we might even say, many
blunders. On this chapter, besides,
he could not compete with Mr.
Herriot and still less (in spite of
his friendship with Mr. George
Scelle) with Mr. Francois Albert.
But still the fact remains that during
his absence the posts have been
occupied. We do not imagine Mr.
Albert Thomas returning to sit in
the socialist seats under the ferula
of Mr. Leon Blum.... But is he
not born under a good star? A lucky
turn of events will perhaps facilitate
his re-entrance into the French
political life. Who knows but that
he is not the man of a new Sacred
Union which is expected by the
warriors, disgusted with the sordid
pastimes of the pre-war sectarians?
... Mr. Albert Thomas has enough
political pliancy to know how to
profit by timely circumstances. We
also believe that he is too faithful
to his convictions that we need fear
him to be accessible to equivocal
party combinations.

在那里，阿尔贝·托马斯先生（Mr. Albert Thomas）将能够自由地完善他的政治教育……各国的大臣、官员、雇主和工人都会来到他身边，他将很容易观察到他们因他所施加的对待而产生的民族或社会情感反应。

并非闲职

然而，不要以为阿尔贝·托马斯先生仅仅把他在日内瓦的主任职位看作是一把可以睡觉的椅子，或者——借用费迪南德·布吕诺（Ferdinand Brunot）先生的话来说——是一个设备特别精良的政治心理学实验室。人们常常提起，阿尔贝·托马斯先生曾自称为“社会政治中的流浪犹太人”。无论人们对他在世界各首都推销的货物价值持何种看法，阿尔贝·托马斯先生的磨难与访问，对他本人而言至少具有极大的意义。在他面前，那些原本对法国人或社会主义者紧闭的高级国际官方大门敞开了。而阿尔贝·托马斯先生有许多朋友乐于帮助他让这些门保持微开……如果这位前军备部长正如某些圈子所相信的那样，怀有朝一日入驻凯道西（Quai d'Orsay，即法国外交部）的秘密野心，那么他这一周足迹踏遍巴尔干，下个月又前往伦敦、柏林或罗马（奎里纳尔宫和梵蒂冈），并且不久前刚从魁北克到华盛顿，或许不久后将前往拉丁美洲的奔波，无疑为他提供了非凡的准备和最好的个人前期宣传……毫无疑问，这样多样的接触也抹去了他身上的某些偏见（取其褒义），并且在与各种风格的政治架构磨合中，他自己的学说也磨平了棱角。

仍是社会主义者

然而，不要抱有任何幻想！无论今天人们用什么华丽的名称来装饰，阿尔贝·托马斯先生的政治思想仍然浸透着社会主义色彩。难道他自己不是深受饶勒斯（Jaures）形象的影响，并对他的记忆保持着近乎子女般的 affection 吗？此外，他能否像巴雷斯（Barres）那样，即使愿意，也甘心切断贯穿其一生的连续脉络？青年时代热情奉献给一项事业的回忆，议会生涯中那些令这位演说家始终珍视的痕迹，有时令人烦恼但也充满共同奋斗成果的同志情谊，对于视你们为传统的灵魂来说，你们的力量是多么强大！

撇开所有琐碎的文字争执，我们可以毫不冒犯地说，阿尔贝·托马斯先生首先是一个具有社会精神和民主精神的人。国际劳工局局长没有丝毫官僚气；他确实是一位使徒。五年来，他以对手也不得不钦佩的坚韧和灵活，试图用尚且脆弱的国际劳工公约杠杆，撬动惯例或自私的重石，并清除战后经济困难为社会立法先驱们设置的（格外坚固的）障碍。

这位粗犷的工匠坚持工作，并非出于纯粹的职业虚荣心，尽管迄今为止取得的成果平平。毫无疑问，他真诚地相信他的工具和方法的价值；但他更坚信，通过国际劳工大会，以及通过他的程序和大量的通信，他增进了工人和弱者的利益。

作为一名民主主义者，阿尔贝·托马斯先生是深刻而自豪的。他从未想过隐藏自己的平民渊源。毫无疑问，他欣赏当前处境的有利条件；很少有资本家像他那样熟悉如此多样的欧洲人物。但是，无论是与君主的交往还是官方的接待，都没能让他头脑发热。脱下礼服和高顶礼帽后，他又变回了那位“普瓦图”（Poitevin）面包师之子，举止简朴，平易近人。这一点毋庸置疑。透过阿尔贝·托马斯先生演讲中的议会辞藻，传递着一股强烈的民主气息，这种气息曾激励着饶勒斯，或许在内心深处，这只是那些知识分子的一种人道主义慈善形式。那些没有忘记战前旧伎俩并开始认真担心其重现的人会急忙说：祸根就在这里。这种对和平与人道的热情必将把我们引向战争和社会斗争。难道你们没看到阿尔贝·托马斯先生在日内瓦逐渐忘记了他曾在法国担任国防领袖之一吗？难道你们没听到他在教育联盟或共和联盟中，将自己与宗派性的分裂运动联系在一起吗？

爱国者

事实是，国际劳工局局长由于自身的轻率，也常因周围人的过失或疏忽，为其政治反对派提供了许多质疑其爱国心的机会。他自己有时也不免带着些许焦虑感受到良心的特殊困境。然而，接触过他并目睹他在国际职能中工作的法国人，几乎无法相信他不再是他们在战争期间所认识的那位爱国者。即使不考虑他谈论祖国时的语调，这样一个清醒的头脑怎能忘记他欠法国智力训练的情分？看到一位法国人在某些国际空谈的混乱和平庸中理清混沌的思想，对论点进行分类、归纳和评估，这对他的同胞来说是一种多么令人欣慰的印象。随着他的论证展开，黑暗丛林中透出光明，笔直平静的林荫道向四面八方敞开，宛如法式公园。在某些十字路口，我们不得不离开这位演说家，但这令人遗憾……为什么阿尔贝·托马斯先生不能像梳理思想那样管理人事呢？

虽然是一名世俗人士，阿尔贝·托马斯先生持自由主义态度，并对宗教非常尊重。这仅仅是为了为其目前的工作和未来计划保留天主教徒同情的策略吗？作为法国工人法律保护协会（French Association for the Legal Protection of the Workers）中有影响力的成员，阿尔贝·托马斯先生对社会基督徒的感受和工作太熟悉了，对青年精神也太了解了，以至于他对天主教徒不仅仅表现出出于利益的礼貌。我知道，有时在演讲的热潮中，这位国际劳工立法的使徒可能会说出威胁性的话语。他曾说：“只有那些准备烧毁旧庙宇以建立新庙宇的人，才能期待伟大的成就。”一位较少热情而较多批评的观察者，有时会对这位无信仰者以教条式的口吻断言必须相信国际劳工立法的益处感到震惊。在严肃的日内瓦会议上，微笑并不流行。也许这是因为在骨子里，讽刺是贵族式的。

行动之人

我们必须尊重阿尔贝·托马斯先生的信念，但如果我们认为有必要，这并不妨碍我们试图限制其溢出。此外，很难想象如此热烈的性情会掩盖一个怀疑论者的灵魂。阿尔贝·托马斯先生不是商人，而是行动之人。至于这个人被演员角色塑造到了什么程度，还有待观察。通常，在聆听这位演说家时，我们在区分表演成分和真诚成分之间犹豫不决。从无数迹象中，我们认出了议会讲台的影响：声音的起伏、风暴前的突然沉默、双手从胡须挥向头发并敲击文件夹的手势，甚至在情感的流露中，我们都有一种“技巧”的印象，对此我们感到遗憾，就像惋惜在大提琴上滥用颤音一样。幸运的是，在艺术家之下，我们很快又找到了那个人。

目前，国际劳工局为这位行动之人提供了顺应其天性的愿望，即通过口才和外交手段，投身于一项具有崇高意识形态的事业。但每项伟大的工作都有其时机……阿尔贝·托马斯先生离开日内瓦的那一天会怎样？毫无疑问，在过去几年里，他缺席议会使他避免了许多困难，甚至可以说是许多失误。在这一方面，他无法与赫里欧先生（Mr. Herriot）竞争，更不用说（尽管他与乔治·斯塞尔先生 Mr. George Scelle 有友谊）与弗朗索瓦·阿尔贝先生（Mr. Francois Albert）相比了。但事实仍然是，在他缺席期间，职位已被占据。我们无法想象阿尔贝·托马斯先生在莱昂·布鲁姆先生（Mr. Leon Blum）的管束下回到社会主义席位就座……但他不是生来就有好运吗？局势的幸运转折或许会促进他重新进入法国政治生活。谁知道他会不会成为战士们所期待的新“神圣联合”（Sacred Union）的人物，这些战士已对战前宗派分子的卑劣消遣感到厌恶？……阿尔贝·托马斯先生拥有足够的政治灵活性，懂得如何利用适时的环境。我们也相信，他对自己的信念如此忠诚，以至于我们不必担心他会卷入模棱两可的党派勾结。

THE OSAKA MAINICHI & THE TOKYO NICHI NICHI, OSAKA, SUNDAY, DECEMBER 2, 1928

Mr. Thomas Is Disillusioned With
Actual Labour Conditions in China

Visitor Explains Object of
Investigation in
Far East

Special to The Osaka Mainichi
SHANGHAI, Dec. 1.—Mr. Albert
Thomas, Chief of the International
Labour Office of Geneva, arrived
here this morning from Nanking.
The train was delayed by one hour
and 50 minutes and his program in
Shanghai was somewhat upset, but
as soon as he settled himself in his
hotel he said to a correspondent of
this paper as follows:
“I came to the Far East not to
make any concrete investigation of
conditions. As a matter of fact,
it will be impossible for anyone to
make a complete investigation by
staying only three weeks in Japan
or two weeks in China. My object
in visiting here is to see that closer
relations of the International La-
bour Office with Japan and China are
established, in order to protect the
service of that office, so that a way
of securing reports of scientific in-
vestigations concerning the labour
problem from the Far East might
be arranged. I hope that the in-
ternational labour conventions and
recommendations will be more cri-
tically studied in order to promote
the welfare of mankind.
“Only two weeks have I been in
China, and it is risky for me to
state my impressions, but I shall
say a few words about my impres-
sions.”

Chinese Standard Low
“The standard of living of the
Chinese labourers is lower than I
had imagined. The labour condi-
tions in the big industries managed
in the new style with big capital
furnished by China herself, Japan,
and other countries are not bad, to
be sure. But the safety devices for
preventing accidents are not suffi-
ciently installed. The labour condi-
tions in small plants managed in the
old style are very bad. I noticed
a large number of minors being in-
dustrially employed. This is con-
trary to the principle of the inter-
national labour machinery. I hope
that China will abolish the system
of the employment of minors.
“Japan sends properly chosen
delegates to the International La-
bour Conferences every time, but
China has not done so yet. I hope
that China will send properly chosen
delegates hereafter, two for the
Government, one each for the em-
ployers and the labourers.

I have exchanged views with the
National Government officials on
this matter in Nanking. I under-
stand that the National Govern-
ment, which has established the
Legislative Board as one of the five
boards of the Government, has
drafted social welfare laws, some of
which are excellent ones. When the
draft is completed, I shall be per-
mitted to look it over, in order that
I may study it in comparison with
the conventions and recommenda-
tions adopted in Washington in
1919.

Not Afraid of Left Wing
“I was not informed as yet about
the agitation against me conducted
by the Leftists in Japan in order to
try to prevent my visit to Japan.
But I expect as much, because the
harder the International Labour
Office works the more excited the
members of the Third International
will become. I expect to reach
Japan within a few days, but I do
not pay much attention to this agi-
tation against me. There are many
persons in Japan who understand
the work we are doing.”
Mr. Thomas and his party will
stay in Shanghai for a day or two
and sail for Japan aboard the
N.Y.K. liner Shanghai Maru on De-
cember 3. He will stop overnight
in Kobe before proceeding to stay
there about two weeks.
Mr. Thomas received a very warm
welcome wherever he went in China.
The newspapers have devoted much
space to report his movements.

a. e. (Pol)
A.R. 12/26

《大阪每日新闻》与《东京日日新闻》，大阪，1928年12月2日，星期日

托马斯先生对中国实际劳工状况感到失望

访客阐述其在远东调查之目的

《大阪每日新闻》专电
上海，12月1日电。——日内瓦国际劳工局局长阿尔伯特·托马斯（Albert Thomas）先生今晨从南京抵达此处。火车晚点一小时五十分钟，他在上海的行程因此受到一定影响，但他一在旅馆安顿下来，便向本报记者发表了如下谈话：
“我来到远东，并非为了对当地状况进行任何具体的调查。事实上，任何人仅在日本停留三周或在中国停留两周，都不可能完成全面的调查。我此次访问的目的是促成国际劳工局与日本和中国建立更紧密的关系，以完善该局的服务，从而安排一种途径，以便获取关于远东劳工问题的科学调查报告。我希望国际社会能更严谨地研究国际劳工公约和建议书，以促进人类福祉。
“我在中国仅待了两周，此时谈论我的印象是有风险的，但我仍愿就我的印象略谈几句。”

中国标准低下
“中国工人的生活水平比我想象的要低。诚然，在由中国自身、日本及其他国家提供大额资本、以新式管理经营的大型工业中，劳工状况并不糟糕。但是，预防事故的安全装置安装得并不充分。在以旧式管理经营的小型工厂中，劳工状况非常恶劣。我注意到有大量未成年人在工业中被雇佣。这违背了国际劳工机制的原则。我希望中国能废除雇佣未成年人的制度。
“日本每次都派遣经过适当遴选的代表参加国际劳工会议，但中国尚未这样做。我希望中国今后能派遣经过适当遴选的代表，其中两名代表政府，雇主和劳工各一名代表。

我在南京就此事与国民政府官员交换了意见。我了解到，已将立法院设立为政府五院之一的国民政府，已起草了社会福利法律，其中一些是非常优秀的。草案完成后，我将获准审阅，以便将其与1919年在华盛顿通过的公约和建议书进行比较研究。

不惧怕左翼
“我尚未获悉日本左翼人士为防止我访问日本而针对我进行的煽动活动。但我对此早有预料，因为国际劳工局工作越努力，第三国际的成员就越激动。我预计几天内抵达日本，但我并不太关注这些针对我的煽动活动。日本有许多人理解我们所做的工作。”
托马斯先生及其随行人员将在上海停留一两天，并于12月3日乘坐日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）的“上海丸”号邮轮启程前往日本。他将在神户过夜，随后在那里停留约两周。
托马斯先生在中国所到之处均受到热烈欢迎。报纸花费了大量篇幅报道他的行踪。

a. e. (Pol)
A.R. 12/26

中国标准低下
“中国工人的生活水平比我想象的要低。诚然，在由中国自身、日本及其他国家提供大额资本、以新式管理经营的大型工业中，劳工状况并不糟糕。但是，预防事故的安全装置安装得并不充分。在以旧式管理经营的小型工厂中，劳工状况非常恶劣。我注意到有大量未成年人在工业中被雇佣。这违背了国际劳工机制的原则。我希望中国能废除雇佣未成年人的制度。
“日本每次都派遣经过适当遴选的代表参加国际劳工会议，但中国尚未这样做。我希望中国今后能派遣经过适当遴选的代表，其中两名代表政府，雇主和劳工各一名代表。

“我在南京就此事与国民政府官员交换了意见。我了解到，已将立法院设立为政府五院之一的国民政府，已起草了社会福利法律，其中一些是非常优秀的。草案完成后，我将获准审阅，以便将其与1919年在华盛顿通过的公约和建议书进行比较研究。

不惧怕左翼
“我尚未获悉日本左翼人士为防止我访问日本而针对我进行的煽动活动。但我对此早有预料，因为国际劳工局工作越努力，第三国际的成员就越激动。我预计几天内抵达日本，但我并不太关注这些针对我的煽动活动。日本有许多人理解我们所做的工作。”
托马斯先生及其随行人员将在上海停留一两天，并于12月3日乘坐日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）的“上海丸”号邮轮启程前往日本。他将在神户过夜，随后在那里停留约两周。
托马斯先生在中国所到之处均受到热烈欢迎。报纸花费了大量篇幅报道他的行踪。

"Le Journal de Shanghai." December 4, 1928.

AN INTERVIEW WITH MR. ALBERT THOMAS.

Mr. Georges Mresthe contributes the following article to the "Journal de Shanghai" which publishes as a leading article:-
The foreign and Chinese Press has published many inaccurate reports of the object of the visit of Mr. Albert Thomas to China. In an interview I had with him at the Astor House, Mr. Thomas, who is President of the International Labour Bureau, corrects these wrong reports as follows:-
"In coming to China, I had several objects, the principal being to secure more complete representation of China on the League of Nations and on the Bureau of International Labour. The 54 nations who are represented on the Bureau have each four delegates: two representing their respective governments, one representing the employers and one representing the labourers. The Nationalist Government has promised me to take the necessary steps to place China on the same footing as the other nations.
"This Bureau has drafted Labour Regulations which are submitted for ratification to its various members. Up to the present there have been 25 conventions. Only Luxemburg has ratified them all, France has ratified 12, Great Britain 13, and China one: the one prohibiting the use of white phosphorus in the manufacture of matches.
"The difficulty with China is that this country has no special legislation, but the Nationalist Government is now working on this and has agreed to submit to the Bureau its draft of laws for our technical advice with regard to the arrangement of these laws in the same manner that Poland, and several South American States have done. Nanking appears to me to be willing to ratify several of the conventions..
"I have also dealt with the question of the application of China's social legislation in the foreign Settlements and I have had interviews with mill proprietors to request them whether they are willing to submit the solutions to the Bureau.
"Another of my subjects in coming out to China was to secure information. Article 396 of the Peace Treaty which created the Bureau of International Labour, suggests the gathering of information throughout the world for the establishing new conventions and new legislation.
"A stay of 15 days is rather of short duration, but I have ascertained when talking with the heads of Ministries at Nanking, that serious efforts have been made in China.
"This is why, if my Council consent, a Bureau of Social Information of the Bureau of International Labour , will be established in China. It will be administered on a scientific basis which will be in a position to furnish with accurate information on all questions which are of interest to us. Such a Bureau already exists in Japan and other countries.
"In conclusion, I want to say that I am extremely satisfied with my tour in China and with my interviews with members of the Chinese Government as well as with representatives of the labourers. I am particularly happy at the evidence of good will manifested by the Chinese Government and at its sincere desire to create social legislation in China. I want also to express my thanks for the warm welcome which I have received everywhere in China at the hands of the authorities, of the representatives of labourers and their employers and from the intellectual Chinese teachers and students."
Mr. Thomas left for Japan at 9 a.m. yesterday by the Shanghai Maru. He was accompanied by his secretary, Mr. Marius Viple.

《上海日报》（Le Journal de Shanghai），1928年12月4日。

采访阿尔伯特·托马斯先生。

乔治·梅雷斯特（Georges Mresthe）先生为《上海日报》撰写了以下文章，该报将其作为社论刊登：
外国媒体和中国媒体发布了大量关于阿尔伯特·托马斯先生访华目的的不实报道。我在礼查饭店（Astor House）与他进行了一次采访，身为国际劳工局局长的托马斯先生纠正了这些错误报道，内容如下：
“我来中国有几个目的，主要目的是争取中国在国际联盟和国际劳工局中获得更充分的代表权。在该局拥有代表权的54个国家各有四名代表：两名代表各自政府，一名代表雇主，一名代表劳工。国民政府已向我承诺，将采取必要步骤，使中国获得与其他国家同等的地位。
“该局已起草劳工条例，并提交其各成员国批准。截至目前，已有25项公约。只有卢森堡批准了全部公约，法国批准了12项，英国批准了13项，而中国仅批准了一项：即禁止在火柴制造中使用白磷的公约。
“中国的困难在于该国没有专门的立法，但国民政府目前正在致力于此，并同意将其法律草案提交给该局，以寻求我们在法律编排方面的技术建议，波兰和几个南美国家也曾这样做。在我看来，南京愿意批准几项公约。
“我还处理了中国社会立法在外国租界适用的问题，并与纱厂业主进行了会谈，询问他们是否愿意将解决方案提交给该局。
“我此次来华的另一个议题是获取信息。创建国际劳工局的和平条约第396条建议在全球范围内收集信息，以制定新的公约和新的立法。
“15天的停留时间相当短，但我通过与南京各部部长的交谈得知，中国已做出认真努力。
“因此，如果我的理事会同意，将在中国设立国际劳工局的社会情报局。该局将以科学基础进行管理，能够就我们感兴趣的所有问题提供准确信息。此类机构在日本和其他国家已经存在。
“最后，我想说，我对在中国的巡视以及与中国政府成员和劳工代表的会谈感到非常满意。我对中国政府表现出的善意以及其在中国建立社会立法的真诚愿望感到特别高兴。我还要感谢 authorities、劳工和雇主代表以及中国知识分子教师和学生在中国各地给予我的热烈欢迎。”
托马斯先生于昨日上午9时乘“上海丸”号启程前往日本。他的秘书马里乌斯·维普尔（Marius Viple）先生陪同前往。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 4, 1928

M. ALBERT THOMAS
AND CHINA
Arrangement for Co-operation
Between China and Interna-
tional Labour Office

Shanghai, Dec. 3.
M. Albert Thomas, Director of
the International Labour Office of
the League of Nations, sailed this
morning for Japan. Before his
departure, he requested the Kuo
Min News Agency to circulate the
following message:—
“I am leaving China to-day after
a fortnight’s stay, during which I
met the Kuomintang Party leaders,
members of the Government, and
leaders of workers and employers’
organizations.
“With the Minister of Foreign
Affairs and the Minister of Indus-
try, Commerce and Labour, I have
arranged for collaboration between
China and the International Labour
Office. I appreciate the warm wel-
come I have received on all sides
and leave with the conviction that
new China will collaborate active-
ly with the international institu-
tions at Geneva.
“I am highly satisfied with the
results of my journey and the con-
tacts I have made; particularly as
I find the existence of a stable and
united government in China, cap-
able of maintaining the unity of
the Chinese Republic and economic
reconstruction after years of civil
war.
Need of Active Government
“Europe should take account of
the change and of these efforts. A
united government and a united
China was the first condition of re-
newed authority in international
affairs, but that government must
be active. I am strongly of the
opinion that a country of 400 mil-
lion should not ignore the activities
and pre-occupations at Geneva—
where all countries meet on an
equal footing with equal rights.
“I have asked China to under-
take the social legislation, now
lacking, so that the International
Labour Office may secure its ap-
plication in the concessions and
leased territories. For this pur-
pose, the Labour Office will give the
collaboration promised at Washing-
ton and will work to secure equal-
ity of treatment for Chinese in all
countries.
“The principles of sovereignty
and welfare of peoples proclaimed
by the Apostle of New China, Sun
Yat-sen, echo the principles of
modern Western communities and
should be the basis of the entente
between all peoples.—(Sd.) Albert
Thomas.”

M. ALBERT Thomas,
the International La[bour]
accompanied by his st[aff] left for
Japan yesterday aftern[oon].

《字林西报》，1928年12月4日，星期二

阿尔贝·托马先生
与中国
中国与国际劳工局之间的合作安排

上海，12月3日。
国际联盟国际劳工局局长阿尔贝·托马（Albert Thomas）先生于今晨启程前往日本。临行前，他委托国民通讯社发布如下消息：—
“我在华逗留两周后，今日离开中国。在此期间，我会见了国民党领导人、政府成员以及工人和雇主组织的领袖。
“我已与外交部长及工商劳工部长就中国与国际劳工局之间的合作事宜作出安排。我对各方给予我的热情欢迎表示赞赏，并怀着新中国将积极与日内瓦的国际机构进行合作的信念离去。
“我对此次行程的成果及所建立的联系深感满意；特别是因为我发现中国存在一个稳定且统一的政府，有能力在多年内战之后维持中华民国的统一并进行经济重建。
需要积极的政府
“欧洲应当考虑到这一变化及这些努力。统一的政府和统一的中国是重振国际事务权威的首要条件，但该政府必须是积极有为的。我强烈认为，一个拥有四亿人口的国家不应忽视日内瓦的活动和关切——在那里，所有国家以平等的权利平等地相聚。
“我已请中国承担目前缺失的社会立法工作，以便国际劳工局能够确保其在租界和租借地内的实施。为此，劳工局将提供在华盛顿承诺的合作，并将致力于确保中国人在所有国家获得平等待遇。
“新中国的倡导者孙中山所宣示的主权与人民福祉原则，与现代西方社会的原则相呼应，应成为各国人民之间谅解的基础。——（签名）阿尔贝·托马。”

阿尔贝·托马先生，
国际劳[工局]
在其职[员]陪同下，于昨日下午启程前往日本。

赴日

呼吁中国派遣代表参加下一届世界
劳工大会；发现此地工作
状况极其糟糕

据南京官方消息，目前正在上海进行短期访问的国际联盟国际劳工局局长阿尔贝·托马（Albert Thomas）先生，已邀请国民政府派遣两名分别代表中国雇主和中国劳工的代表，出席明年在日内瓦举行的国际劳工大会会议。该提议将提交国务会议审议并采取行动。
托马先生在上海匆匆度过了两天，行程紧凑，使他得以接触中国的资本方和劳工界、地方当局以及社会和工业组织。预计他将于今日启程前往日本。
周六，他参观了几所劳工学校和浦东模范村，并受到地方当局的接见。他在泛太平洋协会发表了讲话，并出席了上海市市长举办的晚宴。
昨日，他的日程安排包括参观国货展览会、杨树浦社会中心、上海学院和国立劳动大学。他与当地工会代表进行了会谈，当天的其他活动还包括在上海基督教青年会发表公开演讲，以及与全国基督教协进会、基督教青年会、

National Committee, Y.W.C.A.,
National Committee. Last night
he attended a dinner party given
by the Department of Social
affairs.

Object Of Trip

"Speaking generally, the chief
object of my trip to China is to
improve the relationships between
China and the International
Labour Bureau," declared M.
Thomas in an interview.

As a result of the peace treaty
which China signed with Austria
after the war, she automatically
became a member of the Labour
Bureau but had not taken an
active part in the international
labour conferences held annually
at Geneva, nor had she ratified
the various labour conventions
which had been adopted.

To newspaper representatives
at Hankow, M. Thomas declared:
"It is my aim to try and per-
suade the Chinese Government to
bring their labour laws in har-
mony with the spirit of the
international labour convention. I
understand the Nanking National
Government has drafted a factory
law and I shall study its pro-
visions when I reach Nanking to
see whether it is in accord with
the spirit of the international
labour convention. I quite realise
the many obstacles which con-
front the present Government in
the enforcement of labour laws in
view of the existence of conces-
sions in China."

"Working Conditions Terrible"

Questioned while he was at
Hankow regarding labour condi-
tions in China, M. Thomas stat-
ed: "After my round of inspection
of the various mills I find con-
ditions very low, but the reason
for same may be accounted for by
the fact that China has just come
to the end of a civil war. The
conditions of the railways and
rolling stock are exactly the same
as in Europe at the end of the
world war. The only difference is
this, in Europe reconstruction
went on rapidly while in China
there is an unusual delay. I was
much impressed with the modern
plant used in the various indus-
tries but the working conditions
are terrible. I noticed a lot of
children employed at these mills,
and I must say, that I shall fight
in all countries where child labour
is used and night hours for
women. It tends to have a strong
effect on their moral and physical
development and will only form
a terrible future generation."

When asked as to what is then
the salvation of the Chinese work-
ing men he answered: "It is
hard for me to say now as I have
only been a few days in China,
nevertheless, I can tell you one
thing which applies equally here
as in other parts of the universe.
The working people must have an
organization. We must protect
ourselves from each other. So the
working man must organise and
by his strength obtain justice. I,
for one, am not a believer in equal
pay for all. There must be a
greater remuneration for those
who work harder."

Present Government Strong

"Regarding the present Govern-
ment I think it is a great improve-
ment. China wants a strong Gov-
ernment and I firmly believe this
Government is stronger than any
she has ever had. 'Rome was not
built in day' is an old axiom,
so naturally it will take time for
this Government to create and
improve conditions throughout this
vast country. I earnestly hope
my visit will not be fruitless and
that at forthcoming conference
next May in Geneva China will be
well to the fore."

全国委员会的代表举行讨论会。昨晚，他出席了社会局举办的晚宴。

出访目的

“总的来说，我此次访华的主要目的是改善中国与国际劳工局之间的关系，”托马先生在一次采访中表示。

由于中国在战后与奥地利签署了和平条约，她自动成为劳工局的成员，但并未积极参与每年在日内瓦举行的国际劳工会议，也未批准已通过的各项劳工公约。

托马先生在汉口对记者团表示：“我的目标是试图说服中国政府使其劳工法律与国际劳工公约的精神相一致。据悉，南京国民政府已起草了一部工厂法，我抵达南京后将研究其条款，看其是否符合国际劳工公约的精神。我充分认识到，鉴于中国存在租界，现政府在执行劳工法方面面临诸多障碍。”

“工作状况糟糕”

在汉口被问及中国的劳工状况时，托马先生表示：“在视察了各家工厂后，我发现状况非常低下，但这可以归因于中国刚刚结束内战这一事实。铁路和机车车辆的状况与一战结束时的欧洲完全相同。唯一的区别在于，欧洲的重建迅速进行，而中国则出现了异常的延误。各行业使用的现代化设备给我留下了深刻印象，但工作条件却极其糟糕。我注意到这些工厂雇佣了许多童工，我必须说，我将在所有使用童工和安排女性夜间工作的国家进行斗争。这会对他们的道德和身体发展产生强烈影响，只会造就可怕的未来一代。”

当被问及中国工人的出路何在时，他回答说：“我现在很难说，因为我在中国只待了几天，不过，我可以告诉你们一件同样适用于这里和宇宙其他地方的事情。劳动人民必须有一个组织。我们必须互相保护。因此，工人必须组织起来，并通过自己的力量获得正义。就我个人而言，我不相信所有人同工同酬。那些工作更努力的人必须获得更高的报酬。”

现政府强大

“关于现政府，我认为这是一个巨大的进步。中国需要一个强大的政府，我坚信这个政府比她以往任何政府都更强大。‘罗马非一日建成’是一条古老的格言，因此，这个政府自然需要时间来创造和改善这个广阔国家各地的状况。我真诚希望我的访问不会徒劳无功，并希望在下个月五月于日内瓦举行的即将召开的会议上，中国能名列前茅。”

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, DECEMBER 2, 1928.

M. ALBERT THOMAS
IN SHANGHAI

Addresses Gathering
At Astor House
Hotel Tiffin

M. Albert Thomas, Director of the International Labour Bureau of the League of Nations, at Geneva, yesterday arrived in Shanghai from Nanking. He was accompanied by his secretary, a Chinese interpreter, Dr. H. H. Kung, Nationalist Minister of Industry, Commerce and Labour, and Dr. C. T. Wang, Nationalist Minister of Foreign Affairs.

They were met at the Shanghai North Station by Mr. George Fitch, Hon. Secretary of the Pan-Pacific Association, a number of newspapermen, and nearly a dozen Chinese officials of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai. The party then proceeded to the Bureau of Foreign Affairs in motor cars, after which M. Thomas and his secretary went to their rooms at the Astor House Hotel.

This morning M. Thomas is to receive foreign and Chinese newspapermen at a press conference to be held at 11 o'clock at the Astor House Hotel. To-morrow he is scheduled to leave for Japan. M. Thomas is in the Far East to make a study of the labour situation.

Large Crowd Present

A large crowd was present yesterday noon at a tiffin in his honour at the Astor House, given by the Pan-Pacific Association. The labour champion gave an interesting talk of about 30 minutes duration, which, however, was not fully understood by many present as it was delivered in his native tongue—French.

Mr. Edward Philan, his secretary, translated a part of the address, it being stated that lack of time prevented a full translation. Mr. T. Tehou, Chief of the Bureau of Industry, Commerce and Labour of the Chinese Government presided.

"Why Come To China?"

On every hand, M. Thomas said in his address, people have been asking "Why did you come to China?" It was impossible, he stated, to come to any definite conclusions regarding the country since he has been here a short time and has had no real opportunity to make a careful study of the situation. The speaker pointed out that it would be unwise to draw conclusions without having real facts upon which to base them.

In Geneva, he declared, things were not done in that manner. Before conclusions were reached a detailed study of the problem in hand was made, so that any conclusions reached would be really available and serve a purpose.

Speaking of his visit to China M. Thomas asserted that he had come to lay the foundation for closer relationship between this country and the League of Nations Labour Bureau.

The speaker stated that in discussing the work of the Bureau it was necessary to refer to conditions when the Bureau first began to function in the interests of labour all over the world.

World Labour Crisis

The greatest labour crisis the world has ever seen, M. Thomas declared, came in the year 1919. Countries which had been defeated in the Great War had gone into a state of revolution. In the victorious countries labour had met with a new recognition, for the reason that the war had not been between the armies, but between the people.

In those days, it was stated, women worked in the factories and labour was organized to win the war. The result was that in the peace treaties provisions had been made for the betterment of the condition of the labouring people, since some sort of recognition of the efforts of the masses had been needed after the signing of the Armistice.

Solemn declarations had been made, the speaker stated, that the conditions of labour were serious and unjust. A move to bring about a change in these conditions was made with the founding of labour organizations in 36 countries.

To form this great organization, a social bureau government and labour representatives met at Geneva. So far ten conferences have been held—one every year and more progress has been made, it was stated, that people generally realize.

Conditions Improved

In comparison with labour conditions before the war, the conditions are much improved
page_data.zh:
《上海星期时报》，1928年12月2日。

阿尔贝·托马先生
在上海

在礼查饭店午餐会上
向集会发表演说

国际联盟日内瓦国际劳工局局长阿尔贝·托马（M. Albert Thomas）昨日从南京抵达上海。陪同前来的有他的秘书、一名中文译员、国民政府工商部部长孔祥熙博士以及国民政府外交部部长王正廷博士。

泛太平洋协会荣誉秘书乔治·菲奇（George Fitch）先生、数名报界人士以及近十二名大上海市政府中国官员在上海北站迎接了他们。随后，一行人乘车前往外交部，之后托马先生及其秘书前往礼查饭店入住。

今天上午，托马先生将在礼查饭店举行的记者招待会上接见中外报界人士，时间为11点。他计划于明日启程前往日本。托马先生此次来到远东，旨在考察劳工状况。

出席者众多

昨日中午，在泛太平洋协会为他在礼查饭店举办的午餐会上，出席者云集。这位劳工倡导者发表了约30分钟的有趣演讲，但由于使用的是其母语——法语，许多在场人士未能完全理解。

他的秘书爱德华·菲兰（Edward Philan）先生翻译了部分演讲内容，据称因时间不足未能进行全文翻译。中国政府工商局局长周诒春（T. Tehou，音译）先生主持了会议。

“为何来华？”

托马先生在演讲中说，到处都有人问他：“你为何来中国？”他表示，由于在此停留时间短，且没有真正机会对局势进行仔细研究，因此不可能对这个国家得出任何确切的结论。演讲者指出，在没有真实事实作为依据的情况下得出结论是不明智的。

他宣称，在日内瓦，事情并非如此处理。在得出结论之前，会对手头的问题进行详细研究，以便得出的结论切实可行并达到目的。

谈到访华之行时，托马声称，他此行旨在为本国与国际联盟劳工局之间建立更紧密的关系奠定基础。

演讲者表示，在讨论该局的工作时，有必要提及该局最初开始为全球劳工利益运作时的情况。

世界劳工危机

托马宣称，世界有史以来最大的劳工危机发生在1919年。在大战中战败的国家陷入了革命状态。而在战胜国中，劳工获得了新的认可，原因在于战争并非军队之间的对抗，而是人民之间的对抗。

据称，在那段时期，妇女在工厂工作，劳工组织起来以赢得战争。结果是，和平条约中制定了改善劳动人民状况的条款，因为在签署停战协定后，需要对大众的努力给予某种形式的认可。

演讲者称，人们曾庄严宣告，劳工状况严重且不公。随着36个国家成立劳工组织，一场旨在改变这些状况的运动随之展开。

为了组建这一庞大组织，社会局、政府和劳工代表在日内瓦会晤。据称，迄今为止已举行了十次会议——每年一次，取得的进展比一般人意识到的要多。

状况改善

与战前的劳工状况相比，目前的状况有了很大改善

page_data.en:
now, due to co-operation and
unity of labour itself, M. Thomas
said. One thing pointed out by
the labour leader was that child
labour in general has been abolish-
ed and an age limit for children
established. The 8-hour day has
also been generally recognized, he
stated, and women are no longer
required to work all night in mills
and other establishments of that
nature.

The 8-hour day, M. Thomas
explained, gives the labourer more
time for sleep and for intellectual
and moral development. Another
question of great importance to
the labourer, it was stated, and
one that has been taken up in a
serious manner, is that of in-
dustrial insurance, in addition to
the securing of work for the un-
employed, unemployment insurance
and insurance against old age
These matters are of vital im-
portance to labour the world over,
M. Thomas declared.

Human Dignity
The battle for these things is
being waged, he said, in order to
enable labour to live with at least
a share of human dignity and to
improve, not material but moral
conditions. In this manner the
labourer is thus given a chance
to look after his own interests.

When Mr. Tchou presented the
speaker he pointed out that not
only was he welcomed because he
had come a great distance, but
because he had devoted so much
of his time to the welfare of
others.

The guests included Baron S.
Ungern-Sternberg, Mr. W. W.

page_data.zh:
这归功于劳工自身的合作与团结，托马先生说。这位劳工领袖指出的一点是，童工总体上已被废除，并确立了儿童年龄限制。他还表示，八小时工作制也已得到普遍认可，妇女不再被要求在纱厂及其他类似机构中整夜工作。

托马解释说，八小时工作制让劳动者有更多时间睡眠，并进行智力和道德发展。据称，对劳动者而言另一个至关重要且已得到认真处理的问题是工业保险，此外还包括为失业者提供就业机会、失业保险以及养老保险。托马宣称，这些事项对全世界的劳工都至关重要。

人的尊严

他说，为争取这些事物而进行的斗争，旨在使劳工至少能享有部分人的尊严地生活，并改善道德状况而非仅仅是物质状况。通过这种方式，劳动者从而获得了照顾自身利益的机会。

周先生（Mr. Tchou）在介绍演讲者时指出，受到欢迎不仅因为他远道而来，还因为他将大量时间致力于他人的福祉。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 1, 1928.

M. THOMAS SPEAKS
AT NANKING

Declares China Should
Devise Own Labour
Regulations

Nanking, Nov. 30.
M. Albert Thomas, Director of
the International Labour Bureau,
is expected to leave for Shanghai
this evening.
Speaking at an informal meet-
ing at the Ministry of Industry,
Commerce and Labour presided
over by Minister H. H. Kung, M.
Thomas stated that in view of the
fact that labour conditions in
China are different from those in
foreign countries, China should
formulate her own regulations
governing treatment of labourers.
He also expressed the hope that
special deputies will be sent by
the Ministry to inspect factories
periodically and that free schools
be opened for the education of the
children of the labourers.
During his stay in the capital,
M. Thomas was the guest of Dr.
Kung and attended a dinner in
his honour, at which he met
many leaders of the Party and
Government.—Kuo Min.

托马先生
在南京发表讲话

宣称中国应制定
自己的劳工法规

南京，11月30日。
国际劳工局局长阿尔贝·托马先生预计将于今晚启程前往上海。
在由部长孔祥熙主持的工商部非正式会议上，托马先生表示，鉴于中国的劳工状况与国外不同，中国应制定管理劳工待遇的自有法规。他还表示希望部里派遣特别专员定期检查工厂，并为劳工子女开办免费学校。
在首都停留期间，托马先生是孔博士的客人，并出席了为他举办的晚宴，期间会见了许多党政领导人。——《国民新闻》

托马先生
明日抵达

为其两天停留
准备了充实的日程

正在远东巡回考察工业状况的国际联盟劳工局局长阿尔贝·托马先生将于明日从汉口抵达上海，但预计仅在此停留两天。
托马先生将对上海进行匆忙的巡视，并将会见劳工领袖和实业家。大上海市政府已为他准备了接待活动并安排了他的行程。
他的日程安排如下：
12月1日。—上午7点抵达上海。
上午9点至中午期间的访问：大上海市政府；工会及其学校；浦东工业模范村。
下午12点30分，泛太平洋会议举办的晚宴。
下午2点30分，参观工厂。
晚上7点，大上海市政府市长举办的晚宴。
12月2日。—上午的访问：国货展览会及大上海市政府展品；杨树浦社会中心；上海学院；国立劳动大学。
下午2点，在商业工会总部与当地工会代表举行会议。
下午3点30分，在上海基督教青年会举行公开演讲。
下午5点，在博物馆路20号与全国基督教协进会代表、基督教青年会全国委员会代表、基督教女青年会全国委员会代表及劳工代表举行讨论会。
晚上7点30分，社会局举办的晚宴。

访问行程

大上海市政府已做出周密安排，欢迎国际联盟国际劳工局局长阿尔伯特·托马斯（Albert Thomas）先生于明晨抵达上海。

托马斯先生正在研究中国劳工问题，他在此仅停留两天，随后将前往日本。其上海访问的安排由市政府负责。

明晨，托马斯先生将访问市政府、各工会及其学校，以及由基督教青年会（Y.M.C.A.）创办的浦东模范工业村。中午，他将在礼查饭店（Astor House）向泛太平洋协会成员发表演讲，下午将参观各家工厂。晚间，市长张定璠将军将设宴款待他。

周日，这位贵宾将参观国货展览会、杨树浦社会中心、上海大学及国立劳动大学。下午，他将在商业工会总部与当地工会代表举行会议，随后在中华基督教青年会发表演讲。下午5时，他将与全国劳工问题委员会代表举行讨论会，晚间将由大上海社会局设宴招待

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 29, 1928.

M. THOMAS ARRIVES
AT NANKING

Labour Bureau Director
Welcomed By Govern-
ment Officials

Nanking, Nov. 27.
M. Albert Thomas, Director of
the International Labour Bureau,
arrived here from Hankow last
night at 7 o'clock, and was re-
ceived at Hsiakwan station by
representatives of the Govern-
ment.
Accompanied by Mr. T. C.
Tchou (Director of the Labour
Department of the Ministry of
Industry, Commerce and Labour),
M. Thomas is making calls on
various Government officials to-
day. In the evening a reception
in his honour will be given by
Minister H. H. Kung.
Interviewed by the Kuo Min
news agency correspondent, M.
Thomas remarked: "A cursory
survey of about ten days, of
course, cannot give me a very
accurate insight into the actual
Labour conditions of your coun-
try. As far as I am able to
judge, the improvement of the
living conditions of women and
child workers in your country
seems to be the most pressing
need."

（印：MISSION ...）

托马斯先生抵达
南京

劳工局局长
受到政府官员欢迎

南京，11月27日。
国际劳工局局长阿尔伯特·托马斯（Albert Thomas）先生昨晚7点从汉口抵达此处，并在下关车站受到政府代表的接待。

托马斯先生在工商部劳工司司长朱懋澄（T. C. Tchou）先生的陪同下，今天拜访了各位政府官员。晚间，孔祥熙（H. H. Kung）部长将为他举行招待会。

在接受国民新闻社记者采访时，托马斯先生表示：“当然，为期约十天的粗略考察，无法让我对贵国实际的劳工状况有非常准确的了解。据我判断，改善贵国女工和童工的生活条件似乎是最迫切的需求。”

LABOUR.

MEETING OF SECOND HAND CLOTHING SHOP
EMPLOYEES UNION.

The Shun Pao ( Regtd. Fr. Cons. ), Sin Wan ( Regtd.
U.S. Cons. ), China Times ( Regtd. Fr. Cons. ), Eastern
Times ( Regtd. Fr. Cons. ), Shanghai Daily News, and
Mingkuopao publish the following report:-
The Shanghai Second Hand Clothing Shop Employees
Union held a meeting at 9 a.m. yesterday. Woo Pih Hwa
presided.
The following resolutions were passed:-
(1) That all the employees suspend work on
November 24 ( a memorial day ) and that the employers be
first notified in order to avoid any misunderstanding.
(2) That those members of the Union who have
refused to contribute towards the special fund to meet the
expenses of the Union, be first warned and should they
still refuse to pay, the matter be referred to the general
meeting for discussion.
(3) That the shop proprietors be asked to
employ more men at times when more work has to be turned
out within a limited length of time.

MEETING OF UNION OF WAITERS IN THE EMPLOY
OF THE SHANGHAI-NANKING AND SHANGHAI-
HANGCHOW RAILWAYS.

The Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao, China Times, Eastern
Times and Mingkuopao publish the following report:-
The union of waiters in the employ of the
Shanghai-Nanking and Shanghai-Hangchow Railways held a
meeting at 8 p.m. yesterday. Hsu Soong Dong presided.
The following resolutions were passed:-
(1) That any one desiring to join the railway
as a waiter be first requested to join this Union.
(2) That all waiters taken on be introduced
by this Union.
(3) That an advertisement be published in
newspapers announcing that membership badges issued on
April 16 this year are no longer valid and that new
badges be issued.

RECEPTION TO BE GIVEN TO THOMSON, REPRESENTATIVE
OF INTERNATIONAL LABOUR BUREAU.

The Mingkuopao publishes the following report:-
Mr. Thomson, representative of the International
Labour Bureau, will soon come to Shanghai from Peiping to
investigate into labour conditions in Shanghai.
Upon learning of this the Nanyang Brothers'
Tobacco Company Employees Union, the Commercial Press
Employees Union, the Shanghai Newspaper Office Employees
Union, the Shanghai Postal Employees Union and a number
of other labour unions are preparing a reception in his
honour. An office has been established in the second
branch union of the Commercial Press Employees Union.

M. THOMAS IN
PEKING.
HIS CHIEF AIM IN COMING.
TO INVITE CHINESE TO
LABOUR CONFERENCE.
• STATEMENT TO THE PRESS.
Peiping, Nov. 19.
Count Martel, French Minister
to China, and Mr. Albert Thomas,
director of the International La-
bour Bureau at Geneva, arrived
here Sunday morning at 9.30. The
two distinguished guests were
greeted at the Chienmen station by
a large number of Chinese officials
and members of the French Lega-
tion.
Mr. Chi Ta-peng, head of the
Peiping office of the Ministry of
Foreign Affairs, gave a banquet
Sunday night in honour of Count
Martel and Mr. Thomas at the for-
mer Waichiaopu building. Among
those present were Mr. Chang
Chi, Chairman of the Peiping
Branch Political Council, Mayor
Ho Chi-kung, directors of the
municipal bureaux, and members
of the French Legation staff.
“As China is a member of the
International Labour Bureau,”
said Mr. Thomas to a Kuo Wen re-
presentative, “I shall attempt to
invite Chinese labour and capital
to send one delegate each to the
conferences of the Bureau. China
has been so far represented by a
government delegate at the con-
ferences. This is my chief aim
in coming to this country.
“I shall induce the Chinese
National Government, continued
Mr. Thomas, “To ratify the In-
ternational Labour Convention.
The Bureau desires to have Chinese
labour laws in accord with the
spirit of the convention. I will act
as a sort of go-between to help
China to have her labour laws en-
forced in the foreign concessions.”
Mr. Thomas declared that he
would not attempt to investigate
Chinese labour conditions, because
he could not have the time as he is
going to stay in China for a couple
of weeks.
Mr. Thomas is staying at the
Grand Hotel de Pekin with Dr.
Chen Chung-cheng, chief secretary
of the International Labour
Bureau. They will go to Hankow,
Nanking, and Shanghai in a day or
two stopping in the southern cities
for a few days. From Shanghai
Mr. Thomas will proceed to Japan,
Hongkong, Canton, and the South-
Sea islands.
Mr. Thomas will also call on the
authorities of the foreign conces-
sions to request them to assist
the Chinese Government to enforce
her labour laws in the settlements.
The International Labour Bureau
was established nine years ago and
it has now 55 nations as its mem-
bers.—Kuo Wen.

托马斯先生在
北平。
他此次前来的
主要目的。
邀请中国人参加
劳工会议。
• 对新闻界的声明。
北平，11月19日。
法国驻华公使马泰尔伯爵（Count Martel）和日内瓦国际劳工局局长阿尔伯特·托马斯（Albert Thomas）先生于周日上午9:30抵达此处。两位贵宾在前门车站受到了众多中国官员和法国公使馆成员的迎接。

外交部北平办事处主任纪达鹏（Chi Ta-peng）先生于周日晚在原外务部大楼设宴款待马泰尔伯爵和托马斯先生。出席者包括北平政治分会主席张继（Chang Chi）先生、市长何其巩（Ho Chi-kung）先生、各局处长及法国公使馆工作人员。

托马斯先生对《国风》报记者表示：“由于中国是国际劳工局的成员国，我将尝试邀请中国劳工界和资本界各派一名代表参加该局的会议。迄今为止，中国在会议上仅由政府代表出席。这是我此次来到贵国的主要目的。”

托马斯先生继续说道：“我将促使中国国民政府批准《国际劳工公约》。该局希望中国的劳动法符合公约的精神。我将充当某种中间人，帮助中国在外国租界执行其劳动法。”

托马斯先生宣称，他不会试图调查中国的劳工状况，因为他没有时间，他将在中国停留两周左右。

托马斯先生与国际劳工局首席秘书陈仲成（Chen Chung-cheng）博士一同住在北京饭店。他们将在一两天内前往汉口、南京和上海，并在南方城市停留数日。托马斯先生将从上海前往日本、香港、广州和南洋群岛。

托马斯先生还将拜访外国租界当局，请求他们协助中国政府在租界内执行其劳动法。

国际劳工局成立于九年前，目前拥有55个成员国。—《国风》。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 24, 1928

M. ALBERT THOMAS
IN PEKING

Labour Bureau Director of
League of Nations
Touring China

Peking, Nov. 22 (Delayed).
M. Albert Thomas, Director of the International Labour Bureau of the League of Nations, left last night for Hankow by the night express. Interviewed by the Kuo Min News Agency correspondent at the station on his impressions of the labour situation in the north, M. Thomas remarked that China had not yet entered the industrial stage of its development.
“There is little difference between your so-called employers and employees. Furthermore, I notice that your merchants are inclined to consider themselves in the capitalist class which, of course, is a mistake. The Chinese labourers, too, generally entertain the misconception that your Chambers of Commerce are capitalistic organs. It is my belief that your socio-economic problems, if you have any at all, can best be solved by your own Principle of the People’s Livelihood. There need not be any class-struggles in China,” said M. Thomas.
Speaking at the General Labour Union yesterday, Mr. Thomas emphasized the necessity of sound organization and productivity. “You cannot talk about distribution of profits unless you are sure of the source of profits—which is increasing productivity,” M. Thomas told the labour leaders.—Kuo-Min.

阿尔贝·托马先生
在北平

国际联盟劳工局局长
巡视中国

北平，11月22日（延迟报道）。
国际联盟国际劳工局局长阿尔贝·托马（M. Albert Thomas）先生昨晚乘夜车特快前往汉口。在车站接受国闻通讯社记者关于其对北方劳工状况印象的采访时，托马先生表示，中国尚未进入其发展的工业阶段。
“你们所谓的雇主与雇员之间几乎没有差别。此外，我注意到你们的商人倾向于将自己视为资本家阶级，这当然是一种误解。中国劳工也普遍存在一种误解，认为你们的商会是资本主义机构。我相信，如果你们有任何社会经济问题的话，最好通过你们自己的‘民生主义’原则来解决。中国不需要任何阶级斗争，”托马先生说。
托马先生昨天在总工会发表讲话时，强调了健全组织和提高生产力的必要性。“除非你们确信利润的来源——即提高生产力——否则就不能谈论利润分配，”托马先生对劳工领袖们说。——国闻社。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, DECEMBER, 7, 1928

WHAT M. THOMAS
DID NOT SEE

M. Albert Thomas, the famous French Labour leader, Socialist and League of Nations official, came to China as the guest of the Nationalist Government. He was guided about industrial Shanghai by Mr. Thomas Tchou, secretary to General Chiang Kai-shek and concurrently Chief of the Bureau of Labour of the Ministry of Commerce, Labour and Industry. He spent a week-end in this, the principal industrial centre of the country, and saw only what Mr. Tchou wanted him to see. In spite of the fact that the two largest employers of labour in China are British and Japanese firms, he visited no British or Japanese enterprises; his interviews with foreign employers of labour were scant; he made no investigations of hours, wages, welfare work in foreign-owned industries. He is, therefore, not in a position to give a first-hand report on conditions of labour in Shanghai, except in one or two Chinese-owned cotton mills. Any conclusions which M. Thomas may reach must therefore be based upon one-sided, propagandist data provided by Mr. Tchou or upon a priori opinions formed as a result of the efforts of the Second International Socialists to replace the Third International Communists as the effective guides of Chinese labour.

It is most unfortunate that a man of M. Thomas's reputation should have given Shanghai no more than a glance, that he should have permitted anyone to map out his programme and to consume all his time, and that he should have listened, without adequate investigation, to only one side of a story. Such conduct reflects on the International Labour Office of the League of Nations, of which M. Thomas is the head. Organizations of foreign employers of Chinese labour would do wisely to make representations immediately to the secretariat of the League of Nations with regard to M. Thomas's curious conduct and wild conclusions, to which reference was made two day's ago.

It was during M. Thomas's visit to Shanghai that the Ministry of Commerce, Labour and Industry formulated its semi-Communistic Labour Code, ostensibly the product of Mr. Thomas Tchou, who has never been a labourer or an employer of labour but whose experience lies in an industrial secretaryship in the Y.M.C.A. This code, like previous labour codes, has only two objectives: one, is to indicate to socialists and welfare workers in Europe and America that China is ultra-modern in its treatment of labour and that failure to make the code effective is due only to extraterritoriality, etc.; the other is to embarrass foreign employers of labour. It is not intended that this code should apply to Chinese employers of labour, who could not survive a month under its provisions. It cannot be forgotten, for instance, that when the Shanghai Municipal Council sought to enact a child labour law, it was the Chinese, and not the foreign employers of labour, who protested. A visit to the Japanese cotton mills and the British tobacco factories, and a comparison between them and the Chinese silk filatures and the Chinese cotton mills, will easily prove the superiority of labour conditions in foreign-owned industries. M. Thomas as a theoretician of labour is more likely, however, to be influenced by conditions than by conditions. Therefore Mr. Tchou provided a code and hid the conditions.

It is surprising that Dr. H. H. Kung permits his Ministry to be used in this way. Dr. Kung comes of an old family of Shansi bankers and knows what business is and how difficult it is for capital to operate at a profit in this country at this time. Yet, his Ministry is now responsible for this monstrous labour code, as it was responsible for the unfortunate trade-mark muddle and the lessening in usefulness of the Bureau of Economic Information. One cannot repress the thought that the personnel of the Ministry needs over-hauling.

《字林西报》，1928年12月7日，星期五

托马先生
未能见到的情况

著名的法国劳工领袖、社会党人及国际联盟官员阿尔贝·托马先生作为国民政府的客人来到中国。他在工业重镇上海的参观由蒋介石将军的秘书、兼工商部劳工局局长朱学范（Thomas Tchou，音译）先生引导。他在这个全国主要的工业中心度过了一个周末，只看到了朱先生希望他看到的东西。尽管中国最大的两家劳工雇主是英国和日本公司，但他没有访问任何英国或日本企业；他与外国雇主的会谈寥寥无几；他没有对外资工业中的工时、工资和福利工作进行任何调查。因此，除了一两家华资棉纺厂外，他无法就上海的劳工状况提供第一手报告。因此，托马先生可能得出的任何结论，都必须基于朱先生提供的片面、宣传性的数据，或者基于第二国际社会党人试图取代第三国际共产党人成为中国劳工有效指导者的努力所形成的先入为主的观点。

令人极为遗憾的是，像托马先生这样享有盛誉的人对上海只是匆匆一瞥，允许他人规划他的行程并占用了他所有的时间，且在没有充分调查的情况下只听信一面之词。这种行为损害了由托马先生领导的国际联盟国际劳工局的声誉。在华雇佣中国劳工的外国雇主组织应明智地立即向国际联盟秘书处提出交涉，针对托马先生两天前被提及的古怪行为和荒谬结论予以关注。

正是在托马先生访问上海期间，工商部制定了其半共产主义性质的《劳动法典》，表面上这是朱学范先生的产物，他从未做过劳工或雇主，其经验仅限于基督教青年会（Y.M.C.A.）的工业秘书工作。该法典与以往的劳动法典一样，只有两个目标：一是向欧美社会主义者和福利工作者表明，中国在对待劳工方面极其现代化，而法典未能生效仅仅是因为治外法权等原因；二是使外国雇主陷入困境。该法典并不打算适用于中国雇主，因为在这些规定下，他们连一个月都无法生存。例如，人们不应忘记，当上海公共租界工部局试图颁布童工法时，提出抗议的是中国雇主，而非外国雇主。参观一下日本棉纺厂和英国烟草厂，并将其与中国缫丝厂和华资棉纺厂进行比较，将轻易证明外资企业中劳工条件的优越性。然而，作为劳工理论家的托马先生更有可能受条件影响，而非受实际情况影响。因此，朱先生提供了一部法典，却掩盖了实际情况。

令人惊讶的是，孔祥熙博士允许其部里被如此利用。孔博士出身于山西银行世家，深知商业运作之道，以及目前资本在中国盈利经营的困难程度。然而，他的部里现在要对这部荒谬的劳动法典负责，正如它此前对不幸的商标混乱局面以及经济情报局效用降低负有责任一样。人们不禁认为，该部的人员构成需要进行整顿。

THE NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 7, 1928

M. ALBERT THOMAS
FAREWELL
China at Last Reunited and
Starts A Magnificent
Future in Store

Nanking, Dec. 5.
The Central Radio Station this
afternoon broadcast in French and
Chinese the following "farewell
message to the Chinese people"
which M. Albert Thomas, Director
of the International Labour Office
of the League of Nations, prepared
before his departure from China.
We give a translation in English:
"I am happy to have this oppor-
tunity of extending my most cordial
salution to the Chinese people
through the Central Broadcasting
Wireless Station of the Kuomintang.
After so many trying years China
is at last reunited; she is now co-
ordinating her efforts along the
lines of national reconstruction.
She is seeking the amelioration of
those who are toiling and suffering.
At the same time her voice has be-
come increasingly authoritative for
the vindication of her rights as a
Sovereign state and the establish-
ment of justice in her international
relations.

Need for Perseverance
"Such a great achievement calls
for efforts of a special nature.
There are evil forces lurking in the
recesses of the human heart such
as selfishness, inactivity and en-
slaving habits, which obstruct the
expression of the better sentiments
of humanity. It is, therefore, neces-
sary to make constant efforts to
carry on the task that China has
undertaken. If the workers of Eur-
opean nations were successful ten
years ago in creating for themselves
better conditions of life, it is be-
cause they have not ceased to
struggle daily for the vindication
and acquisition of their rights. The
Chinese people should, therefore,
bear in mind that they cannot
obtain liberty and secure their wel-
fare except at the price of extra-
ordinary firmness of purpose and
perseverance.
"I hope that the great work of
popular education which the Kuo-
mintang has undertaken at the pre-
sent period will do much to hasten
the magnificent future that is in
store for a united China. I sincere-
ly hope that the Three Principles
of Dr. Sun Yat-sen, namely, the in-
dependence of the people, the gov-
ernment of the people, and the wel-
fare of the people, will bear abund-
ant fruits in the near future.

Foreign Powers and China
"I hope that above all the sort of
international régime which China
complains of will be substituted by
the pacific efforts of diplomacy, and
that this coupled with the concilia-
tory encouragement of all the peo-
ples of the world will usher in a
new régime of equality and peace.
"On our part, whether we have
in mind the League of Nations or
the International Bureau of Labour,
we shall exert ourselves to offer
your country our earnest co-opera-
tion and our fraternal assistance in
every way in order that we may
together with your country witness
the realization of the common ideal
of humanity, i.e., universal peace
established on the basis of social
justice."—Kuo Min.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1928年12月7日，星期五

阿尔贝·托马先生
告别辞
中国终于统一并开启
辉煌的未来

南京，12月5日。
中央广播电台今天下午用法语和中文广播了国际联盟国际劳工局局长阿尔贝·托马先生在离开中国前准备的以下“致中国人民告别辞”。现译为英文如下：
“我很高兴有机会通过国民党中央无线广播电台向中国人民致以最亲切的问候。经过多年艰难岁月，中国终于统一；现在正沿着国家重建的方针协调努力。她正在寻求改善那些辛勤劳作和受苦受难者的境遇。同时，她的声音在维护其作为主权国家的权利和建立国际关系中的正义方面变得日益具有权威性。

需要坚持不懈
“如此伟大的成就需要特殊的努力。人性深处潜藏着诸如自私、惰性和奴性习惯等邪恶力量，阻碍着人类美好情感的表达。因此，必须不断努力以继续中国所承担的任务。如果欧洲各国的工人在十年前成功为自己创造了更好的生活条件，那是因为他们从未停止为维护和争取权利而每日斗争。因此，中国人民应铭记，除非以非凡的决心和毅力为代价，否则无法获得自由并确保福祉。
“我希望国民党目前开展的民众教育伟大工作，将大大加速统一中国即将到来的辉煌未来。我衷心希望孙中山博士的三民主义，即民族独立、民权政府和民生福利，在不久的将来结出丰硕成果。

列强与中国
“我希望，特别是中国所抱怨的那种国际体制，将通过外交的和平努力而被取代，并且这种努力加上全世界人民的和解性鼓励，将迎来一个平等与和平的新体制。
“就我们而言，无论是考虑到国际联盟还是国际劳工局，我们将竭力在各个方向上向贵国提供我们真诚的合作与兄弟般的援助，以便我们与贵国共同见证人类共同理想的实现，即在社会正义基础上建立的普遍和平。”——国闻社。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 6, 1928.

M. THOMAS ARRIVES
IN JAPAN

Radical Labour Unions
Oppose His Presence
In Country

Tokyo. Dec. 5.
M. Albert Thomas, Director of
the International Labour Office of
the league of Nations at Geneva,
who arrived yesterday at Nagasaki,
where he was welcomed by repre-
sentatives of various labour
organizations, and sailed for Kobe
the same day, in an interview with
Japanese press representatives,
stated as follows:—
“I intend to stay in Japan for
about three weeks for the purpose
of investigating labour conditions.
It is my sincere desire that more
friendly relations between myself
and leaders of various labour
organizations in this country will
be established which is necessary
for me to accomplish my duties at
the International Labour Office of
the League of Nations.
“I am given to understand that
among Japanese labour unions,
those, which are considered the
‘Lefts’ are agitating against my
landing in this country on the
pretext that my visit to Japan
will possibly accelerate the forma-
tion of the league of the ‘Rights,’
but I do not mind it. Though it
is likely that communistic elements
in various places may oppose me,
it cannot be helped, for I think
that is due to the difference of
opinions. I am determined to do
my utmost peacefully, legally and
positively for the realization of
socialism.”—Toho.

日内瓦国际联盟国际劳工局局长阿尔贝·托马先生昨日抵达长崎，受到各劳工组织代表的欢迎，并于同日乘船前往神户。他在接受日本新闻界代表采访时陈述如下：—
“我打算在日本停留约三周，目的是调查劳工状况。我真诚希望与该国各劳工组织领导人建立更友好的关系，这对于我在国际联盟国际劳工局履行职责是必要的。
“据我了解，在日本工会中，那些被视为‘左派’的工会正以我的访问可能会加速‘右派’联盟的形成为借口，煽动反对我登陆该国，但我并不介意。虽然各地的共产主义分子可能会反对我，但这无可奈何，因为我认为这是由于意见分歧所致。我决心和平、合法且积极地为实现社会主义尽最大努力。”——东洋社。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 5, 1928

M. ALBERT THOMAS
ON CHINA

Unequal Treaties the Cause of
Chinese Labour's Hard
Conditions

SINGULAR SPEECH AS
REPORTED

Prominence is given in the Chi-
nese press to a farewell reception for
M. Albert Thomas, Director of the
International Labour Office of the
League of Nations, when he was
entertained by representatives of
the Chinese Labour Unions in
Shanghai.

A man named Er Dah-tsung
presided and delivered the following
speech of welcome:—"We extend a
hearty welcome to Mr. Thomas,
Chief of the International Labour
Bureau, because of his personality
and knowledge. Mr. Thomas has all
the time extended a helping hand to
labourers in the world. He has now
came to our country to investigate
labour conditions and he will seek to
bring about the emancipation of our
labourers. I would like to bring to
the notice of Mr. Thomas the labour
conditions in China. After the May
30 tragedy labourers in China re-
alized the position of our country
and have been working for their
emancipation. Labour Unions have
been organized throughout the
country and labourers have par-
ticipated in patriotic movements.
At present 1,024,078 labourers have
joined labour unions as members.
The hardships of labourers in China
are due to the nondevelopment of
industry and the existence of
unequal treaties. We therefore hope
that Mr. Albert Thomas will work
for the welfare of Chinese labourers
and render assistance to our
country in her efforts to secure
the abolition of the unequal
treaties between China and the
various foreign nations."

M. Thomas's Reply

In reply M. Thomas is reported
to have delivered the following
speech:—

Beloved labour friends, I esteem
it a glory to be able to meet you
here. I would like to inform you
that the object of the International
Labour Bureau is to elevate the
position of labourers in the world,
and to make the livelihood of
labourers a better one. Therefore
it is the desire of the International
Labour Bureau to have all labourers,
particularly Chinese labourers, join-
ing the Bureau. The International
Labour Bureau holds meetings an-
nually. Various countries in the
world send representatives to par-
ticipate at this meeting, but China
has so far not sent any delegates.

Now that China has become united,
representatives should be sent. The
other day I received letters from
labour unions in Nanking and
Shanghai. I studied their conditions
and I shall send them a reply soon.

The Treaties

"I have found that the hardships
of Chinese labourers are due to the
oppression caused by the unequal
treaties; therefore in order that the
position of Chinese labourers might
be elevated the unequal treaties with
foreign countries must first be
abolished. (Italics are ours) As the
Nationalist Government is now
negotiating with the various foreign
nations for the revision of treaties
the unequal treaties will be cancelled
before long.

"As soon as this has been done
the position of Chinese labourers will
be elevated; while Chinese labourers
in foreign countries will be able
to enjoy equal treatment. I believe
that foreign nations will accept the
reasonable demands of Chinese
labourers. I would draw your at-
tention to the fact that every care
should be taken against capitalism
which should in no case be permitted
to exist. I shall do my utmost to
help Chinese labourers to the end,
but I hope that you yourselves will
work hard in the organization of a
strong labour union."

《字林西报》，1928年12月5日，星期三

阿尔贝·托马先生
论中国

不平等条约是造成
中国劳工艰难处境的原因

报道中的奇特言论

中国报纸显著报道了为国际联盟国际劳工局局长阿尔贝·托马（Albert Thomas）先生举行的告别招待会的情况，他在上海受到了中国工会代表的款待。

一位名叫 Er Dah-tsung（音译）的人主持了会议，并发表了以下欢迎辞：“我们热烈欢迎国际劳工局主任托马先生，这是出于对他的人格和学识的敬重。托马先生一直向全世界的劳动者伸出援手。他现在来到我国调查劳工状况，并将致力于谋求我们劳工的解放。我想提请托马先生注意中国的劳工状况。在‘五卅’惨案之后，中国劳工认识到了国家的处境，并一直在为自身的解放而努力。全国各地已组织了工会，劳工也参与了爱国运动。目前已有1,024,078名劳工加入工会成为会员。中国劳工的苦难是由于工业不发达以及不平等条约的存在所致。因此，我们希望阿尔贝·托马先生能为中国劳工的福祉而努力，并在我国争取废除中国与各外国之间不平等条约的努力中提供援助。”

托马先生的答复

据报道，托马先生在答复中发表了以下演讲：

亲爱的劳工朋友们，能在这里与你们会面，我深感荣幸。我想告知各位，国际劳工局的宗旨是提高全世界劳工的地位，改善劳工的生活。因此，国际劳工局希望所有劳工，特别是中国劳工，加入本局。国际劳工局每年举行会议。世界各国派遣代表参加此会议，但中国迄今未派遣任何代表。

既然中国已经统一，理应派遣代表。日前我收到南京和上海工会的来信。我研究了他们的情况，并将很快给予回复。

关于条约

“我发现，中国劳工的苦难是由于不平等条约造成的压迫所致；因此，为了提高中国劳工的地位，必须首先废除与外国的不平等条约。（着重号为笔者所加）鉴于国民政府目前正与各外国谈判修订条约，不平等条约不久将被取消。

“一旦做到这一点，中国劳工的地位将得到提高；而在外国的中国劳工也将能够享受平等待遇。我相信各国会接受中国劳工的合理要求。我要提请你们注意这样一个事实：必须处处提防资本主义，决不允许其存在。我将竭尽全力帮助中国劳工到底，但我希望你们自己在组织一个强大的工会方面努力工作。”

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 5, 1928

M. Thomas's Indiscretions

Chinese newspaper reports are
not exactly evidence, but there
seems reason to believe that M.
Albert Thomas has been "flapping
his mouth" with a good deal more
freedom than he should have done.
In yesterday's issue we printed a
statement issued by him through
the Kuo Min News Agency on his
departure from China, in which he
says:—

"I find the existence of a stable and
united government in China, capable
of maintaining the unity of the Chi-
nese Republic and economic reconstruc-
tion after years of civil war."

There is no reason to believe that
a reputable agency like the Kuo
Min invented this remarkable
statement, which, to put it mildly,
is very "intelligent anticipation"

indeed; and the statement makes
one feel that there is some truth in
the wild and mischievous assertion
attributed to him at a labour union
reception on Sunday that "the
hardships of the Chinese labourers
are due to the oppression caused by
the unequal treaties." It is parti-
cularly regrettable that a man who
holds the important position of
Director of the International
Labour Bureau of the League of
Nations should talk such pernicious
rubbish. A writer in the "Journal
de Shanghai" recalls that M.
Thomas succeeded M. Jaurès as
leader of the French Socialist
party in 1914, adding that "if he
had less lyrical faculty than the
great tribune, he possessed a more
profound sense of realities." Four-
teen years have evidently worked
a change in M. Thomas: it seems
a case of all lyrics and no realities
now. M. Thomas tells the "Journal
de Shanghai" that a bureau is to
be established in China, in connec-
tion with the Geneva office, "which
will be able at any moment to
furnish us with exact information
on all questions interesting to us."
We hope M. Thomas will see that
some exact information about the
treaties is included and to what
the hardships of Chinese labourers
are really due.

《字林西报》，1928年12月5日，星期三

托马先生的失言

中国报纸的报道并非确凿证据，但有理由相信，阿尔贝·托马先生“信口开河”的程度远超他应有的分寸。在昨天的版面中，我们刊登了他通过国闻通讯社在他离开中国时发表的声明，其中他说：—

“我发现中国存在一个稳定且统一的政府，有能力在多年内战之后维持中华民国的统一并进行经济重建。”

没有理由相信像国闻社这样信誉良好的机构会捏造这一非凡的声明，退一步说，这确实是非常“聪明的预判”；而且这一声明让人感觉到，周日在一个工会招待会上归咎于他的那句荒谬且恶毒的话——“中国劳工的苦难是由于不平等条约造成的压迫所致”——可能确有几分真实性。特别令人遗憾的是，身为国际联盟国际劳工局局长这样重要职位的人，竟会散布如此有害的废话。《上海日报》（Journal de Shanghai）的一位撰稿人回顾说，托马先生于1914年继饶勒斯（Jaurès）先生之后成为法国社会党领袖，并补充说，“虽然他的抒情天赋不如那位伟大的演说家，但他对现实有着更深刻的感知。”十四年显然改变了托马先生：现在看来，他似乎只有抒情而无视现实。托马先生告诉《上海日报》，将在中国设立一个与日内瓦办事处联系的局，“该机构将能随时向我们提供关于我们感兴趣的所有问题的确切信息。”我们希望托马先生确保将一些关于条约的确切信息包括在内，并查明中国劳工的苦难究竟是由什么造成的。

Made by W.I. Robertson. Forwarded by J.K. Owens A.C. Pol.

Mr. Albert Thomas, Director of the International Labour
Bureau of the League of Nations, left Geneva at the end of
October 1923 as the representative of the labour bureau on a
tour of the Far East to study the industrial situation and
visited Berlin, Moscow, Warsaw and Harbin en route to China.
Accompanied by his staff and in company with Count Martel, French
Minister to China, he arrived at Peking on November 15. On
November 24 he arrived at Hankow where he remained for two days
and on the evening of November 26 reached Nanking. On December 1
he arrived in Shanghai and visited British American Tobacco
Company's factory, Pudong; the Nanyang Brothers Cigarette Company's
factory, Pudong; as well as several Chinese owned concerns
in the International Settlement. At 12.30 p.m. the same day he
attended a tea given in his honour at the Astor House by the
Pan Pacific Association in Shanghai and in the evening was
present at a dinner given in his honour by the Municipality of
Greater Shanghai at 43 Avenue Dubail.

On December 2, he visited the Chinese Native Goods
Exposition, the Nantao Tramway Employees' Union, the Chien Tuh
Savings Society, Zhabei, where a reception was given by some
representatives of the local labour unions and 40 Kuomintang
members, and in the evening of the same day he attended a dinner
party given in his honour by about 100 Chinese merchants in the
Chinese General Chamber of Commerce, while at 3.40 p.m. his
secretary, Mr. Philan, delivered an address on the organisation
of the International Labour Bureau at Geneva in the Chinese
Y.M.C.A. 201 Szechuen Road.

关于托马斯先生任何一次访谈被认为最真实的记录，是乔治·马雷斯特 (Georges Maresthe) 先生在12月4日的《上海日报》(Le Journal de Shanghai) 上发表的报道，他写道：“外国和中国媒体发布了许多关于阿尔伯特·托马斯先生访华目的的不实报道。我在酒店与他进行了一次访谈，托马斯先生是国际劳工局局长，他对这些错误报道进行了如下更正：

“我来中国有几个目的，主要目的是争取中国在国际联盟和国际劳工局获得更充分的代表权。在该局有代表的54个国家各有四名代表：两名代表各自政府，一名代表雇主，一名代表劳工。国民政府已向我承诺采取必要步骤，使中国与其他国家处于同等地位。

“该局起草了劳动法规，并提交其各成员批准。截至目前，已有25项公约。只有卢森堡批准了所有公约，法国批准了18项，英国批准了13项，而中国仅批准了一项：即禁止在火柴制造中使用白磷的公约。

“中国的困难在于该国没有社会立法，但国民政府目前正在致力于此，并同意将其法律草案提交给该局，以就

BULLETIN
OF THE
LABOUR RESEARCH ASSOCATION
OF CHINA

Vol. I No. 1 April 1929 20 Cents

TO OUR READERS

The Labour Research Association is an outgrowth of
the visit of M. Albert Thomas, Director of the International
Labour Office, to China. M. Thomas had at the time some
long conversations with persons interested in labour con-
ditions in China, and sympathetic with the work of the
Office, who gave him full assistance and some brief reports
upon the situation here.

M. Thomas felt keenly the lack of definite information
on conditions in this country, particularly in European
languages. After his departure, therefore, several persons
who had been in touch with him here decided to form an
association and to supply the Labour Office with informa-
tion on the subjects needed. This group included both
Chinese and foreigners, and after discussion of the work
before them decided that their investigations could be for
the service both of the International Labour Office and of
persons in China interested in labour conditions. With a
government one of the most fundamental principles of
page_data.zh:
供 J.A. 库克 (Cook) 先生知悉
贾苏切森 (Jasucheson)
1929年4月10日

公报
中国劳工研究协会

第一卷 第一期 1929年4月 20美分

致读者

劳工研究协会是国际劳工局局长阿尔伯特·托马斯 (Albert Thomas) 先生访华的产物。托马斯先生当时与一些关心中国劳工状况并同情该局工作的人士进行了长谈，这些人给予了他充分的帮助，并提供了一些关于此处情况的简要报告。

托马斯先生深切感到缺乏关于本国状况的确切信息，尤其是缺乏欧洲语言的信息。因此，在他离开后，几位曾在此与他接触的人决定成立一个协会，并向劳工局提供所需主题的信息。这个团体包括中国人和外国人，在讨论了摆在他们面前的工作后，他们决定他们的调查既可以服务于国际劳工局，也可以服务于在中国关心劳工状况的人士。对于一个政府来说，其最基本的原则之一是

page_data.en:
— 2 —

which is its devotion to the people's livelihood, such reports might be of particular value. Accordingly, it was considered of value to publish reports in China of investigations made, having same printed in Chinese and in English (or French), and bringing them out in bulletin form so as to be available to all parties interested in such information.

Most of our readers, we trust, have already some acquaintance with the nature of the International Labour Office created by the Versailles treaty. The I. L. O. is as organization separate and distinct from the League of Nations, and consists of representatives of government, labour, and capital of the nations affiliated,—now including most nations of the world. The organization was formed upon the recognition, forced upon all in recent years, that lasting peace can be established and maintained only if based upon social justice, and that there exist widespread conditions which make for discontent and unrest. In the improvement of these conditions it is necessary to work on an international scale, so the I. L. O. drafts conventions and recommendations which are later brought before the governing bodies of the various nations for adoption and enforcement in their territory. Protection of workers in certain dangerous employments, protection of woman and child labour, investigations into compulsory labour, co-operation, trade union organization, etc., are taken up by the organization. Its work, broadly, falls into two divisions: scientific research,—the collection of information on all subjects related to conditions of labour and industrial life; and the preparation and adoption of conventions based upon such information.

The work of the Labour Research Association of China is of the first category. We aim to gather information on
page_data.zh:
— 2 —

致力于民生，此类报告可能具有特别的价值。因此，人们认为在中国出版调查报告是有价值的，将这些报告用中文和英文（或法文）印刷，并以公报形式发布，以便所有对此类信息感兴趣的各方都能获取。

我们相信，大多数读者已经对凡尔赛条约创立的国际劳工局的性质有所了解。国际劳工局是一个独立于国际联盟的组织，由附属国的政府、劳工和资本代表组成——现在包括世界上大多数国家。该组织的成立是基于近年来迫使所有人认识到的一点，即只有基于社会正义才能建立和维持持久和平，并且存在广泛导致不满和动荡的状况。为了改善这些状况，必须在国际规模上进行工作，因此国际劳工局起草公约和建议书，随后提交各国管理机构在其领土内采纳和执行。该组织处理的问题包括保护从事某些危险职业的工人、保护妇女和童工、调查强迫劳动、合作、工会组织等。其工作大致分为两类：科学研究——收集与劳工状况和工业生活有关的所有主题的信息；以及在此基础上准备和通过公约。

中国劳工研究协会的工作属于第一类。我们的目标是收集有关

page_data.en:
— 3 —

the conditions of workers in mills and factories, on farms
and in mines, in shops and in domestic service; information
on the relations between employers and employees,
whether regular wage labour, piece-work, contract labour,
or slave labour; information on the legal position of work-
ers and the protection accorded them by law ; information
on organizations formed by them to further their economic
interests (co-operative associations, trade unions, mutual
aid societies, etc.). Such information as we gather is to
be put at the disposal of the International Labour Office,
and is also to be published here in China.

As regards this bulletin, we also hope to print, from
time to time, information upon conditions in other coun-
tries which may be of relevance in consideration of certain
industries or occupations in China. We shall be grateful
to any who will give us their assistance in our work. The
Association, having no Government subsidy, is dependent
upon the voluntary work and contributions of its members
and of others sympathetic with its aims. Our first number
is small in size, and contains but one report, but we expect
to grow.

The Labour Research Association is open to all,
regardless of nationality, who agree with its aims as set
forth in its preamble. We welcome all who wish to
co-operate with us in this work.

THE LABOUR RESEARCH ASSOCIATION OF CHINA.
page_data.zh:
— 3 —

关于工厂和作坊、农场和矿山、商店以及家庭服务业中工人的状况；关于雇主与雇员之间关系的信息，无论是固定工资劳动、计件工作、合同劳动还是奴役劳动；关于工人的法律地位及法律给予他们的保护的信息；关于他们为促进自身经济利益而组建的组织（合作社、工会、互助会等）的信息。我们收集到的此类信息将提供给国际劳工局，并在中国这里出版。

关于本公报，我们也希望不时刊登有关其他国家状况的信息，这些信息在考量中国某些行业或职业时可能具有相关性。我们将感激任何在工作中给予我们协助的人。本协会没有政府补贴，依靠其成员及其他同情本协会目标的人士的志愿工作和捐款。我们的第一期篇幅较小，仅包含一份报告，但我们期望未来能有所发展。

劳工研究协会向所有赞同其序言中所述宗旨的人开放，不分国籍。我们要欢迎所有希望在此项工作中与我们合作的人。

中国劳工研究协会。

CONSTITUTION
OF THE
LABOUR RESEARCH ASSOCIATION OF CHINA

ARTICLE I (Purpose)
Recognizing that peace, internally and internationally, can be maintained only if based upon social justice, and that in the realization of better and juster social conditions it is of fundamental importance to gather and to distribute information on all subjects relating to existing conditions of labour and industrial life; and for the purpose of gathering such information in China and putting same at the disposal of the International Labour Office created by the Treaty of Versailles in 1919; and further for the purpose of publishing such information, both with regard to China and other countries, in bulletin form at regular intervals here; we, the undersigned, form hereby the Labour Research Association of China.

ARTICLE II (Membership)
Section 1.—Anyone who subscribes to the aims of the Labour Research Association of China, as set forth in Article I of this Constitution, and who is proposed by a member in good standing or the Association, shall be eligible to membership upon payment of initiation fee.
Section 2.—An entrance or initiation fee of Mex. $2.00 shall be paid by each member of the Association, and regular dues of $6.00 yearly. The membership fee for workers and students of low income shall be $2.00 yearly, and no initiation fee shall be charged.
Section 3.—In case any member of the Association is found to be working against the objects of the Association

第一条（宗旨）
认识到只有基于社会正义，才能维持内部及国际和平；而在实现更好、更公正的社会条件方面，收集和传播有关现有劳工状况及工业生活各方面信息具有根本重要性；为了在中国收集此类信息并将其提供给1919年《凡尔赛条约》所设立的国际劳工局；并为了定期在此以公报形式发布有关中国及其他国家的此类信息；我们，下列签署人，特此成立中国劳工研究协会。
