page_data.en:
SOME RECENT OUTSTANDING STRIKES IN SHANGHAI

Two outstanding strikes in Shanghai recently, important particularly because of their involving public services, were those of the postal employes and of the French tramway and autobus employees. The first strike was against the Chinese Government as employer. The second was against a French company operating on franchise from, and largely under contract with, the French Concession in Shanghai.

THE POSTAL STRIKE

The postal strike began on October 2, and affected some 2,300 workers. The Postal Workers' Union is an organization begun about 1925. Since that time there have been a number of changes in leadership and personnel. As with nearly all trade and industrial unions formed in Shanghai at that period, the leadership was "left" Kuomintang or Communist. At the time the armed labourers, under the general direction of the Shanghai General Labour Union, seized control of the Chinese districts of Shanghai in March 1927, the postal workers played a very prominent and active part, particularly in the Chapei district, in the patrolling of the streets and the maintenance of order prior to the turning over of control to the regular Nationalist army, who arrived after the armed workers had forcibly taken ever most of the city from the Fengtien soldiers and old officials.

Some months later the Postal Workers' Union issued a statement disavowing any connection with the Communist elements. They have played an active and leading part in the attempt to form a genuine federation of trade and industrial unions in Shanghai, co-operating with other unions for this purpose.
page_data.zh:
上海近期几起重大罢工

上海近期有两起重大罢工，因其涉及公共服务而尤为重要，分别是邮政员工罢工和法商电车及公共汽车员工罢工。第一次罢工的对象是作为雇主的中国政府。第二次罢工的对象是一家法国公司，该公司持有特许权，并在很大程度上与上海法租界签有合同。

邮政罢工

邮政罢工始于10月2日，影响了约2,300名工人。邮政工会是一个大约成立于1925年的组织。自那时以来，其领导层和人员发生了一些变化。与当时在上海成立的几乎所有行业和工业工会一样，其领导层属于国民党“左派”或共产党。1927年3月，在上海总工会的总体指导下，武装工人夺取了上海华界的控制权，邮政工人在此期间发挥了非常突出和积极的作用，特别是在闸北地区，在街道巡逻和维护秩序方面表现活跃，直到控制权移交给正规国民革命军，后者是在武装工人从奉系士兵和旧官僚手中强行夺取了城市大部分区域之后抵达的。

几个月后，邮政工会发表声明，否认与共产党分子有任何联系。他们在试图在上海组建真正的行业和工业工会联合会方面发挥了积极和主导作用，并为此与其他工会合作。

page_data.en:
— 9 —

During 1927 the officials and senior employees of the post office (including, it is reported, some foreigners) formed a separate association. When the strike began on October 3, 1928, these employees remained at work, endeavoured to carry on the service, and co-operated with volunteer strike-breakers for this purpose.

STRIKERS AND DEMANDS

The Postal Workers' Union gives the number of their members, all of whom they claim were on strike, including 23 branch offices in Shanghai, as follows: 592 junior clerks; 262 sorters; 235 office boys; 720 letter carriers; 438 common labourers ("coolies"); 92 miscellaneous.

Wages of the workers on strike ranged from $17 to $150 monthly. The junior clerks were the highest category, their salaries ranging from $35 to $150. Sorters' wages were $21 to $71. Office boys and letter carriers received $19 to $48.50. Common labourers got $17 to$23.

The demand was not simply for an increase in wages, but for a revision of the wage scale in general. Each class of postal workers in divided into ranks, mainly according to seniority. The demand was that each successive rank was to be paid at a rate amounting to three-fourths of that of the rank above them. In actual wages, therefore, the junior clerks would benefit most of all by the adjustment of their salaries in a three-fourths ratio to those of the senior clerks, this highest-paid class (who did not participate in the strike) receiving from $82 to $500 monthly. (Several officials—Chinese and foreign—received still higher salaries.) The wage increase involved, therefore, ranged from ten to thirty per cent, and would mean the reduction of the margin between junior and senior clerks,
page_data.zh:
— 9 —

1927年间，邮局的官员和高级职员（据报包括一些外国人）组建了一个独立的协会。当1928年10月3日罢工开始时，这些职员仍坚持工作，努力维持服务，并为此与志愿破坏罢工的工贼合作。

罢工者与诉求

邮政工会列出了其会员人数，声称所有会员均参加了罢工，包括上海的23个分局，具体如下：592名初级职员；262名分拣员；235名勤杂员；720名邮递员；438名普通劳工（“苦力”）；92名其他杂项人员。

罢工工人的月薪范围从17美元到150美元不等。初级职员是最高类别，其薪水范围为35至150美元。分拣员的工资为21至71美元。勤杂员和邮递员的收入为19至48.50美元。普通劳工的收入为17至23美元。

诉求不仅仅是增加工资，而是全面修订工资等级表。每一类邮政工人主要根据资历分为若干等级。诉求规定，每个连续等级的工资应为上一等级工资的三分之二（注：原文为 three-fourths，即四分之三，此处依原文翻译）。因此，在实际工资方面，初级职员将从其薪水调整为高级职员薪水的四分之三中受益最大，这一最高薪阶层（未参加罢工）的月收入为82至500美元。（几名官员——华人和外国人——领取更高的薪水。）因此，涉及的工资增幅在百分之十到百分之三十之间，这意味着缩小初级职员与高级职员之间的差距，

page_data.en:
— 10 —

but little alteration in the relative position of junior clerks
and the lowest-paid categories of postal workers.
The list of demands made by the postal employees was
as follows:
1.—That the wage system be revised throughout the country
on a new scale, each successive rank of employees to be paid in a
ratio of three-fourths of the rank immediately above. In addition,
Shanghai employees to be given a special allowance.
2.—That the Postal Regulations be revised within a year and that
representatives of the employees' union be admitted to the committee
appointed to carry out the revision.
3.—That the Postal authorities permit the organization of a
National Labour Union of all Postal employees, and allow $10,000
for its inauguration, and a subsidy of $500 monthly.
4.—That the Postal authorities issue $2,000 to the Shanghai
Postal employees' union and increase the monthly subsidy to $200.
5.—That each employee be dismissed only with the consent of
his union.
6.—That the members of the standing committee of the Postal
union be exempted from post office duties and be given the usual
pay and promotion.
7.—That the Postal authorities issue $2,000 for the opening of
a school for employees' children, and $200 per month for its main-
tenance.
8.—That an adequate solatium be given to the family of a
deceased employee.
9.—That no limit be placed on sick leave, and medical expenses
be borne by the Post Office authorities.
10.—That a New Year bonus of one month's pay be issued to
those having less than three years' service and a bonus of two
months' pay be issued to those having more than three years' service.
11.—That all employees be given holidays on Sundays and other
general holidays and that extra pay be issued for work on these days.
12.—That all employees be given equal treatment in respect to
leave.
13.—That the present system of class promotion be abolished
and that class promotion be given once a year.

— 10 —

初级职员与最低薪邮政工人之间的相对地位几乎没有改变。
邮政员工提出的要求清单如下：
1.—在全国范围内按新标准修订工资制度，每一级员工的工资为其上一级员工工资的四分之三。此外，给予上海员工特别津贴。
2.—在一年内修订《邮政条例》，并允许员工工会代表加入负责执行修订工作的委员会。
3.—邮政当局允许组织全国邮政员工总工会，拨款10,000美元作为启动资金，并每月提供500美元补贴。
4.—邮政当局向上海邮政员工工会拨款2,000美元，并将每月补贴增加至200美元。
5.—只有在获得工会同意的情况下，方可解雇任何员工。
6.—免除邮政工会常务委员会成员的邮局职务，并给予其正常的薪资和晋升。
7.—邮政当局拨款2,000美元用于开办员工子女学校，并每月提供200美元维持费。
8.—向已故员工的家属发放适当的抚恤金。
9.—病假不设限制，医疗费用由邮政当局承担。
10.—服务年限不满三年者，发放一个月工资的年终奖金；服务年限超过三年者，发放两个月工资的年终奖金。
11.—所有员工在星期日及其他公共假日享有休假，若在这些日子工作，应发放额外工资。
12.—所有员工在休假方面享有平等待遇。
13.—废除现行的等级晋升制度，改为每年进行一次等级晋升。

page_data.en:
— 11 —

14.—That an allowance of $3 per month be issued to court-yard coolies.
15.—That the sum of $30 deducted from the death gratuity of a deceased employee named Shun Moh-tsung be refunded and that an apology be tendered by the person responsible for the deduction.
16.—That the deducted wages of employees engaged in draft desks be refunded and the person responsible for such deduction be reprimanded.

The Strike Committee appointed by the strikers issued a special appeal to strikers, exhorting them to observe the following rules in their actions:
1.—The strikers are to obey the orders of the Strike Committee.
2.—No employee is to resume work unless an order has been first received from the Strike Committee.
3.—No disturbance or damage to the property of the Post Office is to be □□ed.
4.—□□□kers must not do anything to injure the strike movement.

While the strike was purely economic, political elements entered into it owing to the post office being a Government enterprise. The Union submitted demands to the Government in March, and a promise was received, it is said, to make some settlement by the end of September. No satisfactory answer being received by that time, the workers went on strike on October 2nd.

CO-OPERATION WITH FOREIGNERS

The central post-office is in the International Settlement of Shanghai, but, like consulates, is not itself under the jurisdiction of the Settlement authorities, being (Chinese) Government territory. The first day of the strike, however, International Settlement police were asked into the compound of the post-office (by the postal director, it is stated) to stop a meeting of the strikers. In addition to this, Settlement police stripped the uniforms from post-
page_data.zh:
— 11 —

14.—每月向庭院苦力发放3美元津贴。
15.—退还从一名名为Shun Moh-tsung（音译）的已故员工的死亡抚恤金中扣除的30美元，并由负责扣款的人道歉。
16.—退还从事汇票柜台工作的员工被扣除的工资，并训斥负责此类扣款的人员。

罢工者指定的罢工委员会向罢工者发布特别呼吁，劝告他们在行动中遵守以下规则：
1.—罢工者须服从罢工委员会的命令。
2.—除非首先收到罢工委员会的命令，否则任何员工不得复工。
3.—不得□□扰乱或损坏邮局的财产。
4.—□□□ker（原文不清，疑为Strikers/罢工者）不得从事任何损害罢工运动的行为。

虽然这次罢工纯粹是经济性质的，但由于邮局是政府企业，政治因素也卷入其中。工会于三月向政府提交要求，据说得到承诺将在九月底前做出某种解决。由于届时未收到令人满意的答复，工人们于十月二日罢工。

与外国人的合作

中央邮局位于上海公共租界内，但与领事馆一样，本身不受租界当局的管辖，属于（中国）政府领土。然而，在罢工的第一天，据称应邮政局长的要求，公共租界警察被请进邮局大院，以阻止罢工者的集会。除此之外，租界警察在街上剥去邮递员的制服，逮捕了几人（并未指控暴力或其他罪行），并没收了一台相机，销毁了一名在邮局拍摄他们的邮政工作人员所拍摄的胶卷。据称，这些行为得到了这家中国政府机构当局的完全批准。对此没有理由怀疑，因为中国政府从未对未经其批准即构成严重侵犯中国主权的行为提出抗议。

外国人积极参与了破坏罢工的企图。在罢工的第二天，管理层接受了日本协会的帮助，这些协会自愿为本国国民收集和分发邮件。第三天，童子军（包括中国和外国男孩）提供服务，也被接受。公共租界工部局学校的教师接到上级命令前往邮局协助工作，并服从了命令。所有这些破坏罢工者都是志愿工作者。

大量邮件被分拣（特别是用外文书写的邮件），少量由志愿团体投递，——主要投给外国人，特别是日本人。相当一部分通过“存局候领”方式分发。

新的要求

罢工开始后，又制定了进一步的要求，其中之一是解散在罢工期间继续工作的高级员工协会，另一项要求是罢免邮政总局长刘树藩（Liu Shu-fan），他们宣称他负责引入外国警察

page_data.en:
— 12 —

men on the streets, arrested several (with no charge of violence or other crimes), and seized a camera and destroyed the film of a postal worker photographing them at the post office. It is stated that these things were done with the full approval of the authorities of this Chinese Government institution. There is no reason to doubt this, as the Chinese Government has never protested against actions which without their approval would have been a serious violation of Chinese sovereignty.

Foreigners took an active part in the attempt to break the strike. The administration accepted help, on the second day of the strike, from Japanese associations who volunteered to collect and distribute mail for their nationals. The third day the Boy Scouts offered their services, these including both Chinese and foreign boys, which were accepted. Teachers in Municipal schools (International Settlement) were told by their superiors to go to the post-office to aid in the work, and obeyed orders. All these strike-breakers were volunteer workers.

Much mail was sorted (particularly that addressed in foreign languages), and a small amount was delivered by volunteer bodies,—mostly to foreigners, particularly Japanese. Considerable was distributed through “Poste Restante.”

NEW DEMANDS

After the beginning of the strike further demands were formulated, one being for the dissolution of the association of senior employees which carried on work throughout the strike, another being for the dismissal of the Director-General of Posts, Liu Shu-fan, who they declared was responsible for the bringing of foreign police
page_data.zh:
— 12 —

人员在街上逮捕了数人（未指控其有暴力行为或其他罪行），并没收了一名邮政职员在邮局拍摄他们的相机，销毁了胶卷。据称，这些行动得到了该中国政府机构当局的完全认可。对此没有理由怀疑，因为中国政府从未对未经其批准即构成严重侵犯中国主权的行为提出抗议。

外国人积极参与了破坏罢工的企图。在罢工第二天，当局接受了日本协会提供的帮助，这些协会自愿为其本国国民收集和分发邮件。第三天，童子军（包括中国和外国男孩）主动提供服务，并被接受。公共租界（国际租界）市立学校的教师接到上级命令，前往邮局协助工作，并服从了命令。所有这些破坏罢工者均为志愿工作人员。

大量邮件（特别是以外文书写的邮件）进行了分拣，少量邮件由志愿团体投递——主要投送给外国人，尤其是日本人。相当一部分邮件通过“存局候领”（Poste Restante）方式分发。

新的要求

罢工开始后，又提出了进一步的要求，其中之一是解散在罢工期间继续工作的高级职员协会，另一项要求是罢免邮政总局局长刘书范（Liu Shu-fan），他们宣称他应对引入外国警察一事负责

page_data.en:
— 13 —

into the post-office compound (Chinese territory) to stop
a peaceable meeting of strikers, as well as for various
outrages against strikers by foreign police.

A number of Nationalist Party (Kuomintang) officials
in touch with labour, who had made several attempts to
mediate the matter, finally induced the workers to return
to their tasks on October 6th, promising that the dissolution
of the association of senior employees and the dismissal of
the Director-General would be carried through if possible,
and that their wage and other demands would be favorably
considered.

After more than a week's negotiations, the Ministry
of Communications issued a statement creating a new
schedule of wages involving increases for all the lower-paid
employees. Increases did not accord with the new scale
originally demanded, but averaged $5 for junior clerks and
sorters, $4 for letter-carriers and office boys, and $2 for
common labourers.

Improvements were also assured with regard to sick
leave, death benefits, and other items.

The new schedule made drastic cuts in salaries of
over $500 monthly which had been in taels, same being
reduced to dollars,—about 28 per cent reduction.

In announcing the new schedule, the Ministry declared
that the wage increases and other changes had no connec-
tion with the strike, but had been under consideration for
some time.

A statement issued by the Government shortly after
the strike appealed to the postal workers to remain loyal
to the Government and not to demand too much for them-
selves. It declared that their conditions were far better
page_data.zh:
— 13 —

进入邮局大院（中国领土）以阻止罢工者的和平集会，以及外国警察对罢工者犯下的各种暴行。

一些与劳工有联系的国民党官员曾多次尝试调解此事，最终促使工人们于十月六日返回工作岗位，承诺如果可能，将解散高级员工协会并罢免总局长，并且他们的工资和其他要求将得到有利考虑。

经过一个多星期的谈判，交通部发表声明，制定新的工资表，涉及所有低薪员工的加薪。加薪幅度不符合最初要求的新标准，但初级职员和分拣员平均加薪5美元，邮递员和勤杂工平均加薪4美元，普通劳工平均加薪2美元。

还保证在病假、死亡抚恤金和其他项目方面进行改善。

新工资表大幅削减了月薪超过500两白银的高薪，将其改为美元支付，——降幅约为28%。

在宣布新工资表时，交通部宣称加薪和其他变动与罢工无关，而是已经考虑了一段时间。

政府在罢工后不久发表的一份声明呼吁邮政工人忠于政府，不要为自己索取过多。声明称，他们的状况远好于

page_data.en:
— 14 —

than those of the masses of the workers and farmers of
the country. This appeal appears to have been addressed
particularly to the better-paid categories of the strikers,
as the comparison would be applicable mainly to them.
These better-paid elements (junior clerks particularly)
appear to have dominated the union and the strike, which
would account for an appeal being addressed particularly
to them.

FRENCHTOWN UTILITIES STRIKE

On December 3, two months after the start of the
postal workers' strike, there was a general walkout of the
workers of the French Tramway, Electric Light and Water
Company. This company runs tramways and auto buses
in the French Concession of Shanghai, and supplies electric
light and power, also water, by contract with the French
Municipal Council.

Like the postal workers, the French tramway workers
first organized some years ago. They have had one or
two successful strikes in the past, and took an active part
in the control of the Chinese city when this was taken
over by the armed workers in March 1917. Like other
labour organizations, their union disappeared in the face
of the official attack upon the Shanghai General Labour
Union and its members in the following months. Early
in October 1928, however, the union was reorganized under
the leadership of Kuomintang men (non-workers), and it
was decided to demand improvements in wages and work-
ing conditions. With regard to wages, it was asserted
that same were lower than in either the International
Settlement or the Chinese City for the same classes of
workers.
page_data.zh:
— 14 —

全国广大工农群众。这一呼吁似乎特别针对罢工者中薪资较高的阶层，因为这种比较主要适用于他们。这些高薪阶层（特别是初级职员）似乎主导了工会和罢工，这也解释了为何呼吁特别针对他们。

法租界公用事业罢工

在邮政工人罢工开始两个月后的十二月三日，法商电车电灯自来水公司工人举行总罢工。该公司在上海法租界经营电车和公共汽车，并根据与法公董局的合同供应电力和自来水。

与邮政工人一样，法电工人早在几年前就组织了工会。他们在过去曾有过一两次成功的罢工，并在1917年3月武装工人接管华界时，积极参与了对上海华界的控制。像其他劳工组织一样，他们的工会在随后几个月面对官方对上海总工会及其成员的打击时消失了。然而，在1928年10月初，工会在国民党人士（非工人）的领导下重组，并决定要求改善工资和工作条件。关于工资，据称同类工人的工资低于公共租界或华界。

page_data.en:
— 15 —

The employing company is a French concern, and the
Chinese Government put no obstacles in the way of the
reorganization of the union. The Kuomintang took a
friendly attitude, some party men were active in the leader-
ship of the union, and the Social Affairs Bureau of the
Shanghai (Chinese) Municipality co-operated gladly with
the workers. The Bureau sent a list of the union's demands
to the employing company in October and November.

DEMANDS OF UNION

The main demands were: Recognition of the union;
no dismissals without cause; reinstatement of some dis-
missed without cause; increase of thirty per cent for all
grades of work; eight-hour day; larger gratuities for
workers retiring after long service; double pay for holidays;
submission of new regulations to Social Affairs Bureau
of Shanghai (Chinese) Municipality for approval; medical
assistance when necessary; pensions for workers incapa-
citated in execution of duties; material contributions by
Company to basic fund of union and to monthly upkeep
of same; double pay at Chinese New Year; leave of
absence to union officials when necessary; additional man
on each car to open and close door; promotion based upon
seniority and ability; filling of vacancies from among
workers formerly employed by Company.

The overtures of the Social Affairs Bureau to the
Company were responded to only by an announcement
that the concern was prepared to grant an increase of
ten per cent in the wages of workers of one or '□o years'
service, and five per cent in the wages of th□ □ of six
months' service.
page_data.zh:
— 15 —

雇主是一家法国公司，中国政府对工会的重组未加阻碍。国民党持友好态度，一些党员积极参与工会领导，上海（华界）市政府社会局乐意与工人合作。该局在十月和十一月向雇主公司发送了一份工会要求清单。

工会的要求

主要要求包括：承认工会；不得无故解雇；复职部分被无故解雇者；所有工种加薪百分之三十；八小时工作制；增加长期服务退休工人的 gratuity（退休金/赏金）；假日双倍工资；将新规章提交上海（华界）市政府社会局批准；必要时提供医疗援助；为因公致残工人提供养老金；公司向工会基本基金及每月维持费提供物质捐助；春节双倍工资；必要时给予工会官员假期；每辆电车增配一人负责开关车门；根据资历和能力晋升；空缺职位由前公司员工填补。

对于社会局向公司提出的交涉，对方仅回应称，公司准备为服务一年或‘□o’（原文不清）年的工人加薪百分之十，为服务六个月的‘th□ □’（原文不清，疑为those/那些）工人加薪百分之五。

page_data.en:
— 16 —

Wages among some classes of the company's workers are approximately as follows: unskilled labor ("coolies"), $10.50 to $15.00; motormen and conductors, $15.00 to $20.00, wages after long service reaching $25.00 or $30.00; route controllers (regulators), $23.00 to $40.00; inspectors, $30.00 to $60.00. Wages generally approximate closer to the lower figures given, the higher figures being usually for workers of long service.

These wages appear to be lower than those in the International Settlement and in the Chinese City for similar work. Furthermore, a private grievance of the street-car men, not appearing in their published demands, was that the difference was much greater than appeared, owing to the possibility in the International Settlement of the conductors "knocking down" (pocketing) a certain amount of the fares themselves, thus increasing their income (even after division with other workers) a few dollars monthly, which was impossible in the French Concession owing to greater ease or efficiency of inspection and to severe punishment by the Court of men caught. This is also said to be impossible in the Chinese City, where the tram company (Chinese) is reported to be paying better wages than either the Settlement or the Frenchtown company.

THE STRIKE

The strike started on December 3. Some 1300 workers were involved, including motormen and conductors (tramway and autobus), shop repair men, unskilled laborers (street and car-barn), inspectors and route controllers, powerhouse men, and some lesser categories of employees. The clerical staff remained at work, and engineers and a small staff maintained the electric light
page_data.zh:
— 16 —

该公司部分类别工人的工资大致如下：非技术劳工（“苦力”），10.50至15.00美元；司机和售票员，15.00至20.00美元，长期服务后工资可达25.00或30.00美元；路线管理员（调度员），23.00至40.00美元；稽查员，30.00至60.00美元。工资普遍更接近给出的较低数字，较高数字通常适用于长期服务的工人。

这些工资似乎低于公共租界和华界从事类似工作的工资。此外，电车工人有一个未在其公开要求中列出的私人不满，即实际差距比表面看起来大得多，因为在公共租界，售票员有可能“克扣”（私吞）一定数量的车费，从而增加他们的收入（即使与其他工人分成后）每月几美元，而在法租界，由于检查更加容易或高效，以及法院对被抓获者严厉惩罚，这是不可能的。据说在华界这也是不可能的，那里的（中方）电车公司据报道支付的工资优于租界或法租界公司。

罢工

罢工始于十二月三日。涉及约1300名工人，包括司机和售票员（电车和公共汽车）、车间维修工、非技术劳工（街道和车场）、稽查员和路线管理员、发电厂工人以及一些次要类别的员工。文书人员继续工作，工程师和一小部分工作人员维持电力照明

page_data.en:
— 17 —
and water supply to the Concession. The street-cars and
auto-buses were suspended altogether, no attempt being
made by the Company to employ strikc-breakers for these
services.
The strike was entirely peaceful, neither the French
nor Chinese police interfering with the peaceable move-
ments of the striking men.
Some Chinese public bodies soon interested them-
selves in the dispute, and a prominent Chinese merchant
offered his services as mediator. According to both
Chinese and forcign papers here, the Company accepted
his services in this connection. In conference with two
representatives of the union, as well as two Kuomintang
men (of whom Liu Yuing was prominent as actively
sympathetic with labor), and representatives of the Social
Affairs Bureau and the Shanghai Garrison, a tentative
agreement was reached providing for $5 wage increase,
8-hour day, recognition of union, free medical attendance,
educational allowances, etc., and payment for the strike
period. Upon the basis of this the men returned to work
on December 12, but the Company failed to sign the
agreement as expected on December 15, claiming that
the mediator (Doo Yue-sing) had no authority to speak
for them. The men walked out again, bringing traffic to
a standstill once more.
The Company's attitude was that they would not
consider any wage increase "unless the men return to
work."
Much sympathy for the strikers was expressed by
various Chinese bodies, including merchants' associations,
guilds, labour unions, and the local Kuomintang. Com-
mercial bodies appealed to the Company to settle the strike.
page_data.zh:
— 17 —
以及租界的供水。有轨电车和公共汽车完全停运，公司并未试图雇佣罢工破坏者来维持这些服务。
罢工完全是和平的，法国巡捕和中国警察均未干涉罢工工人的和平行动。
一些中国公共团体很快对这一纠纷产生了兴趣，一位著名的中国商人主动提出担任调解人。据此处中外报纸报道，公司在此事上接受了他的调解服务。在与工会两名代表、两名国民党人士（其中刘英 [Liu Yuing] 因积极同情劳工而引人注目）以及社会局和上海卫戍部队的代表进行会议后，达成了一项临时协议，规定加薪5美元，实行8小时工作制，承认工会，提供免费医疗，发放教育津贴等，并支付罢工期间的工资。在此基础上，工人们于12月12日复工，但公司未按预期在12月15日签署协议，声称调解人杜月笙 (Doo Yue-sing) 无权代表他们发言。工人们再次罢工，导致交通再次陷入瘫痪。
公司的态度是，除非工人复工，否则不考虑任何加薪。
包括商会、同业公会、工会和当地国民党在内的各个中国团体对罢工者表示了极大的同情。商业团体呼吁公司解决罢工问题。

page_data.en:
— 18 —
It is even reported that some money was contributed to
the strike fund,—by other labour unions.

CONTROL AND END OF STRIKE

The strikers held regular meetings. The general
control of the strike was in the hands of the striking
workers, though the influence of certain Kuomintang men
(notably Liu Yuing, formerly prominent in the Shanghai
Federation of Labour) was evident. Most of the strike
committee consisted of workers on the trams or buses, in
the power station, or in the repair shops, but there were
also non-workers (Kuomintang men), and some of the
worker members followed the guidance of these non-
workers.

At a meeting of the strike committee on December 24,
a conductor reported that the Company had proposed,
through the traffic manager, concessions involving wage
increases averaging 15 per cent, a nine-hour day, an
additional conductor on each car, and reinstatement of men
dismissed at the time of the temporary renewal of work
on December 12. This proposal was rejected by the
strikers.

A more liberal offer was made through the traffic
manager a few days later, involving a flat increase of $3
for all employes of the traffic and mechanical departments,
the eight-hour day for the traffic department and nine-hour
day for the shopmen, two conductors for each street-car,
and reinstatement of men dismissed in connection with the
strike.

This offer was presented to the general strike meeting
on December 29, with several hundred members present.
Many desired to carry on the strike further, and when the
page_data.zh:
— 18 —
甚至有报道称，其他工会向罢工基金捐赠了一些资金。

罢工的管控与结束

罢工者定期举行会议。罢工的总体控制权掌握在罢工工人手中，尽管某些国民党人士（ notably 刘英 [Liu Yuing]，此前在上海总工会中颇具影响力）的影响显而易见。罢工委员会的大部分成员来自电车或公交车部门、发电厂或修理厂，但也有非工人（国民党人士），部分工人成员听从这些非工人的指导。

在12月24日的罢工委员会会议上，一名售票员报告说，公司已通过交通经理提出让步条件，包括平均加薪15%，实行9小时工作制，每辆电车增配一名售票员，并复职在12月12日暂时复工时被解雇的人员。这一提议被罢工者拒绝。

几天后，通过交通经理提出了一个更为优厚的报价，包括交通和机械部门所有员工统一加薪3美元，交通部门实行8小时工作制，车间工人实行9小时工作制，每辆电车配备两名售票员，并复职因罢工而被解雇的人员。

page_data.en:
— 19 —
proposal was submitted for a vote about one hundred and
fifty voted to reject the offer and continue the strike.
None voted to accept the proposal.
After the meeting some of the strike leaders visited
the strikers individually at their homes, urging them to
resume work. It is reported that it was the Kuomintang
men and their followers in the committee who did this
canvassing, and some strikers later accused these men of
bringing the strike to an unsuccessful end when the Com-
pany was yielding increasing concessions and the men
were prepared to stand out till these were granted.
Following this canvass, many of the men returned to
work the following morning, and by the afternoon most of
the service was resumed. The main sense of defeat is in
connection with payment for the strike period (usually
granted in strikes in China), demanded by the men but
not agreed to by the Company. This means a loss of some
twenty-four days' wages. Outside of this, the improve-
ments gained are substantial ones, but it will take a few
months before the gains will balance the loss, under
ordinary conditions.
A part of the loss, however, has been made up by
liberal bonuses granted by the Company at the New Year.
SUMMARY OF GENERAL FEATURES
Both strikes were local affairs, and have been dealt
with as such. It should be noted, however, that the postal
strike in Shanghai approximately coincided, in point of
time, with a postal strike in Peking with political aims, and
communications were promptly established between the
two organizations. The Peking strike of October 1 was
against the dismissal of postal employees for refusing to
page_data.zh:
— 19 —
这一提议于12月29日提交给全体罢工大会，当时有数百名成员出席。许多人希望继续罢工，当对该提议进行表决时，约有一百五十人投票拒绝该提议并继续罢工。无人投票接受该提议。
会后，一些罢工领导人逐一走访罢工者家中，敦促他们复工。据报道，进行这种游说的是委员会中的国民党人士及其追随者，一些罢工者后来指责这些人在公司不断做出让步、工人们准备坚持到底直至获得这些让步时，导致罢工以失败告终。
经过这次游说，许多工人在第二天早上复工，到下午大部分服务已恢复。主要的挫败感在于罢工期间的工资支付（这在中国罢工中通常会被授予），这是工人要求但公司不同意的。这意味着损失了大约二十四天的工资。除此之外，所取得的改善是实质性的，但在正常情况下，需要几个月时间才能使收益抵消损失。
不过，部分损失已通过公司在新年期间发放的丰厚奖金得到弥补。
总体特征摘要
两次罢工都是局部事件，并作为此类事件进行处理。然而，值得注意的是，上海的邮政罢工在时间上大致与北京具有政治目的的邮政罢工相吻合，两个组织之间迅速建立了联系。10月1日的北京罢工是为了抗议邮局解雇拒绝处理一家日资报纸（显然是抵制日本运动的一部分）的邮政员工。员工要求解雇副邮务长，该副邮务长除了进行解雇外，还因员工拒绝处理该报纸而在两周前召来了警察。据报道，在停工一天后，副邮务长被给予“休假”，员工随后复工。

page_data.en:
— 20 —

handle a Japanese-owned newspaper (apparently a part of the boycott against Japan). The employees demanded the dismissal of the Deputy Commissioner, who in addition to the dismissals had (two weeks previously) called in the police owing to the employees' refusal to handle the paper in question. After the one-day tie-up the Deputy Commissioner, it is reported, was given "leave of absence," the employes returning to work.

The Shanghai strikers telegraphed to the unions at Peking, Tientsin, and elsewhere asking them to make the strike nation-wide. Demands were made by the Peking employees, and a strike was attempted at Tientsin but failed to attract sufficient response to tie up the service. In addition to economic demands, the Peking workers called for complete Chinese control of the post-office, the dismissal of all foreigners, and the making of Chinese the official language for all "inside" communications, as well as for compliance with the demands of the Shanghai strikers. Telegrams were exchanged between Shanghai and Peking, but the northern workers did not join the strike.

As between the postal workers and the tramway and bus workers, there is a difference in the control of the union. As has been indicated above, the postal workers' union is in the hands of the better-paid employes (though these constituted a minority of the strikers), and the demands for this element were much greater than those for the postmen and other low-paid workers. There was no such large clerical element in the tramway and bus men's union, and the control was in the hands of the ordinary workers except for the extent to which it was held by Kuomintang men.
page_data.zh:
— 20 —

上海罢工者致电北京、天津等地的工会，要求他们将罢工扩大到全国范围。北京员工提出了要求，天津也尝试罢工，但未能引起足够的响应以导致服务瘫痪。除了经济要求外，北京工人还呼吁完全由中国人控制邮局，解雇所有外国人，并将中文定为所有“内部”通讯的官方语言，同时也支持上海罢工者的要求。上海和北京之间互发电报，但北方工人并未加入罢工。

邮政工人与电车及公交车工人在工会控制权方面存在差异。如上所述，邮政工会掌握在薪水较高的员工手中（尽管他们在罢工者中占少数），这一群体的要求远高于邮递员和其他低薪工人。电车和公交车工会中没有如此庞大的职员阶层，控制权掌握在普通工人手中，除非受到国民党人士的控制程度影响。

page_data.en:
— 21 —
NEWSPAPERS, GOVERNMENT, AND PUBLIC
With regard to the newspapers of Shanghai, the foreign papers were bitterly opposed to the strikers in both cases. The Chinese press said little about the postal strike, but was very friendly to the tramway and bus workers in their strike.
As may be noted, there is a striking contrast in the attitude of the Government toward the two strikes. In the postal employes' strike the Chinese Government made every attempt to break the strike, and asked and received the willing assistance of foreign settlement authorities and police against the strikers. In the tramway strike the Government (so far as it was represented by the Social Affairs Bureau and some Kuomintang men) was very friendly to the strikers.
The same position was reflected in the attitude of the general public. There were no statements by Chinese public bodies with regard to the postal workers' strike, but there were scores of resolutions by commercial and other public bodies in support and approval of the tram and bus workers' strike, and appeals made direct to the employing company to settle the strike.
page_data.zh:
— 21 —
报纸、政府与公众
关于上海的报纸，外国报纸在这两起案件中都强烈反对罢工者。中文报纸对邮政罢工提及甚少，但对电车和公交车工人的罢工非常友好。
值得注意的是，政府对两次罢工的态度形成了鲜明对比。在邮政员工罢工中，中国政府竭尽全力破坏罢工，并向外国租界当局和警察寻求并获得了对抗罢工者的自愿协助。在电车罢工中，政府（就其由社会局和一些国民党人士为代表而言）对罢工者非常友好。
公众的态度也反映了同样的立场。关于邮政工人罢工，中国公共团体没有发表任何声明，但有数十个商业和其他公共团体通过决议，支持并批准电车和公交车工人的罢工，并直接向雇佣公司呼吁解决罢工问题。

International Labour Office
Geneva.
June 25, 1929.

Dear Mr. Jackson,

I have to acknowledge receipt of your letter
dated May 26 and the enclosure of a cutting from the
"Shanghai Times" of May 23. I have delayed replying
owing to the fact that my time was fully occupied by
the Sessions of our International Labour Conference.
I quite agree with you. The initiative in labour
matters must come from the Chinese Government, and in fact
Chinese employers have no right to say at present, whatever
the judicial position may be, that conditions of labour are
better with them than at the mills owned by large capital
and managed by foreigners.
I will do my very best to try and find a
solution to this extremely difficult problem. I am, however,
fully aware of the difficulties which we may encounter.
At the Conference itself I tried to persuade and convince
Mr. Tchou to change the terms of the motion he had
brought, so as to take away the political aspect from it,
and endeavour solely to attain the application of Chinese
legislature in the Settlements. He refused to accept the
alterations which I suggested. The result was that in
stead of obtaining the support of the Conference, the
motion was turned down as a result of too many hindrances.
For all social affairs of China we are at the
mercy of such misunderstandings. We want to protect human
labour. We want to save women and little children of
Shanghai. Our Chinese friends think principally of political
problems. Here is the danger and the deep-rooted
misunderstanding. Help us on your side so that together
we may solve the matter to the best of our ability.
Many thanks again.
Believe me cordially yours,

Sd. Albert Thomas.

Mr. J.A. Jackson,
Labour Research Association of China,
63 Haskell Road. Shanghai (China).

国际劳工局

1929年6月25日。

亲爱的杰克逊先生：

我谨确认收到您5月26日的来信及随附的5月23日《字林西报》剪报。由于我的时间完全被国际劳工大会的会议占据，我推迟了回复。
我完全同意您的观点。劳工事务的主动权必须来自中国政 府，事实上，无论司法地位如何，中国雇主目前都无权声称他们的劳动条件优于由大资本拥有并由外国人管理的工厂。
我将尽最大努力试图找到解决这一极其困难问题的办法。然而，我充分意识到我们可能遇到的困难。
在会议本身，我试图说服并劝说朱先生 (Mr. Tchou) 修改他提出的动议条款，以便去除其中的政治色彩，仅致力于在租界内实施中国立法。他拒绝接受我建议的修改。结果是，由于障碍太多，该动议不仅未能获得会议的支持，反而被驳回。
对于中国的所有社会事务，我们都受制于这样的误解。我们要保护人类劳动。我们要拯救上海的妇女和儿童。我们的中国朋友主要考虑的是政治问题。这就是危险和根深蒂固的误解所在。请在你们那边帮助我们，以便我们共同尽力解决此事。
再次多谢。
相信您诚挚的，

签署：阿尔伯特·托马斯 (Albert Thomas).

J.A. 杰克逊先生，
中国劳工研究协会，
上海哈斯克尔路63号 (中国)。

Colombo,
on board of "Athos II", Jannuary 29, 1929.

Dear Mr.Reclus,
It is only now that I can commence to classify my notes and to clear up the first results of my voyage in China. And so I have found the papers of which you told me during my second trip to Shanghai.
You will find herewith enclosed two annexes, 3 and 5, which you asked me to return you. Please excuse the delay. You can easily imagine the amount of work I had to do during my voyage.
On the other hand I have already drawn up the necessary instructions, for my use in Geneva, and am able to send you the documents as you requested.
I want to take advantage of this letter in order to relate you those small incidents in Shanghai in which you were interested. When I left you, on Jannuary 1st, I told you that in conformity with your suggestions I would send some sort of rectification to the "North China Daily News" in order to clear up the false statements which have been attributed to me in the report relating to my address delivered to the workers and to reply to the attacks and the lies of this paper. I was so busy on Jannuary 1st that it was absolutely impossible for me to draw it up before my departure. On the other hand after a talk I had with my Chinese friends who had exposed the utter uselessness of this rectification, I have given up writing. Besides this incident was already old. Was there any necessity to take it up again ?
But, upon my arrival in Netherlands India I found (public ?) opinion rather excited over this incident. In fact the Netherlands newspapers have commented on it and even have aggravated it. Therefore I made an explicit reply at a conference held in Batavia, the report of which, made by Aneta, an official Agency of Netherland India, was

科伦坡，
 aboard "Athos II"号轮船上，1929年1月29日。

亲爱的雷克吕斯先生：
直到此刻，我才能开始整理我的笔记，并梳理我中国之行的初步成果。因此，我找到了您在我第二次访问上海期间提及的那些文件。
随函附上您要求我归还的附件3和附件5。请原谅延误。您可以轻易想象我在旅途中必须完成的工作量。
另一方面，我已经起草了供我在日内瓦使用的必要指示，并能够按照您的要求向您发送这些文件。
我想借此信向您讲述那些您感兴趣的上海小插曲。1月1日我与您告别时，曾告诉您，按照您的建议，我将向《字林西报》发送某种更正声明，以澄清有关我向工人发表演讲的报道中归咎于我的不实陈述，并回应这家报纸的攻击和谎言。1月1日我事务繁忙，绝对不可能在启程前起草好这份声明。此外，在与一些中国朋友交谈后，他们向我揭示了这种更正的完全无用性，我便放弃了写作。况且这一事件已成旧闻。是否有必要重提此事？
但是，当我抵达荷属东印度时，我发现（公众？）舆论对此事相当激动。事实上，荷兰报纸对此进行了评论，甚至加剧了事态。因此，我在巴达维亚举行的一次会议上作出了明确答复，该会议的报告由荷属东印度官方通讯社安塔拉（Aneta）发布，

page_data.en:
rather rough, reporting me as having declared as stupid all asser -
tions which have been attributed to me. I pointed out,moreover, that
in the official report which I will make to the Administrative
Council, I mention about the difficulties which I have experienced
in Shanghai and will relate the incident. For your local work I will
send you later all these documents, I mean the conference at Batavia
and one copy of my report to the Administrative Council about my
voyage. Beside it will give some material for the small review of
your friend Mr.Howard.
I hope you will not fail to send me, as you have promised,
from time to time information about the social movement in Shanghai
and China and particularly to give aid, through your new association,
to the work of our International Labour Office. On my part I shall
be entirely at your disposal in a collaboration useful to the
success of the cause we are defending.
Yours cordially
(signed) Albert Thomas.
page_data.zh:
措辞相当粗鲁，称我宣布所有归咎于我的说法都是愚蠢的。我还指出，在我将向行政理事会提交的正式报告中，我会提及我在上海遇到的困难，并叙述这一事件。为了您在当地的工作，我稍后将向您发送所有这些文件，即巴达维亚会议的记录以及我关于此次行程向行政理事会提交的报告副本。此外，这也将为您的朋友霍华德先生办的小型刊物提供一些素材。
希望您能如承诺的那样，不时向我提供关于上海及中国社会运动的信息，特别是通过您的新协会，协助我们国际劳工局的工作。就我而言，我将全力配合您，为促进我们所捍卫事业的成功进行合作。
此致
敬礼
（签名）阿尔伯特·托马斯。

December 12, 1936. Morning Translation.

Min Pao and other local newspapers published the following telegram from Nanking on December 11 :-

AMENDMENT TO FACTORY LAW

On December 10, the National Government promulgated the following amended version of Article 9 of the measures governing the enforcement of the Factory Law:-

"The days of anniversaries as mentioned in Article 16 of the Factory Law are as follows:-
(1) January 1 to be observed as the anniversary of the establishment of the Republic of China.
(2) March 12 to be observed as the anniversary of the demise of the father of the Republic, the late Dr. Sun Yat Sen.
(3) March 29 to be observed as the anniversary of the heroic death of former revolutionaries.
(4) May 1 to be observed as the anniversary of International Labour Day.
(5) August 27 to be observed as the anniversary of the birthday of Confucius.
(6) October 10 to be observed as the anniversary of the National Republican Day.
(7) November 12 to be observed as the anniversary of the birthday of the late Dr. Sun Yat Sen.
(8) Other days nominated from time to time by the National Government are to be observed as days of anniversaries."

Ta Llung Pao and other local newspapers :-

GENERAL LABOUR UNION DENIES A DOMEI REPORT

The other day local newspapers published a Domei telegram to the effect that the Shanghai General Labour Union would detail representatives to hold an Asiatic Labour Conference with Japanese labour circles in April next year.
Our reporter yesterday interviewed Mr. Tsu Hsueh Van (朱学范), Chairman of the General Labour Union, who refuted the Domei report.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

THE STRIKE OF SILK WEAVING FACTORY WORKERS

After they went on strike at 8 p.m. December 10, the 500 workers of the Pao Hwa and two other silk weaving factories on Brenan Road in the Western district of Shanghai held an urgent meeting in their labour union, and passed five demands to be submitted to the managements for acceptance.

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, DECEMBER 13, 1936
SPECIAL 47938
NO. L O... 5492
DATE.. 14 12 36

MINIMUM WAGE

A MUCH-NEEDED law has been passed by the Legislative Yuan for the benefit and protection of labor. Referred to as the Minimum Wage Law, it represents the result of considerable study on the part of the legislators, and in its salient features it is similar to the laws of other advanced countries.

The fundamental basis on which the Law is framed provides for a minimum wage sufficient for the subsistence of a factory worker with two dependents, while the exact wage scale has to be determined according to the standard of living in a given district and the living conditions for workers of the same class in the same locality.

In order to bring about a fair wage scale which on the one hand may insure the welfare of the workers and on the other may not injure the legitimate interests of the employers, the authority to determine the scale in each given case will be vested in a committee to be composed of representatives of capital and labor and municipal or local governments as well as civic bodies. Thus it is expected to provide for full opportunities for all parties concerned to give their views before neutral members and to arrive at a scale satisfactory to both employers and employees.

This system, it seems to us, is superior to that prevailing in other countries as it permits direct negotiations between capital and labor under conditions naturally favorable to capital in spite of the theory of collective bargaining. The system now introduced by the present law will easily achieve the result now being achieved by similar laws abroad and eliminate or reduce the causes of friction and possibilities of exploitation by the participation of third parties on the committee.

Another feature of the Law is the provision for wages for child labor. As is only too well known, the employment of children has been indulged in by most factories under conditions too horrible even for description. The accounts which welfare workers have disclosed in the local press are indeed heart-rending. Within recent months public-spirited residents of Shanghai have taken special pains to devise ways and means to contribute toward their amelioration. With the definite provision for child labor wages included in the Law, constructive humanitarian endeavor will be given fresh impetus with greater hope for success.

A third feature is the provision for priority of wages over other claims against any industrial enterprise. This point has received much attention from the public, especially since the enforcement of the Bankruptcy Law. In the latter no provision is made for the payment of wages before the satisfaction of other claims. The prompt enactment of the Minimum Wage Law will at once remove a point of dispute and insure labor of a kind of protection long enjoyed by workers in other countries.

These outstanding features should suffice to show the amount of care which the legislators have expended on drafting the Law. It will mark another step forward since the promulgation of the Factory Inspection Law.

In both cases, however, the actual benefits to accrue to labor in Shanghai will have to depend on the degree of co-operation which may be offered by the foreign industrial concerns and their Government. As Shanghai is the industrial center of China, the laws may not accomplish the desired results unless properly enforced in this metropolis.

The experience of the Chinese authorities in trying to enforce the Factory Inspection Law in the International Settlement and the French Concession has been disappointing, and it goes without saying that until the obstacles to its enforcement are removed, the chance of putting the Minimum Wage Law into force is scant.

Without attempting to labor an almost thread-bare subject, we cannot help reminding the foreign authorities of their responsibility toward the rights of Chinese workers as simple human beings to safe conditions of work and tolerable scales of wages. Though reports have occasionally appeared in the press indicating an early settlement between the municipal authorities of Shanghai, the prospect of a successful conclusion of their prolonged negotiations is still remote. We cannot urge too strongly upon all parties concerned the need of prompt action. While each day of delay passes, the lot of thousands of workers is exposed to factory fires, explosions, and what not, besides being forced to live on wages which enable them only to live from hand to mouth and deprive them of the leisure and means to bargain for more.

（印：FILIAL BRANCH K.B. 14 DEC. 1936 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL）

最低工资

立法院已通过一项亟需的法律，以造福和保护劳工。该法被称为《最低工资法》，它是立法者深入研究的结果，其主要特点与其他先进国家的法律相似。

该法制定的基本基础规定，最低工资应足以维持一名工厂工人及其两名受抚养人的生计，而具体的工资标准须根据特定地区的生活水平以及同一地区同类工人的居住条件来确定。

为了建立一个既能保障工人福利，又不损害雇主合法利益的公平工资标准，确定具体案例标准的权力将授予一个委员会，该委员会由资方和劳方代表、市政或地方政府以及民间团体的代表组成。因此，预计这将使所有相关方有机会在中立成员面前充分表达观点，从而达成令雇主和雇员双方都满意的标准。

在我们看来，这一制度优于其他国家的现行制度，因为它允许资方和劳方在自然有利于资方的条件下进行直接谈判，尽管存在集体谈判的理论。现行法律引入的这一制度将轻易实现国外类似法律目前所取得的成果，并通过委员会中第三方的参与，消除或减少摩擦根源及剥削可能性。

该法的另一个特点是关于童工工资的规定。众所周知，大多数工厂在极其恶劣、甚至难以描述的情况下雇用儿童。福利工作者在当地报刊上披露的情况确实令人心碎。近几个月来，上海热心居民特意费心设计各种方法，致力于改善这一状况。随着法律中纳入关于童工工资的明确规定，建设性的人道主义努力将获得新的动力，成功的希望更大。

第三个特点是规定工资优先于对任何工业企业的其他债权。这一点受到了公众的广泛关注，尤其是在《破产法》实施以来。后者未规定在其他债权得到满足之前支付工资。《最低工资法》的迅速颁布将立即消除一个争议点，并确保劳工获得一种长期以来在其他国家工人所享有的保护。

这些突出特点足以表明立法者在起草该法时所付出的心血。这标志着自《工厂检查法》颁布以来的又一步进展。

然而，在这两种情况下，上海劳工实际获得的利益将取决于外国工业企业及其政府提供的合作程度。由于上海是中国的工业中心，除非在这座大都市得到适当执行，否则这些法律可能无法达到预期效果。

中国当局试图在国际租界和法租界执行《工厂检查法》的经验令人失望，不言而喻，在执行障碍消除之前，《最低工资法》生效的机会微乎其微。

我们不想在这个几乎老生常谈的话题上赘述，但不得不提醒外国当局，他们对作为中国工人——仅仅是作为人类——享有安全工作条件和可忍受工资标准的权利负有责任。虽然报刊上偶尔出现报道，暗示上海市政当局之间即将达成解决方案，但长期谈判成功结束的前景仍然渺茫。我们要强烈敦促所有相关方采取迅速行动。每拖延一天，成千上万工人的处境就暴露在工厂火灾、爆炸等危险之中，此外还被迫依靠仅能勉强糊口的工资生活，使他们没有闲暇和手段去争取更多权益。

（印：附属分支 K.B. 1936年12月14日 上海工部局）

REVISION OF RULES FOR THE REGISTRATION OF FACTORIES

In December, 1931, the Ministry of Industry promulgated rules for the registration of factories. Up to the present, only a few factories throughout the country have registered.
The Ministry of Industry has now revised the rules for the registration of factories and prepared a form for the registration of factories.
According to the revised rules, a Chinese factory which employs more than 30 workers on ordinary days or which manufactures goods by means of machinery shall make a supplementary registration within 6 months following the promulgation of these revised rules, failing which it will be fined and ordered to register. Similar treatment will be accorded to a new factory that fails to apply for registration within two months after its establishment.
The Bureau of Social Affairs has sent copies of a registration form to local factories.

June 11, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

China Times and other local newspapers:

REVISED RULES GOVERNING THE REGISTRATION OF FACTORIES

The Ministry of Industry has revised the Rules governing the registration of factories. The revised Rules are as follows:-
Article 1. Any factory established in China which employs more than 30 workers at ordinary times or which manufactures products by means of machine power is allowed to apply for registration in accordance with these Rules.
Article 2. At its establishment, a factory shall apply for registration to the Hsien or City Government in whose district it is located. A factory located in the district of a City Government which is under the direct control of the Executive Yuan should register with the Bureau of Social Affairs of the City Government.
Article 3. In applying for registration, the principal responsible persons or the manager of a factory shall first fill in three registration forms (three copies each) and then submit a petition for registration. Two copies only of each form will be required in the case of a factory located in the district of a City Government which is under the direct control of the Executive Yuan.
Article 4. A Hsien Government or a City Government or the Bureau of Social Affairs of a City Government, after receiving an application from a factory for registration, shall make an investigation before granting the application.
Article 5. A factory which has been organized as a company, irrespective of the fact whether or not it uses the term "factory", shall apply for registration as a factory in addition to registering itself as a company.
Article 6. A Hsien Government or a City Government or the Bureau of Social Affairs of a City Government which is under the direct control of the Executive Yuan will issue a certificate to a factory located in its district after its registration has been approved. A sum of $1 will be charged as fee for a certificate and 20 cents duty stamp will be collected when the certificate is issued.
Article 7. After a factory has been permitted to register, its name and address, the name of its manager, the names of its technical experts, the kinds of goods to be manufactured and the number of its registration certificate will be published in the Gazette of the Ministry of Industry.
Article 8. When a registered factory desires to make any alteration in the details mentioned in the registration form, it must give reasons for the change and request the superior authorities to keep them on record.
Article 9. When a factory removes, it shall report the matter to the authorities where it had been registered and should then apply for registration to the registration authorities of the place to which it has removed, according to Article 3 of these Rules. A similar procedure should be followed in case a factory establishes a branch.

实业部已修订工厂注册规则。修订后的规则如下：
第一条. 凡在中国设立、平日雇佣工人超过30名或使用动力机器制造产品的工厂，均准依照本规则申请注册。
第二条. 工厂成立时，应向所在地的县或市政府申请注册。位于直属于行政院的市政府辖区内的工厂，应向该市政府社会局注册。
第三条. 申请注册时，工厂主要负责人或经理须先填写三份注册表格（每份三联），然后提交注册申请书。位于直属于行政院的市政府辖区内的工厂，每份表格仅需填写两份。
第四条. 县政府、市政府或直属于行政院的市政府社会局在收到工厂注册申请后，应在批准前进行调查。
第五条. 凡组织为公司形式的工厂，无论其名称中是否含有“工厂”字样，除办理公司注册外，还应作为工厂申请注册。
第六条. 县政府、市政府或直属于行政院的市政府社会局在批准其辖区内的工厂注册后，将颁发证书。证书收费1元，并在发证时收取20分印花税票。
第七条. 工厂获准注册后，其名称和地址、经理姓名、技术专家姓名、制造货物种类及注册证书编号将在《实业部公报》上刊登。
第八条. 已注册工厂如需变更注册表中提及的任何细节，必须说明变更理由，并请求上级当局备案。
第九条. 工厂搬迁时，应向原注册机关报告，然后根据本规则第三条向迁入地的注册机关申请注册。工厂设立分支机构时，也应遵循类似程序。

（批注：30.5492）

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, APRIL 29, 1935
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
C. I. D. REGISTER

New Rules For
Registration Of
Factories Made

All Plans With More
Than 30 Workers Must
Register Information

Local Organs Will In-
vestigate Organization

NANKING, April 28.—(Kuomin)
—A set of new regulations govern-
ing factory registration was adopt-
ed at the last meeting of the Exe-
cutive Yuan.

All factories operating within
Chinese territory which employ more
than 30 workers or use machine
power for the production of goods
will be required to register with the
local government organ concerned.

Following is a translation of the
new regulations:—

Art. 1.—All factories situated
within the territory of the Republic
of China, which ordinarily employ
more than 30 workers or use ma-
chine-generated power for the
manufacture of goods,—with the ex-
ception of those under the direct
control of the Ministry of War,—
shall apply for registration in ac-
cordance with these regulations.

Art. 2.—Application for registra-
tion shall be made, at the time of
establishment, to the local district
or municipal government where
the factory is situated. Where the
factory is situated in a municipality
under the direct jurisdiction of the
Executive Yuan, application shall
be made to the Bureau of Social
Affairs of the Municipality.

Art. 3.—In applying for registra-
tion, the proprietor or manager of
the factory shall fill up in tripli-
cate the two prescribed registration
forms (issued by the Ministry of
Industry) and submit the same to-
gether with a petition for registra-
tion; in the case of municipalities
under the direct jurisdiction of the
Executive Yuan, two copies shall
suffice.

Investigations Necessary

Art. 4.—Upon receipt of the
forms together with the petition for
registration, the district or muni-
cipal government or the Bureau of
Social Affairs concerned shall im-
mediately make investigations con-
cerning each of the items contain-
ed in the forms and, if satisfactory,
shall thereupon grant registration.
Upon granting registration, the
local government organ concerned
shall report to the Ministry of In-
dustry, either through the pro-
vincial department concerned or
direct, for record.

Art. 5.—Factories which are or-
ganized as companies shall, irre-
gardless whether their capital stock
is paid up or not, apply for factory
registration, in addition to their
separate registration as companies
under the Company Law.

Art. 6.—Factories which have
been granted registration shall be
given certificates issued by the dis-
trict or municipal government if
they are situated in a district or an
ordinary municipality; and by the
municipal bureau of Social Affairs
if they are situated in a munici-
pality under the direct jurisdiction
of the Executive Yuan. These certi-
ficates shall be printed by the re-
gistration organs concerned ac-
cording to the form prescribed by
the Ministry of Industry. A fee of
one dollar and a stamp tax of 20
cents is chargeable for each certi-
ficate issued.

Art. 7.—Upon registration being
granted, the name and location of
the factory and the names of its
directors, principal technicians, the
products manufactured, and the
number of its certificate shall be
published in the "Industrial Ga-
zette."

Art. 8.—In case of any change in
the matters set forth in the re-
gistration forms after registration
has been granted, the factory con-
cerned shall give the reasons for
such changes and report the same
for record.

Art. 9.—In case of removal, the
factory concerned must, besides re-
porting to the original registration
organ, apply to the organ concerned
of the place to which it removes,
for registration according to Art-
icle 3 of these regulations.

Applies To Branches

The above provision shall apply
also to the establishment of branch
factories.

Art. 10.—When a factory closes
down, it shall report immediately to
the organ with which it was re-
gistered, which shall in turn report
to the Ministry of Industry for re-
cord.

Art. 11.—Factories which have
been granted registration shall,
within two months after the end
of each business year, compile and
submit to the local district or
municipal government concerned,
for transmission to the Ministry of
Industry for examination, a report
on the factory affairs during the
preceding business year by filling
up in triplicate the form prescribed
by the ministry. In the case of
municipalities under the direct
jurisdiction of the Executive Yuan,
only two copies need be submitted
to the Bureau of Social Affairs for
transmission.

Art. 12.—Upon promulgation of
these revised regulations, all fac-
tories which have not yet been re-
gistered shall apply for registra-
tion within six months from date
of promulgation. Those failing to
do so within the period shall be
liable to a fine according to Article
5 of the Law Governing Execution
of Administrative Measures and
shall be compelled to apply for re-
gistration. The above provision
shall apply also to new factories
which fail to apply for registration
within two months after their es-
tablishment.

Art. 13.—These regulations shall
become effective upon the date of
promulgation thereof.

File
JW
29 APR. 1935

《字林西报》，1935年4月29日，星期一
上海公共租界工部局
刑事侦缉处登记簿

制定工厂注册新规

凡雇员超过30人之工厂须注册信息

地方机关将调查其组织情况

南京，4月28日电。（国民通讯社）——行政院在最近一次会议上通过了一套关于工厂注册的新规章。

所有在中国领土内运营、雇佣工人超过30名或使用机器动力生产货物的工厂，均须向有关地方政府机关办理注册。

以下是新规章的译文：—

第一条.— 凡位于中华民国领土内，通常雇佣工人超过30名或使用机器动力制造货物的工厂，除直接受陆军部管辖者外，均应按照本规章申请注册。

第二条.— 注册申请应在工厂设立时，向工厂所在地的区或市政府提出。如工厂位于行政院直辖特别市，应向该市社会局提出申请。

第三条.— 申请注册时，工厂业主或经理应填写由实业部颁发的两种规定注册表格一式三份，并连同注册申请书一并提交；如属行政院直辖特别市，提交两份即可。

需进行调查

第四条.— 收到表格及注册申请书后，有关的区或市政府或社会局应立即对表格中所列各项进行调查，如认为满意，即予注册。准予注册后，有关地方政府机关应通过有关省厅或直接呈报实业部备案。

第五条.— 凡按公司形式组织的工厂，无论其股本是否缴足，除依《公司法》单独进行公司注册外，还应申请工厂注册。

第六条.— 获准注册的工厂，如位于区或普通市，由区或市政府颁发证书；如位于行政院直辖特别市，由该市社会局颁发证书。这些证书应由有关注册机关按照实业部规定的格式印制。每发一张证书，收取手续费一元及印花税二角。

第七条.— 准予注册后，工厂名称及地点、董事及主要技师姓名、制造产品及证书编号，均应在《工业公报》上公布。

第八条.— 注册获准后，如注册表格所列事项有任何变更，有关工厂应说明变更原因，并报告备案。

第九条.— 如遇搬迁，有关工厂除向原注册机关报告外，还必须依照本规章第三条之规定，向迁入地有关机关申请注册。

适用于分厂

上述规定亦适用于设立分厂。

第十条.— 工厂停业时，应立即向原注册机关报告，该机关随即转报实业部备案。

第十一条.— 获准注册的工厂，应在每个营业年度结束后的两个月内，按照实业部规定的格式填写报表一式三份，编制上一营业年度的厂务报告，提交有关区或市政府，以便转送实业部审核。如属行政院直辖特别市，只需向该局社会局提交两份，以便转送。

第十二条.— 本修订规章颁布后，所有尚未注册的工厂应在颁布之日起六个月内申请注册。逾期未办者，将依据《行政执行法》第五条处以罚款，并被强制申请注册。上述规定亦适用于设立后两个月内未申请注册的新工厂。

第十三条.— 本规章自颁布之日起生效。

档案
JW
1935年4月29日

April 25, 1935. Morning Translation.

Shanghai Morning Post (official organ of Gen.Chiang Kai Shek)
and other local newspapers:

KOREAN SHOT BY FELLOW COUNTRYMAN IN FRENCH CONCESSION

Chin Yang Seu (金洋秀 ), a naturalized Chinese
citizen of Korean origin, age 36, resides in an upstairs
room of house No. 200 Rue Porte de l'Ouest in the French
Concession. He is a dealer in Korean ginseng.
At 9 p.m. yesterday, Chin Yang Seu went to
Rue Brenier de Montmorand to make some purchase. As he
was walking in the vicinity of Sie Men Li (西門里 ), Rue
Porte de l'Ouest on his way home, another Korean ran up
to him from Rue Brenier de Montmorand and fired a shot
at him. Chin was struck in the neck and fell to the
ground. The assailant made good his escape.
The French Police later removed the injured man
to Ste. Marie Hospital on Route Pere Robert. It is
learned that the condition of the Korean is very serious.
Efforts are being made by the French Police to effect the
arrest of the gunman.

China Times and other local newspapers:

ENFORCEMENT OF ARTICLE 13 OF THE FACTORY LAW TO BE POSTPONED
TILL AUGUST 1936.

The Shanghai City Government is in receipt of
the following dispatch from the Ministry of Industry:-
"This Ministry has received the following
instructions from the Executive Yuan:-
'Your Ministry some time ago sent a petition
asking for instructions as to whether the preparatory
period for the enforcement of Article 13 of the Factory
Law is to be postponed or to be carried out. This Yuan
referred the matter to the Central Political Council for
decision and is now in receipt of an order from the
National Government containing the following letter from
the Central Political Council:-
With reference to the item referred to in Article
13 of the Factory Law relating to the prohibition
of female hands working late into the night,
the Council has called a meeting to discuss the
matter. A preparatory period of two years has
been fixed for the enforcement of this Article.
A petition from the Ministry of Industry received
through the Executive Yuan states that if night
work is prohibited to female workers at this time
of trade depression, the female workers would be
thrown out of employment. At a recent meeting,
the Council resolved to postpone the preparatory
period for the enforcement of Article 13 of the
Factory Law till August 1, 1936.
'The Ministry is hereby instructed to act in
compliance with the above letter.'
"The Ministry now notifies the City Government
of this decision and requests the Government to instruct
its subordinate organs to that effect."

法租界一朝鲜人被同乡枪击

金洋秀（Chin Yang Seu），归化中国籍的朝鲜人，36岁，居住在法租界西江路（Rue Porte de l'Ouest）200号的一间楼上房间。他是一名朝鲜人参商人。
昨晚9时，金洋秀前往蒙莫朗路（Rue Brenier de Montmorand）购物。在回家途中，当他行走在西门里（Sie Men Li）附近的西江路一带时，另一名朝鲜人从蒙莫朗路跑向他，并向他开了一枪。金颈部中弹，倒在地上。袭击者成功逃脱。
法国巡捕随后将伤者送往罗伯特神父路（Route Pere Robert）的圣玛丽医院。据悉，这名朝鲜人的伤势非常严重。法国巡捕正努力缉拿枪手。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS. SATURDAY, APRIL 7, 1934
NEW FACTORY RULES APPROVED
Long Programme Based on 1931 Act Safeguards
Women and Children : Five Stages

The "China Times," reports that
the Central Factory Inspection
Bureau of the Ministry of Industries
has formulated a programme for fac-
tory inspection in five stages. The
Ministry has approved and authorized
the proposal, which has been com-
municated to the Shanghai City Gov-
ernment and through it to its Bureau
of Social Affairs.
A translation of the clauses of the
Factory Act to which reference
is made in the news report is
presented below. The Factory act
was declared in force in 1931.

First Stage

Article 3. Factories shall keep a
workers' register and record the fol-
lowing particulars concerning each
worker:
1. Name, age, native place, and
address.
2. Year and month of entry into
the factory
3. The kind of work, hours and
remuneration
4. Skill and conduct
5. Efficiency of work
6. Rewards and penalties received
in the factory
7. Kinds of illness and injuries
suffered by the worker and the
causes thereof.
Article 4. Once every six months
factories shall submit to the Proper
Authorities a report containing the
following particulars:
1. Report of workers' names
2. Illness and injuries suffered by
workers, and their treatment and
results
3. Accidents and measures taken
for the relief thereof.
4. Termination of employment of
workers and reasons therefor.

Child and Female Labour

Article 6. Males and females above
the age of 14 but who have not com-
pleted their sixteenth year shall be
deemed child workers. Child work-
ers are permitted to be engaged only
in light and easy work.
Article 7. Child and female work-
ers shall not be employed in the
following work:
1. In handling explosive, inflam-
matory or poisonous articles
2. In places which are exposed to
dust or poisonous odours and gas
3. In fixing, cleaning, oiling, in-
specting or repairing moving ma-
chines, power transmitting equip-
ment, or risky parts thereof, or in
adjusting belts and ropes.
4. In connecting highly charged
electric wires
5. In handling molten metals or
the residue thereof.
6. In handling furnaces or boilers:
or
7. Other work that is immoral or
of a dangerous character.
Article 59: For the purpose of
practice, apprentices shall not be
engaged in any of the occupations
enumerated in Article 7.
Article 65. During the period of
apprenticeship the factory shall re-
quire the master craftsmen to the
best of their ability to train appren-
tices for the trade specified in the
contract of apprenticeship.

Compensation and Pensions

Article 45. Pending the enforce-
ment of Labour Insurance Laws, the
factory shall pay to the workers in-
jured or killed in the performance
of their duty all medical expenses
and compensation or pensions. The
sum of compensation or pension shall
be based on the following scale, but
if the capital of the factory shall be
less than fifty thousand dollars, the
factory may petition the proper au-
thorities to reduce the sums to be
paid.
1. For workers temporarily in-
capacitated, the factory shall, besides
bearing the medical expenses, pay
them each day a sum amounting to
two thirds of their regular wages for
a period not exceeding six months.
Upon the expiration of the said
period, the factory may reduce the
amount of the compensation to half
of the workers' average wage for a
period of not more than one year.
2. For workers permanently dis-
abled in the performance of their
duty, the factory shall pay a sum com-
mensurate with the extent of the dis-
ablement. Such compensation, how-
ever, shall under no circumstances
exceed three years' regular wages, or
be less than one year's wages.
3. For workers killed in the course
of their employment the factory shall,
besides paying a sum of fifty dollars
as funeral expenses, pay to the legal
heirs a pension of three hundred
dollars, plus two years' regular
wages.
The regular wage mentioned above
shall be based upon the workers'
average wage during the last three
months of their employment.
Funeral expenses and pensions
shall be paid at one and the same
time, but compensation for injuries
or sickness or disablement may be
paid at regular intervals.
Article 48. Should any accident oc-
cur resulting in the death or grave
injury to a worker, the factory shall,
within five days, report its occurence
and the consequent measures taken
to the Proper Authorities.

Apprentices' Contracts

Article 56. Factories taking ap-
prentices shall first conclude contracts
with them or their legal represent-
atives. The contract shall be made
in triplicate, one copy for each of the
contracting parties and one to be
submitted to the Proper authorities
for registration. The contract shall
contain the following articles:
(1) The name, age, native place and
address of the apprentice.
(2) The kind of trade the apprentice
is to follow.
(3) The date on which the contract
is made and its duration
(4) Mutual obligations: should the
apprentice be required to pay tuition,
the amount and time for payment
shall be stipulated. Where the con-
tract of apprenticeship provides re-
muneration for the apprentice's ser-
vices, the amount and the time of
payment shall likewise be stipulated.
The above contract shall not re-
strict the apprentice's freedom to
work upon the expiration of the ap-
prenticeship.
Article 61. During the whole term
of apprenticeship, the apprentices
shall be supplied with board, lodging
and medical care by the factory, in
addition to a proper allowance for
incidentals each month.
In addition to the above specific
clauses to be applied, the first stage
shall include the application of
specific rulings and laws on inspec-
tion. During the first stage also pre-
paration shall be made for the
succeeding stages.

《字林西报》。1934年4月7日，星期六
新工厂规章获批准
基于1931年法案的长期计划提供保障
妇女与儿童：五个阶段

据《时报》报道，
实业部中央工厂检查局
已制定分五个阶段进行的工厂
检查计划。该部已批准并授权
此项提案，并已通报上海市政府，
再由市政府转达其社会局。
下文呈列新闻报道中所提及的
《工厂法》条款之译文。《工厂法》
于1931年宣布施行。

第一阶段

第三条 工厂应保存工人名册，并记录
每位工人的下列详情：
1. 姓名、年龄、籍贯及住址。
2. 进厂年月
3. 工作种类、工时及薪酬
4. 技能与品行
5. 工作效率
6. 在厂内所受之奖惩
7. 工人所患疾病及受伤种类及其
原因。

第四条 工厂应每六个月向主管当局
提交一份报告，包含下列详情：
1. 工人姓名报告
2. 工人所患疾病及受伤情况，及其
治疗和结果
3. 事故及为此采取的救济措施。
4. 工人雇佣关系的终止及原因。

童工与女工

第六条 年满十四岁但未满十六岁的
男女，视为童工。童工仅准许从事
轻便易做的工作。
第七条 童工及女工不得受雇从事
下列工作：
1. 处理爆炸性、易燃性或有毒物品
2. 在暴露于粉尘或有毒气味及气体
的场所
3. 固定、清洁、加油、检查或修理
运转中的机器、动力传输设备或其
危险部件，或调整皮带和绳索。
4. 连接高压电线
5. 处理熔融金属或其残渣。
6. 操作熔炉或锅炉；或
7. 其他不道德或具有危险性质的
工作。
第五十九条：出于实习目的，学徒
不得从事第七条所列的任何职业。
第六十五条：在学徒期间，工厂应
要求师傅尽其所能，按照学徒合同
中规定的行业培训学徒。

赔偿与抚恤金

第四十五条：在劳工保险法施行之前，
工厂应向在执行职务中受伤或死亡的
工人支付所有医疗费用及赔偿或抚恤金。
赔偿或抚恤金的数额应依据下列标准，
但若工厂资本少于五万元，工厂可向
主管当局申请减少支付金额。
1. 对于暂时丧失劳动能力的工人，
工厂除承担医疗费用外，还应每天
向其支付相当于其正常工资三分之二的
金额，期限不超过六个月。
上述期限届满后，工厂可将赔偿金额
减至工人平均工资的一半，期限不超过
一年。
2. 对于在执行职务中永久残疾的工人，
工厂应支付与残疾程度相称的金额。
然而，此类赔偿在任何情况下不得超过
三年的正常工资，也不得少于一年的
工资。
3. 对于在受雇期间死亡的工人，工厂
除支付五十元作为丧葬费外，还应向
法定继承人支付三百元抚恤金，外加
两年的正常工资。
上述正常工资应以工人受雇最后三个月
的平均工资为基础。
丧葬费和抚恤金应一次性支付，但
因受伤、疾病或残疾的赔偿可按定期
间隔支付。
第四十八条：若发生导致工人死亡或
重伤的事故，工厂应在五天内向主管
当局报告事故发生情况及随后采取的措施。

学徒合同

第五十六条：招收学徒的工厂应首先
与学徒或其法定代理人签订合同。合同
应一式三份，缔约各方各执一份，另一份
提交主管当局登记。合同应包含下列
条款：
(1) 学徒的姓名、年龄、籍贯及住址。
(2) 学徒将从事的行业种类。
(3) 合同签订日期及期限
(4) 双方义务：若要求学徒支付学费，
应规定金额及支付时间。若学徒合同
规定为学徒的服务提供报酬，同样应
规定金额及支付时间。
上述合同不得限制学徒在学徒期满后的
工作自由。
第六十一条：在整个学徒期间，工厂除
每月提供适当的零用津贴外，还应为
学徒提供食宿及医疗照顾。
除了上述要适用的具体条款外，第一
阶段还包括适用有关检查的具体裁决
和法律。在第一阶段，还要为后续阶段
做好准备。

（印：S.M.M. 工部局警务处 刑事侦缉处 档案室 编号 1. O....... 9. 日期....................）

Second Stage—Health, Safety, etc.
Article 41. All factories shall take the following precautions.
1. Safety precautions against risks of personal injury to workers.
2. Safety precautions regarding the structure of the factory
3. Precautions regarding the proper installation of machines.
4. Precautions for the prevention of fire and floods.
Article 42. All factories shall have the following sanitary provisions:
1. Provision for good ventilation
2. Provision for pure drinks.
3. Provision for lavatories and toilet facilities.
4. Provision for light
5. Provision for poison prevention.
Article 43. All factories shall give their workers safety instruction.
Article 44. Whenever the safety and sanitary provisions of a factory are found inadequate, the Proper Authorities may require improvement within a definite period of time, and in case of necessity may also forbid the use of any part of the factory.

The Number of Apprentices
Article 63. The total number of apprentices taken by a factory shall not exceed one third of its regular workers.
Article 64. Should a factory take more apprentices than it can adequately train, the Proper Authorities may order a partial reduction, and also set a limit to the number of apprentices the factory may take thereafter.

In the second stage also, laws and rulings with respect of inspection must also be enforced, while supervision to the conditions of stage one, and preparation for the conditions in the stages to follow are included in the work to be done. This principle of continued supervision of previously applied regulations and preparation for those of the next stages is included in the work proposed to be done at each stage outlined.

Third Stage—Hours of Work
Article 9. Factories that use the system of day and night shifts shall so arrange their working schedules that the shifts for the workers may be interchanged at least once a week.
Article 10. Besides the provisions in Article 8, in cases of natural, accidental or seasonal changes, the working hours may be extended; but the total number of working hours shall not exceed twelve hours per day, and the overtime work shall not exceed thirty six hours per month.
Article 11. The regular working day for child workers shall under no circumstances exceed eight hours.
Article 12. Child workers shall not work between the hours of seven o'clock in the evening and six o'clock the following morning.
Article 58. The hours of training for apprentices shall be governed by the provisions of Chapter III of this Law. (Clauses 9-12 above are part of Chapter III).
Article 14. Any worker who works continuously for a period of five hours shall have half an hour's rest.
Article 15. All workers shall have one day's rest in every seven days.
Article 16. All factories shall cease work on holidays designated by law or orders of the government.

Apprentices, Child and Adult Workers
Article 36. All factories shall provide supplementary education for child workers and apprentices and shall be responsible for all the expenses thereof incurred. Such supplementary education shall not be less than ten hours per week. For other workers who have no opportunity for education, the factories shall also establish, within their means, educational facilities.
The time for conducting the above mentioned education shall be arranged outside working hours.

Fourth Stage—Children
Article 5. No person, male or female, who has not completed his or her fourteenth year shall be employed in any factory as a worker.
Boys and girls above the age of 12 and below the age of 14 who are already employed in factories prior to the promulgation of this law may, with the consent of the Proper Authorities, be permitted to remain in this employment when this law is put into effect.
Article 57. Neither male or female persons below the age of fourteen shall be engaged as apprentices, excepting those who were already engaged as apprentices prior to the enforcement of this law.
Article 13. Female workers shall not work between the hours of ten o'clock in the evening and six o'clock on the following morning.
Article 37. Female workers shall be given full wages before and after childbirth, amounting altogether to eight weeks in duration.

Fifth Stage—Working Day
Article 8. In principle the regular working day for adult workers is eight hours; but may be extended to ten in cases of necessity due to varying local conditions and the nature of the work.
Article 17. All workers who work continuously for a fixed period shall be allowed a special vacation which shall be based on the following scale.
1. All workers who have worked continuously for more than one year and less than three years shall be allowed a vacation of seven days a year.
2. All workers who have worked continuously for more than three years but less than five years shall be allowed a vacation of ten days a year.
3. All workers who have worked continuously for more than five years but less than ten years shall be allowed a vacation of fourteen days a year.
4. All workers who have worked continuously for more then ten years shall gave an additional day for each additional year added to his vacation, but the total shall not exceed thirty.
page_data.zh:
第二阶段——健康、安全等
第四十一条 所有工厂应采取下列预防措施。
1. 针对工人人身伤害风险的预防措施。
2. 关于工厂结构的预防措施
3. 关于机器正确安装的预防措施。
4. 防火及防洪的预防措施。
第四十二条 所有工厂应具备下列卫生设施：
1. 良好通风设施
2. 纯净饮用水设施。
3. 盥洗室及厕所设施。
4. 照明设施
5. 防毒设施。
第四十三条 所有工厂应向其工人提供
安全指导。
第四十四条：凡发现工厂的安全及卫生
设施不足时，主管当局可要求在限定
期限内改进，并在必要时也可禁止使用
工厂的任何部分。

学徒人数
第六十三条 工厂招收的学徒总数不得
超过其正式工人的三分之一。
第六十四条：若工厂招收的学徒超过其
能充分培训的数量，主管当局可命令
部分削减，并限定该工厂此后可招收的
学徒人数。

在第二阶段，也必须执行有关检查的法律
和裁决，同时对第一阶段状况的监督以及
为后续阶段状况所做的准备也包含在待办
工作中。这种对先前已适用法规进行持续
监督并为下一阶段法规做准备的原则，包含
在概述的每个阶段拟开展的工作中。

第三阶段——工作时间
第九条 采用日夜轮班制的工厂，应如此
安排其工作时间表，使工人的轮班至少
每周互换一次。
第十条：除第八条规定外，在自然、意外
或季节性变化的情况下，可延长工作时间；
但工作总时数每天不得超过十二小时，且
加班每月不得超过三十六小时。
第十一条：童工的正常工作日在任何情况
下不得超过八小时。
第十二条：童工不得在晚上七点至次日
早上六点之间工作。
第五十八条：学徒的培训时间应受本法
第三章规定的管辖。（上述第9-12条属于
第三章的一部分）。
第十四条：任何连续工作五小时的工人
应有半小时休息时间。
第十五条：所有工人每七天应有一天休息。
第十六条：所有工厂应在法律指定或政府
命令规定的节假日停工。

学徒、童工及成年工人
第三十六条：所有工厂应为童工和学徒
提供补习教育，并负责由此产生的一切
费用。此类补习教育每周不得少于十小时。
对于其他没有受教育机会的工人，工厂也
应在其能力范围内设立教育设施。
进行上述教育的时间应安排在工作时间
之外。

第四阶段——儿童
第五条：未满十四岁的任何人，无论男女，
不得在任何工厂受雇为工人。
在本法颁布前已在工厂受雇的12岁以上、
14岁以下的男孩和女孩，经主管当局同意，
在本法生效时可获准继续受雇。
第五十七条：未满十四岁的男女不得受雇
为学徒，但在本法施行前已受雇为学徒者
除外。
第十三条：女工不得在晚上十点至次日
早上六点之间工作。
第三十七条：女工在产前产后应获得全额
工资，共计八周。

第五阶段——工作日
第八条：原则上，成年工人的正常工作日
为八小时；但因各地情况不同及工作性质
需要，可延长至十小时。
第十七条：所有连续工作满一定期限的
工人应享受特别休假，休假依据下列标准。
1. 所有连续工作一年以上、三年以下的
工人，每年可享受七天休假。
2. 所有连续工作三年以上、五年以下的
工人，每年可享受十天休假。
3. 所有连续工作五年以上、十年以下的
工人，每年可享受十四天休假。
4. 所有连续工作十年以上的工人，每增加
一年工龄，休假增加一天，但总数不得超过
三十天。

November 21, 1932. Afternoon Translation.

LABOUR.

Min Pao and other local newspapers publish the following telegram
from Nanking:

THE REVISED FACTORY LAW.

On November 19, the Legislative Council held a
meeting and passed the revised Regulations of the Factory
Law as follows:-

CHAPTER ONE. GENERAL RULE.

Article 1. This Law will apply to any factory employing more
than 30 workers.
Article 2. The controlling authorities mentioned in this Law,
unless specially stipulated, will mean the Municipal
Government in cities and Hsien Government in Hsiens.
Article 3. A factory shall keep a registration book for the
workers in which are to be recorded the following particulars
and shall report to the control organ concerned for record:-
A) Name, sex, age, native place, and address of a worker.
B) Date of entry.
C) Nature of work, working period and reward.
D) Physical constitution.
E) Reward or fine.
F) Nature of wounds or sickness and the causes.
Article 4. A factory shall submit every six months a report
to the control organ on the following matters:-
A) Changes of particulars in the workers' registration
book.
B) Wounds or sickness of workers and the medical treatment.
C) Incidental matters of a factory and the remedy.
D) Causes for the discharge of workers.

CHAPTER TWO. CHILD AND FEMALE WORKERS.

Article 5. A factory is not allowed to employ male and female
workers under 14 years of age. A factory may after the
promulgation of this Law secure sanction from the control
organ concerned to permit male and female workers over 12
years of age but below 14, who had been taken on before
the enforcement of this Law.
Article 6. Male and female workers under 14 years old are
classified as child workers and must be given light work.
Article 7. Child and female workers are prohibited to undertake
the following kinds of work:-
A) Dealing with articles which may cause explosion, or fire
and poisons.
B) Working in dust powder or places where poisons are to
be found.
C) Fixing, dusting, oiling, inspecting, repairing etc. of
dangerous parts of moving machinery.
D) Fixing of electric wires in high positions.
E) Mining work.
F) Lighting fires of boilers.
G) Other kinds of work which are detrimental to morals or
dangerous to life.

劳工。

《民报》及其他本地报纸刊登了来自南京的下列电文：

修订工厂法。

11月19日，立法院召开会议，通过了修订后的《工厂法》条例，内容如下：-

第一章. 总则。

第一条. 本法适用于雇佣工人三十名以上的任何工厂。
第二条. 本法所述之主管机关，除另有特别规定外，在城市指市政府，在县指县政府。
第三条. 工厂应备置工人登记簿，记录下列事项，并向有关主管机关报备存档：-
A) 工人的姓名、性别、年龄、籍贯及住址。
B) 入职日期。
C) 工作性质、工作时间及报酬。
D) 身体状况。
E) 奖赏或罚款。
F) 受伤或患病性质及原因。
第四条. 工厂应每六个月向主管机关提交关于下列事项的报告：-
A) 工人登记簿中事项的变更。
B) 工人的伤病及医疗情况。
C) 工厂的偶发事件及补救措施。
D) 解雇工人的原因。

第二章. 童工及女工。

第五条. 工厂不得雇佣十四岁以下的男女工人。本法颁布后，工厂可向有关主管机关申请批准，允许雇佣在本法实施前已录用的十二岁以上、十四岁以下的男女工人。
第六条. 十四岁以下的男女工人归类为童工，必须安排轻便工作。
第七条. 禁止童工及女工从事下列种类的工作：-
A) 处理可能引起爆炸、火灾及有毒的物品。
B) 在粉尘飞扬或存在毒物的场所工作。
C) 对运转机械的危险部位进行固定、除尘、加油、检查、修理等。
D) 在高处架设电线。
E) 采矿工作。
F) 锅炉生火。
G) 其他有伤风化或危及生命的工作。

November 21, 1932.
Afternoon Translation

LABOUR

CHAPTER THREE. WORKING HOURS.

Article 8. The daily number of working hours of adult work-
is fixed at 8. The working hours may be extended to ten
should such prolongation be necessary due to conditions
in the district or the nature of the work.
Article 9. Should a factory adopt the system of day and
night shift work, the shifts must be changed at least
once a week.
Article 10. With the exception of the stipulations contained
in Article 8, the working hours may be further extended
with the approval of the Labour Union concerned. The
daily working hours must not exceed 12 and the total
prolongation must not exceed 46 hours in one month.
Article 11. The daily number of working hours for child
workers must not exceed 8.
Article 12. Child workers shall not work within the period
from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. on the following day.
Article 13. Female workers shall not work within the period
of 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. on the following day.

CHAPTER FOUR. REFRESHMENTS AND HOLIDAYS.

Article 14. A recreation of half an hour shall be given to
workers after doing five hours of work.
Article 15. One day holiday shall be given to workers every
7 days.
Article 16. A factory shall allow holidays on the various
anniversaries which are defined by the National Governmen-
as holidays.
Article 17. A worker shall be allowed to have a special
holiday after continuing at work for a certain period.
Holidays will be governed as follows:-
A) 7 days holiday in a year shall be given to a worker
after a service of more than a year but less than 3
years.
B) A yearly holiday of 10 days shall be granted to a worker
after a service of over 3 years but less than 5 years.
C) A yearly holiday of 14 days shall be granted to a worker
after a service of over 5 years but less than 10 years.
D) An additional day shall be given as a special holiday
to a worker with over ten years service. Total days
of leave in a year are not to exceed 30.
Article 18. A factory shall pay the wages for the holidays
according to Articles 15 and 17. Workers who do not wish
to have special holidays shall be given double pay for
the holiday period.
Article 19. Holidays of workers in the employ of military
and public utility authorities may be cancelled at the
discretion of the control organs.

CHAPTER FIVE. WAGES.

Article 20. The minimum wages of workers shall be fixed
according to the cost of living of the place where the
factories are located.

劳工

第三章. 工作时间。

第八条. 成年工人的每日工作时间定为八小时。若因地区情况或工作性质确有必要，工作时间可延长至十小时。
第九条. 若工厂采用日夜轮班制，班次必须至少每周轮换一次。
第十条. 除第八条规定外，经有关工会批准，工作时间可进一步延长。每日工作时间不得超过十二小时，且每月累计延长时间不得超过四十六小时。
第十一条. 童工的每日工作时间不得超过八小时。
第十二条. 童工不得在晚上八点至次日早上六点期间工作。
第十三条. 女工不得在晚上十点至次日早上六点期间工作。

第四章. 休息与假期。

第十四条. 工人工作五小时后，应给予半小时休息时间。
第十五条. 每七天应给予工人一天假期。
第十六条. 工厂应在国民政府规定的各类纪念日给予假期。
第十七条. 工人连续工作一定期限后，应享有特别假期。假期规定如下：-
A) 工作满一年以上但不足三年者，每年给予七天假期。
B) 工作满三年以上但不足五年者，每年给予十天假期。
C) 工作满五年以上但不足十年者，每年给予十四天假期。
D) 工作满十年以上者，额外增加一天特别假期。全年休假总天数不得超过三十天。
第十八条. 工厂应按照第十五条和第十七条的规定支付假期工资。不愿休特别假期的工人，应按假期时间的双倍支付工资。
第十九条. 受雇于军事及公用事业机构的工人，其假期可由主管机关酌情取消。

第五章. 工资。

第二十条. 工人的最低工资应根据工厂所在地的生活费用确定。

November 21, 1932.
Afternoon Translation.

LABOUR

Article 21. A factory shall issue wages to workers in the
currency of the district.
Article 22. The period for the payment of wages shall be
definitely fixed and the issue shall be at least twice a
month. This shall also apply to the issue of wages to
workers on piece work basis.
Article 23. When a factory prolongs the working hours,
according to stipulations of Article 10 and 19, the wages
will be issued at an increase of one third or two thirds
according to the amount of wages per hour a worker receives
on ordinary days.
Article 24. The same scale of wages will be paid to male
and female workers who undertake work of the same nature.
Article 25. A factory must not detain wages of workers
to be held as a fund against a worker's violation of
the agreement or of compensation.

CHAPTER SIX. TERMINATION OF WORKING AGREEMENTS.

Article 26. At the expiration of a definite working agreement
the same may be renewed with the approval of both sides.
Article 27. Should a factory wish to terminate a working
agreement which does not stipulate any period of time,
the workers interested must be notified in advance. The
period for such notice shall be as stipulated here below:-
A) Advance notice of the termination of a working
agreement shall be made ten days to a worker with over
3 months but less than one year service.
B) Advanced notice shall be made 20 days to a worker with
more than a year but less than 3 years service.
C) Advance notice shall be made 30 days to a worker with
over three years service.
Article 28. After the receipt of such notice, a worker is
allowed to ask for leave of absence during the working
period with a view to enabling him to find another position.
However, a worker is not allowed more than two days leave
in a week. A worker is entitled to full pay during the
period of such leave of absence.
Article 29. When a factory gives advance notice to a worker
of the termination of an agreement in accordance with
Article 27, it shall issue wages to the worker, to which
he is entitled. Furthermore, the factory shall pay the
worker 50 per cent of his wages for the period of the
previous notification defined in the same article.
In the event of a factory wishing to terminate an agreement
forthwith without acting in compliance with Article 27,
full wages for the period of the notice shall be issued.
Article 30. A factory may terminate an agreement with a
worker before the date of its expiration on the following
grounds, but workers shall be notified beforehand in
accordance with Article 27:-
A) When the business of the whole part or a part of a
factory is suspended.
B) When a factory has been forced to suspend operations
for more than one month.
C) When a worker is unable to carry out the work entrusted
to him by the factory.
