劳工

第二十一条. 工厂应以当地货币向工人发放工资。
第二十二条. 工资发放周期应明确固定，且每月至少发放两次。这也适用于计件工人的工资发放。
第二十三条. 当工厂根据第十条和第十九条的规定延长工作时间时，工资应按工人平日每小时工资标准的三分之一或三分之二增加发放。
第二十四条. 从事相同性质工作的男女工人，应支付同等标准的工资。
第二十五条. 工厂不得扣留工人工资作为工人违反协议或赔偿的基金。

第六章. 劳动协议的终止。

第二十六条. 定期劳动协议期满时，经双方同意可予续订。
第二十七条. 若工厂希望终止未规定期限的劳动协议，必须提前通知相关工人。通知期限规定如下：-
A) 对工作满三个月但不足一年的工人，终止劳动协议应提前十天通知。
B) 对工作满一年但不足三年的工人，应提前二十天通知。
C) 对工作满三年以上的工人，应提前三十天通知。
第二十八条. 工人在收到此类通知后，允许在工作时间内请假以便寻找其他职位。但是，工人每周请假不得超过两天。在此请假期间，工人有权获得全额工资。
第二十九条. 当工厂根据第二十七条向工人发出终止协议的通知时，应发放工人应得的工资。此外，工厂还应支付该条文中规定的先前通知期内工资的百分之五十。
若工厂希望立即终止协议而不遵守第二十七条的规定，则应发放通知期内的全额工资。
第三十条. 工厂可基于下列理由在协议到期日前终止与工人的协议，但须按照第二十七条的规定事先通知工人：-
A) 当工厂全部或部分业务暂停时。
B) 当工厂被迫停工超过一个月时。
C) 当工人无法履行工厂委派的工作时。
（待续。）

November 22, 1932.                                  Afternoon Translation

LABOUR

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

THE REVISED FACTORY LAW.
(Continued from yesterday)

Article 31. A factory may terminate a working agreement
prior to its expiration and without previous notice on the
following grounds:-
A) When a worker violates the Regulations of the factory
concerned and the affair is of a serious nature.
B) When a worker neglects his duty without cause for over
3 days or for more than 6 days in a month.
Article 32. If a worker, who is not on time agreement, wishes
to terminate it, he shall notify his factory a week before
the date of his intention of ending the agreement.
Article 33. A worker may terminate his working agreement prior
to its expiration and without previous notice on the
following grounds:-
A) When a factory acts in violation of the working
agreement or of the important stipulations of the
Labour Law.
B) When a factory fails without cause to issue wages at
the regular time.
C) When a factory ill-treats workers.
Article 34. Whenever a dispute arises between a factory and
workers over Clauses C of Article 30, Clause A of Article
31 and all the Clauses of Article 33; a factory meeting
may be held to settle the difference.
Article 35. A worker is allowed to demand that his factory
grant him a certificate when his service is terminated
properly and a factory can not reject such a demand.
Excepting the case of a worker who has acted in contravention
of Article 32 or of the various Clauses of Article 31.
The abovementioned certificate shall contain the following
particulars:-
A) Name, sex, age, native place and address of a worker.
B) Nature of work.
C) Working period in the factory and result of work.

CHAPTER SEVEN. WELFARE OF WORKERS.

Article 36. A factory shall allow child workers and apprentices
to continue their education and shall provide the
educational expenses. The minimum number of hours for
education are 10 in a week. A factory shall do its best
to assist adult workers in their education. The period
for education shall be fixed outside working hours.
Article 37. Eight weeks leave shall be given to a female
worker before and after her childbirth. Full pay shall
be granted to a female worker for over 6 months service.
Those who have worked for less than 6 months are entitled
to 50 per cent of the wages only.
Article 38. A factory shall render within its power every
assistance to workers in the matters of their savings,
co-operation society, etc.

1932年11月22日。                                  下午译件

劳工

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

修订工厂法。
（接昨日）

第三十一条. 工厂可基于下列理由，在协议到期日前终止劳动协议且无需事先通知：-
A) 当工人违反有关工厂规章且情节严重时。
B) 当工人无故旷工超过三天，或一个月内累计超过六天时。
第三十二条. 若未按定期协议受雇的工人希望终止协议，应在其打算结束协议之日的一周前通知工厂。
第三十三条. 工人可基于下列理由，在协议到期日前终止劳动协议且无需事先通知：-
A) 当工厂违反劳动协议或《劳动法》的重要规定时。
B) 当工厂无故未能按时发放工资时。
C) 当工厂虐待工人时。
第三十四条. 当工厂与工人之间就第三十条C款、第三十一条A款及第三十三条各款发生争议时，可召开厂务会议以解决分歧。
第三十五条. 工人在正当终止服务时，有权要求工厂出具证明，工厂不得拒绝此要求。但工人违反第三十二条或第三十一条各款的情况除外。
上述证明应包含下列事项：-
A) 工人的姓名、性别、年龄、籍贯及住址。
B) 工作性质。
C) 在厂工作期限及工作表现。

第七章. 工人福利。

第三十六条. 工厂应允许童工及学徒继续受教育，并提供教育费用。每周最低教育时数为十小时。工厂应尽力协助成年工人接受教育。教育时间应定在工作时间之外。
第三十七条. 女工在分娩前后应给予八周假期。工作满六个月以上的女工，应给予全额工资。工作不满六个月者，仅有权获得百分之五十的工资。
第三十八条. 工厂应在其能力范围内，在储蓄、合作社等方面为工人提供一切协助。

LABOUR

Article 39. A factory shall, within its power, construct
houses for workers and provide proper amusements for them.
Article 40. Should a factory possess a surplus at the end of
a year's business, it shall, after paying a dividend to
its shareholders, grant workers, who have not committed
any fault throughout the year, a reward or distribute
any surplus among them.

CHAPTER EIGHT. SAFETY AND SANITARY ARRANGEMENTS IN A FACTORY.

Article 41. A factory shall provide the undermentioned
arrangements for safety:-
A) Safety arrangements for workers.
B) Structural safety of a factory.
C) Safety arrangements for fixing of engines.
D) Safety arrangements against fire, water, etc.
Article 42. A factory shall provide the following sanitary
arrangements:-
A) Fresh air.
B) Clean food.
C) Washing places and lavatories.
D) Lighting.
E) Arrangements against poisonous materials.
Article 43. A factory shall train workers to guard against
any incident.
Article 44. When a control organ regards the safety or
sanitation arrangements in a factory as imperfect, it may
set a time limit for the introduction of improvements.
The control organ may also prohibit the use of any part of
the factory if necessary.

CHAPTER NINE. WORKERS' ALLOWANCES AND PENSION.

Article 45. Until the Labour Insurance Law is enforced,
a factory shall issue medical grants and pensions to workers
who are injured or who die when carrying out their duties.
The scale of such medical grants and pensions will be as
follows:-
A) In addition to paying medical expenses, a factory shall
issue a daily allowance of two-thirds of the average
amount of wages to workers who are incapacitated because
of injuries. Should any injured worker fail to
recover his health after a period of 6 months, this
allowance may be reduced by 50 per cent. The period
for the issue of such allowance is limited to one year.
B) A factory shall issue an allowance to crippled workers
who are permanently deprived of the use of the whole
or a part of their working power as a result of injuries.
The amount of such allowance will depend upon the
condition of the injured part. The maximum amount of
such allowance shall not exceed the average wage of a
worker for 3 years and the minimum amount shall not be
less than the average wage for a year.
C) Besides issuing $50 to a deceased worker as his funeral
expenses, a factory shall allow a compassionate grant of

第三十九条。工厂应在其能力范围内，为工人建造住房，并提供适当的娱乐设施。
第四十条。若工厂在年终营业后有盈余，在向股东支付股息后，应向全年无过失的工人发放奖励，或将盈余分发给工人。

第八章。工厂的安全与卫生安排。

第四十一条。工厂应提供下列安全安排：
A) 工人的安全安排。
B) 工厂的结构安全。
C) 发动机安装的安全安排。
D) 防火、防水等安全安排。
第四十二条。工厂应提供下列卫生安排：
A) 新鲜空气。
B) 清洁食物。
C) 洗漱处和厕所。
D) 照明。
E) 防毒材料安排。
第四十三条。工厂应培训工人以防范任何事故。
第四十四条。当主管机关认为工厂的安全或卫生安排不完善时，可设定限期进行改进。如有必要，主管机关也可禁止使用工厂的任何部分。

第九章。工人津贴与养老金。

第四十五条。在《劳工保险法》实施之前，工厂应向在执行职务时受伤或死亡的工人发放医疗补助和抚恤金。此类医疗补助和抚恤金的标准如下：
A) 除支付医疗费用外，工厂应向因伤丧失劳动能力的工人发放相当于平均工资三分之二的每日津贴。若受伤工人在6个月后仍未恢复健康，此津贴可减少50%。此类津贴的发放期限限于一年。
B) 工厂应向因伤永久丧失全部或部分劳动能力的残疾工人发放津贴。此类津贴的金额将视受伤部位的情况而定。此类津贴的最高金额不得超过工人三年的平均工资，最低金额不得少于一年的平均工资。
C) 除向死者发放50元作为丧葬费外，工厂还应向其家属发放一笔

Afternoon Translation

LABOUR

$300 to his relatives as well as a sum equivalent to
two years' average wage of the deceased. This average
shall be calculated on the basis of the average wage
earned by the deceased during the last 3 months.
Funeral expenses and the compassionate grant will be
issued in one payment, but allowances for sickness
and injuries may be paid in several instalments.
A factory whose capital is less than $50,000 may petition
the control organ for a deduction of the amount.
Article 46. Only the wife or husband of a worker can receive
the above compassionate grant. A worker who has no wife
or husband may be issued the compassionate grant in the
following ways: — if there be no will:—
A) Son or daughter.
B) Father or mother.
C) Grandson.
D) Blood brother or sister.
Article 47. A worker may request his factory to advance
not more than one month's wages or for the payment of the
whole or a part of his savings, when he needs money for
marriage, funeral or for other big events.
Article 48. A factory shall submit to the control organ
within five days a report on the circumstances and the
measures taken in any incident involving the death of,
or serious injury to, a worker.

CHAPTER TEN. FACTORY MEETINGS.

Article 49. A conference shall be organised to be attended
by an equal number of factory representatives and workers.
The factory representatives will be those who are well
acquainted with the condition of the factory and of
workers. The control organ shall be petitioned to detail
deputies to supervise the election of labour representatives.
Article 50. The duties of a factory conference are as
follows:—
A) To study an increase in the working speed.
B) To improve the relations between a factory and its
workers and to solve any disputes that may arise
between them.
C) To assist in the enforcement of the agreements of
public bodies, of labour agreements and of the factory
regulations.
D) To negotiate over questions of increasing working hours.
E) To improve the safety and sanitary arrangements.
F) To suggest improvements in the condition of a factory
or work shop.
G) To devise matters of benefit to workers.
Article 51. The question of the work shop mentioned in
one of the Clauses of Article 50 shall be dealt with at
the very beginning by representatives of the workers
of the work shop and the management of the factory.
A factory conference shall settle any dispute over
matters relating to the work shop. In case the dispute
can not be settled by the factory conference, the

300元的抚恤金，以及相当于死者两年平均工资的款项。该平均工资应按死者最后三个月的平均工资计算。丧葬费和抚恤金将一次性发放，但病假和工伤津贴可分期支付。资本少于50,000元的工厂可向主管机关申请减免金额。
第四十六条。只有工人的妻子或丈夫才能领取上述抚恤金。没有妻子或丈夫的工人，可按以下方式发放抚恤金：若无遗嘱：—
A) 儿子或女儿。
B) 父亲或母亲。
C) 孙子。
D) 亲兄弟姐妹。
第四十七条。工人在因结婚、丧葬或其他重大事件需要资金时，可请求工厂预支不超过一个月的工资，或支付其全部或部分储蓄。
第四十八条。工厂应在发生涉及工人死亡或重伤的任何事故后五天内，向主管机关提交关于事故情况及所采取措施的报告。

第十章。工厂会议。

第四十九条。应组织一个由同等数量的工厂代表和工人参加的会议。工厂代表应是熟悉工厂和工人状况的人员。应请求主管机关派遣代表监督劳工代表的选举。
第五十条。工厂会议的职责如下：—
A) 研究提高工作速度。
B) 改善工厂与工人之间的关系，并解决双方可能出现的任何纠纷。
C) 协助执行公共机构协议、劳工协议及工厂规章。
D) 就增加工作时间的问题进行谈判。
E) 改善安全和卫生安排。
F) 对工厂或车间的状况提出改进建议。
G) 策划有利于工人的事项。
第五十一条。第五十条某款中提到的车间问题，应首先由车间工人代表和工厂管理层处理。工厂会议应解决有关车间事项的任何纠纷。若工厂会议无法解决纠纷，则

November 22, 1932.
Afternoon Translation.

LABOUR

controversy shall be dealt with in accordance with
Regulations governing measures for the settlement of
disputes between labour and capital.
Article 52. A worker reaching the age of 16 possesses the
right to elect a representative of workers.
Article 53. Chinese workers who have reached the age of
20 and who have worked for more than 6 months in a factory,
have the right to be elected as representatives of workers.
Article 54. The number of representatives of workers and
of a factory to attend a factory conference is limited
from 3 to 9 for each side.
Article 55. Representatives of workers and of a factory will
each appoint a chairman to the factory conference, who
will occupy the chair by turn. Two meetings of the
factory conference will be held in a month, but emergency
meetings may be convoked if absolutely necessary.
A meeting of a factory conference must have over 50 per
cent of representatives present. A resolution can not
be passed without the approval of more than two-thirds
of the representatives present.

CHAPTER ELEVEN. APPRENTICES.

Article 56. When a factory accepts an apprentice, it shall
enter into a contract with the apprentice or his legal
representative. Three copies of the contract are required,
two to be kept by each side and the third to be sent to
the control organ for record. The contract shall embody
the following points:-
A) Sex, age, native place and address of an apprentice.
B) Number of trades to be learned.
C) Date of the signing; and the duration of the contract.
D) Obligations of both parties.
This contract must not contain any restrictions on the
freedom of the apprentice to conduct business when the
term of the apprenticeship expires.
Article 57. Children of both sexes under 12 years of age
shall not be engaged as apprentices except in the cases
where children had become apprenticed prior to the
enforcement of this Law.
Article 58. The duration of an apprenticeship shall be
defined according to Chapter 3 of this Law.
Article 59. Apart from learning trades, an apprentice must
not undertake the different kinds of work mentioned in
Article 7 of this Law.
Article 60. An apprentice shall obey the orders of his
trainer and carry out his duties faithfully and diligently.
Article 61. A factory shall not only pay for the lodging,
food and medicine of its apprentices during the period
of their training, but also issue an appropriate allowance
to them. The scale of this allowance will be drafted by
the control organ concerned according to the conditions
in the district and the economic situation of the factory
and will be submitted to the Ministry of Industry for
sanction.

劳工

争议应按照关于解决劳资纠纷措施的规定进行处理。
第五十二条。年满16岁的工人拥有选举工人代表的权利。
第五十三条。年满20岁且在工厂工作超过6个月的中国工人，有被选为工人代表的权利。
第五十四条。参加工厂会议的工人代表和工厂代表的人数，每方限制在3至9人之间。
第五十五条。工人代表和工厂代表将各指定一名工厂会议主席，轮流主持。工厂会议每月举行两次，但在绝对必要时可召开紧急会议。工厂会议必须有超过50%的代表出席。决议未经超过三分之二出席代表批准，不得通过。

第十一章。学徒。

第五十六条。工厂招收学徒时，应与学徒或其法定代理人签订合同。合同需一式三份，双方各执一份，第三份送交主管机关备案。合同应包含以下要点：
A) 学徒的性别、年龄、籍贯和地址。
B) 学习的工种数量。
C) 签订日期；以及合同期限。
D) 双方的义务。
本合同不得包含任何限制学徒在学徒期满后进行从业自由的条款。
第五十七条。除在本法实施前已成为学徒的儿童外，不得雇用12岁以下的男女儿童为学徒。
第五十八条。学徒期限应根据本法第三章规定确定。
第五十九条。除学习手艺外，学徒不得从事本法第七条所述的各种工作。
第六十条。学徒应服从训练员的命令，忠实勤勉地履行职责。
第六十一条。工厂不仅应在学徒培训期间支付其食宿和医药费用，还应向其发放适当的津贴。此津贴标准将由相关主管机关根据地区情况和工厂经济状况起草，并提交实业部批准。

THE REVISED FACTORY LAW.
(Continued from yesterday)

Article 62. Except in special cases, an apprentice is not allowed to leave a factory during the period of his apprenticeship. Should an apprentice disappear from a factory without the approval of the management, he or his legal representative shall repay the allowances for food, lodging and medicine which the management had spent for the apprentice during his stay in the factory.
Article 63. A factory shall not engage apprentices in the xxxxxxxx excess of one-third of the number of ordinary workers.
Article 64. When a factory engages too many apprentices, the control organ may order a reduction of the number and fix the maximum number that may be engaged by the factory.
Article 65. A factory shall instruct trainers to do their utmost to teach apprentices during their apprenticeship and to direct them according to the trades mentioned in their contracts.
Article 66. A factory may terminate the contract of an apprentice on the following grounds other than for the reasons in the various Clauses of Article 31:-
a) Disobedience by an apprentice to proper direction.
b) Acts of larceny by an apprentice and his repeated disregard of warnings.
Article 67. Besides the various Clauses of Article 33, an apprentice or his legal representative may terminate his contract in the following cases:-
a) Failure of a factory to carry out its obligations as stipulated in the contract.
b) Acts on the part of a factory which may endanger the health or the conduct of an apprentice.

CHAPTER TWELVE. FINES.

Article 68. A factory is liable to a fine of more than $100 but less than $500 in case of violation of Articles 7, 11, 12 and 13 of this Law.
Article 69. A fine of more than $50 but less than $300 will be imposed upon a factory for contravention of Articles 5, 8, 9, 10, 37 and 63 of this Law.
Article 70. A factory will be fined over $50 but less than $200 for violation of Article 45 of this Law.
Article 71. A factory will be fined a sum below $100 should it infringe Articles 3, 4, 14 to 19 and 36 of this Law.

Article 72. A foreman of a factory who fails to execute his duties faithfully or causes an untoward incident or aggravates the incident because of his laziness is liable to an imprisonment of less than one year or to a fine of not more than $500.
Article 73. A worker who obstructs the operations of a factory by force or who damages the goods or furniture of a factory will be punished according to law.
Article 74. A worker will be punished according to law in case he threatens or compels by violence anybody to go on strike. ,

修订工厂法。
（接昨日）

第六十二条。除特殊情况外，学徒在学徒期间不得离开工厂。若学徒未经管理层批准从工厂失踪，他或其法定代理人应偿还管理层在该学徒留厂期间为其支付的食宿和医药津贴。
第六十三条。工厂雇用的学徒人数不得超过普通工人人数的三分之一。（原文不清）
第六十四条。当工厂雇用过多学徒时，主管机关可命令减少人数，并规定工厂可雇用的最高人数。
第六十五条。工厂应指示训练员在学徒期间尽力教导学徒，并根据合同中提到的工种指导他们。
第六十六条。除第三十一条各款所述原因外，工厂可基于以下理由终止学徒合同：
a) 学徒不服从正当指导。
b) 学徒有盗窃行为且屡教不改。
第六十七条。除第三十三条各款外，学徒或其法定代理人在以下情况下可终止合同：
a) 工厂未能履行合同规定的义务。
b) 工厂方面有危及学徒健康或品行的行为。

第十二章。罚款。

第六十八条。工厂若违反本法第七、十一、十二和十三条，须处以100元以上500元以下的罚款。
第六十九条。工厂若违反本法第五、八、九、十、三十七和六十三条，须处以50元以上300元以下的罚款。
第七十条。工厂若违反本法第四十五条，须处以50元以上200元以下的罚款。
第七十一条。工厂若侵犯本法第三、四、十四至十九和三十六条，须处以100元以下的罚款。

第七十二条。工厂领班若不忠实履行职责，或因懒惰导致不幸事故或加重事故后果，须处以一年以下监禁或500元以下罚款。
第七十三条。工人若以武力阻碍工厂运营，或损坏工厂货物或家具，将依法惩处。
第七十四条。工人若威胁或以暴力强迫任何人罢工，将依法惩处。

AMENDED REGULATIONS GOVERNING ENFORCEMENT OF REVISED FACTORY
LAW.

At a meeting held recently by the Legislative
Council, the following amended Regulations governing the
enforcement of the Revised Factory Law were passed:-
Article 1. The workers described in Article 1 of the Revised
Factory Law are those who directly undertake work of
production or to supplement production. Employees or
workers who have no connection with the work of production
are not included.
Article 5. A factory shall send a petition to the control
organ within two months after the enforcement of the
Revised Factory Law for permission to retain the male and
female child workers over 12 years of age but under 14
years, who had been in the employ of the factory prior to
the promulgation of the Revised Factory Law. The petition
shall contain a worker's name, sex, age, native place,
date of entry into the factory, and nature of work.
Article 8. A factory which adopts a system of day and night
shift work shall provide a book for the registration of
the names, sexes, ages, date and the hours of work of the
shifts.
Article 9. The anniversary days mentioned in Article 16 of
the Revised Factory Law are:-
a) January 1, the anniversary of the establishment of the
Republic of China.
b) March 12, the anniversary of the death of the late
Dr. Sun Yat-sen.
c) March 29, the anniversary of the execution of 72 victims
of the Kwangtung Uprising.
d) May 1, Labour Day.
e) May 5, the anniversary of the inauguration of the
Chinese Revolutionary Government.
f) July 9, the anniversary of the commencement of the Anti-
Northern Expedition.
g) October 10, the National Holiday.
h) November 12, the anniversary of the birth of the late
Dr. Sun Yat-sen.
i) All other holidays that may be specially designated
by the National Government.
Article 20. A factory which employs female workers shall
provide a room for workers to suckle babies, and if within
its power, the factory shall also establish a house for
the shelter of babies and engage nurses to care for them.

Sir,
New National Factory Law
It is of great importance in the interests of
the Municipal Council and smooth working with the
Chinese Authorities that the enforcement of all
Chinese national and bureaucratic laws applicable
to Chinese residents in the Settlement should be
entrusted to the Municipal Police or some other body
of employees directly responsible to the Council.
There are clauses in the new National Factory Law
which imply that its enforcement will be undertaken
by the Municipality of Greater Shanghai. Until these
clauses are either cancelled or interpreted in a
manner satisfactory to the Municipal Council, the
application of the new National Factory Law to
concerns in the Settlement should not even be
considered.
There are, in addition to the objectionable
articles already mentioned, in the new National
Factory Law unpractical clauses which, if enforced,
would lead to strikes, lockouts and unemployment and
the disturbances of the public peace which are an
inevitable accompaniment of these conditions. In
order to make the law suitable for enforcement in

先生，
新国家工厂法
出于工部局的利益以及与中国当局顺利合作的需要，将所有适用于租界内中国居民的中国国家法律及行政法令的执行权，委托给市政警察或其他直接向工部局负责的雇员机构，至关重要。
新的国家工厂法中有些条款暗示，其执行将由大上海市政府承担。在这些条款被取消或以工部局满意的方式予以解释之前，甚至不应考虑将新国家工厂法适用于租界内的企业。
除了上述令人反感的条款外，新的国家工厂法中还有一些不切实际的条款，如果强制执行，将导致罢工、闭厂和失业，以及随之必然发生的扰乱公共治安的行为。为了使该法适合在

been copied from the laws of Soviet Russia, should
be either cancelled or considerably modified.

regards the method of the enforcement of the law are :-

J.K. Shieno

REGULATIONS BEARING ON THE FACTORY LAW
PROMULGATED 16th DECEMBER 1930
EFFECTIVE FROM 1st FEBRUARY 1931.

Art.1 These regulations are made in pursuance of Art.76 of the
Factory Law.
Art.2 The authorities concerned in the enforcement of the Factory
Law and provisions of these regulations, are subject to the
direction and supervision of the highest competent authority.
Art.3 A factory shall keep record books as prescribed in Articles
3 & 4 of the Factory Law; it shall submit a copy of the re-
cords to the competent authority at regular periods, and see
that the originals are duly preserved.
The register of names of workers and other books of record
and tables shall be in the form prescribed by the highest
competent authority.
Art.4 Before the promulgation of the Law of Census, if any doubt
arises as to the age of a worker employed in a factory, the
legal agent of the worker shall be responsible for proof of
age.
Art.5 A factory shall, within two months after the enforcement of
the Factory Law, submit the names, native place, age, date
of entering the factory, nature and kind of work engaged in,
of all persons under the age of 14 but over 12 years employed
by the factory before the promulgation of the Factory Law
to the competent authority for sanction to reduce the
admission age.
Art.6 If the working hours be prolonged in accordance with articles
8 & 10 of the Factory Law, the factory shall report the rea-
sons therefor in detail to the competent authority.
Art.7 A factory shall publish the time for beginning and ending
work, for taking meals and for rest during the day, also
the holidays throughout the year.
Art.8 In cases where a factory adopts the system of day and night
shifts, it shall enter the names of workers and the date and

Art. 16 A factory shall adopt the plan of either issuing bonuses or
distributing a share of the profits, as prescribed in Art.
40 of the Factory Law; whichever plan is adopted it shall
be stated in the factory regulations.
Factories established prior to the enforcement of the
Factory Law shall submit the plan adopted in accordance with

Art. 17 Factories employing ordinarily more than 300 workers shall
provide on the premises a room supplied with medicines for
urgent cases, and shall employ physicians to attend daily
at the factory to give medical aid and to watch over the
health of workers.

Art. 18 The apportioning of work among child-workers, females and
workers over 50 years of age shall be decided on after the
condition of their health has been enquired into.

Art. 19 No children shall be admitted into any place where articles
of a dangerous nature or injurious to health are manufac-

Art. 20 Factories employing female workers shall, whenever possible
establish a nursery and employ nurses to take charge of
infants.

Art. 21 The buildings of a factory shall be designed by registered
architects in accordance with the provisions of Articles 40
and 42 of the Factory Law.

Art. 22 All machinery and boilers in a factory shall, before being
used, or after use, be examined at fixed intervals by experts
to ensure their efficiency. If found to be unsafe, they shall
not be put into use until after repairs or replacements have
been made.

Art. 23 Factory buildings and their annexes shall be provided with
the requisite number of exits or fire escapes.

Art. 24 The doors of working places shall open outwards and shall
not be locked during working hours.

第十六条。工厂应按照《工厂法》第四十条之规定，采用发放奖金或分配利润红利的计划；无论采用何种计划，均应在工厂规章中注明。
在《工厂法》施行前设立的工厂，应在该法施行后两个月内，将依照前款采用的计划提交主管机关。

第十七条。通常雇用工人超过三百名的工厂，应在厂区内提供一间配备急救药品的房间，并聘请医生每日到厂提供医疗援助并监护工人健康。

第十八条。童工、女工及五十岁以上工人的工作分配，应在查问其健康状况后决定。

第十九条。任何制造危险性质或有害健康物品的场所，不得招收儿童进入。

第二十条。雇用女工的工厂，应尽可能设立托儿所，并聘请保姆照料婴儿。

第二十一条。工厂建筑应按照《工厂法》第四十及四十二条之规定，由注册建筑师设计。

第二十二条。工厂内所有机器和锅炉，在使用前或使用后，应由专家定期检查以确保其效能。如发现不安全，在修理或更换之前不得使用。

第二十三条。工厂建筑及其附属设施应配备必要数量的出口或消防逃生通道。

第二十四条。工作场所的门应向外开启，且在工作时间内不得上锁。

Art. 26 Where a factory comes under one of the following conditio...:

第二十五条 厂内严禁吸烟及携带易燃物品。
第二十六条 凡工厂具备下列情形之一者，其厂房及附属建筑物之地址须经主管官署核准：
1. 所制造之物品及所用之原料具有危险性者。
2. 制造过程中产生之气体或液体有害于公共卫生者。
第二十七条 制造过程中产生之有毒气体、液体或其他物质，工厂应依其性质及数量予以过滤、净化或溶解处理；不得倾弃于河流、溪涧、池塘或井中。
第二十八条 工人在工作时间内受伤或患病时，工厂应请医师诊治或送医院治疗。如有死亡情事，工厂应立即向主管官署报告，并通知死者家属。
第二十九条 工厂法第四十五条规定之津贴、丧葬费、抚恤金等，工厂应按下列方式支付给工人：
1. 受伤或残废工人之津贴，至少每半月支付一次。
2. 丧葬费应于工人死亡之次日，一次性支付给其家属。
3. 工厂法第四十六条规定之抚恤金，应于工人死亡后一个月内支付给受益人。
第三十条 工厂应记录医疗津贴、丧葬费、抚恤金等之支付日期、金额及受领人姓名。
第三十一条 如对丧葬费或抚恤金之合法受领人有疑义时，受领人应觅具保人。

The election of representatives of workers for the first

第一届工人代表之选举，应在工厂拟定选举计划并于工厂法施行后两个月内提交主管官署核准后进行。
若工厂已成立工会，前项所述之选举计划应由工会签署并附具意见。

第三十三条 在选举工人代表时，应选举五至九名候补代表，以便在正式代表无法出席工厂委员会会议时代替出席。
第三十四条 工人代表之选举办法，应于选举前三日在工厂内显眼处张贴公告公布，并至少在选举前向工人口头解释一次。
第三十五条 工厂委员会中工人代表之任期为一年，但可连选连任。
第三十六条 工厂应将代表及全厂工人名单提交主管官署备案。重新委任及重选时亦同。

and shall at every meeting of the Council appoint a secre-
tary to record the following particulars :-
1. Date and place of meeting.

第三十七条 工厂应备置工厂委员会会议记录簿，并于每次会议时指定一名秘书记录下列事项：
1. 会议日期及地点。
2. 出席会议之代表、主席及秘书姓名。
3. 讨论内容及决议。
4. 其他报告及建议。
会议结束前，主席应向会议宣读会议记录，并签名盖章。

Subject (in full) The New National Factory Law.

Made by and Forwarded by C. D. I. Robertson.

The perusal of the new Factory Law, promulgated
by the National Government on December 30, 1930, and
scheduled to become effective from August 1, 1931, leaves
the impression that the code has been drafted for the
sole benefit of the employee, that the interests of the
employer have been entirely ignored and that the promul-
gation of the Law is intended to make the profitable
existence of an industrial concern an impossibility.

The following articles directly concern the
police in so far as they challenge the authority of the
Council in police matters.

Chapter I. General Provisions

Article 2 : Unless specially provided, the term "proper
authority" in this Law shall mean the
Municipal Government in municipalities
(shih) and the District Authority in
districts (hsien).

Article 4 : Every six months each factory shall submit
to the proper authority copies of the
following documents :-
(1) The book of records.
(2) The records of sickness and treatment given.
(3) The records of accidents and the measures
taken.
(4) The records of disengagement of the
workers and the reasons for same.

Chapter 4. Rest and Holidays

Article 19: All workers engaged in work of a military nature
or in public service may not be given the
rest days and holidays, if the proper authority
considers it necessity.

Chapter 5. Wages

Article 20: The fixing of the minimum wage rate of the
workers shall be based upon the conditions and
the standards of living in the different
localities where the factories are established.

Chapter 8. Safety and Health

Article 44: Whenever the safety and health provisions of

主题（全称） 新国家工厂法。

撰写及呈报人 C. D. I. Robertson。

阅毕国民政府于1930年12月30日公布、定于1931年8月1日生效的新《工厂法》后，给人的印象是，该法典的起草 solely 为了雇员利益，完全忽视了雇主利益，且颁布该法的意图在于使工业企业有利可图的生存成为不可能。

以下条款因挑战工部局在警务事项上的权威，而直接涉及警方。

第一章 总则

第二条：除非另有特别规定，本法所称“主管官署”，在市（shih）指市政府，在县（hsien）指县政府。

第四条：各工厂每六个月应向主管官署提交下列文件副本：
(1) 登记簿。
(2) 疾病及诊疗记录。
(3) 事故及所采取措施的记录。
(4) 工人解雇及其原因的记录。

第四章 休息与休假

第十九条：凡从事军事性质工作或公共服务之工人，如主管官署认为有必要，可不给予休息日及假日。

第五章 工资

第二十条：确定工人最低工资率，应以工厂所在地之不同地区的生活条件及生活标准为依据。

第八章 安全与卫生

第四十四条：凡工厂之安全与卫生规定不足时，

Chapter 9 : Allowance and Compensation

Article 45 : Before the enforcement of social insurance
laws, for workers who become sick or are
injured or who lose their lives through the
performance of their duty, the factory shall
bear their medical expenses and shall pay
allowances or compensations according to the
following standards. In case the capital
of a factory is less than fifty-thousand
dollars, smaller amounts may be paid with
the approval of the proper authority.
(1) To workers temporarily disabled either
through injury or sickness the factory
shall, besides bearing their medical
expenses, pay allowances amounting to
two-thirds of their regular daily wages
for a period of six months, and upon the
expiration of that period, if the workers
have still not recovered, amounting to
half of the regular daily wages. Such
payments shall only be made for the
period of one year.
(2) To workers permanently disabled either
entirely or in part, through injury or
sickness, the factory shall pay allowances
in proportion to the loss of earning
capacity. The maximum amount of such
allowances shall, however, not exceed the
average wages for three years and the
minimum amount shall not be less than
the average wages for one year.
(3) To the legal heirs of the workers who
lose their lives the factory shall,
besides giving fifty dollars for funeral
expenses, pay compensations amounting to
300 dollars and two years' average wages.
The said average wages shall be calculated
on the basis of the wages for the last
three months.
The funeral expenses and compensations shall
be paid in a lump sum, while allowances for
injury, sickness and disability may be paid
by installments.

Article 48 : Should an accident occur in a factory resulting
in death or serious injury to a worker, the
employer shall report within five days to
the proper authority its occurrence and
measures consequently taken.

第九章 津贴与抚恤

第四十五条：在社会保险法施行之前，对于因执行职务而患病、受伤或死亡的工人，工厂应承担其医疗费用，并按下列标准支付津贴或抚恤金。若工厂资本少于五万元，经主管官署批准，可支付较少金额。
(1) 对于因伤或病暂时残废之工人，工厂除承担其医疗费用外，应在六个月内支付相当于其正常日工资三分之二的津贴；期满若仍未康复，则支付相当于正常日工资一半的津贴。此类支付期限仅为一年。
(2) 对于因伤或病导致全部或部分永久残废之工人，工厂应按丧失劳动能力之比例支付津贴。但此类津贴最高不得超过三年平均工资，最低不得少于一年平均工资。
(3) 对于死亡工人之法定继承人，工厂除给付五十元丧葬费外，还应支付三百元及两年平均工资之抚恤金。上述平均工资按最后三个月之工资计算。
丧葬费及抚恤金应一次性支付，而工伤、疾病及残废津贴可分期支付。

第四十八条：工厂发生事故致工人死亡或重伤时，雇主应于五日内向主管官署报告事故发生情况及随后采取的措施。

Chapter 10. Factory Councils.

Article 49 : Factory councils shall be composed of equal
numbers of representatives of the employers
and the workers. The employers' repre-
sentatives shall be selected by the employers
from those who are familiar with the conditions
of the factory, and the conditions of the
workers, while the workers' representatives
shall be elected by the employees from among
their fellow-workers in the same factory,
under the supervision of the proper authority,
who should be duly notified.

Article 51 : When a dispute arises in a factory, it shall
first be referred to the factory council,
should the council fail to effect a solution,
then it shall be settled in accordance with
the law of Conciliation and Arbitration of
of Labour Disputes.

Chapter 11. Apprenticeship.

Article 56 : Factories taking apprentices shall conclude
contracts either with the apprentices them-
selves, or with their legal guardians. Each
contract shall be written in triplicates,
one copy for each of the contracting parties,
and the remaining copy to be submitted to the
proper authority for registration. The
said contract shall contain the following
particulars :-
(1) The name, age, native place and address
of the apprentice;
(2) The nature of work for which the apprentice
is to be trained;
(3) The date of the conclusion of the contract
and the duration of same;
(4) Mutual obligations; in case premium is
stipulate, the amount of same and the
time of payment; in case remuneration is
to be given the apprentice, the amount
of same and the time of payment.

Article 64 : If the number of apprentices in a factory is
excessive, so that adequate training cannot
be provided, the proper authority may order
a reduction in the number or fix the maximum
number of apprentices in the factory thereafter.

Article 66 : The provisions of Section 31 apply to apprentices,
and the factory may terminate the contract
under any one of the following conditions :-
(1) When apprentices revolt against proper
instructions.

第十章 工厂委员会。

第四十九条：工厂委员会由同等数量的雇主代表和工人代表组成。雇主代表由雇主从熟悉工厂情况及工人状况的人员中选派，工人代表则由同一工厂内的员工在主管官署监督下从其同事中选举产生，并应适时通知主管官署。

第五十一条：工厂发生争议时，应首先提交工厂委员会处理；若委员会未能解决，则依照《劳资争议调解仲裁法》处理。

第十一章 学徒制。

第五十六条：招收学徒之工厂，应与学徒本人或其法定监护人签订合同。每份合同应一式三份，缔约各方各执一份，剩余一份提交主管官署登记。该合同应包含下列事项：
(1) 学徒之姓名、年龄、籍贯及住址；
(2) 学徒受训之工作性质；
(3) 合同签订日期及期限；
(4) 双方义务；如规定有押金，应注明金额及支付时间；如规定给予学徒报酬，应注明金额及支付时间。

第六十四条：若工厂学徒人数过多，以致无法提供充分培训，主管官署可命令减少人数或规定此后工厂学徒之最高限额。

第六十六条：第三十一条之规定适用于学徒，工厂可在下列任一情况下终止合同：
(1) 当学徒不服从正当指导时。

Chapter 12. Penalties.

Article 68 : Factories which violate any of the provisions
of Section 7, 11, 12 and 13 of this Law shall
be liable to a fine amounting to not less
then 100 and not more than 500 dollars.

Article 69 : Factories, which violate any of the provisions
of Section 5, 8, 9, 10, 37 and 63 of this Law
shall be liable to a fine amounting to not
less than 50 and not more than 300 dollars.

Article 70 : Factories, which violate any of the provisions
of Section 45 of this Law shall be liable to
a fine amounting to not less than 50 and not
more than 200 dollars.

Article 71 : Factories, which violate any of the provisions
of Section 3, 4, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 and
36 of this Law shall be liable to a fine
amounting to not more than 100 dollars.

Article 72 : Should trouble or misfortune occur or become
enlarged on account of unfaithfulness or
negligence on the part of foremen, they
shall be liable to imprisonment for a period
of not more than a year, or a fine amounting
to not more than 500 dollars.

Article 73 : Any worker who obstructs the operation of
a factory or destroys the goods and assets
of the factory by means of violence shall
be punished in accordance with the maximum
penal provisions of the criminal law.

Article 74 : Any worker who compels other workers to
strike by force may be immediately discharged
by the employer and handed over to proper
authority for punishment in accordance with
law.

Chapter 13. Appendix.

Article 75 : A factory's regulations and their amendment
shall be approved and promulgated by the
proper authority.

Each of the above articles, with the exception
of Article 20 and those articles contained in Chapter 12,

第十二章。处罚。

第六十八条：凡违反本法第七、十一、十二及十三条任何规定之工厂，应处以不少于一百元且不超过五百元之罚款。

第六十九条：凡违反本法第五、八、九、十、三十七及六十三条任何规定之工厂，应处以不少于五十元且不超过三百元之罚款。

第七十条：凡违反本法第四十五条任何规定之工厂，应处以不少于五十元且不超过二百元之罚款。

第七十一条：凡违反本法第三、四、十四、十五、十六、十七、十八、十九及三十六条任何规定之工厂，应处以不超过一百元之罚款。

第七十二条：若因领班之不忠或疏忽而导致事故或灾祸发生或扩大，其应被判处不超过一年之监禁，或处以不超过五百元之罚款。

第七十三条：任何工人以暴力手段阻碍工厂运营或毁坏工厂货物及资产者，应按刑法最高刑罚规定予以惩处。

第七十四条：任何工人以武力强迫其他工人罢工者，雇主可立即将其解雇，并移交主管当局依法惩处。

第十三章。附则。

refer in some way or other to the power invested in the

and is clearly indicative of the fact that in enforcing

Articles Nos. 68, 69, 70, 71, 72, 73 and 74

encroachment on police authority and suggests bureau-

penalties are provided and as no court is mentioned it
is surmised that in accordance with article 74 the body
competent to assume jurisdiction is the "Proper Authorities",
i.e. the Chinese Authorities.

In pursuance of Article 76 of the Factory Law
are the Regulations Bearing on the Factory Law, promulgated
on December 16, 1930 and effective from the date of
the Factory Law coming into force.

While no mention is made in the Regulations
of the "Proper Authorities", Article 2 reads :
"The authorities concerned in the enforcement of the Factory
Law and provisions of these regulations, are subject to
the direction and supervision of the highest competent
authority."

第六十八、六十九、七十、七十一、七十二、七十三及七十四条（关于处罚部分）显示出侵蚀警察权力的明显意图，并暗示了官僚式的运作。在这些条款中规定了某些处罚，由于未提及法院，据推测，根据第七十四条，有权行使管辖权的机构是“主管当局”，即中国当局。

虽然《细则》中未提及“主管当局”，但第二条规定：“负责执行《工厂法》及本细则规定之有关机关，受最高主管机关之指挥与监督。”

除了《细则》第二条外，从警察角度来看，以下条款也很重要，并有助于揭露中国当局试图在租界内获得更稳固立足点的坚定努力：

第三条：工厂应按照《工厂法》第三及第四条的规定保存记录簿；应定期向主管机关提交记录副本，并确保原件得到妥善保存。工人花名册及其他记录簿和表格应采用最高主管机关规定的格式。

第四条：在《户口普查法》颁布之前，如果对工厂雇佣工人的年龄产生任何疑问，该工人的法定代理人应负责证明其年龄。

第五条：工厂应在《工厂法》施行后两个月内，将《工厂法》颁布前工厂雇佣的所有年龄在十二岁以上、十四岁以下人员的姓名、籍贯、年龄、进厂日期、工作性质及种类，提交主管机关核准，以降低录用年龄。

第六条：如果根据《工厂法》第八及第十条延长工作时间，工厂应向主管机关详细报告其原因。

第十二条：如果工厂完全或部分停止运营，或停工超过一个月，应事先向主管机关报告此事。

第十三条：如果对工人和学徒进行补充指导，工厂应将方案及拟议设备提交主管机关，此后每六个月报告一次情况。

第十六条：工厂应采用《工厂法》第四十条规定的发放奖金或分配利润份额的计划之一；无论采用哪种计划，均应在工厂规章中说明。在《工厂法》施行前设立的工厂，应在《工厂法》施行后两个月内，将按照前节采用的计划提交主管机关。

第三十二条：工厂委员会中的工人代表应在出席人数超过工厂工人总数百分之五十的会议上选举产生。如果工厂各部门距离过远，或部门工人人数过多，代表名额可按各部门工人人数分配，并可分区举行选举。

page_data.en:
Factory Law.

Promulgated by the National Government of the Republic
of China on December 30th, 1929.

N. B.- The Official Version is in Chinese.

Chapter I. General Provisions.

1. This Law shall apply to all factories driven by steam,
gas, electricity or water power, regularly employing workers thirty
or more in number, (hereafter briefly called "the factory" or
"factories").

2. Unless specially provided, the term "proper authority" in
this Law shall mean the Municipal Government in municipalities
(shih) and the District Authority in districts (hsien).

3. The factory shall keep a book of records containing for
each of its workers the following particulars:-
(1) The worker's name, age, native place and address.
(2) The worker's date of entry into the factory.
(3) The worker's occupation, his hours of work and renumera-
tion.
(4) The worker's skill and conduct.
(5) The worker's efficiency.
(6) The rewards and penalties received by the worker.
(7) Diseases contracted and injuries suffered by the worker
and the causes therefor.

4. Every six months each factory shall submit to the proper
authority copies of the following documents:-
(1) The book of records.
(2) The records of sickness and treatment given.
(3) The records of accidents and the measures taken.
(4) The records of disengagement of the workers and the
reasons for same.

Chapter II. Child workers and female workers.

5. The employment of children under the age of fourteen shall
be prohibited in all factories.

Children under the said age, but over twelve years of age,
already employed in factories before the promulgation of this Law,
by consent of the proper authority, may be permitted to remain in
employment.

6. Boys and girls above the age of fourteen and below the
age of sixteen shall be considered child workers.

Child workers are permitted to be engaged only in light and
easy work.
page_data.zh:
工厂法。

由中华民国国民政府于1929年12月30日公布。

注：官方文本为中文。

第一章 总则。

第一条 本法适用于以蒸汽、煤气、电力或水力为动力，经常雇用工人三十名以上之所有工厂（以下简称“工厂”）。

第二条 除另有规定外，本法所称“主管机关”，在市级行政区指市政府，在县级行政区指县政府。

第三条 工厂应备置记录簿，记载每位工人下列事项：
(1) 工人姓名、年龄、籍贯及住址。
(2) 工人进厂日期。
(3) 工人职业、工作时间及薪酬。
(4) 工人技能及品行。
(5) 工人工作效率。
(6) 工人所受奖惩。
(7) 工人所患疾病及所受伤害及其原因。

第四条 各工厂每六个月应向主管机关提交下列文件副本：
(1) 记录簿。
(2) 患病及治疗记录。
(3) 事故及采取措施记录。
(4) 工人离职及离职原因记录。

第二章 童工及女工。

第五条 禁止所有工厂雇用未满十四岁之儿童。

上述年龄以下但已满十二岁之儿童，若在本法公布前已在工厂受雇，经主管机关同意，可准许继续受雇。

第六条 年满十四岁未满十六岁之男女，视为童工。

童工仅准从事轻便工作。

- 2 -

7. Child workers and female workers shall not be employed
in the following types of work:
(1) To handle explosive inflammable or poisonous substances.
(2) To work in places which are exposed to dust or fumes
from noxious fluids.
(3) To clean, oil, inspect, and repair machines in motion
or risky parts of power transmission agencies, and to
repair or adjust belts and ropes.
(4) To manipulate high potential wires.
(5) To handle minerals in liquid form or mineral refuse.
(6) To fire boilers.
(7) To perform other indecent or dangerous work.

Chapter III. Working Hours.

8. The regular working day for adults is eight hours; but
in case there is necessity to extend it, owing to varying local
conditions and the nature of the work, it may be fixed up to
ten hours.

9. Factories which adopt a system of day and night shifts
shall arrange the working schedule in such a way, that the shifts
for the workers may be interchanged at least once a week.

10. Besides the provisions of Section 8, in case of force
majeure, the working hours may be extended; but they shall not
exceed twelve hours a day and the total overtime work shall not
exceed thirty-six hours a month.

11. The regular working day for child workers shall under
no circumstance exceed eight hours.

12. Child workers shall not be permitted to work during the
hours between 7 o'clock in the evening and 6 o'clock the next
morning.

13. Female workers shall not be permitted to work during
the hours between 10 o'clock in the evening and 6 o'clock the next
morning.

Chapter IV. Rest and holidays.

14. Workers after working continuously for five hours shall
have a period of rest of half an hour.

15. All workers shall have one day of rest in each period
of seven days.

16. All factories shall stop work on holidays designated by
law and by order of the National Government.

17. All workers who work continuously in factories for a
definite period shall be granted a special period of rest as
follows:-
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

第七条 童工及女工不得从事下列工作：
(1) 处理爆炸性、易燃性或有毒物质。
(2) 在暴露于粉尘或有害液体烟雾之处所工作。
(3) 清洁、加油、检查运转中的机器或动力传动装置的危险部位，以及修理或调整皮带和绳索。
(4) 操作高压电线。
(5) 处理液态矿物或矿物废料。
(6) 烧锅炉。
(7) 从事其他不雅或危险的工作。

第三章 工作时间。

第八条 成人正常工作日为八小时；但因各地情况不同及工作性质需要延长时，可定为最多十小时。

第九条 实行日夜轮班制的工厂，应安排工作日程，使工人班次至少每周轮换一次。

第十条 除第八条规定外，遇有不可抗力，工作时间可予延长；但每日不得超过十二小时，每月加班总数不得超过三十六小时。

第十一条 童工正常工作日在任何情况下不得超过八小时。

第十二条 禁止童工在晚间七时至次日晨六时之间工作。

第十三条 禁止女工在晚间十时至次日晨六时之间工作。

第四章 休息与休假。

第十四条 工人连续工作五小时后，应有半小时休息时间。

第十五条 所有工人每七天应有一天休息日。

第十六条 所有工厂在法律及国民政府命令规定的假日应停止工作。

第十七条 在工厂连续工作满一定期限的所有工人，应给予特别假期如下：

page_data.en:
- 3 -

(1) All workers who work continuously for more than a year but less than 3 years shall be granted an annual rest of seven days.
(2) All workers who work continuously for more than three years but less than five years shall be granted an annual rest of ten days.
(3) All workers who work continuously for more than five years but less than ten years shall be granted an annual rest of fourteen days.
(4) All workers who work continuously for more than ten years shall be granted an annual rest of one additional day for each additional year. But the total number of annual rest days shall in no case exceed thirty days.

18. All workers shall be given their regular wages for the holidays and rest days provided in Sections 15, 16 and 17: additional wages shall be paid if they do not wish to utilize the rest days to which they are entitled.

19. All workers engaged in work of a military nature or in public service may not be given the rest days and holidays, if the proper authority considers it necessity.

Chapter V. Wages.

20. The fixing of the minimum wage rate of the workers shall be based upon the conditions and the standards of living in the different localities where the factories are established.

21. Wages shall be paid by the employers to the workers in the local legal tender.

22. Wages shall be paid regularly and at least twice a month; the payment of wages for piece work shall be made likewise.

23. Wages for overtime work as provided by Sections 10 and 19 shall be paid at the rate of one and one-third times to one and two-thirds times the ordinary wages calculated according to the hour.

24. Female workers shall be paid at the same rate of wages as male workers when they perform the same kind of work with equal efficiency.

25. Employers are not allowed to deduct in advance a part of the wages of the workers as a deposit for compensation of damages, or security for fines in case of breach of contract.

Chapter VI. Termination of Contracts.

26. Contracts shall be cancelled upon expiration of their stipulated time, but may be renewed by mutual agreement.

27. Employers desiring to cancel a contract for which no stipulation of time is made can only do so by serving to the workers a notice in advance. Unless longer period is provided in the contract the period of notice shall be as follows:-
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

(1) 连续工作一年以上未满三年者，每年给予七天假期。
(2) 连续工作三年以上未满五年者，每年给予十天假期。
(3) 连续工作五年以上未满十年者，每年给予十四天假期。
(4) 连续工作十年以上者，每增加一年增加一天年假。但年假总数在任何情况下不得超过三十天。

第十八条 所有工人在第十五、十六及十七条规定的假日和休息日应照发工资；若工人不愿使用其应享的休息日，应支付额外工资。

第十九条 凡从事军事性质工作或公共服务之工人，若主管机关认为有必要，可不给予休息日和假日。

第五章 工资。

第二十条 确定工人最低工资率，应以工厂所在地之生活状况及生活水平为依据。

第二十一条 雇主应以当地法定货币向工人支付工资。

第二十二条 工资应定期支付，每月至少两次；计件工资之支付亦同。

第二十三条 第十条及第十九条规定的加班工资，应按小时计算，以普通工资的三分之一至三分之二倍加付（即一点三倍至一点六七倍）。

第二十四条 女工若与男工从事同等工作且效率相同，应获得同等工资率。

第二十五条 雇主不得预先扣除工人部分工资作为损害赔偿押金，或作为违约罚款保证金。

第六章 合同终止。

第二十六条 合同期满即行解除，但经双方同意可续订。

第二十七条 雇主欲解除未定期限之合同，须提前通知工人。除非合同中规定了更长的期限，否则通知期如下：

page_data.en:
- 4 -

(1) To workers who have worked in the factory continuously
for more than three months but less than one year,
the period of notice shall be 10 days.
(2) To workers who have worked in the factory continuously
for more than one year but less than three years, the
period of notice shall be 20 days.
(3) To workers who have worked in the factory continuously
for more than three years the period of notice shall
be 30 days.

28. The workers after receiving the notice for the termina-
tion of contract may ask leave of absence during working hours
for the purpose of seeking employment. But the total length of
such absence shall not exceed two working days in a week. No
deduction of wages shall be made for such absence.

29. If the employers desire to terminate the contract in
accordance with Section 27, they shall give the workers, besides
their regular wages, an extra sum amounting to one half of the
regular wages for the notice period. If the employers desire to
terminate the contract immediately regardless of the provisions
of Section 27, they shall give the workers an extra sum amounting
to the regular wages for the notice period provided in the said
section.

30. The employers may terminate the employment of their
workers before the expiration of the contract under any one of
the following conditions. But notice shall be given in accord-
ance with the provision of Section 27.
(1) When a factory totally or in part suspends operation.
(2) When a factory, owing to force majeure is obliged to
suspend operation for a period of more than a month.
(3) When a worker is incapable of doing properly the work
he has undertaken.

31. The employers may terminate the employment of their
workers before the expiration of the contract without notice under
any one of the following conditions:
(1) When a worker repeatedly violates the factory's
regulations.
(2) When a worker fails to report for work without just
cause for more than three consecutive days or when
a worker absents himself more than six days within
one month.

32. If the workers desire to terminate the contract for
which no stipulation of time is made, they shall give to the
employers one week's notice.

33. The workers may terminate the contract before its
expiration without notice under any one of the following conditions:-
(1) When the employers violate the terms of contracts or
important provisions of labor laws and orders.
(2) When the employers fail to pay the wages when due with-
out just cause.
(3) When the employers assault or maltreat the workers.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

(1) 对在工厂连续工作三个月以上未满一年的工人，通知期为十天。
(2) 对在工厂连续工作一年以上未满三年的工人，通知期为二十天。
(3) 对在工厂连续工作三年以上的工人，通知期为三十天。

第二十八条 工人收到解除合同通知后，可在工作时间内请假寻找工作。但此类请假每周总计不得超过两个工作日。此类请假不得扣减工资。

第二十九条 若雇主依据第二十七条规定解除合同，除正常工资外，还应向工人支付相当于通知期内正常工资一半的额外款项。若雇主不顾第二十七条之规定立即解除合同，应向工人支付相当于该条规定之通知期内正常工资的额外款项。

第三十条 雇主在下列任一情况下，可在合同期满前终止雇用工人。但须按照第二十七条之规定给予通知。
(1) 工厂全部或部分停工时。
(2) 工厂因不可抗力被迫停工一个月以上时。
(3) 工人不能胜任其所承担的工作时。

第三十一条 雇主在下列任一情况下，可在合同期满前不经通知终止雇用工人：
(1) 工人屡次违反工厂规章时。
(2) 工人无正当理由连续旷工三天以上，或一个月内旷工超过六天时。

第三十二条 若工人欲解除未定期限之合同，应提前一周通知雇主。

第三十三条 工人在下列任一情况下，可在合同期满前不经通知解除合同：
(1) 雇主违反合同条款或劳动法律法规的重要规定时。
(2) 雇主无正当理由未按期支付工资时。
(3) 雇主殴打或虐待工人时。

page_data.en:
- 5 -

34. Disputes arising from the interpretations and applica-
tions of Paragraph 3 of Section 30 and Paragraph 1 of Section 31
and Section 33 may be referred to the Factory Council for settle-
ment.

35. Unless the workers violate the provisions of Section 32
or commit one of the offences contained in Section 31, upon the
termination of contracts they shall each be given a certificate
which should contain the following:-

(1) The name, age, native place, and address of the worker.
(2) The kind of work engaged in by the worker.
(3) The period of time during which the worker was with
the factory and his records.

Chapter VII. Workers' Welfare.

36. The employers shall provide supplementary education of
not less than ten hours per week for child workers and apprentices,
and shall bear all the expenses therefor. For other employees,
the employers shall also within the means of possibility, provide
educational facilities. The time required for such educational
work shall not be taken from the working hours.

37. Female workers shall be given leave with full wages
before and after child-birth, amounting altogether to eight weeks.

38. Within the means of possibility the employers should
co-operate with workers to promote workers' savings, and co-
operative enterprises.

39. Within the means of possibility the employers should
promote proper amusements for the workers.

40. At the end of each current year, if the factory's
accounts show a surplus, after deductions of interest on shares
and appropriations for the reserve fund, either a bonus or a
share of the actual profit shall be given to those workers who
have committed no demerit.

Chapter VIII. Safety and Health.

41. The factories shall provide the following safety
provisions:-

(1) Safety provisions against life and bodily risks of the
workers.
(2) Safety provisions in the structural details of the
factory.
(3) Safety provisions regarding the proper installation
and fencing of machines.
(4) Safety provisions regarding fire and flood prevention.

42. The factories shall provide the following health pro-
visions:

(1) The provisions for good ventilation.
(2) The provisions for pure drinking supplies.
page_data.zh:
- 5 -

第三十四条 因解释和适用第三十条第三款、第三十一条第一款及第三十三条而产生的争议，可提交工厂委员会解决。

第三十五条 除非工人违反第三十二条之规定或犯有第三十一条所列罪行之一，否则在合同终止时，应向每人发给证明书，内容应包括：

(1) 工人姓名、年龄、籍贯及住址。
(2) 工人从事的工作种类。
(3) 工人在厂期间及其记录。

第七章 工人福利。

第三十六条 雇主应为童工及学徒提供每周不少于十小时的补习教育，并承担所有费用。对于其他雇员，雇主也应在能力范围内提供教育设施。此类教育工作所需时间不得占用工作时间。

第三十七条 女工在产前产后应给予带薪假期，共计八周。

第三十八条 雇主应在能力范围内与工人合作，促进工人储蓄及合作事业。

第三十九条 雇主应在能力范围内为工人提倡正当娱乐。

第四十条 每届年终，若工厂账目显示盈余，在扣除股息及公积金拨款后，应向无过失工人发放奖金或分享实际利润。

第八章 安全与卫生。

第四十一条 工厂应提供下列安全设施：

(1) 针对工人生命及身体风险的安全设施。
(2) 工厂结构细节方面的安全设施。
(3) 机器正确安装及防护方面的安全设施。
(4) 防火及防洪方面的安全设施。

第四十二条 工厂应提供下列卫生设施：

(1) 良好通风设施。
(2) 纯净饮用水供应设施。

page_data.en:
- 6 -

(3) The provisions for suitable lavatories and toilet
facilities.
(4) The provisions for good light.
(5) The provisions for the prevention against poisoning.
43. The employer shall give proper training to workers in
accident prevention.
44. Whenever the safety and health provisions of a factory
are inadequate the proper authority may require improvements to
be made within a definite time-limit. In case of necessity the
proper authority may also stop the operation of the whole or of
a part of the factory.

Chapter IX. Allowance and Compensation.

45. Before the enforcement of social insurance laws, for
workers who become sick or are injured or who lose their lives
through the performance of their duty, the factory shall bear their
medical expenses and shall pay allowances or compensations accord-
ing to the following standards. In case the capital of a factory
is less than fifty-thousand dollars, smaller amounts may be paid
with the approval of the proper authority.
(1) To workers temporarily disabled either through injury
or sickness the factory shall, besides bearing their
medical expenses, pay allowances amounting to two-thirds
of their regular daily wages for a period of six months,
and upon the expiration of that period, if the workers
have still not recovered, amounting to half of the
regular daily wages. Such payments shall only be made
for the period of one year.
(2) To workers permanently disabled either entirely or in
part, through injury or sickness, the factory shall pay
allowances in proportion to the loss of earning
capacity. The maximum amount of such allowances
shall, however, not exceed the average wages for three
years and the minimum amount shall not be less than
the average wages for one year.
(3) To the legal heirs of the workers who lose their lives
the factory shall, besides giving fifty dollars for
funeral expenses, pay compensations amounting to 300
dollars and two years' average wages. The said average
wages shall be calculated on the basis of the wages
for the last three months.

The funeral expenses and compensations shall be paid in a
lump sum, while allowances for injury, sickness and disability
may be paid by installments.

46. Unless otherwise stated in the will of the workers, t. .
persons who are entitled to receive compensations are the wives
or the husbands of the workers as the case may be; in case of
absence of either the order of beneficiaries shall be as follows:
(1) sons and daughters, (2) father and mother, (3) grandchildren,
(4) brothers and sisters.
page_data.zh:
- 6 -

(3) 提供适宜的盥洗室及厕所设施。
(4) 提供良好的照明。
(5) 提供预防中毒的措施。
43. 雇主应对工人进行适当的事故预防培训。
44. 凡工厂的安全与卫生规定不足时，主管当局可责令其在限期内加以改进。如有必要，主管当局亦可责令停止全部或部分工厂的运营。

第九章. 津贴与赔偿。

45. 在社会保险法实施之前，对于因执行职务而患病、受伤或死亡的工人，工厂应承担其医疗费用，并按照下列标准支付津贴或赔偿金。若工厂资本少于五万美元，经主管当局批准，可支付较少金额。
(1) 对于因受伤或疾病暂时丧失劳动能力的工人，工厂除承担其医疗费用外，应在六个月内支付相当于其正常日工资三分之二的津贴；期满若仍未康复，则支付相当于正常日工资二分之一的津贴。此类支付期限仅为一年。
(2) 对于因受伤或疾病导致完全或部分永久丧失劳动能力的工人，工厂应按其收入能力损失的比例支付津贴。但此类津贴的最高数额不得超过三年的平均工资，最低数额不得少于一年的平均工资。
(3) 对于死亡工人的法定继承人，工厂除给付五十美元丧葬费外，应支付三百美元及两年平均工资的赔偿金。上述平均工资应按最后三个月的工资计算。

丧葬费及赔偿金应一次性付清，而因伤、病及残疾的津贴可分期支付。

46. 除非工人在遗嘱中另有声明，有权领取赔偿金的人员视情况为工人的妻子或丈夫；若无配偶，受益人顺序如下：(1) 子女，(2) 父母，(3) 孙子女，(4) 兄弟姐妹。

page_data.en:
- 7 -

47. Should a worker urgently need money on occasions of marriage or death, he may request the factory to advance him one month's wages or refund his savings, if any, either in toto or in part.

48. Should an accident occur in a factory resulting in death or serious injury to a worker, the employer shall report within five days, to the proper authority its occurrence and measures consequently taken.

Chapter X. Factory Councils.

49. Factory councils shall be composed of equal numbers of representatives of the employers and the workers. The employers' representatives shall be selected by the employers from those who are familiar with the conditions of the factory, and the conditions of the workers, while the workers' representatives shall be elected by the employees from among their fellow-workers in the same factory, under the supervision of the proper authority, who should be duly notified.

50. The duties and functions of the factory council shall be as follows:-
(1) To promote working efficiency.
(2) To improve the relations between employers and employees, and to settle disputes between them.
(3) To assist in the enforcement of contracts and the factory's regulations.
(4) To deliberate and decide upon overtime work.
(5) To improve safety and health conditions in the factory.
(6) To propose improvements in factories or workshops.
(7) To make plans for the workers' welfare.

51. When a dispute arises in a factory, it shall first be referred to the factory council, should the council fail to effect a solution, then it shall be settled in accordance with the Law of Conciliation and Arbitration of Labour Disputes.

52. All workers over eighteen years of age shall be entitled to elect representatives to the factory council.

53. All Chinese citizens over twenty-four years of age having worked in a factory for at least a period of half a year shall be eligible as workers' representatives to the factory council.

54. The representatives of the employers and the workers on the factory council shall be five to nine in number for either side.

55. Representatives of each side shall elect a chairman to preside in turn at factory council meetings.

There shall be regular meetings once a month; special meetings may be convened in case they are considered necessary.
page_data.zh:
- 7 -

47. 工人在婚丧等急需用钱时，可请求工厂预支一个月工资或退还其储蓄（如有），全额或部分均可。

48. 若工厂发生事故导致工人死亡或重伤，雇主应在五日内向主管当局报告事故发生情况及随后采取的措施。

第十章. 工厂委员会。

49. 工厂委员会由雇主代表和工人代表同等人数组成。雇主代表应由雇主从熟悉工厂状况及工人情况的人员中选派，工人代表应由同一工厂的员工在同厂工友中选举产生，选举过程须在主管当局监督下进行，并应 duly 通知主管当局。

50. 工厂委员会的职责与职能如下：-
(1) 提高工作效率。
(2) 改善雇主与雇员之间的关系，并解决双方之间的纠纷。
(3) 协助执行合同及工厂规章。
(4) 审议并决定加班工作事宜。
(5) 改善工厂内的安全与卫生条件。
(6) 提出工厂或车间的改进建议。
(7) 制定工人福利计划。

51. 工厂发生纠纷时，应首先提交工厂委员会处理；若委员会未能解决，则依照《劳资争议调解仲裁法》进行处理。

52. 所有年满十八岁的工人均有权选举工厂委员会代表。

53. 所有年满二十四岁、且在工厂工作至少半年的中国公民，均有资格当选为工厂委员会的工人代表。

54. 工厂委员会中雇主代表和工人代表的人数，每方均为五至九人。

55. 各方代表应选举一名主席，轮流主持工厂委员会会议。

每月举行一次定期会议；如有必要，可召开特别会议。

page_data.en:
- 8 -

Chapter XI. Apprenticeship.

56. Factories taking apprentices shall conclude contracts either with the apprentices themselves, or with their legal guardians. Each contract shall be written in triplicates, one copy for each of the contracting parties, and the remaining copy to be submitted to the proper authority for registration. The said contract shall contain the following particulars:-

(1) The name, age, native place and address of the apprentice;
(2) The nature of work for which the apprentice is to be trained;
(3) The date of the conclusion of the contract and the duration of same;
(4) Mutual obligations; in case premium is stipulated, the amount of same and the time of payment; in case remuneration is to be given the apprentice, the amount of same and the time of payment.

The said contract shall not in any way prejudice the free pursuit of the occupation by the apprentice after having served his term of apprenticeship.

57. Children under the age of fourteen shall not be admitted into factories as apprentices. Those below this age who have entered factories before the enforcement of this Law shall, however, be exempt from this provision.

58. The hours of work for the training of apprentices shall be the same as those provided in Chapter III of this Law.

59. Except for the purpose of giving training, apprentices shall not engage in the types of work enumerated in Section 7 of this Law.

60. It shall be the duty of apprentices to be obedient, and faithful to their instructors and to be diligent in their work.

61. During the term of apprenticeship the apprentices shall be supplied with board, lodging, and medical treatment when needed by the employers. They shall, moreover, be given a certain amount of pocket money.

62. Except in cases of great necessity, no apprentice shall quit the factory before the expiration of the term of apprenticeship; in case an apprentice quits without the consent of the factory, he or his legal guardian shall refund the expenses incurred by the factory for board, lodging and medical treatment received.

63. The total number of apprentices taken by a factory shall in no case exceed one-third of its regular workers.

64. If the number of apprentices in a factory is excessive, so that adequate training cannot be provided, the proper authority may order a reduction in the number or fix the maximum number of apprentices in the factory thereafter.

65. During the whole term of apprenticeship it shall be the duty of the factory to enable and require the instructors to do

第十一章. 学徒制度。

56. 招收学徒的工厂应与学徒本人或其法定监护人签订合同。每份合同应一式三份，缔约各方各执一份，剩余一份提交主管当局登记备案。该合同应包含以下细节：-

(1) 学徒的姓名、年龄、籍贯及住址；
(2) 学徒受训的工作性质；
(3) 合同签订日期及期限；
(4) 双方义务；若规定有押金，应注明金额及支付时间；若规定给予学徒报酬，应注明金额及支付时间。

该合同不得以任何方式损害学徒在学徒期满后自由从事职业的权利。

57. 未满十四岁的儿童不得作为学徒进入工厂。但在本法实施前已进入工厂的未满此年龄者，不受本条规定的限制。

58. 学徒受训的工作时间应与本法第三章规定的时间相同。

59. 除受训目的外，学徒不得从事本法第七条所列的各类工作。

60. 学徒有义务服从指导教师的教导，忠诚勤勉地工作。

61. 在学徒期间，雇主应向学徒提供食宿，并在需要时提供医疗待遇。此外，还应给予一定数量的零用钱。

62. 除非有重大必要，学徒在学徒期满前不得离开工厂；若学徒未经工厂同意擅自离开，其本人或其法定监护人应偿还工厂为其支付的食宿及医疗费用。

63. 工厂招收的学徒总数绝不得超过其正式工人的三分之一。

64. 若工厂学徒人数过多，以致无法提供充分的培训，主管当局可命令减少人数，或规定此后工厂学徒的最高限额。

65. 在整个学徒期间，工厂有责任使并要求指导教师尽力

page_data.en:

their utmost to give the apprentices the training stipulated in
the contract.

66. The provisions of Section 31 shall apply to apprentices,
and the factory may terminate the contract under any one of the
following conditions:-
(1) When apprentices revolt against proper instructions.
(2) When apprentices commit theft and do not repent in
spite of repeated admonitions.

67. The provisions of Section 33 shall apply to apprentices;
the apprentices and their legal guardians may terminate the con-
tract under any one of the following conditions:-
(1) When the factory is not in a position to discharge its
obligations stipulated in the contract.
(2) When the factory causes detriment to the health or
degeneration of the conduct of apprentices.

Chapter XII. Penalties.

68. Factories which violate any of the provisions of Section
7, 11, 12, and 13 of this Law shall be liable to a fine amounting
to not less than 100 and not more than 500 dollars.

69. Factories, which violate any of the provisions of
Section 5, 8, 9, 10, 37, and 63 of this Law shall be liable to a
fine amounting to not less than 50 and not more than 300 dollars.

70. Factories, which violate any of the provisions of
Section 45 of this Law shall be liable to a fine amounting to not
less than 50 and not more than 200 dollars.

71. Factories, which violate any of the provisions of
Section 3, 4, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 and 36 of this Law shall be
liable to a fine amounting to not more than 100 dollars.

72. Should trouble or misfortune occur or become enlarged
on account of unfaithfulness or negligence on the part of foremen,
they shall be liable to imprisonment for a period of not more than
a year, or a fine amounting to not more than 500 dollars.

73. Any worker who obstructs the operation of a factory or
destroys the goods and assets of the factory by means of violence
shall be punished in accordance with the maximum penal provisions
of the criminal law.

74. Any worker who compels other workers to strike by □ □
may be immediately discharged by the employer and handed over to
proper authority for punishment in accordance with law.

Chapter XIII. Appendix.

75. A factory's regulations and their amendment shall be
approved and promulgated by the proper authority.

76. The ordinances for the administration of this Law shall
be drawn up separately.

77. The date of enforcement of this Law shall be announced
by order.

按照合同规定给予学徒培训。

66. 第三十一条的规定适用于学徒，工厂可在下列任一条件下终止合同：-
(1) 学徒反抗正当指导时。
(2) 学徒犯有盗窃行为，且经多次劝诫仍不悔改时。

67. 第三十三条的规定适用于学徒；学徒及其法定监护人可在下列任一条件下终止合同：-
(1) 工厂无法履行合同规定的义务时。
(2) 工厂损害学徒健康或导致学徒品行堕落时。

第十二章. 罚则。

68. 工厂违反本法第七、十一、十二及十三条任何规定者，处以不少于一百美元且不超过五百美元的罚款。

69. 工厂违反本法第五、八、九、十、三十七及六十三条任何规定者，处以不少于五十美元且不超过三百美元的罚款。

70. 工厂违反本法第四十五条任何规定者，处以不少于五十美元且不超过二百美元的罚款。

71. 工厂违反本法第三、四、十四、十五、十六、十七、十八、十九及三十六条任何规定者，处以不超过一百美元的罚款。

72. 若因领班的不忠或疏忽导致事故或灾祸发生或扩大，其应处不超过一年的监禁，或不超过五百美元的罚款。

73. 任何工人以暴力手段阻碍工厂运营或破坏工厂货物及资产者，依刑法最高刑罚规定处罚。

74. 任何工人通过 □ □ 强迫其他工人罢工者，雇主可立即将其解雇，并移交主管当局依法惩处。

第十三章. 附则。

75. 工厂规章及其修订须经主管当局批准并颁布。

76. 本法施行细则另行制定。

77. 本法施行日期以命令公布之。

LAW GOVERNING FACTORY INSPECTION

The following is a translation of the Law Governing
Factory Inspection, which was recently promulgated by
the Government : -

to in the present Law shall be defined in
accordance with the provisions of Article
1 of the Factory Law.

Article 2 : The term "controlling official organ", re-
ferred to in the present Law, unless other-
wise stated, shall apply to the Municipal
Government in municipalities and to the
Hsien Government in Hsien districts.

Article 3 : Inspection of factories shall be carried out
by inspectors appointed by the Central labour
administrative organ.

(1) those which concern the age of male and
female workers and the nature of their work,
as provided under Chapter II of the Factory
Law and other labour enactments, (2) those
which concern working hours, as provided
under Chapter III of the Factory Law and
other labour enactments, (3) those which
concern the hours of rest and holidays of
workers, as provided under Chapter IV of

female workers before and after childbirth,
as provided under Chapter VII of the Factory
Law and other labour enactments, (5) those
which concern the safety and sanitary pro-
visions, as provided under Chapter VIII of
the Factory Law and other labour enactments,
(6) those which concern accidents and fata-
lities in factories and the death and in-
jury of workers, (7) those which concern the
age, number and treatment of apprentices,
as provided under Chapter XI of the Factory
Law and other labour enactments, (8) those
which concern the book of records and re-
gistration of workers, as provided under the
Factory Law and the Law governing the Appli-
cation of the Factory Law, and (9) all other
matters which by law are liable to inspection.

the following classes of candidates, who,
having been trained, are found to be fully
qualified : (1) those who have graduated

工厂检查法

以下是政府最近颁布的《工厂检查法》译文：-

第一条：本法所称“工厂”一词，应依照《工厂法》第一条之规定界定。

第二条：本法所称“主管官署”，除另有规定外，在市指市政府，在县指县政府。

第三条：工厂检查由中央劳动行政机关委任之检查员执行之。

第四条：检查事项如下：(1) 关于男女工年龄及其工作性质者，依《工厂法》第二章及其他劳动法规之规定；(2) 关于工作时间者，依《工厂法》第三章及其他劳动法规之规定；(3) 关于工人休息时间及休假者，依《工厂法》第四章及其他劳动法规之规定；(4) 关于女工产前产后假期者，依《工厂法》第七章及其他劳动法规之规定；(5) 关于安全及卫生设施者，依《工厂法》第八章及其他劳动法规之规定；(6) 关于工厂内意外事故及死亡事件，以及工人死伤者；(7) 关于学徒之年龄、人数及待遇者，依《工厂法》第十一章及其他劳动法规之规定；(8) 关于工人名册及登记事宜者，依《工厂法》及《工厂法施行条例》之规定；(9) 其他依法应受检查之一切事项。

第五条：工厂检查员应从下列各类经训练合格之候选人中委任：(1) 毕业于国内外技术学校或高等学府者，及 (2) 在工厂工作十年以上，具备所需充分知识与技能者。

from technical schools at home and abroad
or institutions of higher grade, and (2)
those who have worked in factories for over
ten years and possess the adequate know-
ledge and skill required.

Article 6 : Factory inspectors, in accordance with the
instructions of the Central labour admini-
strative organ, visit all factories and
their branch or extension workshops in cer-
tain specified areas to make periodic or
irregular inspections.

Article 7 : When discharging his official duty, a fac-
tory inspector shall carry with him a certi-
ficate establishing his identity and
authority.

Article 8 : Inspection of Government-owned factories
shall be carried out by the inspector joint-
ly with the Government offices which con-
trol the factories.

Article 9 : Factory inspectors shall have authority to
question employees and labour union officers
and request them to make responsible ans-
wers and shall also be authorised to examine
all books, records and other documentary
evidence pertaining to such affairs, as
provided under Article 4 of the present Law.

Article 10 : When necessary a factory inspector may re-
quest the assistance of the local adminis-
trative or police officials in the execu-
tion of his duty.

Article 11 : Every three months a factory inspector shall
submit a report to the "controlling official
organ", setting forth the following parti-
culars relating to the district under his
inspection : (1) statistics concerning the
number and character of the factories, (2)
statistics concerning the number and occu-
pation of workers, (3) conditions of child
labour, (4) fluctuations of employment and
unemployment, (5) statistics concerning
factory accidents, (6) actual working hours
observed in the different factories, (7)
statistics concerning sickness among and
injuries to workers, (8) safety provisions
observed in various factories, (9) hours
of rest and holidays allowed to workers in
different factories and (10) sanitary con-
ditions existing in the factories and (10)
sanitary conditions existing in the fac-
tories.

Article 12 : When a factory is found to be in the condi-
tion described under Article 44 of the
Factory Law, the factory inspector shall re-
port without delay the matter to the "con-
trolling official organ" for action.
page_data.zh:

第六条：工厂检查员应遵照中央劳动行政机关之指令，巡视特定区域内之所有工厂及其分厂或附属车间，进行定期或不定期检查。

第七条：工厂检查员执行职务时，应携带证明其身份及职权之证书。

第八条：国营工厂之检查，应由检查员会同管辖该工厂之政府机关共同执行之。

第九条：工厂检查员有权询问雇员及工会职员，并要求其作出负责任之答复；并有权查阅与本法律第四条所述事项有关之一切账簿、记录及其他书面证据。

第十条：必要时，工厂检查员在执行职务时可请求地方行政或警察官员予以协助。

第十一条：工厂检查员每三个月应向“主管官署”提交报告，陈述其视察区内之下列详情：(1) 关于工厂数量及性质之统计；(2) 关于工人人数及职业之统计；(3) 童工状况；(4) 就业与失业之波动；(5) 关于工厂意外事故之统计；(6) 各工厂实际遵守之工作时间；(7) 关于工人患病及受伤之统计；(8) 各工厂遵守之安全设施；(9) 各工厂准许工人之休息时间及假日；以及 (10) 工厂内现有之卫生状况。

第十二条：如发现工厂处于《工厂法》第四十四条所述之状况，工厂检查员应立即将该事项报告“主管官署”以采取行动。

page_data.en:

Article 13 : If the safety or sanitary conditions of
a factory call for immediate improvement
or alteration, the factory inspector shall
issue instructions for such work to be done.
If the factory workers' Union concerned
fails to obey such instructions, the ins-
pector shall immediately report the matter
to the "controlling official organ" for
action.

Article 14 : Factory inspectors are forbidden : (1) to
receive or extort bribes, (2) to make false
or garbled reports, (3) to disclose secrets
of industrial processes, (4) to estrange
the good feelings existing between the fac-
tory management and the workers, (5) to
accede without proper authority to any de-
mand by the factory management or the work-
ers and (6) to hold concurrently any other
public office or engage in trade or business.

Article 15 : If a factory inspector commits any act in
contravention of the law or is negligent
in his duty, the factory management or the
workers may report the matter to the "con-
trolling official organ".

Article 16 : For the purpose of improving safety or
sanitary conditions, a factory inspector
may submit his suggestions both to the
factory management and the workers, be-
tween whom he should devise means for se-
curing co-operation in order to improve
the safety or sanitary conditions of the
factory.

Article 17 : If a factory inspector commits any of the
offences mentioned in Article 14 of the
present Law, he shall be suitably punished,
and if the offence be a criminal one, he
shall be prosecuted in court.

Article 18 : The management of a factory shall be liable
to a fine not exceeding $200 for refusing
without satisfactory reason to allow an
inspector admission to the factory.

Article 19 : Factory employees or officers of the workers'
union shall be liable to a fine not exceed-
ing $100 without good reason for refusal to
answer an inspector's or for resisting his
examination of the books or documents men-
tioned under Article 9 of the present Law.

Article 20 : The date for enforcement of the present Law
shall be fixed by a separate order.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

第十三条：如工厂之安全或卫生状况需要立即改善或变更，工厂检查员应发出指示要求进行该项工作。如相关工厂工会不服从该等指示，检查员应立即将该事项报告“主管官署”以采取行动。

第十四条：禁止工厂检查员有下列行为：(1) 收受或勒索贿赂；(2) 作虚假或歪曲之报告；(3) 泄露工业流程之秘密；(4) 离间工厂管理层与工人间之良好感情；(5) 未经适当授权而答应工厂管理层或工人之任何要求；及 (6) 兼任其他公职或从事贸易商业活动。

第十五条：如工厂检查员有违法或失职行为，工厂管理层或工人可向“主管官署”举报。

第十六条：为改善安全或卫生状况，工厂检查员可向工厂管理层及工人提出建议，并在两者之间筹划合作方法，以改善工厂之安全或卫生状况。

第十七条：如工厂检查员犯有本法第十四条所述之任何罪行，应予以适当惩处；如属刑事犯罪，应交法庭起诉。

第十八条：工厂管理层如无充分理由拒绝检查员进入工厂，应处以不超过200元之罚款。

第十九条：工厂雇员或工会职员如无充分理由拒绝回答检查员提问，或抗拒检查员查阅本法第九条所述之账簿或文件，应处以不超过100元之罚款。

第二十条：本法施行日期另行命令定之。

第五条：工厂检查员应从下列各类经训练合格之候选人中委任：(1) 毕业于
国内外技术学校或高等学府者，及 (2) 在工厂工作十年以上，具备所需充分
知识与技能者。

第六条：工厂检查员应遵照中央劳动行政机关之指令，巡视特定区域内之所有
工厂及其分厂或附属车间，进行定期或不定期检查。

第七条：工厂检查员执行职务时，应携带证明其身份及职权之证书。

第八条：国营工厂之检查，应由检查员会同管辖该工厂之政府机关共同执行之。

第九条：工厂检查员有权询问雇员及工会职员，并要求其作出负责任之答复；
并有权查阅与本法律第四条所述事项有关之一切账簿、记录及其他书面证据。

第十条：必要时，工厂检查员在执行职务时可请求地方行政或警察官员予以协
助。

第十一条：工厂检查员每三个月应向“主管官署”提交报告，陈述其视察区内
之下列详情：(1) 关于工厂数量及性质之统计；(2) 关于工人人数及职业之统
计；(3) 童工状况；(4) 就业与失业之波动；(5) 关于工厂意外事故之统计；
(6) 各工厂实际遵守之工作时间；(7) 关于工人患病及受伤之统计；(8) 各工
厂遵守之安全设施；(9) 各工厂准许工人之休息时间及假日；以及 (10) 工厂
内现有之卫生状况。

— 93 —

page_data.en:
Art. 12: When a factory is found to be in the condition described under Article 44 of the Factory Law, the factory inspector shall report without delay the matter to the "controlling official organ" for action.

Art. 13: If the safety or sanitary conditions of a factory call for immediate improvement or alteration, the factory inspector shall issue instructions for such work to be done. If the factory workers' union concerned fails to obey such instructions, the inspector shall immediately report the matter to the "controlling official organ" for action.

Art. 14: Factory inspectors are forbidden: (1) to receive or extort bribes, (2) to make false or garbled reports, (3) to disclose secrets of industrial processes, (4) to estrange the good feelings existing between the factory management and the workers, (5) to accede without proper authority to any demand by the factory management or the workers and (6) to hold concurrently any other public office or engage in trade or business.

Art. 15: If a factory inspector commits any act in contravention of the law or is negligent in his duty, the factory management or the workers may report the matter to the "controlling official organ."

Art. 16: For the purpose of improving safety or sanitary conditions, a factory inspector may submit his suggestions both to the factory management and the workers, between whom he should devise means for securing co-operation in order to improve the safety or sanitary conditions of the factory.

Art. 17: If a factory inspector commits any of the offences mentioned in Article 14 of the present Law, he shall be suitably punished, and if the offence be a criminal one, he shall be prosecuted in court.

Art. 18: The management of a factory shall be liable to a fine not exceeding $200 for refusing without satisfactory reason to allow an inspector admission to the factory.

Art. 19: Factory employees or officers of the workers' union shall be liable to a fine not exceeding $100 without good reason for refusal to answer an inspector's or for resisting his examination of the books or documents mentioned under Article 9 of the present Law.

Art. 20: The date for enforcement of the present Law shall be fixed by a separate order.

Note: The foregoing, though a fairly accurate rendering of the original, is not an official translation. Owing to the subtleties peculiar to each language translations are apt to give room for divergence from the meaning of the original text, which alone, however, is authoritative.—Ed.

— 94 —
page_data.zh:
第十二条：如发现工厂处于《工厂法》第四十四条所述之状况，工厂视察员应立即将此事项报告“主管官署”以采取行动。

第十三条：如工厂之安全或卫生状况需要立即改善或变更，工厂视察员应发出指令要求进行此类工作。如相关工厂工会不服从该等指令，视察员应立即将此事项报告“主管官署”以采取行动。

第十四条：禁止工厂视察员：(1) 收受或勒索贿赂，(2) 作虚假或混乱之报告，(3) 泄露工业流程之秘密，(4) 离间工厂管理层与工人之间既存之良好感情，(5) 未经适当授权而答应工厂管理层或工人之任何要求，以及 (6) 兼任其他公职或从事贸易及商业活动。

第十五条：如工厂视察员有任何违反法律之行为或玩忽职守，工厂管理层或工人可向“主管官署”报告此事。

第十六条：为改善安全或卫生状况，工厂视察员可向工厂管理层及工人提出建议，并应在二者之间 devised（设计/筹划）合作手段，以改善工厂之安全或卫生状况。

第十七条：如工厂视察员犯有本法第十四条提及之任何罪行，应予以适当处罚；如该罪行属刑事犯罪，则应向法院提起公诉。

第十八条：工厂管理层如无充分理由拒绝允许视察员进入工厂，须承担不超过200美元之罚款。

第十九条：工厂雇员或工会官员如无正当理由拒绝回答视察员之询问，或阻挠其查阅本法第九条所述之账簿或文件，须承担不超过100美元之罚款。

第二十条：本法之施行日期由另行命令规定。

Sino-Japanese Trade in 1930

The effect of the slump in silver is seen in the returns of China's trade with Japan during 1930, when both imports and exports showed a marked decrease as compared with the preceding year. The value of goods exported from China to Japan, according to official Japanese figures, was Yen 278,374,060, and of Japanese goods exported to points in China Yen 399,424,000, showing a balance in favour of Japan of Yen 121,050,000. This surplus on the year's trade was Yen 42,051,000 less than the excess of Japan's exports to China in 1929. The following are the figures for 1930 showing the trade between China and Japan expressed in thousands of yen:—

Japan's exports to South China show an increase of nearly 3½ million yen, as compared with the preceding year, but Japanese business with other parts of the Republic shows a heavy decline. Exports to Manchuria dropped by more than 29 million yen, to North China by 7½ million, to the Central Provinces by over 50 million, to Kwangtung by nearly 38 million, and to Hongkong by more than 5 million yen.

Exports to Japan from all parts of China during 1930 show a sharp decrease as compared with the trade done during the preceding year. The returns for Manchuria show a drop in value of more than 5 million yen, and a decrease of 9¼ million in exports from the Northern Provinces to Japan. The export trade with Japan from the Central Provinces dropped by 29 millions last year as compared with 1929, there was a drop of nearly 3 millions in exports from the South, though Hongkong's figures show the very small decrease of Yen 74,000 as compared with the preceding year's exports to Japan, but the business done with Japan from Kwangtung shows a drop for 1930 of no less than Yen 40,802,000.

银价暴跌的影响体现在1930年中国对日贸易的数据中，与上一年相比，进出口均显示显著下降。根据日本官方数据，中国出口至日本的货物价值为278,374,060日元，日本出口至中国各地的货物价值为399,424,000日元，显示出有利于日本的顺差为121,050,000日元。这一年度贸易顺差比1929年日本对华出口超出额少了42,051,000日元。以下是1930年以千日元表示的中日贸易数据：

1930年中国各地对日本的出口与上一年度的贸易相比显示急剧减少。满洲的数据显示价值下降了500多万日元，北方各省对日出口减少了925万。去年中部各省对日出口贸易与1929年相比下降了2900万，南方出口下降了近300万，尽管香港的数据显示与上一年对日出口相比仅微幅减少74,000日元，但广东对日业务在1930年下降了不少于40,802,000日元。

Review of the Bond Market

Owing to the approach of the "Spring Holidays," when there was to be a general settlement of account, the bond market for the week ending February 12 was rather quiet, there being no large buying or selling. A total business of $29,695,000 was registered for forward transactions, including $6,415,000 for Cigarette (1931), $5,145,000 for Rehabilitation (1930), $5,405,000 for Troop Reduction, $4,605,000 for Customs (1930), $3,360,000 for Disbandment, $2,915,000 for 96 Million, $1,205,000 for 6% Consols etc.

During the first three days of the week, the market was comparatively brisk. Every day saw from $6,000,000 to $7,000,000 worth of bonds changing hands. On Thursday and Friday the sum registered was in each case less than $5,000,000, and business was suspended on Saturday.

A total of $236,300 was registered for spot transactions, including $97,500 for Customs (1930), $67,000 for Disbandment, $35,800 for Troop Reduction. The market in general showed a downward trend, a fall of from $0.60 to $0.70 being registered for Customs (1930), Rehabilitation (1930) and Cigarette (1931) at the beginning of the week.
