Review of the Gold Bar Market

The local gold bar market during the week ending February 14 again showed very unstable tendencies. Quotations rose and fell in such a violent manner that the market was at times entirely beyond control, and the fluctuations caused a good deal of anxiety and even consternation among Exchange speculators. Affected by the continuous rise recorded during the previous week, the market opened on Monday with a sensational appreciation, but on Tuesday and Wednesday, owing to overwhelming selling by the bears, there was an equally phenomenal decline. The bears were supported in their operations by the report that a conference for the stabilization of silver would be convened by the United States, and the hurried covering by the bulls in order to avoid payment of exorbitant premiums during the carry-over (which took place on Saturday) further depressed the market. However, the fall was checked during the afternoon session of Thursday, when there was a sudden change of attitude in local banking circles as well as by some of the leading dealers, who suspended bear activities in view of the easiness of foreign exchange rates. The rise was continued until the week-end, when the market closed with a very firm tone. The peak price of the week, Tls. 791.00, was reached on Tuesday, February 10, while the bottom price, Tls. 736.50, was touched on Thursday, February 12, representing a fluctuation of Tls. 54.50 as against Tls. 51.70 recorded during the preceding week.

Due to the continual slump of local exchange rates, the market on Monday, February 9, showed a remarkable rise. Business opened at Tls. 773.00 and soon rose to Tls. 778.50. Later, as a number of large dealers bought heavily, mostly for covering purposes, quotations moved steadily upward until business closed at noon at Tls. 788.00. During the afternoon, the market climbed further upward. Business opened at Tls. 788.50, rising quickly to Tls. 789.50, but an easier tone prevailed and quotations slid gradually downward until the low mark of Tls. 783.50 was reached. About 4:30 the market revived, and business closed firmly at Tls. 789.00. On Tuesday, February 10, there was a strong opening but a weak close. Business opened at Tls. 782.00, it slid suddenly to Tls. 774.00, and later fluctuated very sharply up to ... when business closed at Tls. 782.30. The afternoon session opened at Tls. 782.50, and owing to feverish activities by the bulls, quotations eventually went up to at Tls. 791.00, the highest price recorded in local financial history. As soon as this figure was touched, cable advices from abroad reported an appreciation of silver values, suddenly weakening the market, which closed at Tls. 771.50.

On Wednesday, February 11, business continued to show a downward tendency. The market opened at Tls. 760.00, but soon fell to Tls. 751.50, subsequently fluctuating very actively around the mark of Tls. 760.00, until business closed at noon at Tls. 758.50. The afternoon market opened at Tls. 757.50 and closed at Tls. 751.00. The former figure being the highest mark touched, while the lowest was Tls. 747.00, showing a margin of Tls. 10.50. Owing to the easiness of local exchange rates, the market recovered after a weak opening in the morning session of Thursday, February 12. Business opened at Tls. 742.50 but quickly dropped as low as Tls. 736.50, the week's bottom price. Later a large amount of bars, as well as exchange bills issued a few months ago, had to be covered, and the market showed a reaction which sent quotations to Tls. 752.80 before business closed at noon at Tls. 752.50. During the afternoon, the market was very uncertain. After opening at Tls. 756.50 and a subsequent drop to Tls. 752.00, quotations moved upward and downward until Tls. 756.00 was quoted at the close.

On Friday, February 13, the market continued to soar. Business opened in the morning at Tls. 756.50 but soon slid to Tls. 749.50, the low mark of the day. Then quotations moved steadily upward, and after touching the high mark of Tls. 767.50, business closed at Tls. 766.20. During the afternoon, a further appreciation took place, business opening at Tls. 772.50 and moved sharply to Tls. 782.00, the peak price of the day. Later a number of dealers came out as big sellers, and quotations dropped abruptly to Tls. 770.50. The closing price showed some recovery, being registered at Tls. 775.00. In view of the approach of the "Spring Holidays," the carry-over was changed from the 16th of the month to Saturday, February 14, when the market opened at 8:30 in the morning in order to allow time for transferring accounts from March to April

金条市场综述

截至2月14日的一周，本地金条市场再次表现出极不稳定的态势。报价剧烈涨跌，致使市场有时完全失控，这种波动在交易所投机者中引起了极大的焦虑甚至恐慌。受前一周持续上涨的影响，周一市场开盘时出现惊人的升值，但周二和周三，由于空头的大量抛售，市场出现了同样显著的下跌。美国将召开稳定白银会议的报道支持了空头的操作，而多头为了在展期（于周六进行）期间避免支付高昂的升水而匆忙平仓，进一步压低了市场。然而，周四下午市时段跌势得到遏制，当时本地银行界以及一些主要交易商的态度突然转变，鉴于外汇汇率宽松，他们暂停了做空活动。涨势一直持续到周末，市场收盘时走势非常坚挺。本周最高价为791.00两，出现在2月10日（星期二），而最低价为736.50两，出现在2月12日（星期四），波动幅度为54.50两，而前一周记录的波动幅度为51.70两。

由于本地外汇汇率持续下跌，2月9日（星期一）的市场显示出显著上涨。交易以773.00两开盘，并迅速涨至778.50两。随后，由于许多大交易商大量买入（主要为平仓目的），报价稳步上升，直至中午休市时收于788.00两。下午市期间，市场进一步攀升。交易以788.50两开盘，迅速涨至788.50两（注：原文此处似有笔误，结合上下文应为更高价位或维持高位，但依原文译出为789.50两更合逻辑，此处依下文“rising quickly to Tls. 789.50”修正理解，但原文写的是opened at 788.50, rising to 789.50），但市场气氛转软，报价逐渐下滑，直至触及783.50两的低点。约4:30时市场复苏，交易以789.00两坚挺收盘。2月10日（星期二），市场高开低走。交易以782.00两开盘，突然滑落至774.00两，随后剧烈波动，最高达……（原文不清），中午休市时收于782.30两。下午市以782.50两开盘，由于多头的狂热活动，报价最终涨至791.00两，创下本地金融史上的最高纪录。一旦触及这一数字，来自海外的电报报道白银价值升值，导致市场突然走弱，最终以771.50两收盘。

2月11日（星期三），交易继续呈现下跌趋势。市场以760.00两开盘，但很快跌至751.50两，随后在760.00两附近剧烈波动，直至中午休市时收于758.50两。下午市以757.50两开盘，收于751.00两。前者为触及的最高点，而最低点为747.00两，价差为10.50两。由于本地外汇汇率宽松，2月12日（星期四）上午市在弱势开盘后市场得以恢复。交易以742.50两开盘，但迅速跌至736.50两，即本周最低价。随后，由于必须对大量金条以及几个月前开具的外汇票据进行平仓，市场出现反弹，报价升至752.80两，中午休市前收于752.50两。下午市期间，市场非常不确定。在以756.50两开盘并随后跌至752.00两后，报价上下波动，收盘时报756.00两。

2月13日（星期五），市场继续飙升。上午交易以756.50两开盘，但很快滑至749.50两，为当日低点。随后报价稳步上升，在触及767.50两的高点后，交易收于766.20两。下午市期间，价格进一步升值，交易以772.50两开盘，并急剧涨至782.00两，为当日峰值。随后，一些交易商成为大卖家，报价骤降至770.50两。收盘价显示有所回升，录得775.00两。鉴于“春节假期”临近，展期日从本月的16日改为2月14日（星期六），市场于上午8:30开盘，以便有时间将账户从3月转移至4月

dealers were obliged to pay a premium of from Tls. 7.00 to Tls. 8.00 for each

Quotations for March delivery opened at Tls. 774.70, and after touching a high

Industrial Notes

Encouragement to Inventions and Discoveries.—The establishment of a Special Committee for the encouragement of scientific and industrial inventions has been recommended by the Central Research Council in a petition submitted to the National Government. It is pointed out that in order to lay firmly the foundation upon which the Nation is to be re-built, it is imperative to encourage in every way scientific inventions and discoveries. For this purpose, a number of scientific research institutes should also be established in the important cities all over the country. The National Government has instructed the Central Research Council to confer with the Ministries concerned, particularly the Ministries of Education and Industries, in regard to the proposal.—Kuo Min.

Japanese Textile Factories Extended.—One result of the new tariff which came into operation on January 1st is the decision of Japanese cotton-spinners in Shanghai to extend their plants for the manufacture of qualities of cloth formerly imported from Japan. Additional spindles are being installed, together with automatic weaving-machines, and a large number of operatives will be added to the staffs of these factories. By increasing the productive capacity of the mills, and extending the range of goods turned out, it is hoped to retain and even increase the business done in lines the import of which from Japan may be affected by the new tariff.

Commercial Notes

Exports of Cassia Oil.—An official bureau has been opened at Wuchow for the examination of cassia oil intended for shipment abroad. The object is to maintain a high standard of quality, and prevent the export of oil of inferior grade. The expenses incurred in connection with the maintenance of the bureau will be met by collecting inspection-fees from dealers in cassia-oil desiring certificates of quality.

Silk Exports from Canton.—The 1930-1 silk season will show an improvement in the export of raw silk from Canton, but a heavy drop in the export of waste silk from that port. Since 1927-8 there had been an increasing quantity of waste silk shipped abroad from Canton, the figure for 1929-30 reaching a total of 36 566 bales. 工业简讯

鼓励发明与发现。——中央研究院在向国民政府提交的请愿书中建议成立一个特别委员会，以鼓励科学和工业发明。指出为了牢固奠定国家重建的基础，必须通过各种方式鼓励科学发明和发现。为此，还应在全国各重要城市建立若干科学研究机构。国民政府已指示中央研究院就该项提案与有关各部，特别是教育部和实业部进行磋商。——《国民新闻》

日本纺织工厂扩建。——1月1日生效的新关税带来的一个结果是，上海的日本棉纺商决定扩建其工厂，以生产以前从日本进口的布料品种。正在安装额外的纱锭以及自动织布机，这些工厂的员工中将增加大量操作工。通过提高工厂的生产能力并扩大产品范围，希望能保留甚至增加那些可能受新关税影响的从日本进口商品的业务量。

桂油出口。——梧州已设立一个官方机构，用于检查拟运往国外的桂油。其目的是保持高质量标准，防止劣质油出口。维持该机构所产生的费用将通过向希望获得质量证书的桂油交易商收取检验费来支付。

广州丝绸出口。——1930-31年度生丝季，广州的生丝出口量将有所改善，但该港口的废丝出口量将大幅下降。自1927-28年以来，从广州运往国外的废丝数量不断增加，1929-30年度的总数达到36,566包。然而，本期总数几乎不会

即将签订中阿商业条约。——国民政府不久将启动谈判，以签订新的中阿（中国-阿根廷）商业条约。外交部在给驻智利圣地亚哥代办张厉生（Chang Li-ao，音译）先生的电报中指示，与驻圣地亚哥的阿根廷公使开始讨论，以便早日达成条约。——《国民新闻》

行政院批准设立航政局计划。——据悉，交通部提交的在上海、汉口、广州、天津和哈尔滨设立五个航政局的计划已获行政院批准。——《国民新闻》

疏浚苏州河。——黄浦浚浦局刚刚开始一项预计需要数年才能完成的任务。苏州河将从其汇入黄浦江处向上游疏浚至

— 102 —

page_data.en:
Ya Chi Tun, about five miles beyond Jessfield. The work is being done by the Conservancy Board at the request of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai. For about twelve years this undertaking has been the subject of desultory discussion, and the Whangpoo Conservancy Board has consistently expressed its willingness to carry out the work, but until now no definite proposals had been put forward, and consequently nothing was done. Meanwhile, of course, the silting process continued, and the amount of traffic on the creek steadily increased, so that the work which is now begun will be correspondingly more difficult than it would have been ten or twelve years ago. The dredging operations now started are expected to take some years to complete, when it is hoped to deepen the creek to a depth six feet below lowest low water, and at the same time to give this depth of water over a maximum width consistent with the safety of the banks.

Canton-Hankow Railway Extension.—Work has been resumed in north Kwangtung on the section of the Canton-Hankow railway between Shiukwan and Lokcheong. This stretch of line has been divided into sections, one of which was completed about two months ago. The second section, between Lokcheong and Ping Shek, is now under construction, and it is hoped will be completed before the summer, although this part of the line runs through very mountainous country. Ten tunnels have to be driven through the hills, and it is estimated that this section of the line will cost about $13,000,000 to build. Locomotives and rolling-stock have been already ordered, and if operations are not interfered with should be running on the track between Shiukwan and Lokcheong within a few weeks.

Miscellaneous Notes

Population in Newchwang.—According to a census recently taken by the district authorities of Newchwang, there are 44,606 households in the city with a total population of 283,558, of which 170,832 are males and 112,726 are females.

Protection to Guild Houses.—Stressing the inviolability of private property, the Ministry of Industries, in a circular despatch to the Provincial and Municipal Governments throughout the country, urges that steps be immediately taken to protect the guild-houses against unlawful encroachments. The despatch draws attention to the increasing number of cases in which buildings belonging to guilds have been either unlawfully confiscated or occupied. Apart from the fact that the guild-houses, being private property, are entitled to due protection under Law, the despatch points out, the activities of the various industrial or commercial guilds, tending as they do to foster cooperation among the merchants, are highly beneficial to commerce and industry. Any attempt calculated to hamper the growth of the guilds is strongly deprecated by the Ministry.—Kuo Min.

粤汉铁路延伸段。——粤汉铁路韶关至乐昌段在粤北地区的工程已恢复施工。该段线路已划分为若干工区，其中一个工区已于约两个月前完工。第二段，即乐昌至坪石段，目前正在建设中，尽管该段线路穿越多山地区，仍希望在夏季前完工。需在山岭中开凿十条隧道，据估计该段线路的建设成本约为13,000,000元。机车和车辆已经订购，如果施工不受干扰，应在数周内可在韶关至乐昌之间的轨道上运行。

保护会馆。——实业部在向全国各省市政府发出的通令中，强调私有财产的神圣不可侵犯性，敦促立即采取措施保护会馆免受非法侵占。该通令提请注意，属于会馆的建筑物被非法没收或占用的案件日益增多。通令指出，除了会馆作为私有财产依法应受到适当保护这一事实外，各种工业或商业会馆的活动有助于促进商人之间的合作，对工商业极为有益。任何企图阻碍会馆发展的行为都受到实业部的强烈谴责。——《国民新闻》。

工厂法
（中英文文本）

由中华民国国民政府颁布，

page_data.en:
The New National Factory
Law

Translated by
NORWOOD F. ALLMAN AND LOWE CHUAN-HUA

Chapter I.
General Provisions
ARTICLE 1. This Law shall apply to all factories where
the machinery is driven by steam, electric, or water
power and where in ordinary times thirty or more
laborers are employed.
ARTICLE 2. When used in this Law, unless the
regulations otherwise indicate, the term “Proper
Authorities” means the municipal government in
municipalities and the district government in the
districts (Hsien).
ARTICLE 3. Factories shall keep a laborers’ register and
record fully the following particulars concerning each
laborer:—
1) Name, age, birthplace and address;
2) Year and month of entry into the factory;
3) The kind of work, hours and remuneration;
4) Skill and conduct;
5) Efficiency of work;
6) The rewards and penalties received in the factory;
7) The kinds of illness suffered by the laborer and
the causes thereof.
ARTICLE 4. Once every six months factories shall
submit to the Proper Authorities a report, containing
the following particulars:—
1) A register of the laborers’ names;
2) Illness suffered by the laborers, treatment and
results;
3) Accidents and measures taken for relief thereof;
4) The dismissal of laborers and reasons therefor.

Chapter II.
Child and Female Labor
ARTICLE 5. No person, male or female, who has not
completed his or her fourteenth year shall be employed
in any factory as a laborer.
Boys or girls above the age of twelve and below the
age of fourteen who are already in employment prior
to the promulgation of this Law may, with the consent
of the Proper Authorities, have the age limit extended
when this Law is put into effect.

1
page_data.zh:
新国家工厂法

译者
诺伍德·F·奥尔曼 (NORWOOD F. ALLMAN) 和 罗传华 (LOWE CHUAN-HUA)

第一章.
总则
第一条. 本法适用于所有以蒸汽、电力或水力驱动机械，且在平时雇用三十名或以上工人的工厂。
第二条. 在本法中使用时，除非法规另有规定，“主管机关”一词在市指市政府，在县指县政府。
第三条. 工厂应保存工人登记册，并详细记录每位工人的下列事项：—
1) 姓名、年龄、籍贯和住址；
2) 进厂年月；
3) 工作种类、工时和报酬；
4) 技能和品行；
5) 工作效率；
6) 在厂内受到的奖惩；
7) 工人所患疾病种类及其原因。
第四条. 工厂每六个月应向主管机关提交一份报告，包含下列事项：—
1) 工人姓名登记册；
2) 工人所患疾病、治疗情况及结果；
3) 事故及采取的救济措施；
4) 解雇工人及其原因。

第二章.
童工与女工
第五条. 任何未满十四周岁的男女，不得在任何工厂受雇为工人。
在本法颁布前已受雇的十二周岁以上、十四周岁以下的男孩或女孩，经主管机关同意，在本法生效时可延长年龄限制。

1

page_data.en:
ARTICLE 6. Males or females above the age of fourteen
but who have not completed their sixteenth year shall
be deemed child laborers and are permitted to perform
light or easy work only.
ARTICLE 7. Child and female labor shall not be em-
ployed in the following work:—
1) In handling explosive, inflammatory or poisonous
articles;
2) In places which are exposed to dust or poisonous
odors and gas;
3) In fixing, cleaning, oiling, inspecting, or repairing
moving machines, power transmitting equipment,
or risky parts thereof, or in adjusting belts and
ropes;
4) In connecting highly charged electric wires;
5) In handling molten metals or the residue thereof;
6) In handling furnaces or boilers; or
7) Other work that is immoral or of a dangerous
character.

Chapter III.
Working Hours.
ARTICLE 8. In principle the number of working hours
for adult laborers shall be eight per day; but may be
extended to ten per day in cases of necessity due to
varying local conditions or the nature of the work.
ARTICLE 9. All factories that use the system of day and
night shifts shall so arrange their working schedules
that the shifts for the laborers may be interchanged
at least once a week.
ARTICLE 10. Notwithstanding the provisions of Article
8 the employers may, on the ground of natural,
accidental or seasonal changes, extend the working
day, but the total number of working hours shall not
exceed twelve per day, and the overtime work shall not
exceed thirty-six hours per month for any laborer.
ARTICLE 11. The regular working day for child
laborers shall, under no circumstances, exceed eight
hours.
ARTICLE 12. Child laborers shall not work between
the hours of seven o'clock in the evening and six o'clock
the following morning.
ARTICLE 13. Female laborers shall not work between
the hours of ten o'clock in the evening and six o'clock
the following morning.

Chapter VI
Rest and Holidays
ARTICLE 14. Any laborer who works continuously for
a period of five hours shall enjoy half an hour's rest.

2
page_data.zh:
第六条. 年满十四周岁但未满十六周岁的男女，视为童工，仅准许从事轻便或简易工作。
第七条. 童工和女工不得从事下列工作：—
1) 处理爆炸性、易燃性或有毒物品；
2) 在暴露于粉尘、有毒气味和气体的场所；
3) 固定、清洁、加油、检查或修理运转中的机器、动力传输设备或其危险部件，或调整皮带和绳索；
4) 连接高压电线；
5) 处理熔融金属或其残留物；
6) 操作熔炉或锅炉；或
7) 其他不道德或具有危险性质的工作。

第三章.
工作时间
第八条. 原则上，成年工人的工作时间为每天八小时；但因各地情况不同或工作性质需要，可延长至每天十小时。
第九条. 所有实行日夜轮班制的工厂，应安排工作时间表，使工人的班次至少每周轮换一次。
第十条. 尽管有第八条的规定，雇主可因自然、意外或季节性变化延长工作日，但总工作时间每天不得超过十二小时，且任何工人的加班时间每月不得超过三十六小时。
第十一条. 童工的正常工作日在任何情况下不得超过八小时。
第十二条. 童工不得在晚上七点至次日早上六点之间工作。
第十三条. 女工不得在晚上十点至次日早上六点之间工作。

第六章
休息与假日
第十四条. 任何连续工作五小时的工人，应享有半小时的休息时间。

2

page_data.en:
ARTICLE 15. All laborers shall have a full day's rest in
every seven days.
ARTICLE 16. All factories shall cease work on holidays
designated by law or orders of the Government.
ARTICLE 17. All laborers who work continuously for
a fixed period shall be allowed a special holiday which
shall be based on the following scale:—
1) All laborers who have worked continuously for
more than one year but less than three years,
shall be allowed a holiday period of seven days each
year;
2) All laborers who have worked continuously for
more than three years but less than five years,
shall be allowed a holiday period of ten days per
year;
3) All laborers who have worked continuously for
more than five years but less than ten years,
shall be allowed a holiday period of fourteen days
a year;
4) All laborers who have worked continuously for
more than ten years shall have an additional day
for each additional year added to his holiday period,
but the total number of days shall not exceed
thirty.
ARTICLE 18. All laborers shall be paid their regular
wages for the holidays and rest periods provided in
Articles 15, 16 and 17.
In cases where the laborers do not wish to enjoy
the special holiday to which they are entitled, their
wages for the said period shall be doubled.
ARTICLE 19. Where military establishments or public
utility works are concerned, the Proper Authorities
may refuse to grant holiday periods whenever they
deem such action necessary.

Chapter V.
Wages
ARTICLE 20. Minimum wages of the laborers shall be
determined in accordance with the living conditions
prevalent in the various localities in which the factories
are established.
ARTICLE 21. Wages shall be paid by the factories to
the laborers in the local legal tender.
ARTICLE 22. Regular wages based either on the time-
rate or the piece-rate shall be paid to the workers
at least twice a month. Wages shall be paid on fixed
dates.
ARTICLE 23. Whenever an extension of working hours
is made in accordance with Article 10 or Article 19,
the laborers' wages shall be increased from one-third

3
page_data.zh:
第十五条. 所有工人每七天应享有一整天的休息。
第十六条. 所有工厂在法律或政府命令规定的假日应停止工作。
第十七条. 所有连续工作满一定期限的工人，应享受特别假期，具体标准如下：—
1) 所有连续工作满一年以上但不足三年的工人，每年应享有七天假期；
2) 所有连续工作满三年以上但不足五年的工人，每年应享有十天假期；
3) 所有连续工作满五年以上但不足十年的工人，每年应享有十四天假期；
4) 所有连续工作满十年以上的工人，每增加一年工龄，假期增加一天，但总天数不得超过三十天。
第十八条. 所有工人在第十五条、第十六条和第十七条规定的假日和休息期间，应照常领取工资。
如果工人不愿享受其应得的特别假期，则该期间的工资应加倍支付。
第十九条. 涉及军事设施或公共事业工程时，主管机关如认为必要，可拒绝批准假期。

第五章.
工资
第二十条. 工人的最低工资应根据工厂所在地的生活状况确定。
第二十一条. 工厂应以当地法定货币向工人支付工资。
第二十二条. 基于计时或计件的正常工资，每月至少支付两次。工资应在固定日期支付。
第二十三条. 凡根据第十条或第十九条延长工作时间的，工人的工资应增加三分之一

3

page_data.en:
to two-thirds of their regular wages calculated on an
hourly basis.
ARTICLE 24. Male and female laborers of the same
occupation and of equal efficiency shall receive equal
wages.
ARTICLE 25. Factories shall not deduct in advance the
wages of the laborers as security for penalties for
breach of contract or as indemnity for damages.
Chapter VI.
Termination of Working Contracts
ARTICLE 26. Contracts entered into for a stipulated
period of time may, upon expiration, be renewed only
by mutual agreement.
ARTICLE 27. In cases where the contract has no stipula-
tion as to its term, the factory may cancel the same
only by serving on the laborers a notice in advance.
The time allowed by the notice shall be based upon the
following scale, but this provision shall not apply to
contracts which have stipulations concerning the man-
ner of termination:—
1) Ten days' advance notice to laborers who have
worked in the factory for more than three months
but less than one year;
2) Twenty days' advance notice to laborers who have
worked for more than one year but less than three
years;
3) Thirty days' advance notice to laborers who have
worked for more than three years.
ARTICLE 28. Laborers who have received notices of
dismissal may ask for a leave of absence in order to
apply for other jobs, but said leave of absence shall
not exceed two working days a week. Wages during
the said period shall be paid to said laborers.
ARTICLE 29. Factories which terminate the working
contract in conformity with the provisions of Article 27
shall pay the laborers, in addition to their regular
wages, half of the wages due for the period of notifi-
cation as stipulated in the said Article. Failing to
comply with the provisions of Article 27, the factories
which desire summary termination of the working
contract, shall pay to the laborers the entire wages
for the period of notification as stipulated in the said
Article.
ARTICLE 30. Factories may terminate the employment
agreements with their laborers under any one of the
following conditions, but must serve previous notices
on them in accordance with the provisions of Article
27:—
1) When a factory totally or partially suspends
operations;
4
page_data.zh:
为其正常工资的三分之二，按小时计算。
第二十四条。从事相同职业且效率相等的男女劳工，应获得同等工资。
第二十五条。工厂不得预先扣除劳工工资，作为违反合同的罚金担保或损害赔偿金。
第六章。
劳动合同的终止
第二十六条。定期订立的合同，期满后仅可在双方同意的情况下续订。
第二十七条。若合同未规定期限，工厂仅可通过提前向劳工发出通知来取消合同。通知所允许的时间应基于以下标准，但本规定不适用于已就终止方式作出规定的合同：—
1) 对于在工厂工作超过三个月但不足一年的劳工，需提前十天通知；
2) 对于工作超过一年但不足三年的劳工，需提前二十天通知；
3) 对于工作超过三年的劳工，需提前三十天通知。
第二十八条。收到解雇通知的劳工可以请假以便寻找其他工作，但该请假每周不得超过两个工作日。上述期间的工资应支付给该等劳工。
第二十九条。工厂依照第二十七条规定终止劳动合同的，除支付正常工资外，还应支付该条规定的通知期内工资的一半。若未遵守第二十七条的规定，希望立即终止劳动合同的工厂，应向劳工支付该条规定的整个通知期的全额工资。
第三十条。工厂可在下列任一条件下终止与劳工的雇佣协议，但必须依照第二十七条的规定提前向他们发出通知：—
1) 当工厂全部或部分停工时；
4

page_data.en:
2) When a factory either through natural disasters or
the force of unforseen circumstances, is obliged to
suspend operations for a period of over one month;
3) When a laborer is incapable of performing his
work.
ARTICLE 31. Factories may terminate the employment
agreements with their laborers without serving on
them any previous notice under any one of the follow-
ing conditions:—
1) When a laborer repeatedly violates the factory's
regulations;
2) When a laborer fails to report for work without
good cause for over three consecutive days or for
over six days within one month.
ARTICLE 32. Laborers may terminate their working
contracts by serving on the factories a notice of one
week, in case said contracts have no stipulation as to
the term thereof.
ARTICLE 33. Under any one of the following conditions
the laborers may terminate their contracts with the
factories without serving on the latter any previous
notice:—
1) When a factory violates the terms of the working
contract or any important provisions of the
Government's labor laws;
2) When a factory fails to pay the wages at the
proper time without just cause;
3) When a factory maltreats the laborers.
ARTICLE 34. Disputes arising from the interpretations
and applications of paragraph 3 of Article 30, para-
graph 1 of Article 31 and Article 33 may be referred to
the Factory Council for settlement.
ARTICLE 35. Upon termination of the working contract,
the laborers may request the factory to issue them
certificates of work. But this stipulation shall not be
applicable in cases where the workers summarily
terminate their contract without conforming with the
provisions of Article 32, or in cases where the contracts
are terminated in accordance with any one of the con-
ditions mentioned in Article 31. The certificates of
work shall contain the following particulars:—
1) The laborers' name in full, age, birthplace and
address;
2) The kind of work engaged in by the laborer;
3) The period of time during which the laborer was
employed by the factory and his record.
5
page_data.zh:
2) 当工厂因自然灾害或不可抗力，被迫停工超过一个月时；
3) 当劳工无法履行其工作时。
第三十一条。工厂可在下列任一条件下终止与劳工的雇佣协议，而无需提前向他们发出任何通知：—
1) 当劳工屡次违反工厂规章时；
2) 当劳工无正当理由连续旷工超过三天，或一个月内旷工超过六天时。
第三十二条。若合同未规定期限，劳工可向工厂发出为期一周的通知，从而终止其劳动合同。
第三十三条。在下列任一条件下，劳工可终止与工厂的合同，而无需提前向后者发出任何通知：—
1) 当工厂违反劳动合同条款或政府劳动法的任何重要规定时；
2) 当工厂无正当理由未能按时支付工资时；
3) 当工厂虐待劳工时。
第三十四条。因解释和适用第三十条第三款、第三十一条第一款及第三十三条而产生的争议，可提交工厂委员会解决。
第三十五条。劳动合同终止时，劳工可要求工厂向其出具工作证明。但若工人未依照第三十二条规定而擅自终止合同，或合同依据第三十一条提到的任一条件终止，则本规定不适用。工作证明应包含以下详情：—
1) 劳工的全名、年龄、出生地和地址；
2) 劳工从事的工作种类；
3) 劳工受雇于工厂的期间及其表现记录。
5

page_data.en:
Chapter VII.
Laborers' Welfare
ARTICLE 36. All factories shall provide supplementary
education for the child laborers and apprentices, and
shall be responsible for all the expenses incurred
thereof. Such supplementary education shall not be
less than ten hours a week. For other laborers who
have no opportunity for education, the factories shall
also establish within their means educational facilities.
The time for conducting the above mentioned education
shall be arranged outside of the working hours.
ARTICLE 37. Female laborers shall be given leave with
full wages before and after child-birth, amounting
altogether to eight weeks in duration.
ARTICLE 38. Factories shall to the best of their ability
assist the laborers in establishing workers' savings and
cooperative societies, etc.
ARTICLE 39. Factories shall to the best of their ability
promote proper amusements for their laborers.
ARTICLE 40. At the end of each fiscal year, after due
appropriations have been made for dividends and
reserve funds the factory shall give those laborers who
have no demerits during the year, either a reward or a
share of the remaining profits.

Chapter VIII.
Safety and Sanitation
ARTICLE 41. All factories shall take the following
safety precautions:—
1) Safety precautions against risks of personal injury
to the laborers.
2) Safety precautions regarding the structure of the
factory.
3) Precautions regarding the proper installation of
machines.
4) Precautions for the prevention of fire and
floods.
ARTICLE 42. All factories shall have the following
sanitary provisions:—
1) Provisions for good ventilation;
2) ,, ,, pure drinks;
3) ,, ,, lavatories and toilet facilities;
4) ,, ,, light;
5) ,, ,, poison prevention.
ARTICLE 43. All factories shall give their laborers
safety education.
ARTICLE 44. Whenever the safety or sanitary provis-
ions of a factory are found inadequate, the proper
Authorities may require improvement within a definite

6
page_data.zh:
第七章。
劳工福利
第三十六条。所有工厂应为童工和学徒提供补习教育，并承担由此产生的一切费用。此类补习教育每周不得少于十小时。对于其他没有受教育机会的劳工，工厂也应在其能力范围内设立教育设施。进行上述教育的时间应安排在工作时间之外。
第三十七条。女劳工在产前和产后应享有带薪休假，共计八周。
第三十八条。工厂应尽最大努力协助劳工建立工人储蓄会和合作社等组织。
第三十九条。工厂应尽最大努力为劳工促进适当的娱乐活动。
第四十条。每个财政年度结束时，在拨出股息和储备金后，工厂应向当年无过失记录的劳工发放奖金或分享剩余利润。

第八章。
安全与卫生
第四十一条。所有工厂应采取以下安全措施：—
1) 防止劳工人身伤害风险的安全措施。
2) 关于工厂结构的安全措施。
3) 关于机器正确安装的措施。
4) 防火和防洪的措施。
第四十二条。所有工厂应具备以下卫生设施：—
1) 良好通风的设施；
2) ,, ,, 纯净饮用水；
3) ,, ,, 盥洗室和厕所设施；
4) ,, ,, 照明；
5) ,, ,, 防毒措施。
第四十三条。所有工厂应向劳工提供安全教育。
第四十四条。一旦发现工厂的安全或卫生设施不足，主管当局可要求在限定

6

page_data.en:
period of time, and in case of necessity may also forbid
the use of any part of the factory.

Chapter IX.

Laborers' Compensation and Pensions

ARTICLE 45. Pending the enforcement of Workers In-
surance Law, the factory shall pay to the laborers
injured or killed in the performance of their duty all
medical expenses and a sum based on the following
scale. If, however, the capital of the factory is less
than fifty thousand dollars, the factory may petition
the Proper Authorities to reduce the sums to be paid
1) For laborers temporarily incapacitated, the factory
shall, besides bearing the medical expenses, pay
them each day a sum amounting to two-thirds of
their regular wage for a period of not more than
six months. Upon the expiration of the said period,
the factory may reduce the amount of compensa-
tion to half of the laborers' average wage for a
period of not more than one year;
2) For workers permanently disabled in the perform-
ance of their duty, the factory shall pay a sum
commensurate with the extent of the disablement.
Such compensation, however, shall under no cir-
cumstances exceed three years' regular wages, or
be less than one year's wages;
3) For laborers killed in the course of their employ-
ment, the factory shall, besides paying a sum of
fifty dollars as funeral expenses, pay to the legal
heirs a sum of three hundred dollars, plus two
years' regular wages. The regular wage mention-
ed above shall be based upon the laborers' average
wage during the last three months of their employ-
ment. Funeral expenses and pensions shall be
paid at one and the same time, but compensation
for injuries or sickness or disablement may be paid
at regular intervals.

ARTICLE 46. Pensions provided for in the previous
Article shall be paid to the wife or husband of the
deceased laborer. Should the deceased leave no wife
or husband, the pension, unless otherwise provided
in the will of the deceased, shall be paid in the
following order:—
1) Children
2) Parents
3) Grandchildren
4) Brothers and sisters

ARTICLE 47. Whenever a laborer urgently needs money
on occasions of marriage or death, he may request the
factory to advance him a sum not exceeding one month's
wages, or the whole or a part of his savings.

7
page_data.zh:
期限内进行改进，并在必要时禁止使用工厂的任何部分。

第九章。

劳工赔偿与抚恤金

第四十五条。在《工人保险法》实施之前，工厂应向在执行职务中受伤或死亡的劳工支付所有医疗费用，并按以下标准支付一笔款项。但是，如果工厂资本少于五万美元，工厂可向主管当局申请减少支付金额
1) 对于暂时丧失劳动能力的劳工，工厂除承担医疗费用外，应在不超过六个月的期间内，每天向其支付相当于其正常工资三分之二的款项。上述期限届满后，工厂可将赔偿金额减至劳工平均工资的一半，期限不超过一年；
2) 对于在执行职务中永久残疾的工人，工厂应支付与残疾程度相称的一笔款项。然而，此类赔偿在任何情况下不得超过三年的正常工资，也不得少于一年的工资；
3) 对于在受雇期间死亡的劳工，工厂除支付五十美元作为丧葬费外，还应向法定继承人支付三百美元，外加两年的正常工资。上述正常工资应以劳工受雇最后三个月的平均工资为基础。丧葬费和抚恤金应一次性支付，但伤病或残疾赔偿金可按定期支付。

第四十六条。前条规定的抚恤金应支付给已故劳工的妻子或丈夫。若死者未留下妻子或丈夫，除非死者遗嘱另有规定，抚恤金应按以下顺序支付：—
1) 子女
2) 父母
3) 孙子女
4) 兄弟姐妹

第四十七条。每当劳工在婚丧事宜中急需用钱时，可请求工厂预支不超过一个月工资的款项，或其储蓄的全部或部分。

7

page_data.en:
ARTICLE 48. Should any accident occur resulting in the
death or grave injury to a laborer, the factory shall,
within five days, report its occurrence and the conse-
quent measures taken to the Proper Authorities.

Chapter X
Factory Council
ARTICLE 49. The Factory Council shall be composed of
an equal number of representatives from both the
factory and the laborers.
The factory representatives on the Factory Council
shall be selected from those who are familiar with the
conditions of the factory and the conditions of the
laborers.
The election of laborers' representatives shall be re-
ported to and supervised by the representatives of the
Proper Authorities.
ARTICLE 50. The duties of the Factory Council shall be
as follows:—
1) To study the improvement of working efficiency;
2) To improve the relations between the factory and
the laborers, and to settle disputes between them;
3) To cooperate in carrying out the working contract
and the regulations of the factory;
4) To cooperate in discussing methods of extending
the working day;
5) To improve the safety and sanitary conditions of
the factory;
6) To submit proposals for the improvement of
factory conditions;
7) To plan welfare enterprises for the laborers.
ARTICLE 51. Matters referred to in the previous Article
and concerning one workshop only shall first be refer-
red to the representatives of the workshop in question
and the factory. Should the representatives fail to
effect a solution or should the matter concern two or
more workshops, then the dispute shall be submitted to
the Factory Council for settlement. Should the Council
fail to effect a solution, then the dispute shall be set-
tled in accordance with the Laws for the Settlement
of Disputes Between Capital and Labor.
ARTICLE 52. Laborers above eighteen years of age shall
have the right to vote for the laborers' representatives
on the Factory Council.
ARTICLE 53. Laborers who are of Chinese nationality,
above 24 years of age and have worked in the factory
for more than six months shall have the right to be
elected as laborers' representatives.
ARTICLE 54. The number of representatives for either
the factory or the laborers shall be limited to from five
to nine.
page_data.zh:
第四十八条。若发生导致劳工死亡或重伤的事故，工厂应在五天内向主管当局报告事故发生情况及随后采取的措施。

第十章
工厂委员会
第四十九条。工厂委员会应由工厂和劳工双方同等数量的代表组成。
工厂委员会中的工厂代表应从熟悉工厂情况和劳工状况的人员中选出。
劳工代表的选举应向主管当局代表报告并接受其监督。
第五十条。工厂委员会的职责如下：—
1) 研究提高工作效率的方法；
2) 改善工厂与劳工之间的关系，并解决双方之间的争议；
3) 配合执行劳动合同和工厂规章；
4) 配合讨论延长工作日的方法；
5) 改善工厂的安全和卫生条件；
6) 提交改善工厂条件的提案；
7) 规划劳工福利事业。
第五十一条。前条所述事项若仅涉及一个车间，应首先提交给该车间的代表和工厂方面。若代表们未能达成解决方案，或事项涉及两个或更多车间，则应将争议提交工厂委员会解决。若委员会未能达成解决方案，则争议应依照《劳资争议处理法》解决。
第五十二条。年满十八岁以上的劳工有权投票选举工厂委员会中的劳工代表。
第五十三条。具有中国国籍、年满二十四岁以上且在工厂工作超过六个月的劳工，有资格被选为劳工代表。
第五十四条。工厂或劳工双方的代表人数应限制在五至九人之间。

page_data.en:
ARTICLE 55. The Chairman of the Factory Council
shall be elected alternatively by the factory
representatives and the laborers' representatives. The
Council shall have one regular meeting each month,
but in case of necessity may call special meetings.

Chapter XI.
Apprentices

ARTICLE 56. Factories taking apprentices shall first
conclude contracts with them or their legal
representatives. The contract shall be made in
triplicate, one copy for each of the contracting parties
and one to be submitted to the Proper Authorities for
registration. The contract shall contain the following
articles:—
1) The name, age, birthplace and address of the
apprentice.
2) The kind of trade the apprentice is to follow.
3) The date on which the contract is made and its
duration.
4) Mutual obligations; Should the apprentice be
required to pay tuition, the amount and time for
payment shall be stipulated. Where the contract
of apprenticeship provided remuneration for the
apprentice's service, the amount and time of
payment shall likewise be stipulated. The above
contract shall not restrict the apprentice's freedom
to work upon the expiration of the apprenticeship.
ARTICLE 57. Neither male nor female persons below the
age of fourteen shall be engaged as apprentices,
excepting those who were already engaged as apprentices
prior to the enforcement of this Law.
ARTICLE 58. The hours of training for apprentices
shall be governed by the provisions of Chapter III of
this Law.
ARTICLE 59. Except for purposes of practice, apprentices
shall not be engaged in any of the occupations
enumerated in Article 7.
ARTICLE 60. Apprentices shall be diligent, obedient and
loyal towards the officers and masters of the factory.
ARTICLE 61. During the whole term of apprenticeship,
the apprentices shall be supplied with board, lodging,
and medical care by the factory, in addition to a proper
allowance for incidentals each month,
ARTICLE 62. Except in cases of great necessity, no
apprentice shall leave the factory during the period of
apprenticeship; otherwise the apprentice or his legal
representative shall refund the board, lodging and
medical expenses incurred by the factory during the
period of apprenticeship already served.

9
page_data.zh:
第五十五条。工厂理事会主席应由厂方代表与劳工代表轮流选举产生。理事会每月举行一次例会，但在必要时可召开特别会议。

第十一章。
学徒

第五十六条。招收学徒的工厂，应首先与学徒或其法定代理人签订合同。合同一式三份，缔约各方各执一份，另一份提交主管当局登记。合同应包含以下条款：—
1) 学徒的姓名、年龄、籍贯及住址。
2) 学徒所从事的行业种类。
3) 合同签订日期及其期限。
4) 双方义务；若要求学徒缴纳学费，应规定金额及支付时间。若学徒合同约定为学徒的服务提供报酬，亦应规定金额及支付时间。上述合同不得限制学徒在学徒期满后的工作自由。
第五十七条。除在本法施行前已被招收为学徒者外，不得招收未满十四岁的男女为学徒。
第五十八条。学徒的培训时间应受本法第三章规定的约束。
第五十九条。除实习目的外，不得让学徒从事第七条所列的任何职业。
第六十条。学徒应对工厂的管理人员和师傅勤勉、服从且忠诚。
第六十一条。在整个学徒期间，工厂除每月提供适当的零用津贴外，还应向学徒提供食宿及医疗照顾，
第六十二条。除非有重大必要，学徒在学徒期间不得离开工厂；否则，学徒或其法定代理人应偿还工厂在已履行的学徒期间内产生的食宿及医疗费用。

9

page_data.en:
ARTICLE 63. The total number of apprentices taken by
a factory shall not exceed one-third of its regular
workers.
ARTICLE 64. Should a factory take more apprentices
than it can adequately train, the Proper Authorities
may order a partial reduction, and also set a limit to
the number of apprentices the factory may thereafter
take.
ARTICLE 65. During the period of apprenticeship the
factory shall to the best of its ability train the appren-
tices for the trade specified in the contract of appren-
ticeship.
ARTICLE 66. In addition to the provisions of Article
31, the factory may terminate the contract of appren-
ticeship under any one of the following conditions:—
1) When the apprentice revolts against proper
instructions;
2) When the apprentice commits theft and fails to
repent, in spite of repeated admonitions.
ARTICLE 67. In addition to the provisions of Article 33,
the apprentice or his legal representative may
terminate the contract of apprenticeship under any
one of the following conditions:—
1) When the factory is incapable of performing its
obligations stipulated in the contract;
2) When a factory becomes dangerous to the life
and health of the apprentice or harmful to his
character.

Chapter XII
Penalties

ARTICLE 68. Factories, violating the provisions of
Articles 7, 11, 12 and 13, shall be fined a sum of not
less than one hundred and not more than five hundred
dollars for each offence.
ARTICLE 69. Factories, violating the provisions of
Articles 5, 8, 9, 10, 37 and 63, shall be fined a sum of
not less than fifty and not more than three hundred
dollars for each offence.
ARTICLE 70. Factories, violating the provisions of
Article 45, shall be fined a sum of not less than fifty
and not more than two hundred dollars for each
offence.
ARTICLE 71. Factories, violating the provisions of
Articles 3, 4, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 and 36, shall be fined
a sum of not more than one hundred dollars for each
offence.
ARTICLE 72. When a factory foreman, due to disloyal
conduct or negligence, causes thereby an accident or
the extension thereof, he shall be punished with impri-

10
page_data.zh:
第六十三条。一家工厂招收的学徒总数不得超过其正式工人的三分之一。
第六十四条。若工厂招收的学徒超过其能充分培训的数量，主管当局可命令部分削减，并限定该工厂此后可招收的学徒人数。
第六十五条。在学徒期间，工厂应尽最大努力按照学徒合同中规定的行业对学徒进行培训。
第六十六条。除第三十一条的规定外，工厂可在下列任一情况下终止学徒合同：—
1) 当学徒反抗正当指导时；
2) 当学徒犯有盗窃行为，尽管经多次劝诫仍不悔改时。
第六十七条。除第三十三条的规定外，学徒或其法定代理人可在下列任一情况下终止学徒合同：—
1) 当工厂无法履行合同中规定的义务时；
2) 当工厂对学徒的生命和健康构成危险或对其品行有害时。

第十二章
罚则

第六十八条。违反第七条、第十一条、第十二条和第十三条规定的工厂，每项违规行为处以不少于一百元且不超过五百元的罚款。
第六十九条。违反第五条、第八条、第九条、第十条、第三十七条和第六十三条规定的工厂，每项违规行为处以不少于五十元且不超过三百元的罚款。
第七十条。违反第四十五条规定的工厂，每项违规行为处以不少于五十元且不超过二百元的罚款。
第七十一条。违反第三条、第四条、第十四条、第十五条、第十六条、第十七条、第十八条、第十九条和第三十六条规定的工厂，每项违规行为处以不超过一百元的罚款。
第七十二条。工厂领班因不忠行为或疏忽，从而导致事故或使事故扩大的，应处以不超

10

page_data.en:
sonment for a period of not more than one year, or
with a fine of not more than five hundred dollars.
ARTICLE 73. Any laborer who obstructs the operation
of the factory or destroys the goods or equipment of the
factory by violence, shall be liable to criminal punish-
ment of the severest degree.
ARTICLE 74. A laborer who by duress forces another
fellow-worker or his fellow-workers to strike, may be
summarily dismissed or sent to the Proper Authorities
for due punishment.

Chapter XIII.
Addenda
ARTICLE 75. The compilation or alteration of factory
regulations shall be submitted to the Proper Authorities
for approval and promulgation.
ARTICLE 76. Regulations for the enforcement of this
Law shall be issued separately.
ARTICLE 77. The date for the enforcement of this Law
shall be fixed by a special order.

END

11
page_data.zh:
过一年的监禁，或处以不超过五百元的罚款。
第七十三条。任何工人以暴力阻碍工厂运营或毁坏工厂货物或设备的，应承担最严厉的刑事处罚。
第七十四条。工人以胁迫手段强迫其他工友或众工友罢工的，可被即行解雇或送交主管当局予以适当惩处。

第十三章。
附则
第七十五条。工厂规章的编制或修改应提交主管当局批准并颁布。
第七十六条。本法施行细则另行制定。
第七十七条。本法施行日期由特别命令确定。

完

SPECIAL POLICE
5492/
19/3/
November 14, 1931. Afternoon

the main issues and other local news, more
precisely the following reports:-
With regard to the number of factories in
the locality and the difficulty in organizing them, the
local branch of social affairs discovered from experience
that seventeen articles of the factory law and regulations
are inapplicable in the existing circumstances. The
bureau submitted a detailed report of the difficulties
encountered by these clauses to the municipality of
Shanghai. Having received it, it forwarded the report
with their explanations and sent it to the Ministry of
Industries for consideration. The problem was subsequently
discussed at the National Conference which ruled that
all the clauses of Nos. 18 and 49 which have yet to be
enforced by the National Government, must be enforced in
accordance with the decisions of the Ministry of Industries.
The following are the seventeen clauses which the Bureau
of Social Affairs regarded as impracticable:-
1. "Those factories using steam, electricity or
hydraulics as their motive power, and the number of
whose workers exceed thirty, are considered as
being subject to the Factory Law."
The weak point is now in those factories which use
both motor and manual power for the operation of
their works. The total number of workers employed
amounts to less than thirty, but when the owners
wish to evade the factory law, they can transfer
their factories from one into two and make it possible
for less than thirty workers to be working in each
factory, and in this manner they are not liable
according to the factory law.
2. "Employment of workers"
This clause is too comprehensive; it is not stated
if cooks, porters or boys come under the category
of workers. As the temporary workers, contract
workers, day workers or piece workers come under the
letter of the factory law.
3. "Registration of factory workers' term of service"
This is impossible of fulfillment because most of
the factory workers cannot remember the date when
they entered the employ of the factories.
3. "Sickness, injuries to workers and their medical
treatment".
Details should be given to show if their sickness or
injuries were caused by the work performed by them.
4. "Owing to unfavourable conditions which causes factories
to sustain losses or delays in the work, the factories
are permitted to lengthen the workers' working hours,
but must report reasons for the extension of the
working hours to the official institutions."
It is not defined if this report must be submitted
prior to or after extending the length of the working
days. In most cases, factory owners have not time
to make such frequent reports.
5. "No juvenile workers must be allowed to work more
than eight hours per day".
This clause affects the work of the grown-up workers
who, in many cases, have to stop their work immediately
the boy's help is withdrawn.
page_data.zh:
特别警察
5492/
19/3/
1931年11月14日。下午

主要问题及其他本地新闻，更确切地说是以下报告：-
关于该地区工厂的数量及其组织困难，社会局地方分局从经验中发现，《工厂法》及其规章中的十七条条款在目前情况下不适用。该局向上海市政府提交了一份关于这些条款所遇困难的详细报告。收到后，市政府附上其解释并将报告转送实业部审议。随后，该问题在全国会议上进行了讨论，会议裁定，国民政府尚未施行的第十八条和第四十九条的所有条款，必须按照实业部的决定予以施行。以下是社会局认为不可行的十七条条款：-
1. “使用蒸汽、电力或水力作为动力，且工人数量超过三十人的工厂，被视为受《工厂法》管辖。”
目前的弱点在于那些同时使用机动和人力进行作业的工厂。雇佣工人总数少于三十人，但当业主希望规避《工厂法》时，他们可以将一家工厂拆分为两家，使每家工厂的工人少于三十人，从而以此方式免除《工厂法》的责任。
2. “工人的雇佣”
此条款过于宽泛；未说明厨师、搬运工或童仆是否属于工人范畴。临时工、合同工、日工或计件工均属于《工厂法》的字面涵盖范围。
3. “工厂工人服务期限的登记”
这是无法履行的，因为大多数工厂工人记不住他们进入工厂受雇的日期。
3. “工人的疾病、工伤及其医疗”。
应提供细节以表明其疾病或工伤是否由其所从事的工作引起。
4. “由于不利条件导致工厂遭受损失或工作延误，允许工厂延长工人的工作时间，但必须向官方机构报告延长工作时间的原因。”
未定义此报告必须在延长工作日之前还是之后提交。在大多数情况下，工厂主没有时间进行如此频繁的报告。
5. “未成年工人每天工作时间不得超过八小时”。
此条款影响成年工人的工作，在许多情况下，一旦撤走童工的协助，成年工人就必须立即停止工作。

page_data.en:
No. 307 14, 1946
STOCKHOLM TRANSLATION

The female workers are all allowed to work before six
o'clock in the morning or after ten o'clock at night.
This rule should not be applied for a long time because it
is very detrimental to the interests of the majority
of the silk and cotton mills as also to the workers
themselves.
1. All workers should be given one day's rest in every
seven days.
If this rule means that the worker has no alternative
but to accept, even if he/she does not want it, it is still
objectionable. Access to the factories
should be given to workers who have
completed a certain period of service.
This time of leave, when fixed by the workers themselves,
is dangerous for it threatens the supervision of all
work because when the workers suddenly come back
during the busiest season when the factories are
engaged in very important work.
2. That full pay be given to workers for rest days, as
stipulated in articles 18 and 19.
A certain kinds of work are continuous and can not
be stopped for a time, is it expected that the employers
change workers to continue the work by giving double
pay? Some of this kind can be given to day workers,
when their pay depends on the amount of work performed.
3. Workers' wages must not be cut by their employers as
compensation for damages or for infringement of their
contracts etc.
Sometimes, workers agree to pay security funds to their
employers on the installment basis by agreeing to
certain reductions being made from their monthly wages.
How is it proposed to deal with this matter?
4. "Contract workers engaged on work having no fixed
time, must inform their employers one week ahead why
they wish to dissolve their contract."
Suppose the workers do not inform their employers of
their desire to terminate their contracts, will it be
possible in these circumstances for the employers to
demand compensation from the workers?
5. "That eight weeks' leave with full pay be given to
female workers before and after child-birth."
Eight weeks time exceeds the necessity for female
workers to be on leave for child birth, and it is also
impossible for factories to sustain such pecuniary losses.
6. "Workers who die or become sick because through their
work must be given medical fees and a pension."
No proper definition of the term "die or become sick
through their work" is given. The workers can claim
that all their sicknesses are due to work.
7. All labour disputes which cannot be settled must be
referred to the Factory Inspection Committee for
conciliation and settlement.
This article requires to be more fully explained.
8. "Five to nine representatives respectively from both
the employers and the employees of the factories
are to be elected members of the above mentioned
Committee."
It should be clearly defined whether workers have
the right to elect their representatives because
workers are not employees of the factories.
9. "Punishment regulations"
There are only a few items covering these regulations and

No. 307 14, 1946
斯德哥尔摩译文

所有女工均被允许在早上六点之前或晚上十点之后工作。
此规则不应长期适用，因为它非常损害大多数丝厂和棉纺厂的利益，同时也损害工人自身的利益。
1. 所有工人每七天应休息一天。
如果此规则意味着工人即使不愿意也必须接受，那仍然是不可取的。应允许已完成一定服务期的工人进入工厂休假。
这段由工人自行确定的休假时间是危险的，因为它威胁到对所有工作的监管，因为当工厂忙于非常重要的工作时，工人们可能在最繁忙的季节突然回来。
2. 按照第十八条和第十九条的规定，在休息日向工人支付全额工资。
某些种类的工作是连续性的，不能暂时停止，是否期望雇主通过支付双倍工资来更换工人以继续工作？其中一些可以给予日工，因为他们的工资取决于完成的工作量。
3. 雇主不得以损害赔偿或违反合同等为由扣除工人工资。
有时，工人同意通过同意从每月工资中扣除一定金额的方式，分期向雇主支付保证金。对此事拟如何处理？
4. “从事无固定期限工作的合同工，必须提前一周通知雇主其希望解除合同的原因。”
假设工人未将其终止合同的意愿通知雇主，在这种情况下，雇主是否可能向工人要求赔偿？
5. “女工在分娩前后应享有八周的全薪假期。”
八周的时间超过了女工休产假的需要，而且工厂也不可能承受这样的金钱损失。
6. “因工作而死亡或生病的工人必须获得医疗费和养老金。”
对“因工作而死亡或生病”一词没有给出适当的定义。工人可以声称他们所有的疾病都是由于工作引起的。
7. 所有无法解决的劳资纠纷必须提交工厂检查委员会进行调解和解决。
本条需要更充分的解释。
8. “工厂雇主和雇员分别选举五至九名代表作为上述委员会的成员。”
应明确界定工人是否有权选举其代表，因为工人并非工厂的雇员。
9. “处罚规定”

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. I. O... 5492
THE NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 19, 1928.

THE CHINESE
FACTORY LAW

Recently we drew attention to the provisions of the Factory Law proposed by the Nationalist Government, pointing out that at a period when the further industrialization of China is in the minds of a great many of the most enterprising merchants, it is likely to have the effect of decisively retarding it. Further inquiry into this subject shows that on the whole we understated the case, but before going into that, the result of inquiry into the origin of the proposed law provides much food for thought. At the time when the Communists were in control in the Wuhan centre another Factory Law was brought into existence, and so far as we have been able to ascertain this one in no essentials differs from that outspokenly Communistic document. In Western countries when an important new measure of this kind is in the minds of a political party it is generally found that only after careful inquiry among leaders of industry, coupled with investigation of the workers' condition, are the provisions of the law laid down. In this case owners of factories have not been consulted in regard to the measure, and so far as can be ascertained the employer of labour whose advice has been asked by the Government has been the director of a printing concern. One would have hoped that the heads of the cotton industry would be the first consulted, but as they were not, and further as they would have told the Government that nothing short of ruin would attend the promulgation of this measure, it takes on a new aspect. It is, in effect, practically drawn word for word from the Communist book of legislation, is utterly inharmonious with the needs of the country in its present state.

We are talking now from the point of view of the Chinese owned mills. This phase of the industrialization of China dates from 1918, and its history in the intervening years has not been especially happy. Now the mill owners are faced with a law which gives satisfaction to no one. In dealing with the subject previously we stated that it would drive fresh capital away from such enterprises in future, but we learn that the introduction of an eight-hour day, as is proposed, will have the additional effect of causing the mills to close. On the other hand the agitators who lead the labour unions have decided that they are not satisfied with it, and strange as it may appear where a piece of legislation is concerned which we described as Socialistic but which the Chinese mill owners do not hesitate to call Communistic, they are dissatisfied with it as being too capitalistically inclined, so the Government measure pleases nobody. In facing the hard facts of the case, however, we see that in any factory law designed for China at the present time the Government should have, in a temporary measure at any rate, taken such circumstances as the following into consideration. Since 1921 until the present day the Chinese mills have not been able to make profits, hence all talk of profit-sharing by the workers is illusory. That the mills are making a profit today is solely a result of the Japanese boycott and may, possibly, not be economically sound. It must be remembered that when mills were a popular feature for investment of Chinese capital in 1918, the cost of machinery was at its highest, and thus commenced the large overhead expenses which have hampered them ever since. There was inexperience among the promoters, and this has had to be paid for. Then they undertook the great task of putting up mills with, say, 40,000 spindles against huge Japanese organizations having 400,000, and the case has proved to be a desperate one. Why in the circumstances hamper a young industry with a set of Communistic laws when other important measures would tend to improve the situation?

By insisting on the elimination of a night shift, the proposed Law enacts that employment will be given to so many fewer workers, for there are no other mills at present existing in China to employ them. A government suggesting such a measure as that in the present state of Chinese industrialization is undertaking a grave responsibility. What might have been done very effectively, however, is a financial measure which would in the course of time have eased the position of the mills effectively. One of the greatest handicaps these companies have had to carry has been their overdrafts, and that is a much more serious matter in China than elsewhere. Whereas Japanese companies can secure an overdraft at about six per cent. per annum, Chinese have to pay between twelve and twenty per cent., and this burden has already greatly handicapped the industry. A strong central bank is required to bring down the rate of interest in China—it need not lend money on its own account, but its presence behind merchant banks would mean that they could give the necessary accommodation with security and on a much lower scale than what is generally considered satisfactory by Chinese banks as they are at present constituted. That would have been a much better line of legislation to take than the one that has been adopted. The Factory Law has not yet been put into force, and Chinese and other millowners have no information whether it will go into force next month or ten years hence. They realize, however, that if it is enforced as at present announced, they will have to shut up, for the eight-hour day is not yet economically sound in China, and that means not only loss of earning power and of capital but hardship for the people who at present get their livelihood through the mills.

《字林西报》，1928年12月19日，星期三。

中国
工厂法

近日我们曾提请注意国民政府拟议的工厂法条款，并指出在中国许多最具进取心的商人正考虑进一步推进工业化的时期，该法很可能产生 decisively 阻碍工业化的效果。对此主题的进一步调查显示，总体而言我们此前低估了问题的严重性，但在深入探讨之前，对拟议法律起源的调查结果提供了许多值得思考的内容。在共产党人控制武汉中心时期，另一部工厂法应运而生，据我们所知，这部法律在本质上与那份公然具有共产主义色彩的文件并无二致。在西方国家，当一个政党酝酿此类重要的新措施时，通常发现只有在对工业领袖进行仔细征询，并结合对工人状况的调查之后，才会制定法律条款。而在本案中，并未就该项措施征询工厂主的意见，据查，政府征询过意见的雇主是一家印刷公司的董事。人们原本希望棉纺业巨头会是首批被征询的对象，但既然他们没有受到征询，而且如果他们受到征询，他们会告诉政府，颁布此项措施将导致毁灭性的后果，这使得情况呈现出新的面貌。实际上，这几乎是逐字逐句地从共产主义立法手册中照搬而来，与中国目前的国情需求完全格格不入。

我们现在是从华资纱厂的角度来谈论这个问题。中国工业化的这一阶段始于1918年，其间的发展历程并非特别顺利。如今，纱厂主们面临着一部令各方都不满意的法律。在前次讨论该主题时，我们曾表示这将使未来的新资本远离此类企业，但我们获悉，如拟议那样实行八小时工作制，还将产生导致纱厂关闭的额外影响。另一方面，领导工会的激进分子已决定他们对此并不满意，尽管看似奇怪，但对于一部我们描述为具有社会主义色彩、而华资纱厂主毫不迟疑地称之为共产主义的法律，他们却因认为其过于倾向资本主义而感到不满，因此政府的这项措施未能取悦任何人。然而，面对严峻的现实，我们看到，任何旨在适用于当前中国的工厂法，政府至少应在临时措施中考虑到以下情况。自1921年至今，华资纱厂一直无法盈利，因此工人分享利润的所有说法都是虚幻的。纱厂今日之所以盈利，完全是抵制日货的结果，这在经济上可能并不稳固。必须记住，1918年纱厂成为华资投资的热门对象时，机器成本处于最高位，从而开始了此后一直困扰它们的高额经常性开支。发起者缺乏经验，而这不得不付出代价。随后，他们承担了建立拥有例如4万锭纱机的纱厂的艰巨任务，以对抗拥有40万锭纱机的庞大日本组织，事实证明这是一场绝望的竞争。既然如此，为何要用一套共产主义法律来束缚一个年轻的工业，而其他重要措施本可以改善局势？

通过坚持取消夜班，拟议法律规定将减少大量工人的就业机会，因为目前中国没有其他纱厂可以雇佣他们。在中国工业化目前的状况下，政府提出此类措施是在承担严重的责任。然而，本可以采取的一项非常有效的措施是金融措施，这将随着时间的推移有效缓解纱厂的处境。这些公司不得不承担的最大障碍之一是它们的透支贷款，这在中国比在其他地方更为严重。日本公司可以以每年约6%的利率获得透支贷款，而中国公司必须支付12%至20%的利息，这一负担已经极大地阻碍了该行业的发展。需要一个强大的中央银行来降低中国的利率——它无需以自己的名义放贷，但它在商业银行背后的存在意味着，这些银行能够以比目前中国银行普遍认为令人满意的水平更低、更安全的条件提供必要的融资。这将是比已采用的方案更好的立法途径。工厂法尚未生效，华资及其他纱厂主无从得知该法将在下个月还是十年后生效。然而，他们意识到，如果按目前宣布的那样强制执行，他们将不得不关闭工厂，因为八小时工作制在中国尚不具备经济合理性，这不仅意味着收入能力和资本的损失，也意味着给目前依靠纱厂谋生的人们带来困苦。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, DECEMBER 9, 1928

CHINA'S FACTORY LAW
Editor, THE CHINA PRESS.
Sir:—From your leading article dated the 5th inst. on the Factory Law proposed by the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Labor one sees there is a good deal of mis-apprehension regarding the aims and the contents of the Law. Since your criticism precedes the public-ation of the provisions of the Law —even in skeleton form—the mind of your readers may be so prejudic-ed as to render an independent and fair appreciation of the issue most difficult, if not impossible. The hasty condemnation of an issue before being given a hearing is, to say the least, an undignified and extraordinary procedure in journ-alism.
With regard to the distribution of profits as provided in Chapter VIII in the proposed Law, your criticism is entirely founded on misconception. The following are the articles dealing with this ques-tion:—
Art. 44.—If a factory, on each occa-sion of balancing its accounts, shows a surplus, after due deductions having been made for expenses and depreciation, one-tenth of the said surplus shall be paid into the reserve fund, which may be ap-plied to the compensation of losses and the expansion of the enterprise.
If the amount of the said surplus ex-ceeds 30 per cent of the total capital invested in the factory, one-half of the sum in excess thereof shall be paid into a special reserve fund.
The special reserve fund may be ap-plied, in addition to the purposes men-tioned in the first paragraph of this ar-ticle, to meeting the insufficiency, if any, of the official interest of the capital in future.
Art. 45.—After due appropriations having been made for the reserve funds from the surplus, an official interest of eight percent on the actual amount of the capital paid in shall be paid to the share-holders as "Capital's" due remuneration. If the surplus is insufficient for this pur-pose, the amount of this interest may be decreased.
If the local rate of official interest is higher or lower than eight percent, the rate may be altered with the permission of the proper authorities.
Art. 46.—After due appropriations hav-ing been made for reserve funds and of-ficial interest, the remaining part of the surplus is the "divisible profits," one-tenth of which shall belong to the Management and the remainder shall be equally divided between "Labor" and "Capital."
Under the term "Labor" are included all the employees of the factory who have served at least for six months, excluding members of the Board of Managers, the Board of Directors and the factory owner. In the management are included members of the Board of Directors, gen-eral managers, managers, chief engineers, heads of business departments and those who have similar responsibilities. In case of ambiguity the Board of Directors or the owner of the factory shall make a decision.
Art. 47.—The debts, if any, of the fac-tory contracted in the past must be paid before official interest and profits are distributed.
Art. 48.—The forty-five percent of the divisible profits belonging to "Capital" shall be distributed in direct proportion to the amount of the capital actually paid in as investment in the factory by the shareholders.
Art. 49.—The forty-five percent of the divisible profits belonging to "Labor" shall be distributed by the factory to the em-ployees in direct proportion to the wages actually received by the latter, having regard moreover to their length of ser-vice and their achievement. Should the employee receive profits in an amount ex-ceeding one month's wages, at least one-half of the sum in excess thereof shall be paid into his savings account or shall be applied to purchasing the shares of the factory.
Art. 50.—Such funds as employees' bene-fit fund, educational fund, pension fund and the share contributed by the factory for the employee's insurance shall all be considered as operating expenses of the factory.
From the above articles it should become apparent that the proposed profit-sharing plan duly takes care of the interests of the investors as well as those of the employees. In-vestors are protected because the payment of interest on their shares has a prior claim, besides receiving forty-five per cent of the divisible profits, if any. The employees, on the other hand, should find an in-centive in this plan to work hard-er, so as to have more to be shared. If Chinese labor is not so efficient as labor in Europe and America, some means should be found to make it more so. The best way is to give Labor a suitable portion of what it helps to produce. The cause for the occasional failures of profit-sharing plans in the West is that they do not give enough to Labor to make it worth while, and they are not regulated by law. In China the system of profit-sharing is no innovation; it has proved its usefulness in the past in many lines of business. What the pro-posed Factory Law does is to adapt it to modern conditions. A success-ful application of this Law will do much to bridge the gap between the so-called "Capital" and "Labor" and will help to create peace and goodwill in industry.
The other criticisms in your lead-ing article are also largely based on a misapprehension of the spirit and substance of the proposed Law. There are two guiding principles in the drafting of the Law, viz. (1) production must be increased through higher efficiency and by placing the control in the hands of the management, and (2) all pos-sible reform in conditions of labor under existing conditions should be introduced. Regarding the first principle, the conditions of dismiss-al play an important role. It is undeniable that dismissal

《字林西报》，1928年12月9日，星期日

中国的工厂法

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生：从贵报本月5日关于农工商部 proposed 的工厂法的社论中可以看出，人们对该法的目标和内容存在不少误解。由于贵报的批评发表在该法条款（即使是纲要形式）公布之前，读者的思想可能会因此产生偏见，使得对该问题进行独立和公正的评价变得极其困难，甚至不可能。在未经听证的情况下匆忙谴责一个议题，退一步说，也是新闻界一种不体面且非同寻常的做法。

关于拟议法律第八章规定的利润分配问题，贵报的批评完全基于误解。以下是处理此问题的条款：

第44条.—工厂每次结算账目时，在扣除费用和折旧后如有盈余，应将所述盈余的十分之一存入公积金，该公积金可用于弥补亏损和扩大企业。

如果所述盈余金额超过工厂总投资资本的百分之三十，则超出部分的一半应存入特别公积金。

特别公积金除用于本条第一款所述用途外，还可用于弥补未来资本法定利息的不足（如有）。

第45条.—从盈余中适当拨出公积金后，应按实缴资本实际金额的百分之八向股东支付法定利息，作为“资本”的应得报酬。如果盈余不足以支付此项费用，可以降低该利息金额。

如果当地法定利率高于或低于百分之八，经主管当局批准，可以更改该利率。

第46条.—在适当拨出公积金和法定利息后，剩余的盈余部分为“可分配利润”，其中十分之一归管理层所有，其余部分在“劳工”和“资本”之间平均分配。

“劳工”一词包括在工厂服务至少六个月的所有雇员，但不包括管理委员会成员、董事会成员和工厂主。管理层包括董事会成员、总经理、经理、总工程师、业务部门负责人以及具有类似职责的人员。如有歧义，由董事会或工厂主作出决定。

第47条.—工厂过去所欠债务（如有）必须在分配法定利息和利润之前偿还。

第48条.—属于“资本”的可分配利润的百分之四十五，应按股东实际投入工厂的资本金额比例直接分配。

第49条.—属于“劳工”的可分配利润的百分之四十五，应由工厂根据雇员实际收到的工资直接分配给雇员，同时考虑到他们的服务年限和业绩。如果雇员获得的利润超过一个月的工资，超出部分的至少一半应存入其储蓄账户或用于购买工厂股份。

第50条.—员工福利基金、教育基金、养老金基金以及工厂为员工保险缴纳的份额等资金，均应视为工厂的经营费用。

从上述条款中可以明显看出，拟议的利润分享计划充分照顾了投资者和雇员的利益。投资者受到保护，因为他们的股份利息支付拥有优先权，此外还能获得百分之四十五的可分配利润（如有）。另一方面，雇员应该在这一计划中找到努力工作的动力，以便有更多的份额可供分配。如果中国劳工的效率不如欧美劳工，就应该找到方法提高效率。最好的办法是让劳工获得其帮助生产的产品的适当份额。西方利润分享计划偶尔失败的原因是，它们给予劳工的份额不足以使其觉得值得，而且不受法律监管。在中国，利润分享制度并非创新；它过去在许多行业已证明其有用性。拟议的工厂法所做的是使其适应现代条件。成功实施该法将大大弥合所谓“资本”与“劳工”之间的差距，并有助于在工业界创造和平与善意。

贵报社论中的其他批评也 largely 基于对拟议法律精神和实质的误解。起草该法有两个指导原则，即：(1) 必须通过提高效率和将控制权掌握在管理层手中来增加生产，以及 (2) 应在现有条件下引入所有可能的劳工状况改革。关于第一个原则，解雇条件起着重要作用。不可否认，解雇

page_data.en:
of workers has become a prolific source of industrial conflicts. The workers demand that no dismissal should take place unless their unions give their approval. In such circumstances no efficiency is possible. The proposed articles governing dismissals provide the conditions under which workers could be dismissed. It is infinitely better that the control of employment should be thus regulated than to leave the whole question to be settled by a trial of strength between "Capital" and "Labor." The granting of the right to dismiss workers by law under justifiable conditions constitutes the cornerstone of the edifice of industrial efficiency.

As to the restriction of child labor, the limitation of working hours and night work for women, the practice is now so common in countries where employers and journalists a few decades ago united to convince the world that reforms were visionary and impossible. The principles of humanity and industrial efficiency in this connection have become so well known that it would be a waste of space to repeat. If young children must work because they need the pittance they earn, there is no reason why able-bodied men with dependents, now workless and starving, should not be given the work the children are made to do. If children have no schools to go to, there is no reason why they should be sent to factories irrespective of night or day, so that the city fathers could sit at ease and think they have no need to give them education. If there are still people who think that women, whether they be mothers or expectant mothers, should work through regular night shifts, so that able-bodied men, now workless, may sleep comfortably at home, these people are hopeless. Their only cure is to send their own mothers, sisters, wives and children to work in factories under present conditions. These people surely do not know that such things are of the past. They are not tolerated in other leading countries and they will not be tolerated here.

It is often complained that the Chinese worker is not efficient. The question is whether he can be or cares to be efficient under existing conditions. Here is the vicious circle: Bad conditions produce inefficiency, inefficiency requires bad conditions. To follow this circle would please some people perhaps, but it is out of the question for the present Chinese Government to tolerate it. It has got to be broken.

If there are some foreign people who think the best thing to do is to leave industrial matters unregulated by law, let them look up the network of industrial legislation and factory inspection in their own countries and see whether they are likely to stop China doing likewise.

If they can realize what the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Labor is doing they should hold themselves ready to help bring on the reforms that are sooner or later bound to come.

Lastly I wish to point out that the proposed Factory Law was not drafted by immature or ignorant persons. Those who are charged with the work have had years of investigation and study of actual conditions. Then the Law was studied very closely by the Law Drafting Commission of the Ministry which sat several times a week for two months and every sentence was studied and voted upon. The Commission was largely composed of prominent industrial experts, employers, labor experts, economists and administrators in their personal capacities. While not everyone on the Commission agreed with the proposed Factory Law in its present form, the majority ruled. There was no difference of view so far as the principles were concerned.

In conclusion, permit me to say that all progressive people, whether Chinese or foreign, should take a constructive interest in the present efforts to put industry in China, until recently so upset, onto a sound and constitutional basis. Only in this way can China's economic development be hastened.

Thanking you for your space,
I am, etc.,
M. THOMAS TCHOU.
Nanking, Dec. 6, 1928.

工人已成为工业冲突的多发源头。工人要求，除非得到工会批准，否则不得进行任何解雇。在这种情况下，效率是不可能的。拟议的关于解雇的条款规定了可以解雇工人的条件。这样规范雇佣控制权，比让“资本”和“劳工”通过实力较量来解决整个问题要好得多。在法律规定的正当理由下赋予解雇工人的权利，构成了工业效率大厦的基石。

至于限制童工、限制妇女工作时间和夜班工作，这种做法在几十年前雇主和记者联合向世界 convince 改革是空想且不可能的那些国家如今已非常普遍。在此方面的人道主义和工业效率原则已广为人知，再重复实属浪费篇幅。如果幼童必须工作是因为他们需要赚取微薄的收入，那么就没有理由不让那些有家庭负担、目前失业且挨饿的成年男子去做孩子们被迫做的工作。如果孩子们没有学校可上，就没有理由不分昼夜地将他们送进工厂，以便城市父老可以安坐无忧，认为无需为他们提供教育。如果还有人认为，无论是母亲还是孕妇，妇女都应该定期上夜班，以便让目前失业的成年男子可以在家舒适地睡觉，那么这些人真是无可救药。治愈他们的唯一办法是将他们自己的母亲、姐妹、妻子和孩子送到当前条件下的工厂工作。这些人肯定不知道这些事情已成为过去。其他主要国家不容忍此类事情，这里也不会容忍。

人们常抱怨中国工人效率不高。问题在于，在现有条件下，他能否提高效率或是否关心提高效率。这是一个恶性循环：恶劣的条件导致低效率，低效率又需要恶劣的条件。遵循这个循环或许会让一些人高兴，但目前的中国政府绝不可能容忍它。必须打破这个循环。

如果有些外国人认为最好的做法是让工业事务不受法律监管，那就让他们查阅自己国家的工业立法和工厂检查网络，看看他们是否可能阻止中国效仿。

如果他们能认识到农工商部正在做什么，他们就应准备好帮助推动迟早必然到来的改革。

最后，我想指出，拟议的工厂法并非由不成熟或无知的人士起草。负责这项工作的人对实际情况进行了多年的调查和研究。随后，该法由部里的法律起草委员会进行了非常仔细的研究，该委员会在两个月内每周开会数次，每一句话都经过研究和表决。委员会主要由著名的工业专家、雇主、劳工专家、经济学家和行政管理人员以个人身份组成。虽然委员会并非每个人都同意目前形式的拟议工厂法，但多数意见占主导。在原则问题上没有观点分歧。

总之，请允许我说，所有进步人士，无论是中国人还是外国人，都应对目前将近期如此动荡的中国工业置于健全和宪法基础之上的努力给予建设性的关注。只有这样才能加速中国的经济发展。

感谢贵报提供版面，

此致，

M. THOMAS TCHOU（朱卓文）

南京，1928年12月6日。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 6, 1928

CHINA'S PROPOSED FACTORY LAW

A Measure of Sixteen Chapters Dealing with Child Labour
Profit-Sharing, Conditions of Work, Etc.

EXISTING PRACTICES TO BE REVOLUTIONIZED

Nanking, Dec. 3.
A Factory Law has been drafted by the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Labour and discussed by the Legal Commission of the Ministry and will shortly be submitted to the Government Council for adoption and enforcement. The Law consists of 16 chapters, namely, general provisions, contracts, dismissals, working hours, rest, standard of production, wages, distribution of profit, sanitation and safety, works' councils, apprenticeship, workers' welfare, special regulations, registration and reports, inspection and penalties.
Chapter I provides that the law is applicable to all factories, established within the territory of the Republic of China and regularly employing more than 30 workers. A factory must first register with the Ministry of Industry Commerce and Labour through the proper local government organ before it can proceed to enlist workers and start operation.

No Employees under Fourteen
Chapter II provides that child labour under the age of 14 should be prohibited in all factories, and all boys and girls above 14 and below 16 are considered as minor workers who will be permitted to be engaged in light and easy work only. A worker may enter into an individual contract with the factory, while the Labour Unions may conclude collective contracts with the factories on behalf of any group of workers. Contracts of both kinds must be in writing and must first be approved by the proper government organs before they can become valid.

When Dismissal May Take Place
Chapter III deals with dismissals of workers. Individual contracts will be cancelled upon expiration of their stipulated time, but may be renewed by mutual agreement. As regards those individual contracts for which no stipulation of time is made, if either party desires the cancellation of the same, a notice must be given to the other party at least one month in advance. For summary dismissals by the factories, a minimum extra sum of money amounting to one month's wages of the workers must be given to the dismissed workers. Before social insurance laws are put into force an additional sum equal to one month must be given.
Employers may terminate their employment of the workers under one of the following conditions:
1. When a factory suspends operation.
2. When any part of factory ceases functioning with permission from the proper authorities.
3. When a factory, either through natural disasters or by force of unforeseen circumstances, is obliged to suspend operation for over a period of one month.
4. When a worker is incapable of doing his work properly or when the nature of the work is unsuitable to the worker.
5. When the average result of a worker for a period of six months is below two-thirds of the required efficiency.
6. When a worker violates the rules of the factory.
7. When a worker fails to report for work without reason for over three consecutive days or when a worker absents himself more than six days within one month.
8. When within one year a worker takes leave of absence for more than two months; or sick leave of more than three months, or when a worker takes a combined ordinary and sick leave of absence for more than four months.

Contracts Cancelled
Workers may consider their contracts with the factories cancelled under one of the following conditions:—
1. When factories violate the terms of the contracts and the Factory Law.
2. When factories fail to pay the wages at proper time without any reason.
3. When factory owners or their employees assault or maltreat workers.
4. When factories neglect the sanitary conditions and safety of the workers.

The Eight-Hour Day
Chapter IV deals with working hours. The regular daily working period for adults is eight hours, but, owing to varying local conditions and the nature of the work, factories may petition the proper local government organ for the extension of the time limit to ten hours. For minors, the working period must, under no circumstances, exceed eight hours. Female workers are absolutely prohibited to work at night during the hours between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. while minor workers are not allowed to work at night from 7 p.m. to 6 a.m., nor to extend their daily working hours.

《字林西报》，1928年12月6日，星期四

中国拟议中的工厂法

一项共十六章的措施，涉及童工、利润分享、工作条件等

现有做法将被彻底改革

南京，12月3日电。农工商部已起草一部《工厂法》，并经该部法律委员会讨论，不久将提交政府委员会通过并施行。该法共十六章，分别为：总则、契约、解雇、工作时间、休息、生产标准、工资、利润分配、卫生与安全、工厂委员会、学徒制度、工人福利、特别规定、登记与报告、检查与处罚。
第一章规定，本法适用于中华民国领土内设立且经常雇用三十名以上工人的所有工厂。工厂在向当地主管政府机关向农工商部注册之前，不得招募工人或开始运营。

禁止雇用十四岁以下员工
第二章规定，所有工厂禁止雇用十四岁以下的童工，凡年满十四岁未满十六岁的男女均视为未成年工人，仅准许从事轻便简易的工作。工人可与工厂签订个人契约，工会亦可代表任何工人群体与工厂签订集体契约。两种契约均须以书面形式订立，并须经主管政府机关批准后方可生效。

何时可予解雇
第三章涉及工人的解雇问题。个人契约在规定的期限届满时终止，但经双方同意可以续订。对于未规定期限的个人契约，任何一方如欲解除契约，必须至少提前一个月通知对方。若工厂进行即时解雇，必须向被解雇工人支付相当于其一个月工资的额外款项。在社会保险法施行之前，还须另行支付相当于一个月工资的金额。
雇主可在下列情形之一终止雇用工人：
1. 工厂停工时。
2. 工厂任何部分经主管当局许可停止运作时。
3. 工厂因自然灾害或不可抗力被迫停工超过一个月时。
4. 工人不能胜任工作或工作性质不适合该工人时。
5. 工人在六个月内的平均工作成果低于规定效率的三分之二时。
6. 工人违反工厂规章时。
7. 工人无正当理由连续旷工超过三天，或一个月内缺勤超过六天时。
8. 工人在一年内请假超过两个月；或病假超过三个月；或事假与病假合计超过四个月时。

契约解除
在下列情形之一，工人可视为其与工厂的契约已解除：—
1. 工厂违反契约条款及《工厂法》时。
2. 工厂无故未能按时支付工资时。
3. 工厂主或其雇员殴打或虐待工人时。
4. 工厂忽视工人的卫生条件和安全时。

八小时工作制
第四章涉及工作时间。成年工人的正常每日工作时间为八小时，但由于各地情况和工作性质不同，工厂可向当地主管政府机关申请将时限延长至十小时。未成年工人的工作时间在任何情况下不得超过八小时。绝对禁止女工在晚上10点至早上6点之间从事夜间工作，未成年工人不得在晚上7点至早上6点之间从事夜间工作，也不得延长其每日工作时间。

page_data.en:
Chapter V provides for rest and recreation of the workers. All adult workers, consecutively for five hours and minor workers, for four hours, must rest at least for 30 minutes. All workers, however, must have a continuous rest of 18 hours every seven days and also stop work during holidays designated and promulgated by the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Labour.
Chapter VI provides three alternative means, to determine the standard of production in the factory.
Chapter VII provides that minimum wages of the workers must be based upon the living conditions and cost of various necessities of life of each particular locality where the factories happen to be. Monthly wages are payable twice a month. Under certain conditions the wages may be reduced or increased.

Distribution of Profits
Distribution of profits is dealt with in Chapter VIII in which it is provided that 10 per cent. of the net profit of the factory after due deductions for the reserve fund should be distributed among the management and directors; 45 per cent. among the shareholders; 45 per cent. among the workers.
Chapter IX provides that factories must appoint special officers to take charge of the sanitary affairs and provide safety devices for the protection of the workers. Adequate attention must be given to cleanliness, ventilation, light, drinking water etc.
Chapter X provides for the establishment of Work's Councils in factories employing not less than 30 regular workers. The Work's Councils shall be composed of an equal number of representatives from both the employers and employees. The employees' representatives shall be separately elected to represent different departments as may be contained in a factory, the basis of representation being graduated according to a rising scale.
The functions of the Works' Council will be to settle disputes among the workers themselves as well as those between the employers and the employees; to submit proposals for the improvement of factory conditions; and to initiate enterprises for the welfare of the workers.

Apprenticeship Rules
Problems concerning apprenticeship are treated in Chapter XI. According to the provisions, no factory will be allowed to engage apprentices without first concluding contracts with the parents or their guardians specifying their treatment and the nature of their work. The local authorities should also be supplied with a copy of the contract.

The period of apprenticeship will not last more than three years during which time the apprentices will be supplied with board and lodging according to the minimum living standard to be determined by the local authorities concerned, and will receive medical care in case of illness. Upon the expiration of one half of the period of apprenticeship, the apprentices will be paid one-fifth of the wage of an ordinary employee; and one-fourth of the wage will be paid upon the expiration of three-fourths of the period. All apprentices below the age of 16 will be subject to the regulations governing child labour.

Recreation and Welfare
Chapter XII on workers' welfare requires the factory to provide its youthful workers and apprentices with adequate educational facilities and to bear the expenses thereof. Recreation will also be provided for the workers by the factories. Factory-owners are also required to formulate their own regulations regarding compassionate grants, bonuses and pensions to their employees, which, however, must be submitted to the local authorities concerned for approval.
The special regulations contained in Chapter XIII provide for special preferential treatment of workers engaged in works of a dangerous or exceptionally exacting nature, for medical expenses and compensation for those injured or killed in the course of their employment; for leave of absence with full pay for women workers for two months on account of child-birth; and return of part or all of the workers' savings in case of marriages or death of their family members.
Chapter XIV provides that all factories shall keep full records of their employees as regard their age, date of employment, nature of work, wages, working hours, ability, conduct, the number of times they have been fined or rewarded, and sickness in the course of their employment.
Chapter XV deals with factory inspection and provides that the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Labour shall establish a factory inspectorate to investigate conditions in factories.
Chapter XVI deals with penalties and fines to be imposed upon any factory found guilty of violating the Labour Law. The fines range from $50 to $300. Any attempt by the factory to evade the terms of the Law regarding the distribution of profit shall be regarded as a criminal offense and shall be made punishable as fraud.—Kuo Min.

第五章规定工人的休息和娱乐。所有成年工人连续工作五小时、未成年工人连续工作四小时后，必须至少休息三十分钟。然而，所有工人每七天必须享有连续十八小时的休息，并在农工商部指定并颁布的节假日期间停止工作。
第六章规定了确定工厂生产标准的三种替代方法。
第七章规定，工人的最低工资必须依据工厂所在地的具体生活状况和各种生活必需品的成本来确定。月薪每月分两次支付。在某些情况下，工资可以减少或增加。

利润分配
第八章涉及利润分配，其中规定，工厂净利润在扣除公积金后，百分之十分配给管理层和董事；百分之四十五分配给股东；百分之四十五分配给工人。
第九章规定，工厂必须任命专门人员负责卫生事务，并提供保护工人的安全设备。必须充分注意清洁、通风、照明、饮用水等事宜。
第十章规定，在雇用不少于三十名固定工人的工厂中设立工厂委员会。工厂委员会由雇主和雇员代表人数相等组成。雇员代表应分别选举产生，以代表工厂内可能包含的不同部门，代表名额基础按递增比例分级确定。
工厂委员会的职能是解决工人内部以及雇主与雇员之间的纠纷；提出改善工厂条件的建议；并发起有利于工人福利的事业。

学徒规则
第十一章处理有关学徒的问题。根据规定，任何工厂在未与父母或监护人签订明确待遇和工作性质的契约之前，不得招收学徒。当地当局也应获得一份契约副本。

学徒期不超过三年，在此期间，学徒将按照有关地方当局确定的最低生活标准获得食宿，并在生病时获得医疗照顾。学徒期过半时，学徒将获得普通员工五分之一的工资；学徒期过四分之三时，将获得四分之一的工资。所有十六岁以下的学徒均受管理童工的法规约束。

娱乐与福利
关于工人福利的第十二章要求工厂为其青年工人和学徒提供充足的教育设施并承担相关费用。工厂还将为工人提供娱乐活动。工厂主还被要求制定关于向其雇员发放抚恤金、奖金和养老金的自有规章，但这些规章必须提交有关地方当局批准。
第十三章所载的特别规定包括：对从事危险或特别繁重工作的工人给予特别优待；对在就业过程中受伤或死亡者提供医疗费用和赔偿；女工因生育享受两个月全薪休假；以及在工人结婚或其家庭成员去世时退还部分或全部储蓄。
第十四条规定，所有工厂应保存其雇员的完整记录，内容包括年龄、受雇日期、工作性质、工资、工作时间、能力、行为、受罚或受奖次数以及受雇期间的患病情况。
第十五章涉及工厂检查，规定农工商部应设立工厂检查局，以调查工厂状况。
第十六章涉及对被判违反《劳动法》的任何工厂实施的处罚和罚款。罚款金额为五十元至三百元不等。工厂任何企图逃避有关利润分配法律条款的行为，均被视为刑事犯罪，并按欺诈罪予以惩处。——国民
