THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 5, 1928

Communism At Nanking

According to a Chinese news agency, the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Labor at Nanking has drafted a Factory Law for the approval of the State Council.
Unfortunately the Law is most ill-advised and communistic in character as to one or two of its features—notably in regard to a division of net profits according to a set scale.
The law states that 45 percent of net profits must go to employees. This would, in some cases, double their wages. It would quickly ruin some kinds of industries. It is quite inconceivable that the State Council would approve of the law as it stands. But why suggest such a communistic impossibility?

WE must take the first available moment to criticise certain provisions of the new Factory Law drafted by the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Labor and to be shortly submitted to the Government Council for adoption.
Everyone seems to be making laws in Nanking except the Legislative Yuan. The Legislative Council has made laws and other councils and ministries, but very little is reported from the body that should be framing laws, the Legislative Yuan, which by reason of its numbers is better suited to thresh out the advisability of a law than any ministry. It would seem obvious that laws needed by ministries should go through the channel of the Legislative Yuan to the Government Council for approval.
The Factory Law comes on the heels of the visit of M. Thomas, the Director of the International Bureau of Labor of the League of Nations, and was in many of its features doubtless inspired by his wise experience. But one may be sure that he would not suggest Chapter 8 of the Act, and doubtless knew nothing about it.

WANT TO DIVIDE THE PROFITS

Chapter 8 provides that 10 percent of the net profit of any factory in China, after due deductions for the reserve fund, should be distributed among the management and directors, 45 percent among the shareholders, and 45 percent among the workers.
This obviously means that the workers are to get, besides their wages, nearly half the net profits of any manufacturing plant. Meanwhile the shareholders get less than one-half, or the same as the workers, while the management and directors, no matter how able, can get but 10 percent or one-tenth the net profits.
It must be remembered that in many cases managing directors and directors get no salaries. Their compensation must come out of net profits unless a new form of organization is devised, the fundamental statutes of incorporation being revised to suit the case. If that were done, it might be possible for directors of Chinese companies to vote themselves salaries so far as any provision in this law is concerned.

LEGISLATION GONE MAD

Chapter 8 of the law means that a million dollar company making a net profit of 10 percent would, instead of giving this 10 percent to shareholders give them only 4½ percent. And in case the net profits were 5 percent then the shareholders would get but 2¼ percent. Business cannot be done that way in China or anywhere else.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1928年12月5日，星期三

南京的共产主义

据一家中国通讯社报道，南京工商部已起草了一部《工厂法》，待行政院批准。
不幸的是，该法就其某些特征而言——特别是关于按固定比例分配净利润的规定——极为失策，且带有共产主义色彩。
该法规定，净利润的45%必须归雇员所有。这在某些情况下会使他们的工资翻倍。这将迅速摧毁某些类型的工业。简直难以想象行政院会批准这样一部法律。但为什么要提出这种共产主义式的荒谬主张呢？

我们必须抓住第一个可用的时机，批评由工商部起草、即将提交政府委员会通过的《新工厂法》的某些条款。
在南京，似乎除了立法院之外，人人都在制定法律。立法委员会制定了法律，其他委员会和部委也在制定，但本应负责立法的机构——立法院——却鲜有报道。鉴于其人数众多，立法院比任何部委都更适合仔细审议法律的可行性。显然，各部所需的法律应通过立法院这一渠道，提交政府委员会批准。
《工厂法》紧随国际联盟国际劳工局局长托马斯先生（M. Thomas）的访问之后出台，其许多特征无疑受到了他明智经验的启发。但可以肯定的是，他不会建议该法第八章的内容，而且对此很可能一无所知。

意图分配利润

第八章规定，中国任何工厂在扣除适当的公积金后，其净利润的10%应分配给管理层和董事，45%分配给股东，45%分配给工人。
这显然意味着，工人除了工资外，还将获得任何制造工厂近一半的净利润。与此同时，股东获得的少于一半，或与工人相同，而无论管理层和董事多么能干，只能获得10%即十分之一的净利润。
必须记住，在许多情况下，常务董事和董事不领取薪水。除非设计一种新的组织形式，修订公司章程的基本条例以适应这种情况，否则他们的报酬必须来自净利润。如果这样做，就本法任何条款而言，中国公司的董事们有可能投票给自己发放薪水。

立法陷入疯狂

该法第八章意味着，一家净利润为10%的百万美元公司，不会将这10%全部给予股东，而只给他们4.5%。如果净利润为5%，那么股东将只得到2.25%。在中国或其他任何地方，生意都不能这样做。

page_data.en:
Let us take another illustration. Say that a factory
pays as much as 20 percent, which may occasionally hap-
pen. Say that such a factory has an investment of four
million dollars and 1,000 employees. In this case each
employee would get $800 a-year or $66.66 a month be-
sides his regular wages. And in some cases this would
be more than his regular wages. Next year the share-
holders might be out of pocket a large amount despite
any reserves that could be made. Business profits
fluctuate. Capital cannot run such risks. There must
be reservoirs of capital for future expansion and for
protracted periods of depression that have been known
to come.
But the best argument against this sort of com-
munistic law is that no one will go into business. In-
dustry will be killed, so far as China is concerned.
Now, in America many companies give a bonus
from the net profits to workers. There are innumer-
able schemes, all different. But not one of them was
directed by law. Every profit-sharing enterprise was
voluntary on the part of the management and share-
holders. Most of the projects give a few shares in the
company to workmen upon the conclusion of a period
of years of employment with the company. Other con-
cerns give a New Year's bonus, which is large or small
according to the net profits for the year. But not one
gives 45 percent of net profits to employees. That is
beyond all reason. We doubt if any firm could con-
tinue to do business if it gave to employees a bonus of
more than 10 or 15 percent of the net profits, for at
least three-quarters of such net profits would have to
go to shareholders or they would pick up and move to
some other country where legislation is not grown over-
night like mushrooms in a cellar. Furthermore, no such
profit-sharing should be attempted except for that por-
tion of the net profits above 10 percent. That is to say,
the first 10 percent of net profit should be inviolable and
should go only to shareholders.
The other chapters of the Factory law are more
reasonable. However, in view of past difficulty in en-
forcing child labor laws in China, it would have been
wiser to put the age limit at 12 instead of 14 years.

As M. Thomas has stated during his recent visit here,
certain countries have done just that. It would be a
good start, and then later, if found desirable, the age
limit for children could be made 14. Say put it at 12
for five years and see how it works.

（批：a p c l
Information
M.B.
O.M.G.
5/2/28）
page_data.zh:
让我们再举一个例子。假设一家工厂
支付高达20%的利润，这种情况偶尔会发
生。假设这样一家工厂的投资额为四
百万美元，拥有1,000名员工。在这种情况
下，每名员工每年将获得800美元，即每月66.66美元，
此外还有其常规工资。在某些情况下，这
甚至超过他的常规工资。明年，股东
可能会亏损一大笔钱，尽管可以提取任
何准备金。商业利润是波动的。资本无法
承担此类风险。必须有资本储备用于未
来的扩张，以及应对已知会发生的长期
萧条期。
但反对这类共产主义式法律的最有力
论据是，没有人会去经商。就中国而言，
工业将被扼杀。
现在，在美国，许多公司从净利润中
向工人发放奖金。有无数的方案，各不
相同。但没有一个是受法律强制的。每
个利润分享企业都是出于管理层和股东
的自愿。大多数项目是在工人为公司服
务满一定年限后，给予他们几股公司股
份。其他公司则发放新年奖金，金额根
据当年的净利润而定，可多可少。但没
有一家公司将净利润的45%给予员工。这
完全不合情理。我们怀疑，如果任何公
司给予员工的奖金超过净利润的10%或
15%，它能否继续经营，因为至少四分之
三的此类净利润必须归股东所有，否则
他们就会收拾行装，搬到另一个法律不
会像地窖里的蘑菇那样一夜之间疯长的
国家。此外，不应尝试对净利润中超过
10%的部分以外的部分进行此类利润分
享。也就是说，前10%的净利润应是不可
侵犯的，且应仅归股东所有。
《工厂法》的其他章节较为合理。然
而，鉴于过去在中国执行童工法的困难，
将年龄限制定为12岁而非14岁会更明智。

正如托马斯先生最近在此访问期间所
指出的，某些国家正是这样做的。这是一
个良好的开端，随后如果发现可取，可以
将儿童的年龄限制改为14岁。比方说，先
定为12岁试行五年，看看效果如何。

（批注：a p c l
信息
M.B.
O.M.G.
28年2月5日）

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 5, 1928

CHINA'S FACTORY
LAW

The provisions of the Factory Law which has been drafted by the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Labour will cause much hard thinking on the part of all employers, Chinese and foreign, large and small. At a time when a very important section of Chinese enterprise is looking forward to 'the industrialization of the country on a huge scale, it is not especially pleasant to be faced with legislation which constitutes State socialism in a tolerably advanced degree and, while seemingly ignoring the interests of employers, is very much of perfection where the employees are concerned. Looking at the summary of provisions which have been announced, the Factory Law is likely to have in the first place the effect of chasing capital away from its proper function as the hand-maiden of industry because of the small return it will offer to investors, and in a country where rates of interest are very much higher than those looked for in Europe and America, that spells disaster. In the second, the privileges secured for the working classes are of such a nature as to lead to chaos in industry. We have seen in Shanghai how much disruption has already been created by the Communist elements among the workers, and not only is there no word of curbing this, but certain of the provisions—notably that providing for the dismissal of a worker who takes more than two months' holiday in a year—are liable to foster it. It is, of course, one thing to draft such laws and another to enforce them, but there are districts where, possibly, they can be enforced and these are exactly the places where industrialism is most developed.

At the outset of the Law we find clauses prohibiting child labour which would be entirely admirable but for the fact that they take no cognizance of the present conditions in this respect. The first attempt to abolish child labour in mills and factories here came from the British mill-owners, and it will be remembered that as a result of their desire to do away with it a commission was appointed to go into the subject. Then it transpired that the Chinese themselves, the parents of these children, were those who most bitterly opposed it. They did so partially on their own economic grounds and partially on the very practical one of not knowing what to do with their children while they were at work, and as a result of the conditions which they revealed, nothing could be done to abolish it. If the Government wishes to introduce this measure successfully it should first make provision so that these factors will not constitute the insuperable opposition which has up to now been the case. We are afraid, however, that the Factory Law cannot be described as strong on the economic side, for when it comes to the introduction of an eight-hour day it ignores the discrepancy in working power which exists between the Chinese and his foreign competitor. It has for long been a matter for serious complaint that the Chinese worker, who, generally speaking, has been content to work long hours and do his work in his own particular fashion and at his own time, will not go out of his way to improve the standard of his work. As a consequence we find that Chinese mills have to employ very many times the number of hands required to perform the same work in Lancashire, and hence the only way in which mills in China can be made to compete and to pay is by long working shifts, generally over eleven hours. The reduction in working hours will mean more expensive goods, but we shall probably be told that protective tariffs will enable the local article to hold its own with the foreign. That means, however, greatly increased prices to the consumer.

In this Law there is too much government interference with the management of factories to please anybody but the pure Socialist, and it ignores the fact that trade almost invariably thrives best on a minimum of red tape. Mention has already been made of the conditions under which employees may be dismissed—for taking more than two months' holiday in a year for instance—and the results of this are so glaring that we need not further expatiate on them. The distribution of profits, however, must be considered in some detail. Ten per cent. of the net profit is to go to management and directors, forty-five per cent. to the shareholders, and forty-five to the workers. This means that if the net profits for a year are five per cent. the workers will receive as their share something less than a month's wages each. (This is worked out on the basis of the capital and pay-sheet of a local company). At the same time the dividend to shareholders would be reduced to roughly two and a half per cent. and it may well be imagined how quickly capital would flee from concerns where the promise of returns is so small. Our investors are not yet educated up to the point where they can contemplate this basis of profit-sharing with equanimity, and, generally speaking, their outlook limits them to sanctioning a bonus where hard work has resulted in greater prosperity. That means the presence of an incentive to increased effort, but it has unfortunately been noted that the Chinese worker does not respond to such by a sustained effort, and the general impression created by the new Law is that it puts him in such a favoured position that he will see no necessity for it. On the whole it is difficult to get away from the belief that the principal effects of the Law will be to nullify the enterprise of Chinese and other capitalists, and, instead of a period of progress, to bring stagnation in its wake.

（批：M/D.C.J. Information J.K.S. A.R. 5/12/28 5/12/28）

《字林西报》，1928年12月5日，星期三

中国的工厂
法

由工商部起草的《工厂法》条款将引起所有雇主，无论是中国人还是外国人，无论是大企业还是小企业，的深思。在中国企业的一个重要部门正期待“国家大规模工业化”之际，面对一部构成相当先进程度的国家社会主义、看似忽视雇主利益而在雇员方面力求完美的立法，并不令人愉快。纵观已公布的条款摘要，《工厂法》首先可能产生的影响是，由于它为投资者提供的回报微薄，将把资本从其作为工业仆役的正常职能中赶走，而在一个利率远高于欧美预期水平的国家，这意味着灾难。其次，为工人阶级争取的特权性质如此，以至于会导致工业混乱。我们在上海已经看到，工人中的共产主义分子造成了多大的破坏，不仅没有只言片语提及遏制这一点，而且某些条款——特别是规定解雇一年内休假超过两个月的工人的条款——反而可能助长这种破坏。当然，起草这样的法律是一回事，执行它们是另一回事，但在某些地区，它们或许能够被执行，而这些地方恰恰是工业最发达的地区。

在该法开头，我们发现禁止童工的条款本来是完全值得称赞的，但它们没有考虑到这方面的现状。这里首次尝试废除纱厂和工厂的童工来自英国纱厂主，人们还记得，由于他们希望消除童工，任命了一个委员会来调查此事。随后发现，中国人自己，即这些孩子的父母，是最强烈反对这一做法的人。他们这样做部分是出于自身的经济原因，部分是出于非常实际的原因，即不知道在他们工作时如何处理孩子，由于他们揭示的情况，无法采取任何措施废除童工。如果政府希望成功引入这一措施，它应首先做出规定，使这些因素不再构成迄今为止那样的不可克服的反对。然而，我们担心，《工厂法》在经济方面并不能被称为强劲，因为在引入八小时工作制时，它忽视了中国人与其外国竞争对手之间存在的劳动能力差异。长期以来，人们严重抱怨的是，中国工人一般来说满足于长时间工作，以自己的特定方式和时间完成工作，而不愿特意提高其工作标准。因此，我们发现中国纱厂必须雇佣比兰开夏郡完成同样工作所需人数多很多倍的工人，因此，中国纱厂能够竞争并盈利的唯一方式是实行长班次，通常超过十一个小时。减少工作时间将意味着商品更昂贵，但我们可能会被告知，保护性关税将使本地产品能与外国产品抗衡。然而，这意味着消费者价格大幅上涨。

在这部法律中，政府对工厂管理的干涉太多，除了纯粹的社会主义者外，不会让任何人满意，它忽视了贸易几乎总是在最少官僚主义的情况下繁荣得最好这一事实。前面已经提到了雇员可能被解雇的条件——例如因一年内休假超过两个月——其结果如此明显，我们无需进一步详述。然而，利润分配必须详细考虑。净利润的10%归管理层和董事，45%归股东，45%归工人。这意味着，如果一年的净利润为5%，工人每人分得的份额将少于一个月的工资。（这是根据当地一家公司的资本和工资单计算得出的）。同时，股东的股息将降至大约2.5%，不难想象，资本会从回报承诺如此微薄的企业迅速逃离。我们的投资者尚未受过教育，能够平静地接受这种利润分享基础，一般来说，他们的观点仅限于批准因努力工作带来更大繁荣而发放的奖金。这意味着存在增加努力的激励，但不幸的是，人们注意到中国工人并没有以持续的努力对此做出回应，新法给人的总体印象是，它将他置于如此有利的地位，以至于他认为没有必要这样做。总的来说，很难摆脱这样一种信念，即该法的主要影响将是使中国和其他资本家的企业精神无效，并且带来的不是进步时期，而是随之而来的停滞。

（批注：M/D.C.J. 信息 J.K.S. A.R. 28年12月5日 28年12月5日）

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 4, 1928

New Factory Law Drafted
And Will Be Submitted To
Government By Ministry

Applies To All Plants Employing More Than
Thirty Workers And Imposes Definite Ban
On Child Labor Under Fourteen

(Kuo Min News Agency)
Nanking, Dec. 3.—A Factory Law has been drafted by the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Labor and discussed by the Legal Commission of the Ministry and will shortly be submitted to the Government Council for adoption and enforcement. The Law consists of sixteen chapters, namely, General Provisions, Contracts, Dismissals, Working Hours, Rest, Standard of Production, Wages, Distribution of Profit, Sanitation and Safety, Works' Councils, apprenticeship, Workers' Welfare, Special Regulations, Registration and Reports, Inspection and Penalties.

Chapter I provides that the law is applicable to all factories, established within the territory of the Republic of China and regularly employing more than thirty workers. A factory must first register with the Ministry of Industry Commerce and Labor through the proper local government organ before it can proceed to enlist workers and start operation.

ON CHILD LABOR
Chapter II provides that child labor under the age of fourteen should be prohibited in all factories and all boys and girls above fourteen and below sixteen are considered as minor workers who will be permitted to be engaged in light and easy work only. A worker may enter into an individual contract with the factory, while the Labor Unions may conclude collective contracts with the factories on behalf of any group of workers. Contracts of both kinds must be in writing and must first be approved by the proper government organs before they can become valid.

Chapter III deals with dismissals of workers. Individual contracts will be cancelled upon expiration of their stipulated time, but may be renewed by mutual agreement. As regards those individual contracts
(Continued on Page 4, Col. 1.)

for which no stipulation of time is made, if either party desires the cancellation of the same, a notice must be given to the other party at least one month in advance. For summary dismissals by the factories, a minimum extra sum of money amounting to one month's wages of the workers must be given to the dismissed workers. Before social insurance laws are put into force an additional sum equal to one month must be given.

GIVES CONDITIONS
Employers may terminate their employment of the workers under any one of the following conditions:
1. When a factory suspends operation.
2. When any part of a factory ceases functioning with permission from the proper authorities.
3. When a factory, either through natural disasters or by force of unforeseen circumstances, is obliged to suspend operation for over a period of one month.
4. When a worker is incapable of doing his work properly or when the nature of the work is unsuitable to the worker.
5. When the average result of a worker for a period of six months is below two-thirds of the required efficiency.
6. When a worker violates the rules of the factory.
7. When a worker fails to report for work without reason for over three consecutive days or when a worker absents himself more than six days within one month.
8. When within one year a worker takes leave of absence for more than two months; or sick leave of more than three months, or when a worker takes a combined ordinary and sick leave of absence for more than four months.

FOR THE WORKERS
Workers may consider their contracts with the factories cancelled under any one of the following conditions:
1. When factories violate the terms of the contracts and the Factory Law.
2. When factories fail to pay the wages at proper time without any reason.
3. When factory owners or their employees assault or maltreat workers.
4. When factories neglect the sanitary conditions and safety of the workers.

Chapter IV deals with Working Hours. The regular daily working period for adults is 8 hours, but, owing to varying local conditions and the nature of the work, factories may petition the proper local government organ for the extension of the time limit to ten hours. For minors, the working period must, under no circumstances, exceed eight hours. Female workers are absolutely prohibited to work at night during the hours between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. while minor workers are not allowed to work at night from 7 p.m. to 6 a.m., nor to extend their daily working hours.

Chapter V provides for rest and recreation of the workers. All adult workers, working consecutively for five hours and minor workers, for four hours, must rest at least for thirty minutes. All workers, however, must have a continuous rest of eighteen hours every seven days and also stop work during holidays designated and promulgated by the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Labor.

Chapter VI provides three alternative means to determine the standard of production in the factory.

Chapter VII provides that minimum wages of the workers must be based upon the living conditions and cost of various necessities of life of each particular locality where the factories happen to be. Monthly wages are payable twice a month. Under certain conditions the wages may be reduced or increased.

Distribution of profits is dealt with in Chapter VIII in which it is provided that 10 per cent of the net profit of the factory after due deductions for the reserve fund should be distributed among the management and directors; 45 per cent among the shareholders; 45 per cent among the workers.

Chapter IX provides that factories must appoint special officers to take charge of the sanitary affairs, and provide safety devices for the protection of the workers. Adequate attention must be given to cleanliness, ventilation, light, drinking water etc.

Chapter X provides for the establishment of Works' Councils in factories employing not less than thirty regular workers. The Works' Councils shall be composed of an equal number of representatives from both the employers and employees. The employees representatives shall be separately elected to represent different departments as may be contained in a factory, the basis of representation being graduated according to a rising scale.

The functions of the Works' Council will be to settle disputes among the workers themselves as well as those between the employers and the employees; to submit proposals for the improvement of factory conditions; and to initiate enterprises for the welfare of the workers.

新工厂法草案拟定
将由部呈交政府

适用于所有雇用三十名以上工人的工厂
并明确禁止雇用十四岁以下童工

（国民通讯社）
南京，12月3日电——农工商部已起草一部《工厂法》，并经该部法律委员会讨论，不久将提交国民政府委员会通过并施行。该法共十六章，分别为：总则、契约、解雇、工作时间、休息、生产标准、工资、利润分配、卫生与安全、工厂委员会、学徒制度、工人福利、特别规定、登记与报告、视察及罚则。

第一章规定，本法适用于在中华民国领土内设立且经常雇用三十名以上工人的所有工厂。工厂在向当地主管政府机关向农工商部办理注册之前，不得招募工人或开工营业。

关于童工
第二章规定，所有工厂禁止雇用十四岁以下的童工；凡年满十四岁未满十六岁的男女工均视为未成年工，仅准许从事轻便简易的工作。工人可与工厂签订个人契约，工会亦可代表任何工人群体与工厂签订集体契约。两类契约均须以书面订立，并须经主管政府机关批准后方可生效。

第三章涉及工人解雇事宜。个人契约在约定期限届满时终止，但经双方同意可予续订。至于未定期限的个人契约
（续第4版第1栏）

若任何一方希望解除契约，须至少提前一个月通知对方。若由工厂即时解雇，须向被解雇工人支付相当于其一个月工资的额外款项。在社会保险法施行之前，还须增发相当于一个月工资的额外款项。

列明条件
雇主可在下列任一情况下终止雇佣关系：
1. 工厂停工时。
2. 工厂部分部门经主管当局许可停止运作时。
3. 工厂因自然灾害或不可抗力被迫停工超过一个月时。
4. 工人不能胜任工作或工作性质不适合该工人时。
5. 工人在六个月内的平均工作成果低于规定效率的三分之二时。
6. 工人违反工厂规章时。
7. 工人无故连续旷工超过三天，或一个月内旷工超过六天时。
8. 工人在一年内请假超过两个月，或病假超过三个月，或事假与病假合计超过四个月时。

保障工人权益
工人在下列任一情况下可视为与工厂的契约已解除：
1. 工厂违反契约条款及《工厂法》时。
2. 工厂无正当理由未按时支付工资时。
3. 厂主或其雇员殴打或虐待工人时。
4. 工厂忽视工人的卫生条件及安全时。

第四章涉及工作时间。成年工人的正常每日工作时间为八小时，但因各地情况不同及工作性质各异，工厂可向当地主管政府机关申请将时限延长至十小时。未成年工的工作时间在任何情况下不得超过八小时。绝对禁止女工在夜间十时至次日晨六时之间工作；未成年工不得在夜间七时至次日晨六时之间工作，亦不得延长其每日工作时间。

第五章规定工人的休息与娱乐。所有成年工人连续工作五小时、未成年工连续工作四小时后，必须至少休息三十分钟。然而，所有工人每七天必须享有连续十八小时的休息，并在农工商部指定并颁布的节假日期间停止工作。

第六章规定了确定工厂生产标准的三种备选方法。

第七章规定，工人的最低工资必须依据各工厂所在地的生活状况及各种生活必需品的费用而定。月薪每月分两次发放。在某些情况下，工资可减少或增加。

第八章涉及利润分配，规定工厂净利润在扣除公积金后，百分之十分配给管理层及董事；百分之四十五分配给股东；百分之四十五分配给工人。

第九章规定，工厂必须任命专职人员负责卫生事务，并提供保护工人的安全设备。必须充分注意清洁、通风、照明、饮用水等事宜。

第十章规定，雇用不少于三十名固定工人的工厂须设立工厂委员会。工厂委员会由资方和劳方代表同等人数组成。劳方代表应分别选举产生，以代表工厂内不同的部门，代表名额按递增比例分级确定。

工厂委员会的职能是解决工人内部以及资方与劳方之间的纠纷；提出改善工厂条件的建议；并发起有利于工人福利的事业。

第十一章涉及学徒制度相关问题。根据规定，任何工厂在未与父母或监护人签订明确规定学徒待遇及工作性质的契约之前，不得招收学徒。当地当局也应获发一份契约副本。学徒期不得超过三年，在此期间，学徒的食宿应按有关地方当局确定的最低生活标准供给，并在患病时获得医疗照顾。学徒期满一半时，将支付相当于普通员工五分之一的工资；期满四分之三时，将支付四分之一的工资。所有十六岁以下的学徒均受童工法规的约束。
第十二章关于工人福利，要求工厂为其青年工人和学徒提供充足的教育设施并承担相关费用。工厂还应为工人提供娱乐设施。厂主还被要求制定关于向其雇员发放抚恤金、奖金和养老金的自有规章，但这些规章必须提交有关地方当局批准。
第十三章所载的特别规定，对从事危险或特别繁重工作的工人给予特别优待；规定对在就业过程中受伤或死亡的工人提供医疗费用及赔偿；规定女工因生育享有两个月全薪产假；并规定在工人结婚或其家庭成员死亡时，退还部分或全部工人储蓄。
第十四章规定，所有工厂应就员工的年龄、受雇日期、工作性质、工资、工作时间、能力、品行、受罚或受奖次数以及受雇期间的患病情况保存完整记录。
第十五章涉及工厂视察，规定农工商部应设立工厂视察局，以调查工厂状况。
第十六章涉及对违反《劳动法》的任何工厂所施加的处罚和罚款。罚款金额从50美元至300美元不等。工厂任何企图规避有关利润分配的法律条款的行为，均被视为刑事犯罪，并按欺诈罪论处。

MOSCOW DICTATES.
China to be the Slave of Bolshevism.
Threatened Ruination of China's Industries.
Factory Laws (Draft.)

1. General.
1. The following laws are made to govern the factory or mine (hereinafter termed the "factory") wherein over 30 labourers are employed. Factory which cannot be placed under these laws will follow the orders issued by the Ministry of Industrial and Commerce.
2. Same laws are to apply to foreign factory within the Empire of the Republic of China, whenever the nature of such factory agrees with article 1.
3. No factory is permitted to enlist labourers or commence operation without the official approval or proper registration with the Ministry of Industry and Commerce on the recommendation of the local directing authorities. Previous to the announcement and coming into force of these laws, any factory which has properly been registered will, within three months from date of announcement of these laws, approach the local directing authorities requesting the change of the registration certificate from the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.
4. Local directing authorities, unless specially specified, are the Municipal authorities in special areas, District Government authorities in districts, and City Government authorities in ordinary cities.

5. The by-laws for the registration of factory are being drafted separately.
6. The factory owner may appoint a suitable person to manage the affairs of the factory, but before the official registration of the factory, the owner of the factory is liable for the responsibilities of the management.
The manager is to be responsible for the carrying out of these laws on behalf of the owner.

2. Contracts.
7. Labourers of either sex are not permitted to be engaged at the age under 12.
8. Easy and light jobs only will be assigned to labourers between the ages of 12 to 16. These are called child labourers.
9. Application should be made for a free certificate ascertaining the age of the labourers if any doubt exists. Prior to the establishment of the Bureau of Census, the local directing authorities will examine the labourers between ages of 12 and 16 on their height and weight, and issue free certificates for ages if such is required. The height and weight of the young labourers will be examined by the local directing authorities three months after the announcement of these laws.
10. Individual labourers may sign a contract with the factory.

11. Labour Union will represent the labourers to negotiate contracts for bodies of labourers and the factory. The above documents are to be made in writing, and will take effect on the approval of the local directing authorities.
12. Any contracts which are made against the law will be substituted in line corresponding with these laws.

3. Termination of Services.
13. On the expiry of individual contracts of fixed periods, renewal will be made with the mutual consent of both parties.
14. Individual contracts of unfixed period will expire on giving 15 days' notice to the other party, unless such is definitely laid down under the conditions.
15. Failing to comply with article 14, the owner of the factory will pay half a month's wages, and on the other hand the labourer will lose the privilege as under article 20.
16. The factory may terminate or discharge labourers on the following conditions:—1. Close down the whole or part of the factory. 2. Any unexpected accidents by nature or fire which cannot be resisted by human beings, and such accidents may cause temporary suspension of the running of the factory for a period exceeding one month. 3. Lack of working ability and qualifications unsuitable. 4. Over three days' leave without reason. 5. Undergoing over one month's imprisonment on any criminal charge. 6. Losing the moving ability for time being (this refers to men over two months' sick leave, or females after confinement unable to resume work after two months).

工厂法（草案。）

14. 不定期限的个人合同，除非条件中有明确规定，否则在向对方发出15天通知后即告期满。
15. 若未遵守第14条，工厂主须支付半个月工资，而另一方面，工人将丧失第20条规定的特权。
16. 工厂可在下列条件下解雇或开除工人：—1. 关闭全部或部分工厂。2. 发生人力无法抗拒的自然灾害或火灾等意外事故，且此类事故可能导致工厂暂时停工超过一个月。3. 工作能力不足及资格不符。4. 无故缺勤超过三天。5. 因任何刑事指控被监禁超过一个月。6. 暂时丧失行动能力（此指男性病假超过两个月，或女性产后两个月仍无法复工）。

page_data.en:
17. The labourers may with-
draw the contract on the
following condition:—1.
The owner of the factory
violates the conditions of
the contract or labour
laws. 2. Wages are not
paid at regular times. 3.
Ill-treatment of labourers.
4. Ill-health and lack of
safety.
18. Reference Para. 1, 2, 3,
under article 16. 15 days'
notice to be given to the
labourers by the factory or
half month's pay in lieu
of notice.
19. Reference Para. 3, 4, of
article 16 and article 17.
Any disputes will be
settled by the factory com-
mittee.
20. Certificates bearing the
following items will be
issued to labourers on the
termination of service or
on the closing of the
factory:—1. Name, age,
native of, and address of
labourer. 2. Nature and
kind of work. 3. Length
of service and detail of
work. 4. Ability and
character. 5. Awards and
punishments.
4. Hours of Work.
21. Eight hours for full grown
persons, which may be
prolonged to nine hours
under special circum-
stances to suit the custom,
season and nature of the
factory on the approval of
the local directing authori-
ties.
22. The hours of work for
child labourers should not
exceed eight hours.
23. In special cases, when the
hours of work may be pro-
longed. In such cases
permission should first be
obtained from the local
directing authorities.
24. The prolonged hours, as
for male grown labourers,
are not to exceed three
hours per day, and 45
hours per month. For
female grown-up labourers
not to exceed two hours
per day and twenty hours
per month.
25. Child labourers are not
permitted to prolong their
hours of work.
26. For male grown-up
labourers no continual
work is permitted for
more than five hours.
Female and child labour-
ers are not to continue
their work for a duration
of more than three hours.
27. No female labourers are
permitted to work be-
tween the hours of 9 p.m.
to 6 a.m. the next morn-
ing.
28. No child labourers are
permitted to work between
the hours of 7 p.m. to 6
a.m., the next morning.
29. A factory which works
continually day and night
may obtain permission
from the local directing
authorities first. And
labourers should "change
hands" at least once a
week.
Leave.
30. Over thirty minutes' rest to
be given to male grown-
up labourers who have
performed five hours'
work and female and child
labourers after three
hours' work.
31. All labourers should have
10 hours' continuous rest
once a week.
32. Leave to be granted on
holidays, as affixed by the
Ministry of Industrial
and Commerce.
33. Any labourer who has
completed six months'
continuous service is per-
mitted to get one week's
special leave, and two
weeks' leave for anyone
who has completed one
year's service. Leave will
be granted on discretion,
providing that the factory
is able to release the man
34. No reductions of pay to be
made on regular leave.
Wages.
35. Wages are paid in con-
sideration of the cost of
living and the location of
the factory, and not by
the amount of money.
36. Factory will fix the wages
as above stated, and must
be approved by the local
directing authorities.
These authorities also have
the power to fix the scale
of wages.
37. Additional wages are to be
paid in the proportions of
1/4 or 1/2 of their regular
hour pay.
38. Wages are to be paid in
local currency. It is pro-
hibited to pay anything
which will represent cash
money.
39. Wages are to be paid
twice a month, on the 1st
and 15th, respectively.
40. No deductions of wages
are to be made in advance
as security for damages or
compensation, etc.
41. For the benefit of labour-
ers, savings, insurance
and social matters might
be introduced with the con-
sent of the labourers. In
such cases, portions of
their pay be deducted on
a pre-arranged scheme
and same be approved by
the local directing au-
thorities.
7. Distribution of Profits.
42. 8 per cent. interest will
be issued to paid-up
capital from the profit
after expenses have been
paid.
43. 20 per cent. of the net
profit will go into the Re-
serve Fund, which will be
under the charge of the
factory, and not to be
touched by either parties
unless for improvement
purposes. Net profit re-
fers to balance of profit
after paying off the 8 per
cent. interest, taxes, etc.
44. Any balance left after the
deduction of the Reserve
Fund will be distributed
at the rate of 40 per cent.
to the labourers, 40 per
cent. to the capitalists,
and 20 per cent. to the
managing staff. Labour-
ers refers to persons who
have served the factory
over six months, and the
managing staff refers to
employees attached to the
administrative supervision
and controlling depart-
ments.
45. 40 per cent. profit for the
capitalists will be propor-
tionally distributed in ac-
cordance with the capital
paid.
46. From 40 per cent. profit
for the labourers, 30 per
cent. to be distributed to
the labourers in propor-
tion to their wages, and
10 per cent. will be re-
served and kept by
the labour committee
nominated by the factory
committee for the purpose
of benefitting the labour-
ers. The above distribu-
tion should not include
the amount of wages for
the number of days dur-
ing sick leave of labour-
ers.
47. Expenditure on compen-
sations, rewards, and
gratuities, and a certain
amount of premium for
insurance is classified
under the ordinary ex-
penditure of the factory.
Health and Safety.
48. A special staff to be detail-
ed by the factory to deal
with the matters of
health and safety.
page_data.zh:
17. 工人可在下列条件下解除合同：—1. 厂主违反合同条件或劳动法。2. 工资未按时支付。3. 虐待工人。4. 健康状况不佳且缺乏安全保障。
18. 参见第16条第1、2、3款。工厂须向工人发出15天通知，或支付半个月工资以代替通知。
19. 参见第16条第3、4款及第17条。任何争议将由工厂委员会解决。
20. 在雇佣终止或工厂关闭时，应向工人签发载有以下项目的证明书：—1. 工人的姓名、年龄、籍贯及住址。2. 工作性质和种类。3. 服务年限及工作详情。4. 能力与品行。5. 奖惩记录。
4. 工作时间。
21. 成年人为八小时，在特殊情况下，经地方主管当局批准，可根据习惯、季节及工厂性质延长至九小时。
22. 童工的工作时间不得超过八小时。
23. 在特殊情况下，工作时间可以延长。在此类情况下，应首先获得地方主管当局的许可。
24. 延长的工时，对于成年男工，每天不得超过三小时，每月不得超过四十五小时。对于成年女工，每天不得超过两小时，每月不得超过二十小时。
25. 不允许童工延长工作时间。
26. 成年男工不得连续工作超过五小时。女工和童工连续工作时间不得超过三小时。
27. 不允许女工在晚上9点至次日早上6点之间工作。
28. 不允许童工在晚上7点至次日早上6点之间工作。
29. 日夜连续作业的工厂，可首先向地方主管当局申请许可。工人应至少每周“换班”一次。
休假。
30. 成年男工工作满五小时，女工和童工工作满三小时后，应给予三十分钟以上的休息时间。
31. 所有工人每周应享有十小时的连续休息。
32. 按照工商部规定的假日给予休假。
33. 任何连续服务满六个月的工人，准许享受一周特别休假；服务满一年者，准许享受两周休假。视情况准予休假，前提是工厂能够放行该人员。
34. 常规休假期间不得减薪。
工资。
35. 工资的确定应考虑生活成本和工厂所在地，而非仅依据金额数量。
36. 工厂应按上述规定确定工资，并须经地方主管当局批准。这些当局也有权制定工资标准。
37. 加班工资应按其正常小时工资的1/4或1/2的比例支付。
38. 工资应以当地货币支付。禁止支付任何代表现金的实物或其他凭证。
39. 工资每月支付两次，分别在1日和15日。
40. 不得预先扣除工资作为损害或赔偿等的保证金。
41. 为工人利益起见，经工人同意，可引入储蓄、保险和社会事务。在此类情况下，可按预定方案从工资中扣除部分款项，并经地方主管当局批准。
7. 利润分配。
42. 支付费用后，从利润中向实缴资本发放8%的利息。
43. 净利润的20%将存入储备基金，由工厂掌管，除非用于改进目的，否则任何一方不得动用。净利润是指支付8%利息、税款等后的利润余额。
44. 扣除储备基金后的任何余额，将按以下比例分配：工人40%，资本家40%，管理人员20%。工人指在工厂服务超过六个月的人员，管理人员指隶属于行政监督和管理部门的雇员。
45. 资本家的40%利润将根据实缴资本按比例分配。
46. 在工人的40%利润中，30%按工资比例分配给工人，10%由工厂委员会提名的劳工委员会保留并保管，用于造福工人。上述分配不应包括工人在病假期间的工资数额。
47. 赔偿金、奖励金和酬劳金的支出，以及一定金额的保险费，归类为工厂的日常支出。
健康与安全。
48. 工厂应指派专门人员负责处理健康和安全事宜。

page_data.en:
49. The following are necessary from the health point of view :—
(a) Cleanliness on the premises.
(b) Free current of air.
(c) Good light.
(d) Good drinking water.
(e) Lavatory.
(f) Anti-poison and dust.
50. Matters of safety :—
(a) Building construction
(b) Individual safety
(c) The installation of machines
(d) Fire prevention.
51. Education is also to be under the heading of safety :—
(a) Lectures
(b) Film shows
(c) Printed matter, such as pictures or pamphlets.
52 If the health and safety matters of the factory are considered unsatisfactory by the local directing authorities, the owner is
compelled to improve matters or even close down the whole or portion of the factory.
53 Labourers may appoint representative, to take part in discussion of matters with reference to health and safety.
(To be continued)

49. 从健康角度来看，以下是必要的：—
(a) 场所清洁。
(b) 空气流通。
(c) 光线充足。
(d) 饮用水良好。
(e) 盥洗室。
(f) 防毒和防尘。
50. 安全事宜：—
(a) 建筑结构
(b) 个人安全
(c) 机器安装
(d) 防火。
51. 教育也归入安全范畴：—
(a) 讲座
(b) 电影放映
(c) 印刷品，如图画或小册子。
52. 如果地方主管当局认为工厂的健康和安全事宜令人不满，厂主将被迫改善状况，甚至关闭全部或部分工厂。
53. 工人可任命代表，参与讨论有关健康和安全的事宜。
（待续）

SHANGHAI MERCURY, MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 17, 1928.

MOSCOW DICTATES.

China to be the Slave of
Bolshevism.

Threatened Ruination of China's Industries

Factory Laws (Draft.)

(CONCLUDED.)

55. Factory Committee.
54. The factory committee may be elected by labourers and factory where 30 labourers are permanently engaged.
56. Members of the committee appointed by the factory should possess the qualification of a good knowledge of the affairs in the factory and position of the labourers. Members appointed by the labourers should be selected among labourers of the same factory.
56. Committee for labourers are voted in accordance with the number of hands in the works, the number of committee thus admitted will be in proportion as follows:
1 committee for 15 labourers.
2 committee for 15 to 30 labourers.
3 committee for 30 to 50 labourers.
5 committee for 50 to 100 labourers.
7 committee for 100 to 200 labourers.
9 committee for 200 to 500 labourers.
11 committee for 500 to 1,000 labourers.
Two additional members will be admitted from per 1,000 for 1,000 to 5,000 labourers. One additional member will be admitted from per 1,000 for over 5,000 labourers. Any factory wherein the number of labourers is below 15 may combine to vote with other houses in the same factory.
57. The duties of the factory committee are: 1. To settle disputes among the labourers. 2. To settle any disputes between labourers of the factory or in the factory. 3. Suggestions regarding improvements of houses. 4. The best means to benefit the labourers.

58. The factory committee consists of one chairman, one secretary, and one steward all of whom are voted for by the committee in writing. Other officers may be elected by vote, when necessary.
59. General meetings are to be called for by the chairman, and to be held once a month. Special meetings for matters of urgency and importance may be called for at any time at the request of two members of the committee.
60. Whenever any member of the labour committee violates the regulations of the factory, the matter should be dealt with by the committee, and in such cases the accused member should leave the meeting during the course of discussion.

Apprentices.
61. No apprentice should be engaged without first submitting the following details to the local directing authorities for approval. Number of apprentices required, nature of work, hours of work, treatment of, period of training.
62. When an apprentice is engaged, a contract is to be made in triplicate with the guardians, copies of which will be kept at the factory, by the guardian, and the local directing authorities. The age of the apprentice, and details as mentioned in paragraphs 2 and 5 under article 61, should at least be included in the contract.
63. Number of apprentices in the factory should not exceed the number of labourers.
64. The age of the apprentice is as laid down under Article 7.
page_data.zh:
《上海水星报》，1928年9月17日，星期一。

莫斯科发号施令。

中国将成为布尔什维主义的奴隶。

中国工业面临毁灭威胁

工厂法（草案。）

（完。）

55. 工厂委员会。
54. 凡长期雇佣30名工人的工厂，可由工人和工厂选举产生工厂委员会。
56. 由工厂任命的委员会成员应具备熟悉工厂事务和工人状况的资格。由工人任命的成员应从同一工厂的工人中选拔。
56. 劳工委员会成员根据工厂人数投票产生，由此获准的委员会人数比例如下：
15名工人设1个委员会席位。
15至30名工人设2个委员会席位。
30至50名工人设3个委员会席位。
50至100名工人设5个委员会席位。
100至200名工人设7个委员会席位。
200至500名工人设9个委员会席位。
500至1,000名工人设11个委员会席位。
1,000至5,000名工人，每1,000人增补2名成员。超过5,000名工人，每1,000人增补1名成员。任何工人人数少于15人的工厂，可与同一工厂的其他部门合并投票。
57. 工厂委员会的职责是：1. 解决工人之间的纠纷。2. 解决工厂内或涉及工厂工人的任何纠纷。3. 关于改善住房的建议。4. 造福工人的最佳途径。

58. 工厂委员会由一名主席、一名秘书和一名干事组成，均由委员会书面投票选出。必要时，可通过投票选举其他职员。
59. 全体会议由主席召集，每月举行一次。遇紧急和重要事项，经两名委员会成员请求，可随时召开特别会议。
60. 每当劳工委员会任何成员违反工厂规章时，此事应由委员会处理，在此类情况下，被指控的成员在讨论过程中应退出会议。

学徒。
61. 在未先将以下细节提交地方主管当局批准之前，不得雇佣任何学徒。所需学徒人数、工作性质、工作时间、待遇、培训期限。
62. 雇佣学徒时，应与监护人签订一式三份的合同，副本分别由工厂、监护人和地方主管当局保存。合同中至少应包括学徒的年龄，以及第61条第2和第5款中提到的细节。
63. 工厂内的学徒人数不得超过工人人数。
64. 学徒的年龄如第7条所规定。

page_data.en:
65. The hours of training and working of the apprentices are as fixed for the child labourers, unless the age reaches 16. Work of a dangerous nature will comply with the rules as laid down for the child labourers.
66. The period of training for an apprentice should not exceed four years.
67. During the course of training of the apprentice, cost of food, board, and medical expenses are to be borne by the factory, the minimum amount of which will be decided by the local directing authorities.
68. On the completion of half the period of training, apprentices are to receive 1/3 pay of the labourers per month, and on the completion of 3/4 period will receive 1/3 pay.
69. In accordance with para 1, 3, 4, 5 of article 16, the dismissal of an apprentice could be effected on one of the following conditions: Apprentice refuses to take up regular training, apprentice steals and fails to reform after being warned.
70. In accordance with para. 1, 3, of article 17, the guardian of the apprentice may cancel the contract on one of the following condition: The apprentice is to work on his own initiative or work outside the factory, the apprentice is not trained in the art as agreed upon in the contract.
71. Apprentice is not permitted to leave the factory prior to the completion of the training period, unless in exceptional cases, otherwise all expenses incurred during his stay in the factory should be refunded by the guardian of the apprentice.

Concessions for Labourers.
72. Factory should be responsible for any expenses incurred on the education of child labourers and apprentices of the factory. Child labourers should receive education at least ten hours per week, and apprentices six hours per week. Other uneducated labourers should receive educational support from the factory as cases happen.
73. If possible, recreation should be encouraged among the labourers.
74. Labourers may appoint representatives to take part in dealing with matters of savings, insurance and social matters as laid down in article 41.
75. Rules are to be drafted by the factory regarding compensation rewards, gratuities in accordance with the position of the factory and with the approval of the local directing authorities.

Special Matters.
76. Special rules should be drafted with regard to the working hours of dangerous and difficult jobs and be approved by the local directing authorities.
77. Labourers, when injured on duty, medical expenses are to be paid by the factory. Within three months of treatment, he should receive certain amount of pay if considered fit and to remain on the roll without discharge.
78. Six weeks' leave will be granted to female labourers during confinement without reduction of pay.
79. Child and female labourers are not permitted to clean, oil, inspect, repair, belt or do any dangerous work during the operation of machinery.
80. Child and female labourers are not permitted to work on poisonous and explosive materials.
81. Child and female labourers are not permitted to work in unhealthy, and dangerous places, and also places where dust and powder are flying about.
82. Advance of pay or the withdrawal of the whole or portion of the savings may be made at the request of the labourer who is in need of money, or in case of marriage or death.

Records and Reports.
83. Books should be kept in the factory for record purposes for labourers as follows: Name, age, native of, address, date of joining, hours and kind of work, qualification and character, awards and punishment, medical records.
84. Factory should report the following matters to the local directing authorities every three months: Labourers' roll, sickness of labourers and methods of curing, accidents and how same being disposed of, causes of the dismissal of labourers, if any.
85. Death or serious injury caused by accidents are to be reported to the local directing authorities in full detail.
86. Factory should give full information to the inspectors from the local directing authorities when any inquiries are made.

Factory Inspection.
87. Inspection bureaux will be established by the Ministry of Industry and Commerce to inspect factories from time to time.
88. Inspection warrant certificates are to be carried by the inspector when inspecting a factory.
89. Inspectors may visit any factory at any time without resistance.
page_data.zh:
65. 学徒的训练和工作时间，除非年龄达到16岁，否则与童工的规定相同。危险性质的工作应遵守为童工制定的规则。
66. 学徒的训练期不应超过四年。
67. 在学徒训练期间，伙食、住宿和医疗费用由工厂承担，最低金额由地方主管当局决定。
68. 在完成一半训练期时，学徒每月应领取工人工资的三分之一；在完成四分之三训练期时，应领取[原文如此，疑为三分之二或保持三分之一]工资。
69. 根据第16条第1、3、4、5款，学徒可在以下条件下被解雇：学徒拒绝接受正规训练，或学徒偷窃且经警告后仍不悔改。
70. 根据第17条第1、3款，学徒监护人可在以下条件下取消合同：学徒擅自工作或到厂外工作，或未按合同约定对学徒进行技艺培训。
71. 除非特殊情况，否则不允许学徒在训练期结束前离开工厂，否则其在厂期间产生的所有费用应由学徒监护人退还。

劳工优待。
72. 工厂应负责本厂童工和学徒的教育费用。童工每周应至少接受十小时教育，学徒每周六小时。其他未受教育的劳工，工厂应视情况提供教育支持。
73. 如有可能，应鼓励劳工进行娱乐活动。
74. 劳工可推选代表参与处理第41条规定的储蓄、保险和社会事务。
75. 工厂应根据自身状况并经由地方主管当局批准，起草关于补偿、奖励和赏金的规则。

特别事项。
76. 应就危险和艰苦工作的工时起草特别规则，并报地方主管当局批准。
77. 劳工因公受伤，医疗费用由工厂支付。在治疗三个月内，如被认为适宜工作，应发给一定数额的工资，并保留其名册身份，不予除名。
78. 女工在分娩期间享有六周假期，工资照发。
79. 机器运转期间，禁止童工和女工从事清洁、加油、检查、修理、安装皮带或任何其他危险工作。
80. 禁止童工和女工从事有毒和爆炸性材料的工作。
81. 禁止童工和女工在不健康、危险的场所，以及粉尘飞扬的场所工作。
82. 劳工因急需资金，或因婚丧事宜，可申请预支工资或提取全部或部分储蓄。

记录与报告。
83. 工厂应保存劳工记录簿，内容包括：姓名、年龄、籍贯、地址、入职日期、工作时间和种类、资格与品行、奖惩记录、医疗记录。
84. 工厂应每三个月向地方主管当局报告以下事项：劳工名册、劳工患病情况及治疗方法、事故及其处理情况、解雇劳工的原因（如有）。
85. 因事故导致的死亡或重伤，应向地方主管当局详细报告。
86. 当地方主管当局视察员进行查询时，工厂应提供完整信息。

工厂视察。
87. 工商部将设立视察局，不定期视察工厂。
88. 视察员视察工厂时，须携带视察委任证。
89. 视察员可随时进入任何工厂，不得受阻。

page_data.en:
90. Inspectors will see that improvements of health and safety of the factory be made at such specified times as directed by the inspection bureau.
91. When the inspector has any suspicion on the ages of the labourers, he may ask the medical officer of the inspection bureau to confirm same, and if the decision is not agreed upon by either party, protest may be made at the bureau.
92. Instructions from the bureau, based on the report from the inspectors, are liable to be protested against in the bureau if such is unsuitable.
93. False accusation, extortion, and any illegal function as may be committed by the inspector, the factory has the right to appeal to the chief labour authorities to be dealt with.

Punishment:
Promoters of any factory who breaches para article 3 of this law, i.e., carrying out operations without permission, will be responsible for all damages.
95. He who breaches para. 2, article 3, i.e., in failing to change the certificate of registration from the Ministry of Industry and Commerce through the local directing authorities will lose the privilege of protection under these laws.
96. He who breaches article 7 and 8, i.e., to engage children under the age of 12, or give hard work to child labourer, a fine will be imposed from $50 to $300.
97. He who breaches article 20, i.e., in refusing to issue the service certificate, a fine of $5 to $10 will be imposed and the certificate issued.
98. He who breaches article, 4 i.e., to prolong the hours of work without approval, a fine from $50 to $300 will be imposed.
99. He who breaches article 5, i.e., in refusing to grant lawful leave, fine from $5 to $10 will be imposed, and leave granted.
100. He who breaches article 39, i.e., not paying the labourers on the regular day, a fine equal to 1 per cent. of the amount of pay for the labourers be imposed.
101. He who breaches article 40 and 41, an amount equal to three times to the amount deducted, be refunded.
102. He who breaches article 7, i.e., dishonestly distributing the profit, the man in charge is be sued in Court under the criminal code for forgery, and the accounts be checked over by an official auditor as appointed by the local directing authorities.

103. He who breaches article 10, a fine from $50 to $300 will be imposed.
104. He who breaches articles 77 and 78, i.e., in refusing to pay medical expenses, etc., action to be taken in Court demanding compensation as likely to cause bodily harm.
105. He who breaches articles 79, 70, 81, i.e., in allowing child and female labourers to work under unhealthy and dangerous conditions, a fine from $50 to $300 will be imposed.
106. He who breaches article 83, i.e., failing to keep a record book or same not properly entered, a fine from $50 to $300 will be imposed every time.
107. He who breaches articles 84 and 85, i.e., failing to forward the report at the fixed time or the report forwarded is inaccurate, a fine from $50 to $300 will be imposed.
108. He who failed to obtain approval of any matters from the official as laid down in these laws, the officials may compel the factory to do so, and in addition a fine from $50 to $300 will be imposed.
109. He who fails to act in the instructions as issued by the official will be fined from $50 to $300.
110. When any actions from the officials are considered unsuitable, the factory may appeal to the provincial labour officials and Ministry of Industry and Commerce for reconsideration. Any actions may inflict any damages on the factory, legal actions might be taken in the Court.
111. On the introduction of these laws, other rules and regulations governing factories are to be abolished.
112. These laws will come into force from the date of announcement.

E. C. J.

90. 视察员将确保工厂按照视察局指定的时间改善卫生和安全状况。
91. 当视察员对劳工年龄存有疑虑时，可要求视察局的医务官予以确认；如任何一方对决定不服，可向该局提出申诉。
92. 局方基于视察员报告发出的指令，如被认为不当，可向该局提出申诉。
93. 对于视察员实施的诬告、勒索及任何非法行为，工厂有权向最高劳工当局上诉，以求处理。

处罚：
任何违反本法第3条第1款（即未经许可擅自经营）的工厂发起人，应对所有损害承担责任。
95. 违反第3条第2款（即未通过地方主管当局变更工商部注册证书）者，将失去本法保护的特权。
96. 违反第7和第8条（即雇佣12岁以下儿童，或让童工从事繁重工作）者，处以50至300元罚款。
97. 违反第20条（即拒绝签发服务证明书）者，处以5至10元罚款，并须签发证明书。
98. 违反第4条（即未经批准延长工作时间）者，处以50至300元罚款。
99. 违反第5条（即拒绝给予合法假期）者，处以5至10元罚款，并须给予假期。
100. 违反第39条（即未在固定日期支付劳工工资）者，处以相当于劳工工资总额百分之一的罚款。
101. 违反第40和41条者，应退还相当于扣除金额三倍的款项。
102. 违反第7条（即 dishonestly [原文不清，意为不诚实地/欺诈性地] 分配利润）者，负责人将依刑法以伪造罪被起诉，账目由地方主管当局指定的官方审计员核查。

103. 违反第10条者，处以50至300元罚款。
104. 违反第77和78条（即拒绝支付医疗费用等）者，将在法院提起诉讼，要求赔偿，因其可能导致身体伤害。
105. 违反第79、80、81条（即允许童工和女工在不健康和危险条件下工作）者，处以50至300元罚款。
106. 违反第83条（即未保存记录簿或记录不当）者，每次处以50至300元罚款。
107. 违反第84和85条（即未按时提交报告或报告不准确）者，处以50至300元罚款。
108. 未按本法规定获得官员批准任何事项者，官员可强制工厂执行，并另处以50至300元罚款。
109. 未按官员发出的指示行事者，处以50至300元罚款。
110. 如认为官员的任何行为不当，工厂可向省级劳工官员和工商部申请复议。任何行为若给工厂造成损害，可在法院提起法律诉讼。
111. 本法实施后，其他管理工厂的规则和规章一律废止。
112. 本法自公布之日起生效。

E. C. J.

page_data.en:
FACTORY LAWS (DRAFT)

1. General.

1 The following laws are made to govern the factory or line (herein-
after termed the 'Factory') where in over 30 laborers are employed.
Factory which cannot be placed under these laws will follow the
orders issued by the Ministry of Industrial and Commerce.

2 Same laws are to apply to Foreign Factory within the sphere of the
Republic of China, however the nature of each factory, refers to
Article 1.

3 No Factory is permitted to enlist laborers or commence operation
without the official approval or proper registration with the
Ministry of Industrial and Commerce at the recommendation of the
Local Directing Authorities. Previous to the enforcement and
coming into force of these laws, any factory which has properly been
registered will within three months from date of announcement of
these laws, approach to the Local Directing Authorities by attesting
the change of the registration certificate from the Ministry of
Industrial and Commerce.

4 Local Directing Authorities unless are specially specified, are
the Municipal Authorities in special areas, District Government
Authorities in Districts, and City Government Authorities in
ordinary cities.

5 The by-laws for the registration of factory are being drafted
separately.

6 The Factory owner may appoint suitable person to manage the
affairs of the factory, but before the official registration of
the factory, the owner of the factory is liable to the responsi-
bilities of the management.
The manager is to responsible for the carrying out of these laws
on behalf of the owner.

2. Contracts.

7. Laborers of either sex are not permitted to be engaged at the
age under 12.

8. Easy and light jobs only will be assigned to laborers between
the ages of 12 to 16. These are called Child Laborers.
page_data.zh:
工厂法（草案）

1. 总则。

1 制定以下法律以管理雇佣劳工超过30人的工厂或生产线（以下简称“工厂”）。
不能纳入本法管理的工厂，应遵循工商部发布的命令。

2 同样法律适用于中华民国境内的外国工厂，但各工厂的性质参见第1条。

3 任何工厂未经官方批准或在地方主管当局推荐下向工商部适当注册，不得招募劳工或开始运营。在本法实施和生效之前，任何已适当注册的工厂，应在本法公布之日起三个月内，凭工商部变更的注册证书，向地方主管当局办理手续。

4 除非特别指定，地方主管当局指特别区域的市政当局、地区的区政府当局以及普通城市的市政府当局。

5 工厂注册细则另行起草。

6 工厂主可任命合适人员管理工厂事务，但在工厂正式注册前，工厂主须承担管理责任。
经理代表工厂主负责执行本法。

2. 合同。

7. 禁止雇佣未满12岁的男女劳工。

8. 仅可分配轻松轻便的工作给12至16岁的劳工。这些劳工称为童工。

page_data.en:
application shall be made for free certificate to ascertain the
age of the laborers if any doubt exists.
Prior to the establishment of the Bureau of Census, the local
directing authorities will examine the laborers between ages of
12 and 16 on their height, weight and issue free certificates for
ages if such is required.
The height and weight of the young laborers will be examined by
the local directing authorities three months after the announcement
of these laws.
10. Individual laborers may sign contracts with the factory.
11. Labor unions will represent the laborers to negotiate contracts
for bodies of laborers and the factory.
The above documents are to be made in writing as will take effect
on the approval of the Local Directing Authorities.
12. Any contracts which are made against the law will be substituted
in lines in correspondence with these laws.

5. Termination of Service.

13. On the expiry of individual contracts of fixed periods, renewal
will be made at the mutual consent of both parties.
14. Individual contracts of unlimited period will expire on giving 15
days notice to the other party, unless such is definitely laid
down under the conditions.
15. Failing to comply with article 14, the owner of the factory will
pay half month's wages, and on the other hand, the laborer will
lose the privilege as under article 20.
16. The factory may terminate or discharge the service of laborers
on the following conditions;
1. Close down the whole or part of the factory.
2. Any unexpected accidents by nature or fire which cannot be
resisted by human beings and such accidents may cause temporary
suspension of the running of the factory for a period exceeding
one month.
3. Lack of working ability and qualifications unsuitable.
4. Over three days leave without reasons.
page_data.zh:
如有疑义，应申请免费证书以核实劳工年龄。
在人口调查局成立之前，地方主管当局将检查12至16岁劳工的身高、体重，并在需要时签发免费年龄证明。
在这些法律颁布三个月后，地方主管当局将对年轻劳工的身高和体重进行检查。
10. 个别劳工可与工厂签订合同。
11. 工会将代表劳工群体与工厂协商合同。
上述文件须以书面形式制定，并经地方主管当局批准后生效。
12. 任何违反法律的合同，均应按本法规定予以修正。

5. 雇佣终止。

13. 固定期限的个人合同期满后，经双方同意可予续订。
14. 无固定期限的个人合同，除非条件中有明确规定，否则在向另一方发出15天通知后即告期满。
15. 如未遵守第14条规定，工厂主需支付半个月工资；反之，劳工将丧失第20条规定的权利。
16. 工厂可在下列条件下终止或解雇劳工：
1. 关闭全部或部分工厂。
2. 发生人力无法抗拒的自然灾害或火灾等意外事故，且此类事故可能导致工厂停工超过一个月。
3. 工作能力不足及资格不符。
4. 无故缺勤超过三天。

page_data.en:
5. Undergoing over one month's imprisonment on any criminal charge.
6. Losing the moving ability for time being (this refers to men
over two months sick leave, or females after confinement unable to
resume work after two months.

17. The Laborers may withdraw the contract on the following conditions:
1. The owner of the factory breaches the conditions of the contract
or Labor Laws.
2. Wages are not paid at regular time.
3. Illtreatment of laborers.
4. Risk of life and loss of a finger.

18. Reference Art. 1, 2, 3, under Article 16. A notice is to be
given to the Laborer by the Factory or in lieu thereof pay in lieu
of notice.

19. Reference Art. 1, 2, 3, of Article 16 and Article 17. Any disputes
arisen will be settled by the Factory Committee.

20. Certificates bearing the following items will be issued to Laborers
on the termination of service or on the closing of the factory;
1. Name, age, native of, and address of Laborers.
2. Nature and kinds of work.
3. Length of service and details of work.
4. Ability and character.
5. Wages and punishments.

4. Hours of Work.

1 Eight hours for full grown persons and may be prolonged to nine
hours under special circumstances as to suit the custom, season
and nature of the factory on the approval of the Local Directing
Authorities.

2 The hours of work for the Child Laborers should not exceed eight
hours.

3 In special cases when the hours of work may be prolonged. In such
cases permission should first be obtained from the Local Directing
Authorities.

4 The prolonged hours as for male grown laborers are not to exceed
three hours per day, and 45 hours per month.

5 For Female grown laborers are not to exceed two hours per day and
page_data.zh:
5. 因任何刑事指控被监禁超过一个月。
6. 暂时丧失行动能力（指男性病假超过两个月，或女性分娩后两个月内无法复工）。

17. 劳工可在下列条件下解除合同：
1. 工厂主违反合同条件或劳动法。
2. 工资未按时支付。
3. 虐待劳工。
4. 生命危险及手指缺失。

18. 参照第16条下的第1、2、3款。工厂应向劳工发出通知，或支付代通知金。

19. 参照第16条的第1、2、3款及第17条。任何产生的争议将由工厂委员会解决。

20. 在雇佣终止或工厂关闭时，应向劳工签发载有以下项目的证明：
1. 劳工的姓名、年龄、籍贯及住址。
2. 工作性质及种类。
3. 服务年限及工作详情。
4. 能力与品行。
5. 工资及处罚情况。

4. 工作时间。

1 成年人为八小时，经地方主管当局批准，可根据习俗、季节及工厂性质延长至九小时。

2 童工的工作时间不得超过八小时。

3 在特殊情况下可延长工作时间。在此类情况下，应首先获得地方主管当局的许可。

4 成年男性劳工的延长时间每天不得超过三小时，每月不得超过45小时。

5 成年女性劳工每天不得超过两小时，且

page_data.en:
twenty hours per month.
26. Child Laborers are not permitted to prolong their hours of work.
For Male Grown Laborers no continual work is permitted for more
than five hours. Female and Child Laborers are not to continue
their work for duration of more than three hours.
27. No Female Laborers are permitted to work between the hours from
8 p.m. to 6 a.m. the next morning.
28. No Child Laborers are permitted to work between the hours from
7 p.m. to 6 a.m. the next morning;
29. Factory which work continually day and night may obtain permission
from the Local Directing Authorities first. And Laborers should
change shifts at least once a week.

C Leave

30. Over thirty minutes rest to be given to Male Grown Laborers who
performed five hours work and Female and Child Laborers after
three hours work.
31. All Laborers should have 18 hours continuous rest once a week.
32. Leave to be granted on holidays as affixed by the Ministry of
Industrial and Commerce.
33. Any Laborer who completed six months continuous service is per-
mitted to get one week's special leave. And two weeks leave
for anyone who has completed one year's service.
Leave will be granted on discretion, providing that the factory
is able to release them the men.
34. No reductions of pay to be made on the regular leaves.

7 Wages.

35. Wages are paid under the consideration of the cost of living
and the location of the factory and not by the amount of money.
36. Factory will fix the wages as above stated and to be approved by
the Local Directing Authorities, these authorities also have the
power to fix the scale of wages.
37. Additional wages are to be paid at the proportions of 1/4 or 1/2
of their regular hour pay.
38. Wages are to be paid in local currency. It is prohibited to
pay anything which will represent the cash money.
page_data.zh:
每月不得超过二十小时。
26. 不允许童工延长工作时间。
成年男性劳工连续工作不得超过五小时。女性和童工连续工作不得超过三小时。
27. 禁止女性劳工在晚上8点至次日早上6点之间工作。
28. 禁止童工在晚上7点至次日早上6点之间工作；
29. 昼夜连续作业的工厂可首先向地方主管当局申请许可。劳工应至少每周轮班一次。

C 休假

30. 成年男性劳工工作五小时后，以及女性和童工工作三小时后，应给予三十分钟以上的休息。
31. 所有劳工每周应享有18小时的连续休息。
32. 按工商部规定的节假日给予休假。
33. 任何连续服务满六个月的劳工，准许享受一周特别休假。服务满一年者，享受两周休假。
休假的批准视情况而定，前提是工厂能够安排人员顶替。
34. 常规休假期间不得减薪。

7 工资。

35. 工资的支付应考虑生活成本及工厂所在地，而非仅依据金额多少。
36. 工厂应按上述规定确定工资，并报地方主管当局批准，这些当局也有权确定工资标准。
37. 加班工资应按其正常小时工资的1/4或1/2比例支付。
38. 工资应以当地货币支付。禁止支付任何代表现金的物品。

page_data.en:
39 Wages are to be paid twice a month on the 1st and 15th respectively.
40 No deductions of wages are to be made in advance as securities to damages or compensations etc.
41 For the benefit of the Laborers, Savings, Insurance and Social matters might be introduced at the consent of the Laborers. In such cases, portions of their pay be deducted on a pre-arranged scheme and same to be approved by the Local Directing Authorities.

7. Distribution of Profits.

42 3% interest will be issued to the paid up capitals from the profit after expenses are being paid.
43 20% of the net profit will go into the Reserve Fund which will be under the charge of the Factory and not to be touched by either parties unless for improvement purposes.
Net profit refers to balance of profit after the paying off the 3% interest and taxes etc.
44 Any balance left after the deduction of the Reserve Fund will be distributed at 40% to the laborers xxxxx, 40% to the Capitalists, and 20% to the Managing Staff.
Laborers refers to persons who served the factory over six months and the Managing Staff refers to employees attached to the Administrative Supervision and Controlling Departments.
45 40% profit for the capitalists will be proportionally distributed in accordance to the capitals paid.
46 From 40% profit for the laborers. 30% to be distributed to the laborers in proportions to their wages, and 10% will be reserved and kept by the Labor Committee nominated by the Factory Committee for the purpose of benefit the laborers.
The above distribution should not include the amount of wages for the number of days during the sick leave of the laborers.
47 Expenditures on compensations, Rewards, and gratuities and certain amount of premium for insurance are classified under the ordinary expenditure of the factory.

8. Health and Safety.

48 Special staff to be detailed by the factory to deal with the matters on Health and Safety.
page_data.zh:
39 工资每月支付两次，分别在1日和15日。
40 不得预先扣除工资作为损害或赔偿等的保证金。
41 为劳工利益起见，经劳工同意，可引入储蓄、保险和社会事务。在此类情况下，可按预定方案从工资中扣除部分款项，并须报地方主管当局批准。

7. 利润分配。

42 支付费用后的利润中，将向实缴资本发放3%的利息。
43 净利润的20%将存入储备基金，该基金由工厂管理，除非用于改进目的，否则任何一方不得动用。
净利润是指支付3%利息及税款等后的利润余额。
44 扣除储备基金后的任何余额，将按40%分配给劳工 xxxxx，40%分配给资本家，20%分配给管理人员。
劳工是指在工厂服务超过六个月的人员，管理人员是指隶属于行政监督和管理部门的员工。
45 资本家的40%利润将根据实缴资本按比例分配。
46 在分配给劳工的40%利润中，30%按工资比例分配给劳工，10%由工厂委员会提名的劳工委员会保留和管理，用于造福劳工。
上述分配不应包括劳工病假期间的工资数额。
47 赔偿金、奖励、酬金及一定数额的保险费支出，列为工厂的日常开支。

Taken from Bureau of Economic Information
Nº28, May 7, 1923.

26/1/24

Labor Legislation in China.
--------------------------

A set of factory regulations was promulgated
by a Presidential Mandate on March 29, 1923 and another
set governing labor Unions has been submitted to
the Parliament for deliberation. At the same time
the Ministry of Communications and the Ministry of
Agriculture and Commerce have each organized a special
labor division to look after matters concerning
labor, while a similar division will soon be organized
in the Foreign Ministry. The first Ministry will
take care of railway laborers, sailors, telegraph
and telephone operators and post office employees;
the second, laborers in ordinary mines, in factories
and on farms; and the last, emigrated laborers.
The Parliament is drafting a special chapter on
labor for the National constitution.
The factory regulations are to be applied to
all factories engaging more than one hundred labor-
ers, as well as to those with less than that number
if their manufacturing process involves danger to
the laborers' life or health. For factories not
in these two categories, special regulations may
be issued at any time by the Ministry of Agriculture
and Commerce. (Art1) Factories owned by foreigners,
if in Chinese territory, come under the present
regulations. (Art.2).
Articles 2 to 10 deal with child labor and
working time. Boys under 10 and girls under 12
are forbidden to work in factories, while boys under
17 and girls under 18 may work only under certain
limitations, and for short hours. They are
certain restriction for adults.
Articles 12 to 16 provide that wages must be
paid in currency, and must not be deducted in
anticipation of fines or damages to be collected .
Factories may keep savings deposits for laborers,
and are expected to provide for laborers' bonus,
old age pension and solatium. When the laborers
are sick or injured during work, they should be
given medical treatment at the expense of the
factory management. Working women should be given
special allowance during confinement. (Articles 17
19 and 20).
The factories, according to Article 18, should
provide supplementary education for their laborers
when needed. Women and children must not work in
places of danger, and the latter are prohibited
from working with poisonous or explosive materials.
There are other provisions relating to protection
of laborers' health in Articles 21 to 25. The
last three articles (26 to 28) put the responsibility
in all these connections on factory managers as
representatives of the proprietors.
The regulations governing labor Unions are
drafted with the intention of controlling and
limiting the activities of these organizations,
in view of the many strikes on railway and in
industries. They require the approval of the
Government in many matters and reports to the
Government in many others. The most important
provision is Art. 13- an unlucky number for the
laborers- because it justifies dissolution of a
Union if its activities (②) disturb the form of
Government)

中国的劳动立法。
--------------------------

1923年3月29日，总统令颁布了一套工厂条例，另一套管理工会的条例已提交议会审议。同时，交通部和农商部分别设立了专门的劳工司，以处理劳工事务，外交部不久也将设立类似的部门。第一个部将负责铁路劳工、海员、电报和电话操作员以及邮局雇员；第二个部负责普通矿山、工厂和农场的劳工；最后一个部负责出国劳工。议会正在为国家宪法起草专门的劳工章节。
工厂条例适用于所有雇佣一百名以上劳工的工厂，以及虽然人数较少但其制造过程危及劳工生命或健康的工厂。对于不属于这两类的工厂，农商部可随时发布特别规定。（第1条）位于中国领土内的外商拥有的工厂，受现行条例管辖。（第2条）。
第2至10条涉及童工和工作时间。禁止10岁以下男孩和12岁以下女孩在工厂工作，而17岁以下男孩和18岁以下女孩只能在某些限制下工作，且工作时间较短。成年人也有某些限制。
第12至16条规定，工资必须以货币支付，不得预先扣除以抵偿罚款或损害赔偿。工厂可为劳工保留储蓄存款，并应为劳工提供奖金、养老金和抚恤金。劳工在工作期间生病或受伤，应由厂方承担医疗费用进行治疗。女工在分娩期间应获得特殊津贴。（第17、19和20条）。
根据第18条，工厂应在需要时为劳工提供补充教育。妇女和儿童不得在危险场所工作，后者禁止接触有毒或爆炸性材料。第21至25条还有其他关于保护劳工健康的规定。最后三条（第26至28条）将所有这些方面的责任归于作为业主代表的工厂经理。
管理工会的条例旨在控制和限制这些组织的活动，鉴于铁路和工业领域发生了许多罢工。条例要求在许多事项上获得政府批准，并在许多其他事项上向政府报告。最重要的条款是第13条——对劳工来说是个不吉利的数字——因为它证明如果工会的活动（②扰乱政府形式），即可解散工会

(b) distubb public peace, (c) endanger the
living of the public, or (d) obstruct communication
and inflict injury on the nation or society.
The first alternative has reference to bolshevism
while the last aims particularly at railways
strikes. It is doubtful whether the regulations
will be passed by Parliament without substantial
modifications.
Another set of regulations, governing working
conditions in mines, has been drafted, but not yet
approved and promulgated. It applies to all mines
which employ at the same time more than 50 under-
ground workers. The mine owners are to be repre-
sented by the chief engineer, who shall look
after the ventilation, presence of gas or water,
and use of explosive in the mines.
No women or children under 12 are allowed to
work underground, while under special conditions
children under 17 may also be prohibited. Working
time is limited to 10 hours a day. The shafts
must be properly supported, and each pocket
must have at least two openings for passage of
laborers. Safety lamps are required of all
mines where presence of coal gas is suspected.
Altogether 63 articles are included in the draft
regulations, most of which deal with minute details.
There are, according to the statistics of the
Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce, more than
43,000,000 mine laborers in the country.
There is no provision concerning wages rates
in any of these regulations nor are any special
regulations governing them excepted to be pro-
mulgated soon. At present the very too widey
to make the determination of a uniform mini-
mum wage possible for the whole country or
useful. They may be as low as two cents a day,
or as high as $4.10, as may be seen from the
Companying table. The very low wages are generally
paid where food and lodging are supplied by the
employer. Otherwise, the lowest wages paid now
in any industry do not fall below $0.20, while
the average is about $0.50 a day.

Provisional Factory Regulations
(Promulgated March 29, 1923)

Art. 1. The present regulations shall apply
to the following factories:
a. Those which at ordinary times employ
more than one hundred laborers.
b. Those in which conditions exist that
are dangerous to the life or injurious to the
health of the laborers.
Factories to be exempted from the operation
of these regulations will be specified by
Ministerial Orders.
Art. 2. Foreign factories established in
Chinese territory and fulfilling the above two
conditions shall equally come under these
regulations.
Art. 3. Factory owners shall not employ
boys under 10 or girls under 12.
Art. 4. Boys under 17 and girls under 18
shall be considered as children.

(b) 扰乱公共治安，(c) 危害公众生计，或 (d) 阻碍交通并对国家或社会造成损害。
第一种情形指的是布尔什维主义，而最后一种情形则特别针对铁路罢工。这些条例能否在未经重大修改的情况下获得国会通过，尚存疑问。
另一套关于矿山工作条件的条例已起草完毕，但尚未批准和颁布。该条例适用于同时雇用五十名以上井下工人的所有矿山。矿主应由总工程师代表，由其负责监管矿山的通风、瓦斯或积水情况以及炸药的使用。
禁止妇女或十二岁以下儿童从事井下工作，而在特殊情况下，十七岁以下儿童也可能被禁止从事此类工作。工作时间限制为每天十小时。井巷必须得到适当支撑，且每个作业面必须至少有两个出口供工人通行。在怀疑存在煤气的矿井中，必须使用安全灯。
草案条例共包含六十三条，其中大部分涉及细微细节。
根据农商部的统计，全国矿工人数超过四千三百万。
这些条例中没有任何关于工资率的规定，预计也不会很快颁布任何专门管理工资的条例。目前，各地差异过大，使得为全国确定统一的最低工资既不可能也无实际意义。从附表中可以看出，日工资低至二分，高至4.10美元。极低的工资通常出现在雇主提供食宿的情况下。否则，目前任何行业支付的最低工资不低于0.20美元，而平均日工资约为0.50美元。

《工厂暂行条例》
（1923年3月29日颁布）

第一条 本条例适用于下列工厂：
a. 平时雇用工人在一百名以上者。
b. 存在危及工人生命或损害工人健康之状况者。
豁免适用本条例的工厂，将由部令具体规定。
第二条 在中国领土内设立并符合上述两个条件的外国工厂，同样受本条例管辖。
第三条 工厂主不得雇用十岁以下男童或十二岁以下女童。
第四条 十七岁以下男童和十八岁以下女童视为童工。

第五条 童工在工厂内仅可从事轻体力劳动。
第六条 童工每日工作时间最多为八小时，不包括休息时间。
第七条 工厂主不得安排童工在晚上8点至凌晨4点之间工作。
第八条 成年工人每月至少休息两天；童工每月至少休息三天。
如遇紧急情况，工厂可暂时停止执行上述规定，但必须向相关政府机关报告。
第九条 各类工人每天必须有一个或多个休息时段。此类休息时段每天总计至少为一小时。
第十条 必须实行日夜轮班的特种工厂，应每十天轮换一次班次工人。
第十一条 工资必须全部以货币支付，除非经工人同意，否则不得以实物支付。
第十二条 工资应按固定周期支付，周期不得超过一个月。
第十三条 如因特殊原因延长工作时间，工厂主应按高于平常的费率向工人支付加班费。
第十四条 工厂主不得从工人工资中预先扣除款项，作为将来收取罚款或赔偿之用。
第十五条 当为鼓励工人储蓄或出于其他有利于工人的目的而扣留部分工资时，必须征得工人本人同意，且有关基金管理的计划须获相关政府机关批准。
第十六条 工人死亡或被解雇时，工厂主应向该工人或其亲属支付所有应付工资，以及存放在工厂的储蓄款项。
第十七条 工厂主应根据本厂情况，制定向工人支付抚恤金、奖金和养老金的计划，并提交相关政府机关批准。
第十八条 工厂主应为做工的童工及未受过教育的成年工人提供适当的补习教育，并承担费用。
此类补习教育，童工每周至少十小时，成年工人每周至少六小时。
第十九条 对于患病或受伤的工人，工厂主应根据情况限制其工作量或完全停止其工作。如果疾病或伤害是因在工厂工作所致，厂主应承担医疗费用，并

ing the machine parts, or attending to the

Art. 23. Children should not be employed

Art. 24. Factories should provide special

Draft Regulations Governing Labor Unions.
(Submitted to the Parliament for deliberation).
Art. 1. Laborers engaged in the same kind of
employment may, in compliance with the present
Regulations, organize unions for maintaining their
livelihood and promoting their common interests.
Art. 2. Labor Unions will be juridical persons.
Art. 3. Labor Unions shall deal with the
following matters:
a. Mutual help for members.
b. Improvement of terms of employment.
c. Investigation of labor conditions.
d. Making proposals to the Government
with respect to labor legislation.
e. Answering inquiries of Government offices.
Art. 4. Labor Union may establish branches.
Art. 5. A labor union may be organize when it is
proposed by at least ten men, who should submit a draft
constitution of the union to the appropriate local
administrative office for approval. Laborers employed
in national or public industries should secure in
addition the approval of the Government office in charge
of the industry.

第二十条 女工在分娩前后应各享有五周的休假，并应获得一定的特殊津贴。
第二十一条 机器运转或动力传输时，不得雇用妇女和儿童清洁、加油、检查或修理机器部件，照看皮带和滑轮，或以任何其他涉及危险的方式参与工作。

第二十四条 工厂应提供保护工人生命和健康的专用设备，此类设备应接受政府官员的检查。
第二十五条 当政府认为工厂的厂房、设备或任何附属结构涉及危险，可能损害工人的生命或健康，或有损公共利益时，工厂主应相应改变构造或布局。如果政府认为有必要，可暂停整个工厂或部分工厂的运营。
第二十六条 工厂主可任命合适的人员担任经理，负责管理工厂。

《工会条例草案》
（提交国会审议）

第一条 从事同类职业的工人，可根据本条例组织工会，以维持生计并促进共同利益。

a. 会员互助。
b. 改善雇佣条件。
c. 调查劳工状况。

a. 工会名称。
b. 总部地址。
c. 工会从事的工作种类。
d. 会员资格以及会员加入和除名的规则。

第八条 工会选举职员或通过决议时，应向相关政府机关报告。如果工会由某些国家或公共产业的工人组织，则应向主管该产业的政府机关报告。

c. 危害公众生计。
