Draft of Factory Legislation.

Reports coming from the Peking correspondent of Kuo Wen News Agency say that the committee called by the Board of Agriculture and Commerce to revise the statutes of agriculture and commerce began its work on March 15, 1923. The committee is composed of twenty-eight members, and in addition there are seventeen advisors. The term of the committee is limited to six months. They began discussion on March 19. The recommendations to be discussed were made either by the Board or by the members of the Committee. Up to the present, there are already many recommendations, in which there is a draft of factory legislation recommended by the Board which is very important to commerce. It was learned that this draft would be discussed after three weeks. The draft reads as follows:

Within these few years, there have been strikes arising from the question of treatment of employees. As the danger from these in the future would be very serious, the government should prepare a kind of industrial statute to be executed as early as possible. Thus both the factory owners and laborers will be able to understand their own positions and fulfil their own duties. The misunderstandings which endanger the peace and order of society might be avoided. Furthermore, as the International Labor Office has asked us several times to prepare factory legislation, we cannot afford to lose their confidence by delaying this work. But the industry of our country is just in its infancy. The ways of life of our people become more difficult day by day. The industrial standard fixed by the League of Nations as to working hours, and ages should be thought over thoroughly. Having examined carefully the conditions of our country, we have made the following draft by referring to the standards of other countries. Those which cannot be carried out at present are either indicated as exceptions or it is suggested that their execution be temporarily postponed. Though the standards are made for the protection of laborers, yet they are also, in a sense, for maintaining industry as well. We recommend them to your committee and submit them for your approval.

Article I. General Regulations.

Section 1. This legislation is applicable to factories which have the following qualifications:

a. Those which have employees up to the number of fifty.
B. This legislation is not applicable to factories having dangerous and unsanitary conditions, for which there are special regulations.

Section 2. Factories established in China but owned by foreigners are allowed to apply this legislation if they are in accordance with the qualification of section 1.

The regulations given above should be obeyed when notification has been given at any time by the authorities of the region in which the factories are situated.

Article II. Age of the Workers.

Section 3. Employment of boys under twelve years of ages and girls under fourteen is prohibited. But those boys above ten years of ages and girls above twelve who have worked in the factory before the execution of this legislation may continue to be employed.

Section 4. Boys between thirteen and seventeen years of age are called minor workers. Those who are above seventeen years of age are called adult workers.
page_data.zh:
工厂立法草案。

据国闻通讯社北京记者报道，农商部为修订农商法规而召集的委员会已于1923年3月15日开始工作。该委员会由二十八名委员组成，此外还有十七名顾问。委员会任期限定为六个月。他们于3月19日开始讨论。待讨论的建议案或由农商部提出，或由委员会委员提出。截至目前，已有许多建议案，其中由农商部提出的工厂立法草案对商业至关重要。据悉，该草案将在三周后进行讨论。草案内容如下：

近几年来，因雇员待遇问题引发的罢工屡有发生。鉴于此类事件未来可能带来严重危害，政府应尽早制定并实施某种工业法规。从而使厂主与劳工均能明确自身地位并履行各自职责。由此可避免危及社会和平与秩序的误解。此外，由于国际劳工局已多次要求我们制定工厂立法，若拖延此项工作，我们将失去其信任。但我国工业尚处于起步阶段。民众生计日益艰难。对于国际联盟所规定的工作时间及年龄等工业标准，应予以 thorough 考量。在仔细考察我国国情后，我们参照其他国家的标准制定了以下草案。目前无法实施的条款，或列为例外，或建议暂缓执行。虽然这些标准旨在保护劳工，但在某种意义上也是为了维持工业发展。现将其推荐给贵委员会，并提交审批。

第一条. 总则。

第一款. 本立法适用于具备下列资格的工厂：

a. 雇员人数达五十人者。
b. 本立法不适用于具有危险及不卫生状况的工厂，此类工厂另有专门法规管辖。

第二款. 在中国设立但由外国人拥有的工厂，若符合第一款之资格，允许适用本立法。

当工厂所在地区的当局随时发出通知时，应遵守上述规定。

第二条. 工人年龄。

第三款. 禁止雇用十二岁以下男童及十四岁以下女童。但在本立法实施前已在工厂工作的十岁以上男童及十二岁以上女童，可继续受雇。

第四款. 十三至十七岁的男童称为未成年工。十七岁以上者称为成年工。

page_data.en:
-2-

Section 5. Minor workers and girls between fifteen and eighteen years
of age can be employed only for easy work.

Section 6. The age at which foreign workers may be employed is subject
to the legislation of their own countries.

Article III. Working Hours.

Section 7. Excluding the time of rest, the working hours of minor and
women workers cannot exceed eight hours a day, and those of the adult
workers cannot exceed ten hours a day. The working hours of those who
work in the same day in two or more factories should be counted as a
whole. In time of emergency, the regulation given above can be changed
temporarily by the executive authorities.

Section 8. If for special reasons, the owner of the factory has real
difficulties in executing the regulation of section 7, he may during
fifteen years from the day of this legislation's taking effect petition
the authorized office for prolongation of two hours per day.

Section 9. If in a certain period, the factory owner wants to have
provisional prolongation of working hours for certain important reasons,
he can petition the executive authorities for prolongation of not more
than two hours a day. But the term of the period shall not exceed seven
days every month.

Section 10. In a certain period, if the factory owner wants to have
prolongation of working hours in consequence of seasons, he can present
a petition with full description of reasons to the executive authorities
for prolongation of no more than one hour per day. But the total should
not be over one third of the season.

Section 11. Factory owners are prohibited from employing minor workers
and women workers to work between 10 p.m. and 4 a.m. of the next day.

Section 12. Those factories which must have night work by turns, are
not subject to the regulation given above for fifteen years from the day
of the execution of this legislation. The classification of all such fac-
tories is fixed by separate orders.

Article IV. The Time of Rest.

Section 13. Factory owners should give at least two days' rest to the
adult workers per month, and to minor and women workers one day's rest
per week. But in time of emergency, the above regulation can be declared
temporarily void.

Section 14. Factory owners should give a time of rest to their employees
one or more times every day. The time of rest as a whole should be over
every day. If the working hours are not over six a day, then the time of
rest can be deducted proportionately.

Section 15. If special factories must adopt the system of having day and
night work by turn, then the work should be exchanged at least every ten
days.

Section 16. Those factories which have the conditions of section nine
and section ten, and which have been permitted to prolong their working
hours, are exempt from the regulation of section 13 during the duration
of that term.
page_data.zh:
-2-

第五款. 未成年工及十五至十八岁的女童仅可受雇从事轻便工作。

第六款. 外籍工人的雇用年龄依其本国法律而定。

第三条. 工作时间。

第七款. 除休息时间外，未成年工及女工每日工作时间不得超过八小时，成年工每日不得超过十小时。同一天在两家或更多工厂工作者的工作时间应合并计算。在紧急情况下，行政当局可暂时变更上述规定。

第八款. 若因特殊原因，厂主在执行第七款规定方面确有困难，可在本立法生效之日起十五年内，向主管机关申请每日延长两小时。

第九款. 若在特定时期内，厂主因某些重要理由希望临时延长工作时间，可向行政当局申请每日延长不超过两小时。但该期限每月不得超过七天。

第十款. 在特定时期内，若厂主因季节原因希望延长工作时间，可向行政当局提交详述理由的申请，申请每日延长不超过一小时。但总延长时间不得超过该季节时长的三分之一。

第十一款. 禁止厂主雇用未成年工及女工在晚上十点至次日凌晨四点之间工作。

第十二款. 必须轮流进行夜间工作的工厂，自本立法实施之日起十五年内，不受上述规定约束。所有此类工厂的分类由单独命令确定。

第四条. 休息时间。

第十三款. 厂主每月应给予成年工至少两天休息，给予未成年工及女工每周一天休息。但在紧急情况下，可暂时宣布上述规定无效。

第十四款. 厂主每天应给予雇员一次或多次休息时间。总的休息时间每天应超过（原文不清，似缺具体时长）。若每日工作时间不超过六小时，则休息时间可按比例扣除。

第十五款. 若特殊工厂必须采用日夜轮班制度，则至少每十天轮换一次工作班次。

第十六款. 符合第九款和第十款条件并已获准延长工作时间的工厂，在该期限内免除第十三款规定的约束。

page_data.en:
-3-

Article V. Wages.
Section 17. Wages of the employees should be paid only in current money, not by commodities.
Section 18. Wages should be paid regularly, and at least three times per month.
Section 19. If working hours are prolonged under special conditions, wages should also be increased in proportion to the hour prolonged.
Section 20. Factory owners should not deduct in advance a certain sum of money from the wages of their employees as a guarantee of reception against the breaking of agreements or damages.
Section 21. If for the advantage profits and savings of the employees, a part of their wages are deducted in commodities, then the regulation of section 17 can be made void. But the factory owner should make a report as to the rules of managing the affairs to the executive authorities xx and get permission from the latter.
Section 22. When the employee has retired or died, the factory owner should pay the wages the employee should have to the employee himself or to his heirs. All of his savings should also be paid back.
Section 23. If the employee demands two months wages in advance or to get back a part or the whole of his savings for marriage or a funeral the factory owner should grant this request, with discretion.

Article VI. Treatment of Workers.
Section 24. Factory owners should respect the personality of their employees.
Section 25. Factory owner should provide insurance for their employees according to insurance legislation. Before the insurance legislation is carried into effect, factory owners should make rules for the pensioning of their employees and submit them to the approval of the executive authorities.
Section 26. Factory owners should provide for pensions and bonuses to be given to their employees, and should submit these provisions to the approval of the executive authorities.
Section 27. Factory owners should give supplementary education to xx their workers and bear all the expenses of this. This rules concerning supplementary education of worker will be fixed by separate orders.
Section 28. Factory owner should pay considerable attention to the health of their workers.

Article VII. Work.
Section 29. The work of wounded or sick workers should be stopped or limited (with full pay?).
Section 30. Women workers should be given five weeks' rest before and after confinement.
Section 31. No minor workers should be ordered to clean, to oil, to examine, or to repair machines when they are in motion or to do other dangerous work.
page_data.zh:
-3-

第五条. 工资。
第十七款. 雇员工资应以现行货币支付，不得以实物支付。
第十八款. 工资应定期支付，每月至少支付三次。
第十九款. 若在特殊条件下延长工作时间，工资也应按延长的小时数成比例增加。
第二十款. 厂主不得从雇员工资中预先扣除一定金额作为防止违约或损坏的保证金。
第二十一款. 若为雇员利益、利润及储蓄起见，从其工资中以实物形式扣除一部分，则可使第十七款规定无效。但厂主应向行政当局 xx 报告管理事务的规则，并获得后者许可。
第二十二款. 当雇员退休或死亡时，厂主应将雇员应得的工资支付给雇员本人或其继承人。其所有储蓄也应退还。
第二十三款. 若雇员因结婚或丧葬需要预支两个月工资或取回部分或全部储蓄，厂主应酌情批准此请求。

第六条. 工人待遇。
第二十四款. 厂主应尊重雇员的人格。
第二十五款. 厂主应根据保险立法为雇员提供保险。在保险立法生效之前，厂主应制定雇员养老金规则，并提交行政当局批准。
第二十六款. 厂主应规定给予雇员的养老金及奖金，并将这些规定提交行政当局批准。
第二十七款. 厂主应为其工人提供补习教育，并承担所有费用。有关工人补习教育的规则将由单独命令确定。
第二十八款. 厂主应高度重视工人的健康。

第七条. 工作。
第二十九款. 受伤或生病工人的工作应停止或限制（是否保留全额工资？）。
第三十款. 女工在分娩前后应享有五周的休息时间。
第三十一款. 不得命令未成年工在机器运转时进行清洁、加油、检查或修理机器，或从事其他危险工作。

page_data.en:
Section 32. No minor and women workers should be put into work involving the application of poisonous, and strong, chemicals or dynamite.

Section 33. No minor and women workers are allowed to work in places which are unsanitary, or dangerous, or where the air is filled with dust, powder, or poisonous gas.

Section 34. Agreements concerning the employment of workers cannot should not conflict with this legislation.

Section 35. Agreements concerning the employment of workers should be submitted to the approval of the executive authorities.

Section 36. If for the purpose of preventing the breaking of agreements and the making of any difficulties by workers, the factory owners are allowed to make rules concerning the imposing of fine to be approved by executive authorities. The fines can be deducted from the savings or wages of the workers after the matter has occurred.

Section 37. Before the expiration of the term of the agreement, if the factory owner wants to dismiss an employee, he should unless for special reasons, notify the latter two months in advance and give the latter a certain sum of money as a compensation.

Article IX. Examination.

Section 38. Executive authorities may send men to investigate those factories within their region and examine into the construction and arrangement of these factories.

Section 39. If the factory and its construction and arrangements are judged by the executive authorities to be dangerous, or detrimental to the public interest, they should be reformed by the factory owner in obedience to orders of the authorities. If the executive authorities deem it necessary, a part or whole of the plant may be condemned.

Article X. Apprenticeship.

Section 40. An apprentice must have the following qualifications:
a. The work he undertakes must lead to the knowledge and skill necessary to a definite profession.
b. He should be under the direction and supervision of a director when he is at work.
c. With regard to the cultivation of moral character, he should be under the guidance of an adviser.
d. His age must be over thirteen.

Section 41. If the factory owner wants to employ apprentices, he should submit rules for such to the approval of executive authorities.

Section 42. The regulations in this legislation concerning workers are not applicable to apprentices.

Article XI. Certification.

Section 43. If the factory owner is doubtful as to the age of an apprentice or worker at the time of employment, the person concerned can petition to the office in charge of the census for a certificate of age, free in charge. Before the execution of the census law, the executive authorities, when petitioned by the person concerned for physical examination, should appoint an official physician to give the examination and give a certificate of age free in charge.
page_data.zh:
第三十二款. 不得安排未成年工及女工从事涉及使用有毒、强效化学品或炸药的工作。

第三十三款. 不允许未成年工及女工在不卫生、危险或空气中充满粉尘、粉末或有毒气体的场所工作。

第三十四款. 关于雇用工人的协议不应与本立法相冲突。

第三十五款. 关于雇用工人的协议应提交行政当局批准。

第三十六款. 为防止违约及工人制造任何困难，允许厂主制定有关罚款的规则，须经行政当局批准。罚款可在事后从工人的储蓄或工资中扣除。

第三十七款. 在协议期满之前，若厂主希望解雇雇员，除非有特殊理由，否则应提前两个月通知后者，并给予后者一定金额作为补偿。

第九条. 检查。

第三十八款. 行政当局可派人调查其辖区内的工厂，并检查这些工厂的建筑及布局。

第三十九款. 若行政当局判定工厂及其建筑布局存在危险或损害公共利益，厂主应遵照当局命令进行整改。若行政当局认为必要，可查封部分或全部厂房。

第十条. 学徒制。

第四十款. 学徒必须具备下列资格：
a. 其所从事的工作必须通向获得特定职业所需的知识和技能。
b. 工作时，他应在主管的指导和监督之下。
c. 在品德培养方面，他应接受顾问的指导。
d. 其年龄必须在十三岁以上。

第四十一款. 若厂主希望雇用学徒，应将相关规则提交行政当局批准。

第四十二条. 本立法中有关工人的规定不适用于学徒。

第十一条. 证明。

第四十三款. 若厂主在雇用学徒或工人时对其年龄存疑，相关人员可向负责户籍登记的机关免费申请年龄证明。在户籍法实施之前，经相关人员申请体检，行政当局应指派官方医师进行检查并免费出具年龄证明。

page_data.en:
--5--

Article XII. Superintendence.

Section 44. A factory owner may appoint a suitable person as factory superintendent to manage all the affairs of the factory. If the factory owner does not live in the region affected by this legislation, he should appoint a superintendent as said above. The appointment of a factory superintendent should be reported to the executive authorities for sanction and registration. But if the factory superintendent is selected from among the directors, or shareholders, or others bearing a special relationship to the concern, then this procedure is not necessary.

Section 45. Except financial obligations, the factory superintendent should bear all the legal responsibilities for the factory owner. If the factory owner is incompetent, or a minor, and if there is also no factory superintendent, the directors or shareholders, or other legal representatives, should be subjected to the regulation given above.

Article XIII. Punishment.

Section 46. If the factory owner disobeys this legislation or does not act in accordance with the orders given by authorities in connection with this legislation, he shall be fined a sum not to exceed one hundred dollars.

Section 47. When the attorney of the factory owner, or an employee disobeys the orders given by the authorities in accordance with this legislation, the factory owner shall not be exempt from penalty on the ground that it is not done intentionally.

Section 48. In carrying out the regulations of article II, the factory owner shall not be exempt from penalty on the ground that he does not know the real age of the workers. But if he has a certificate, then he is not subject to this regulation.

Section 49. If the factory owner is not satisfied with the judgment, he can appeal to the court. And if he suffers loss from wrong doing of the authorities, he can criminal litigation against the authorities.

Article XIV. By-laws.

Section 50. Except for the regulations of Article XII, and Article XIII this legislation is applicable both to private and governmental factories.

Section 51. The regulations of Article VII, Article IX, Article XI, and section 49, are applicable to factories having less than fifty workers.

Section 52. This legislation takes effect on the day of publication.
page_data.zh:
--5--

第十二条 监督。

第四十四条 工厂主可任命一名适当人员担任工厂监督员，以管理工厂的一切事务。如果工厂主不住在本立法所适用的区域内，他应按上述规定任命一名监督员。工厂监督员的任命应报请行政当局批准并登记。但如果工厂监督员是从董事、股东或与该企业有特殊关系的其他人员中选任的，则无需履行此程序。

第四十五条 除财务义务外，工厂监督员应为工厂主承担所有法律责任。如果工厂主无行为能力或为未成年人，且也没有工厂监督员，则董事、股东或其他法定代理人应受上述规定的约束。

第十三条 处罚。

第四十六条 如果工厂主违反本立法或不按照当局根据本立法发出的命令行事，应处以不超过一百元的罚款。

第四十七条 当工厂主的代理人或雇员违反当局根据本立法发出的命令时，工厂主不得以非故意为由免除处罚。

第四十八条 在执行第二条的规定时，工厂主不得以不知道工人的真实年龄为由免除处罚。但如果他持有证明，则不受本条规定的约束。

第四十九条 如果工厂主对判决不服，可以向法院上诉。如果因当局的违法行为而遭受损失，他可以对当局提起刑事诉讼。

第十四条 附则。

第五十条 除第十二条和第十三条的规定外，本立法既适用于私营工厂，也适用于官办工厂。

第五十一条 第七条、第九条、第十一条及第四十九条的规定，适用于工人人数少于五十人的工厂。

第五十二条 本立法自公布之日起生效。

Sir,

From enquiries made it has been ascertained that the managements of the Japan-China Spinning and Weaving Co. Ltd., 96 Robison Road, and the Tokwa Cotton Mill, 88 Ward Road, received an invitation from the Commissioner of Social Affairs for Greater Shanghai asking them to be present at the meeting to be held at the Bureau of Social Affairs at 2 p.m. February 2nd to discuss questions regarding the enforcement of the new Factory Law.

档案号 •
S. 2.    警署。
日期 19□□年1月31日

主题（全称）社会局在租界内执行工厂法。

呈报人：日籍侦探梅本 (J.D.S. Umemoto)。转呈人：助理警务处长 W. Osmaston

先生，

经查询获悉，位于罗宾森路96号的日华纺织株式会社以及位于华德路88号的东和纱厂的管理层已收到大上海社会局局长的邀请，请他们出席定于2月2日下午2点在社会局举行的会议，讨论有关执行新工厂法的问题。

管理层决定不参加会议，但在华日本纱厂业主协会正在考虑此事，拟派一名代表列席观察讨论情况。

H. Umemoto.

中国工厂法成为
讨论议题

民生会议上提出修改若干
条款的建议

国民政府最近颁布的工……（原文不清/残缺）……取的措施，到8月1日时将对法律的适用性有更多的了解。因此，他建议采取以下两种途径之一：敦促政府任命一个委员会来研究该法案并调查某些工商业区域，以便在8月执行法律之前确定必要的修订。否则，鉴于本次会议代表了相当一部分公众舆论，应由会议任命一个委员会来研究并提出对该法案的充分修改建议。

一些批评与支持其原则

来自燕京大学的杰斐逊·兰姆 (Jefferson Lamb) 博士对工厂法的内容提出了一些批评。他指出最低工资规定不明确；提到了八小时工作制原则，但又通过允许普遍规避的延期规定将其否定；他对童工条款、夜班工作条款和利润分享规定提出了批评。他还指出，外国司法管辖权的存在使得普遍执法成为不可能，并提出了修改若干条款的建议。

清华大学陈达 (Chen Ta) 博士的一封信支持了他的立场，信中指出，将法律的适用推迟到8月1日并不影响法律的性质，除非采取行动，否则……（原文不清/残缺）……朱孟实 (M. T. Tchou) 先生和 C. H. Lowe 先生支持按现状适用法律。朱先生指出，该法律有许多缺陷，但也阐述了许多健全的原则。例如，该法律主张八小时原则，然后规定额外工作时间可达十小时，甚至更多加班时间。实际上，一个月中大部分时间每天工作11½小时是合法的——这一标准与 prevailing habit（现行习惯）几乎没有区别。然而，无论法律如何修改，在某些方面对其适用都会遇到阻力。他认为，在尝试评估中国的立法能力之前就要求修订法律，是一种挑战。Lowe 先生认为，该法律是中国在此问题上最好且唯一的成果，应努力毫不拖延地加以应用。此外，他觉得外交部应立即与外国政府进行谈判，以克服

辛德 (Hinder) 小姐指出，不同司法管辖权的存在造成了一种局面，值得会议关注。上海妇女组织联合委员会已经认识到，除非其他司法管辖区保持一致，否则在中国部分地区进行的任何监管尝试都可能落空。因此，该委员会已向实业部、上海公共租界工部局以及法公董局致函，邀请它们与其他当局寻求合作，以最终执行该法律。工部局已表示愿意在立法标准方向上与政府合作，并于2月13日公布了往来信函。实业部回复称，注意到工部局去函中提及，“若无其密切合作，我们的任务无法完成。”

认识到现有局势的实际性质，本次会议也可以挑战当局找到一种可行的合作行动方法。需要克服的一个非常现实的困难是各当局之间对法律概念的不同。要达到的标准是一回事；而要全面并最终实施的法律则是另一回事。

她提到了此前在上海规范童工的努力，并指出其失败或许是一件值得庆幸的事。如果由没有立法职能理事会的租界制定出一套工业法体系，那将是困难的。现在的情况更好，中国政府有了一部法律，外国行政机构可以逐渐融入其中。

对于是按现状适用现行法律还是进行修改，存在明显的意见分歧。预计随着调查结果委员会提出决议，将进一步展开有趣的讨论。

联合会条款

燕京大学的陈吉生 (Gideon Chen) 教授说，工会法中禁止市内同类工会组成联合会、仅允许小型“区联合会”的原则，排除了任何劳动力协调的可能性。朱孟实 (M. T. Tchou) 先生并未如此解释该法律。他假定在市范围内组成联合会是可能的。工会的地方和区级办事处均有权维护与雇主的协议。此外，法律中关于调解和仲裁的规定使工会效力降低，这些规定要求任何争议首先提交给工厂委员会，然后进行调解，接着进行仲裁，最后由所有相关工人进行投票表决。

Regulations For Settlement
Of Labour Disputes

History Of Development Of Industrial Arbitration
In Shanghai Is Traced By Official Of
Bureau Of Social Affairs

(Mr. Koo has been attached
to the Bureau of Social Affairs
in Shanghai in the capacity
of conciliator for a period of
three years. He analyzes very
clearly in this, the first part
of a paper he is presenting to
the Conference on the "Peo-
ple's Livelihood," the history
of efforts in this city toward
the elimination of strikes and
lockouts. It is a clear and
useful statement upon which
many business men and others
will desire to be informed.)
* * *
By KOO PING-YUEN
Since the "May 30th" case of
1925, industrial disputes in Shang-
hai have increased with the rapid
growth of unions, and become one
of China's most important social
problems. Shanghai is the great
industrial and commercial centre
of the country, and so industrial
disputes are no doubt more
numerous here. Thus some means
for the settlement of disputes have
been found urgent. Formerly in-
dustrial disputes were generally
settled either by joint meetings
of the employers and the em-
ployees, or by mediation of a
third party, such as police, Cham-
bers of Commerce, Guilds, Unions
and notable individuals. But upon
the arrival of the National
Revolutionary Army at this city
in spring of 1927, the Shanghai
Political Council soon saw itself
obliged to set up regular channels
for settling industrial disputes. As
a result, "Provisional Regulations
Governing the Board of Arbitra-
tion of Shanghai," consisting of
ten articles, were passed on
May 4, 1927, and another set
of regulations consisting of 20
articles was adopted during the
following week, entitled "Regula-
tions for the Settlement of Dis-
putes between Employees and
Shopkeepers." Although these re-
gulations were promulgated, the
Board was not at that time con-
vened.
Local Shanghai Regulations
These regulations were later
modified and put into effect on
August 18 of the same year by
the order of the Municipal Gov-
ernment of Greater Shanghai with
a new title of "The Provisional
Regulations concerning Concilia-
tion of Dispute between Labour
and Capital." Accordingly, a con-
ciliation board was formed in the
Shanghai General Chamber of
Commerce. It was composed of
13 members; five were chosen
from the labour unions to repre-
sent the workers, five from the
industrial or commercial estab-
lishment concerned, and three
from the Government to act as
disinterested parties and arbitra-
tors, of whom one must be sent
by the Special District Kuomin-
tang and one must be chairman.
Its chief duty was to settle all
disputes arising from the relations
between employees and employers
of any commercial or industrial
establishment located within the

解决劳资纠纷条例

社会局官员追溯上海工业仲裁的发展历史

（顾先生在上海社会局担任调解员已三年。在他提交给“民生”会议的一篇论文的第一部分中，他非常清晰地分析了本市为消除罢工和闭厂所作的努力的历史。这是一份清晰且有用的陈述，许多商人及其他人士都希望了解。）
* * *
作者：顾平远 (KOO PING-YUEN)

自1925年“五卅”案以来，随着工会的迅速增长，上海的劳资纠纷日益增多，并成为中国最重要的社会问题之一。上海是全国最大的工商业中心，因此这里的劳资纠纷无疑更为频繁。于是，寻找解决纠纷的手段变得刻不容缓。过去，劳资纠纷通常由雇主与雇员举行联席会议解决，或由第三方进行调解，如警察、商会、同业公会、工会及知名人士等。但是，1927年春国民革命军抵达本市后，上海政治委员会很快发现自己有义务建立解决劳资纠纷的正规渠道。结果，由十条组成的《上海仲裁会暂行条例》于1927年5月4日通过，随后的一周又通过了一套由二十条组成的条例，题为《解决雇员与店主之间纠纷条例》。虽然这些条例已经颁布，但当时并未召集仲裁会。

上海地方条例

这些条例后来经过修改，并于同年8月18日由大上海市政府命令生效，新标题为《劳资争议调解暂行条例》。据此，在上海总商会内成立了一个调解委员会。该委员会由13名成员组成；其中5人从工会中选出以代表工人，5人来自相关的工商业机构，3人来自政府作为无利害关系的各方及仲裁人，其中一人必须由特别区国民党派出，且一人必须担任主席。其主要职责是解决位于

Municipality of Greater Shanghai.
But, at that time there were other
agencies, such as military head-
quarters. Kuomintang, head-
quarters of labour unions, em-
ployers' associations, etc., assum-
ing to themselves the function of
mediation. This lack of uniformity
of procedure naturally resulted
in confusion, and the Conciliation
Board soon found that its
function could not be carried out
effectively. In the spring of 1928,
the Board was withdrawn by the
order of the Municipal Govern-
ment of Greater Shanghai, and its
functions were transferred to the
Bureau of Agriculture, Labour
and Commerce, which was later
reorganized into the present
Bureau of Social Affairs. Hence-
forth, the Bureau served as the
legal agency for mediation of
industrial disputes until the pro-
mulgation of the National Con-
ciliation and Arbitration Law.

National Laws Promulgated
The Law on the Settlement of
Disputes between Employers and
Employees was adopted and pro-
mulgated by the National Govern-
ment on June 9, 1928. According
to this law, industrial disputes are
to be settled by two government
agencies, namely the Committee
and the Board of Arbitration. The
former is composed of five or
seven members, two representa-
tives of each contending party and
one of three representatives of
the administrative authority who
act as umpires; while the latter
is composed of five members, one
representative of the Municipal
Government, one representative of
the Kuomintang headquarters, one
representative of the local law

court and one representative each
of employers and workers who are
not directly concerned in the dis-
pute. Conciliation may be request-
ed by one or both of the parties
or ordered by the administrative
authorities. Once the Arbitration
Board has given its award, this
latter becomes compulsory, having
the force of a labour contract.
This law was enforced as a proba-
tional measure for one year; its
jurisdiction was later extended for
nine months, and finally amended
on March 17, 1930. The amended
law differed from the original
largely in its application and the
effect of conciliation and arbitra-
tion. Before the law became ap-
plicable to all industrial and com-
mercial employees, it was limited
only to workers. Submission to
conciliation and arbitration be-
came compulsory but the accept-
ance of the verdict became volun-
tary. In case the arbitration fail-
ed to reach terms, it was provided
that the case should be referred
to the local law court for final
settlement. It is yet too early to
comment on the merit of the
amended law; but the original law
has proved a real service in the
settlement of hundreds of dis-
putes in Shanghai and it can now
be reviewed in the proper per-
spective.

(Mr. Koo's paper proceeds to
an interesting analysis of the
working of the original law, which
will appear in a later issue).

大上海市范围内的任何商业或工业机构的雇员与雇主之间产生的所有纠纷。
但是，当时还有其他机构，如军事指挥部、国民党、工会总部、雇主协会等，自行承担调解职能。这种程序上的不统一自然导致了混乱，调解委员会很快发现其职能无法有效履行。1928年春，根据大上海市政府的命令，该委员会被撤销，其职能移交给农工商局，该局后来重组为现在的社会局。此后，该局一直作为调解劳资纠纷的法定机构，直到《全国调解仲裁法》颁布。

国家法律颁布

国民政府于1928年6月9日通过并颁布了《解决雇主与雇员之间纠纷法》。根据该法，劳资纠纷由两个政府机构解决，即委员会和仲裁局。前者由五名或七名成员组成，争端双方各两名代表，以及行政当局的三名代表中的一名担任公断人；后者由五名成员组成，包括市政府代表一名、国民党总部代表一名、地方法院代表一名，以及与纠纷无直接关系的雇主和工人代表各一名。一方或双方均可请求调解，也可由行政当局命令调解。一旦仲裁局作出裁决，该裁决即具有强制性，拥有劳工合同的效力。
该法律作为试行措施实施了一年；其管辖权后来延长了九个月，并最终于1930年3月17日修订。修订后的法律与原法主要在适用范围以及调解和仲裁的效力方面有所不同。在该法适用于所有工商业雇员之前，它仅限于工人。提交调解和仲裁成为强制性的，但接受裁决则是自愿的。如果仲裁未能达成条款，规定应将案件提交地方法院进行最终解决。现在评论修订后法律的优劣还为时过早；但原法已被证明在解决上海数百起纠纷方面发挥了真正的作用，现在可以从适当的角度对其进行回顾。

（顾先生的论文接着对原法的运作进行了有趣的分析，将在后续期刊中刊登）。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, FEBRUARY 23, 1931

FACTORY LAWS OF CHINA
Application A Question of Considerable
Difficulty: Analysis by Expert
BY COL. M. T. TCHOU

This forms part of one of the papers being presented to the Conference on the People's Livelihood whose sessions began yesterday. Colonel Tchou was for some time head of the Department of Labour in the Ministry for Industry, and represented China at the International Labour Conference in Geneva upon two occasions. Col. Tchou analyses in his paper the provisions of the Law on the Settlement of Disputes, the Labour Union Law, the Factory Law, and the Law on Factory Inspection. He then proceeds to examine the all important question of the Administration of these laws.

In Western countries the administration of labour laws has been an arduous task; it is no less difficult in China, if not more so. Industries that have had a free hand in dealing with labour do not like to be harnessed. Already great doubt and opposition have been expressed by numerous leaders of industry. Some freely state that the Factory Law is too advanced and is impossible of enforcement, while others assert that if it is enforced, they would be forced to close their factories, thus throwing thousands of workers out of employment. At the same time some foreign papers have raised the question of China's ability to enforce the law in certain foreign-owned and managed factories, seeing that they still enjoy extraterritorial privileges. A group of Chinese employers also declared that it would be unfair to enforce the law in Chinese factories when it is not enforced in some of the important foreign factories. From this it can be seen that the application of labour laws in China is going to be a question of considerable difficulty, which will challenge the power of organization and execution of the present Government to no small degree.

At the beginning of this discussion it may be useful to review the present machinery of labour administration in China. At the Central Government there is the Ministry of Industries, which has a Department of Labour to deal with matters concerning labour. In the provinces this work usually devolves upon the Bureau of Reconstruction; but matters relating to labour disputes are dealt with by the Bureau of Civil Affairs—this being a peculiarity which was the result of circumstances. In the large cities which have special municipalities, such as Shanghai, Tientsin, Canton, Wuhan, Peking and Nanking, where a large proportion of modern industries of the country is located, there is usually the Bureau of Social Affairs, which is in charge of affairs relating to industry, commerce, labour and other social matters. In the past there has been some difficulty in securing general execution of the orders of the Central Government, owing to sectional political developments and to the lack of trained personnel and of clearly defined functions of the different bureaux in the provincial and special municipal governments. But gradually this difficulty is being overcome as more experience is acquired, and as the country becomes more unified the municipal bureaux have generally proved more effective than provincial bureaux. In other countries the administration of labour affairs is now usually undertaken by government organs specially set up for the purpose as distinct branches of the machinery of government. As modern industry develops in China, probably such machinery will have to be created too.

Party Shoulders Responsibility

At this point it should be pointed out that during the past few years affairs relating to labour organizations have been largely handled by the local and central organs of the Kuomintang, as during this period the direction and supervision of popular organizations have been taken out of the hands of the party, which has set up national and local agencies for the purpose. How long this will remain the case can only be determined by the Party itself. As a consequence of this situation, the responsibility for the enforcement of the Labour Union Law, according to which all unions already in existence will have to be recognized in the near future, will be largely shouldered by the Party, while it is also required that the unions emerging from this process will have to be registered with the local government.

The administration of the Law on the Settlement of Disputes between the Employers and Employees has in the past largely been undertaken by the local and national administrative organs, while the Party also participated to a certain extent, especially in the composition of the Arbitration Boards. Although there had been some irregularities in the application of this Law, the results have generally proved satisfactory. In some instances, where foreign employers were concerned, the application of this law was at first ineffective, as employers enjoying extraterritorial privileges often refused to send representatives to Conciliation Boards, when they were called by Chinese authorities. 《字林西报》，1931年2月23日，星期一

中国的工厂法
适用是一个相当困难的问题：专家分析
作者：M. T. 朱上校 (COL. M. T. TCHOU)

这是提交给昨天开幕的“民生”会议的论文之一的一部分。朱上校曾一度担任实业部劳工司司长，并曾两次代表中国出席在日内瓦举行的国际劳工会议。朱上校在其论文中分析了《解决纠纷法》、《工会法》、《工厂法》和《工厂检查法》的规定。然后，他着手考察这些法律的管理这一至关重要的问题。

在西方国家，劳动法的管理一直是一项艰巨的任务；在中国，这项任务同样困难，甚至更甚。那些在对待劳工方面拥有自由裁量权的工业界不喜欢受到束缚。许多工业领袖已经表达了巨大的怀疑和反对。有些人直言不讳地表示，《工厂法》过于超前，无法执行，而另一些人则断言，如果执行该法，他们将被迫关闭工厂，从而使成千上万的工人失业。同时，一些外国报纸提出了中国在某些外资经营管理的工厂中执行法律的能力问题，鉴于这些工厂仍然享有治外法权特权。一群中国雇主也宣称，如果在一些重要的外国工厂中不执行该法，而仅在中国工厂中执行，那将是不公平的。由此可见，在中国适用劳动法将是一个相当困难的问题，这在很大程度上将挑战现政府的组织和执行能力。

在开始讨论这一点时，回顾一下中国目前的劳工管理机构可能是有益的。在中央政府层面，有实业部，下设劳工司处理有关劳工的事务。在各省，这项工作通常由建设厅负责；但与劳资纠纷有关的事务则由民政厅处理——这是由于特殊情况造成的一种特殊性。在拥有特别市建制的大城市，如上海、天津、广州、武汉、北京和南京，全国现代工业的大部分都位于这些地方，通常设有社会局，负责管理有关工业、商业、劳工和其他社会事务。过去，由于派系政治的发展，以及省和特别市政府中各局缺乏受过训练的人员和职能界定不清，中央政府的命令难以得到普遍执行。但随着经验的积累和国家日益统一，这一困难正逐渐克服，市级局通常被证明比省级局更有效。在其他国家，劳工事务的管理现在通常由专门为此目的设立的政府机构承担，作为政府机器中独立的分支。随着中国现代工业的发展，可能也需要建立这样的机构。

党承担责任

在此需要指出的是，在过去几年中，与劳工组织有关的事务主要由国民党的地方和中央机关处理，因为在此期间，民众组织的指导和监督已从党手中移出，党为此设立了国家和地方机构。这种情况会持续多久，只能由党自己决定。由于这种情况，根据《工会法》（该法规定所有现有工会在不久的将来都必须得到承认），执行该法的责任将主要由党承担，同时也要求由此过程产生的工会必须在当地政府注册。

《解决雇主与雇员之间纠纷法》的管理在过去主要由地方和国家行政机关承担，党也在一定程度上参与，特别是在仲裁局的组成方面。虽然在该法的适用中存在一些不规范之处，但结果总体上是令人满意的。在一些涉及外国雇主的案例中，该法的适用起初无效，因为享有治外法权特权的雇主经常拒绝在中国当局传唤时派遣代表参加调解委员会。然而-

ever, in several cases these employers later saw themselves obliged to respond, in order to overcome the difficulties involved in the disputes with their Chinese employees, and to their surprise found the law helpful. As a result of this, foreign factories situated in territories administered by China seem now to be more inclined to apply this particular law. The situation in foreign administered settlements and concessions, however, has not shown so distinctly such a tendency at present, but it should be obvious that the application of the law here too would prove helpful.

The Principal Problem

For the present, however, the problem of administration centres chiefly around the Factory Law. By its very nature, the law requires the employers to conform to new standards. In all countries, employers generally took an attitude of doubt and aversion towards such measures when first applied and their enforcement required great determination on the part of the government. Organised labour too usually saw to it that the government not only introduced certain minimum reforms by legislation, but also insisted upon their being carried out by some kind of supervisory organ, such as a labour inspectorate. In China organized labour has on a number of occasions made exhorbitant demands; the provisions of the Factory Law naturally fall short of their hopes. But even if this law is not applied, the disappointment will be keen and the reaction will be undesirable.

Apart from the question of certain foreign factories which will probably soon come under Chinese jurisdiction when extraterritoriality is abolished, the question centres on the determination of the Government to apply all its labour laws and the establishment of an efficient factory inspectorate. We do not need to discuss the determination of the Government here; we may dwell a moment on the establishment of the factory inspectorate.

Regional Basis of Inspection

According to the Law on Factory Inspection, the proper authority in a municipality is the municipal government, and in the district (hsien) is the district government. While it is true the inspectors may be selected and trained by the Central Government, it is difficult to see how, except in large special municipalities, the local governments can maintain an efficient factory inspection and enforce the law in a uniform manner, considering the infantile state of the administration of labour affairs in secondary cities and small towns in China. Experience in most Western countries has pointed to the desirability of having factory or labour inspection organized on a national basis. Considering the need of the situation in China, it should at least be organized on a regional basis, if not on a national basis, which is really preferable. There are many economic as well as social arguments in support of this theory. Readers are referred to the recommendations of the 5th Session of the International Labour Conference, which laid down in a clear manner the tried principles governing the organization of factory or labour inspectorates. It is to be hoped that before long China will adopt these principles and make the administration of her labour laws uniformly effective throughout the country.

As to the need of officials of a high grade of moral character as labour administrators and inspectors, too much stress cannot be laid on careful choice and training. Men and women qualified to serve are not only to have the technical preparations that are indispensable but must be devoted to their cause and be willing to sacrifice for it. This I believe is the greatest need in the administration of labour affairs in China today. May we have such men and women in increasing numbers, and may this conference help call forth more of them.

然而，在若干案例中，这些雇主后来发现自己不得不作出回应，以克服在与华籍雇员发生纠纷时所涉及的困难，并且令他们惊讶的是，他们发现法律颇有助益。因此，位于中国管辖领土内的外资工厂目前似乎更倾向于适用这部特定法律。然而，在外人管理的租界和居留地，目前尚未如此明显地显示出这种倾向，但显而易见的是，在此等地适用该法律同样会被证明是有益的。

主要问题

然而就目前而言，行政问题主要围绕《工厂法》展开。就其性质而言，该法要求雇主遵守新的标准。在所有国家，雇主在此类措施初次实施时通常持怀疑和厌恶态度，而其强制执行则需要政府方面具备极大的决心。有组织的劳工也通常确保政府不仅通过立法引入某些最低限度的改革，而且坚持由某种监督机构（如劳工视察处）来执行这些改革。在中国，有组织的劳工曾多次提出过分的要求；《工厂法》的条款自然未能满足他们的期望。但是，即使不实施该法，失望之情也会十分强烈，反应也将是不利的。

除了某些外国工厂的问题——随着治外法权的废除，这些工厂可能很快将受中国管辖——问题的核心在于政府执行其所有劳动法的决心，以及建立一个高效的工厂视察制度。我们无需在此讨论政府的决心；我们可以稍加探讨工厂视察制度的建立。

视察的区域基础

根据《工厂视察法》，市级的主管机关为市政府，县级（hsien）的主管机关为县政府。虽然视察员可由中央政府选拔和培训，但鉴于中国次要城市和小城镇的劳工事务管理尚处于幼稚状态，除大型特别市外，很难看出地方政府如何能维持高效的工厂视察并以统一方式执法。大多数西方国家的经验表明，工厂或劳工视察最好在全国基础上进行组织。考虑到中国的局势需要，至少应在区域基础上进行组织，如果不在全国基础上组织的话，而后者确实是更可取的。有许多经济和社会方面的论据支持这一理论。读者可参考国际劳工大会第五届会议的建议，该会议清晰地规定了经过检验的、指导工厂或劳工视察处组织工作的原则。希望中国不久后将采纳这些原则，使其劳动法的行政管理在全国范围内统一有效。

至于作为劳工行政人员和视察员的高级官员需要具备高尚的道德品质，这一点再怎么强调慎重选择和培训的重要性也不为过。有资格担任此职的男女不仅必须具备不可或缺的技术准备，还必须致力于他们的事业并愿意为此牺牲。我相信这是当今中国劳工事务管理中最大的需求。愿此类男女日益增多，愿本次大会有助于唤起更多这样的人才。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, FEBRUARY 8, 1931

Business And Factory Men
Here Discuss Merits Of
Factory Law In Meeting

Gathering Promised Attempt Will Be Made
To Amend Ruling In Case Of Extreme
Difficulty; Hundred Attend

Considerable discussion on the new Factory Law was held yesterday at the first regular meeting of the Shanghai Association of Scientific Management which took the form of a tiffin party at the Union Club.

The meeting was presided over by Dr. H. H. Kung, Minister of Industry, and attended by about 100 members including many prominent bankers, manufacturers, proprietors and managers of various mills and silk filatures.

The gathering exchanged views regarding business and factory managements, while doubtful points of the new law were also discussed, and explanation was given by officials who were present. After lengthy discussion, decision was reached that in case of extreme difficulty being experienced after the enforcement, now postponed to August 1 this year, amendment to the new law will be sought.

The Factory Law was promulgated by the National Government December 30, 1929, after prolonged deliberation by labor experts. While the Government claims that care has been exercised to meet the needs of the situation in China, and that protection has been furnished to human rights in industry, capitalists express their doubt as to the applicability of the new law. The law which should be enforced on February 1, 1931, was finally postponed until August 1.

At yesterday's meeting the view was expressed by the officials that it is inevitable that difficulty is met in carrying out any new law promulgated by the Government. But, they continued, by putting into trial and careful application this difficulty can soon be overcome and removed.

商界与工厂界人士
在此次会议上讨论
《工厂法》的优点

集会承诺将在极端
困难情况下尝试修正
规定；百人出席

昨日，在上海科学管理协会的第一次例行会议上，就新《工厂法》进行了相当热烈的讨论，会议以在联合俱乐部（Union Club）举行的午餐会形式进行。

会议由实业部部长孔祥熙博士主持，约有100名会员出席，其中包括许多知名银行家、制造商、各家纱厂和缫丝厂的业主及经理。

与会者就商业和工厂管理交换了意见，同时也讨论了新法中的疑点，并由在场官员作了解释。经过长时间讨论，决定若在今年8月1日（现推迟至此日期）实施后遇到极大困难，将寻求对新法进行修正。

《工厂法》经劳工专家长期审议后，由国民政府于1929年12月30日公布。虽然政府声称已谨慎行事以满足中国局势的需要，并为工业中的人权提供了保护，但资本家对新法的适用性表示怀疑。原定于1931年2月1日实施的该法，最终被推迟至8月1日。

在昨日的会议上，官员们表示，在执行政府颁布的任何新法时遇到困难是不可避免的。但他们接着说，通过试行和谨慎应用，这种困难可以很快被克服和消除。

CHINA'S LABOUR
LAWS
Peking Merchants Con-
sider Them Unsuitable

N.C.S.N. SPECIAL SERVICE
Peking, Jan. 31.
China's new factory law, which
is considerably more liberal than
the labour regulations of the most
advanced Occidental states, is en-
tirely unsuited to this country and
can not be enforced, in the opinion
of manufacturers here.
The government at Nanking re-
cently announced that this law
would come into effect on February
1, then agreed to postpone enforce-
ment until August 1, but critics
here point out that as no personnel
has been trained for factory in-
spection work and as the economic
conditions of China are completely
opposed to such drastic changes, the
law must remain a dead letter.
For example, a member of the
board of the International League
for the Prevention of Blindness in
China has issued a statement de-
claring that hundreds of child work-
ers are becoming blind every year
because they are fed exclusively on
steamed bread and salted turnips,
which are deficient in vitamin A. A
law insisting that employers should
feed their child apprentices fresh
cabbages, or one egg a day in win-
ter, or some such equivalent diet,
would prevent the disease, which
causes so many cases of blindness in
Chinese child workers.
While such conditions as these
are prevalent, while there is no
birth registration in this country
to determine childrens' ages, and
no schools to accommodate those
who are now employed in factories,
the idealistic legislators at Nanking
nevertheless have passed a law
establishing the eight hour day,
elimination of child labour, exclu-
sion of women from night work,
employers liability for sickness or
injury, equal pay for men and wo-
men labourers, unemployment com-
pensation, etc., etc.
Social workers and others who
sincerely desire to improve labour
conditions here are expressing their
regret that the government should
have adopted such Utopian regula-
tions instead of a few simple rules
which might make a genuine start
toward factory improvement in
China.
They also point out that a non-
enforceable statute gives oppor-
tunity for extortion and blackmail
to unscrupulous local officials, while
doing nothing to extinguish the
worst features of present day fac-
tory life in China.—United Press.

中国的劳工
法律
北京商人认
为不适用

N.C.S.N. 特约服务
北京，1月31日。
这里的制造商认为，中国的新工厂法比最先进的西方国家的劳工法规要宽松得多，完全不适合本国国情，无法执行。
南京政府最近宣布该法将于2月1日生效，随后同意将实施推迟至8月1日，但这里的批评人士指出，由于没有为工厂视察工作培训人员，且中国的经济状况与如此剧烈的变革完全相悖，该法必将是一纸空文。
例如，中国防盲国际联盟董事会的一名成员发表声明称，每年有数百名童工失明，因为他们只吃馒头和咸萝卜，这些食物缺乏维生素A。一部坚持要求雇主为其童工学徒提供新鲜卷心菜，或在冬季每天提供一个鸡蛋，或类似等价饮食的法律，将能预防这种导致中国童工大量失明的疾病。
尽管此类情况普遍存在，尽管本国没有出生登记来确定儿童年龄，也没有学校来容纳目前在工厂就业的儿童，南京那些理想主义的立法者仍然通过了一部确立八小时工作制、废除童工、禁止妇女从事夜间工作、雇主对疾病或伤害承担责任、男女劳工同工同酬、失业补偿等等的法律。
真诚希望改善此处劳工条件的社会工作者和其他人士对政府采取此类乌托邦式的规章，而不是采取几条简单的规则以真正开始改善中国的工厂状况，表示遗憾。
他们还指出，一部无法执行的法律为无良地方官员提供了敲诈勒索的机会，同时对消除当前中国工厂生活中最恶劣的特征毫无作用。——合众社。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 4, 1931

SHANGHAI MUNICIPALITY
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. 5292
Date 5 - 2 - 31

FACTORY INSPECTION
Analysis of Text of New Ordinances
Issued by Nanking

BY ELEANOR M. HINDER

The Chinese press on February 2 carried the full text of 20 ordinances which have passed the Legislative Yuan governing the appointment and duties of factory inspectors. It will be remembered that the Chinese Government announced in December last that its Factory law would become operative on February 1, 1931, and simultaneously regulations for the administration of the law were published.

No mention was made in these of provision for inspection but, the duty was laid upon local authorities to carry out the law. It was known, however, that the question of inspection had been in the thought of the Ministry, and the ordinances which have now appeared provide the machinery for the actual carrying out of the Law. The postponement of the date of application until August 1, 1931, coupled with the authorization of inspection, gives to administrative authorities sufficient time to prepare for enforcement. From the point of view of the adjustments necessary for large factories and mills, in the purchase of additional equipment, in the financial problems involved, and in facing changed marketing conditions, six months is too short a time. But if wisely used, the period will prove of great use in planning for wise procedure on the part of those upon whom will fall the duty of enforcing law.

From other recent publicity it would seem that it is the intention of the Chinese Government to place the responsibility for the administration of the Factory Law upon "local authorities"—municipal authorities in municipalities, and district authorities in districts. It is presumed that Bureaux of Social Affairs will be specially charged with this duty; and it is further assumed that this should involve bringing action for infraction into the courts where necessary. But the actual factory inspection, the instrument by which the local authorities can find out whether the law is being observed, will be in the hands of inspectors under the Central Labour Administration Organ —the Ministry of Industry. It is presumed that inspectors must then be assigned to cities and districts to work with the local authorities, for "inspectors are under the authority of the Central Labour Administrative Organ and must go where they are assigned to make regular and special inspections."

Responsibility for training these inspectors will rest with the Central Organ. They must be chosen from those who have graduated from "special industrial schools" or who have other skill and knowledge, or have worked in factories for ten years.

ity extends merely to inspection: for example, if there is contravention of the article which provides that if the health and safety provision of the factory are inadequate the proper authority may require improvements within a time limit— the inspector "must report to the authority in charge for action." However, a certain amount of power for action is placed in his hands, for he may issue instructions if the safety and health conditions call for immediate improvement: if orders are not obeyed, he must report to the proper authority for action. He may ask for assistance from the administrative organ of the government or of the police when he needs it.

The inspector must produce evidence of his identity when desiring to enter a factory. Thereafter he has a right to question clerical workers, manual workers, or labour union officers: and he has right to inspect all records which the law states shall be kept. Factories which refuse entry to an inspector are liable to fine up to $200, and those refusing reasonable information may be fined up to $100.

It is apparent that inspectors will be used for the gathering of statistical information which is usually obtained by routine report channels in other countries. It is expected of them that they shall submit quarterly reports covering statistics of factories and workers in different industries, working hours in every factory, conditions with regard to child labour, safety and health provisions, accidents and illness, and labour turnover. This may be regarded as an excellent approach to the whole question of the gathering of accurate facts.

Penalties Provided

A factory inspector shall not take bribes, or write false reports: shall not reveal secrets of industrial processes: shall not create bad feeling between workers and management: or occupy simultaneously other official position or engage in business. For any of these offences he may be punished, and shall, if the offence is criminal, appear in court.

In general the provisions cover well the work which it is apparently proposed the inspector shall do. A date for the enforcement of these clauses will be announced. With the responsibility for administration remaining in the hands of the local authority, the duty of prosecution probably remains there also. In Western countries, factory inspectors have this power. In initial stages of the implementing of a law which may give room for differences in interpretation, the provision of an inspecting staff which is largely a reporting agency is wise. Here in China as elsewhere, the inspector may become useful both to employer and to worker: he can, if he is wise, establish good relations with each. The announcement of this law marks an important step toward the much-to-be-desired goal of regulation of industrial employment.

刑事侦缉处登记室
第5292号
日期 31年2月5日

工厂视察
南京颁布的新条例文本分析

作者：埃莉诺·M·辛德（Eleanor M. Hinder）

2月2日，中文报纸刊登了由立法院通过的关于工厂视察员任命及职责的20项条例全文。人们还记得，中国政府于去年12月宣布，其《工厂法》将于1931年2月1日生效，并同时公布了该法的施行细则。

这些细则中未提及视察 provisions，但规定地方当局有责任执行该法律。然而，众所周知，部里一直在考虑视察问题，而现已公布的条例为实际执行该法提供了机制。将实施日期推迟至1931年8月1日，加上授权进行视察，使行政当局有足够的时间准备执法工作。从大型工厂和纱厂所需调整的角度来看，无论是购买额外设备、解决相关的财务问题，还是应对变化的市场条件，六个月的时间都太短了。但如果能明智地利用这段时间，对于承担执法责任的那些人来说，在规划明智的行动方案方面将证明大有裨益。

从其他最近的公开信息来看，中国政府似乎打算将《工厂法》的管理责任交给“地方当局”——即市级行政区域内的市政当局，以及县级行政区域内的区县政府。据推测，社会局将专门负责此项职责；并进一步假定，这将涉及在必要时向法院提起违规诉讼。但是，实际的工厂视察——即地方当局用以查明法律是否得到遵守的手段——将由中央劳工行政机关——实业部——下属的视察员掌握。据推测，视察员随后必须被派往各城市和地区，与地方当局协同工作，因为“视察员受中央劳工行政机关管辖，必须前往指派地点进行定期和特别视察。”

培训这些视察员的责任将由中央机关承担。他们必须从“专门工业学校”的毕业生中选拔，或者具备其他技能和知识，或在工厂工作过十年的人员中选拔。

[原文此处有缺漏或排版错误，接下文] 权仅限于视察：例如，如果违反了有关条款，即若工厂的健康和安全设施不足，主管当局可要求在限期内改进——视察员“必须向主管当局报告以采取行动”。然而，他手中拥有一定的行动权力，因为如果安全和健康状况需要立即改善，他可以发出指令：如果命令未被遵守，他必须向主管当局报告以采取行动。当他需要时，可以向政府或警察的行政机关请求协助。

视察员在进入工厂时必须出示身份证明。此后，他有权询问职员、体力劳动者或工会干部：并有权检查法律规定必须保存的所有记录。拒绝视察员进入的工厂可能被处以最高200元的罚款，拒绝提供合理信息的工厂可能被处以最高100元的罚款。

显然，视察员将被用于收集统计信息，而这些信息在其他国家通常通过常规报告渠道获得。预计他们将提交季度报告，涵盖不同行业的工厂和工人统计数据、每个工厂的工作时间、童工状况、安全和卫生设施、事故和疾病情况，以及劳动力流动情况。这可以被视为收集准确事实整个问题的一个极佳途径。

规定的处罚

工厂视察员不得受贿，或撰写虚假报告：不得泄露工业流程的秘密：不得在工人和管理层之间制造不良情绪：或同时担任其他公职或从事商业活动。如有任何上述违规行为，他将受到惩罚，如果该行为构成犯罪，则须出庭受审。

总体而言，这些规定很好地涵盖了显然拟议由视察员执行的工作。这些条款的执行日期将会公布。由于管理责任仍留在地方当局手中，起诉的责任可能也留在那里。在西方国家，工厂视察员拥有这种权力。在实施一部可能在解释上存在差异的法律的初始阶段，设立一个主要作为报告机构的视察人员队伍是明智之举。在中国这里，如同在其他地方一样，视察员可能对雇主和工人都有用：如果他明智的话，可以与双方建立良好的关系。这部法律的颁布标志着朝着令人渴望的规范工业就业目标迈出了重要一步。

（批注：归档。请附卷宗。M. 31年2月4日。）

（批：ARCHIVES / J. REGISTRY / 5492 / 6. - 2. - 31.）

FACTORY LAWS DISCUSSED
Debate in Labour Forum Airs Problems of New Regulations

The Shanghai Labour Forum yesterday lived up to its name. It was the ground for the most animated discussion upon the subject of the new Factory Law which the National Government has decreed will be effective February 1. Lawyers; factory owners; "labour bosses"; social workers; professors; officials present in an unofficial capacity; "general public" who had no particular responsibility in relation to the situation created, but whose interest in a matter of vital importance to the community brought them to the forum. The frankness of the exchange of opinion proved the necessity and the value of the continuation of this Forum.

The issue was narrowed by the chairman to the problems involved in the application of the law: not, as he stated, the existence of the law itself, or the individual clauses of it. Yet it proved impossible to discuss the problems involved in enforcement without consideration of the contents; for this obviously creates the problems.

An opening argument sought to show that from a production point of view alone, quite apart from additional expenditures involved, immediate and total application of the law would be impossible for industry itself. Based upon the existing 22 hours working day of two shifts, with two rest days per month, and allowing the time lost for holidays at the present time, the total working hours per machine per year in a cotton mill at the present rate is 7,216. Upon the new basis, when women may work from 6 a.m. till 10 p.m. in shifts to conform to the hours clauses, there are 96 working hours per machine per working week of six days. Allowing the minimum annual leave, and the eight statutory holidays, there are 15 days per year when the machine does not work its 16 hours. The total annual work will then be 4,772 hours. This would involve a reduction of 2,444 working hours per machine per year; approximately one third. What industry can stand such adjustment and live? The present situation should change, and change should begin now; but how can this so large immediate adjustment be made?

Difficulty of Replacement

The argument was put forward that nowhere in the law is it stated that the machines cannot work 24 hours a day: three shifts can be worked, and successfully, as has been shown by the introduction of three eight hour shifts by a Tientsin cotton mill, it was stated. It was assumed in argument that a third shift composed of men workers could be introduced into the cotton mills, since women are forbidden to work the third shift from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. A factory owner present stated that this was impossible: it would take a long period of training to teach men the work now performed by women.

The statement was made that it was believed the National Government had not gone into this legislation without due knowledge of the consequences. That it was assured, in other words, that there was ability on the part of industry to stand it. Indeed, as far back as 1927, the government had sought the advice and consultation of bankers and industrialists as to the content of a factory law. It seemed to be the opinion of one member of the group that there had been insufficient consultation; but it was declared upon accurate knowledge by others that this conferring had taken place. Nowhere in the world, it was stated, did industrial legislation come into being without protest. Sometimes it was from the workers group if they were not sufficiently enlightened to know the value of the limitations put upon their work; more often from employers whose self-interest was at stake. What was important at this time was an attitude of goodwill on the part of employers. It should be realized that lack of regulation worked against industries themselves. China's labour was generally said to be less effective than some other labour in the world; and one of the reasons for this might well be the long hours of work and poor wages which made the worker a less alert operative. The law as proposed was revolutionary; there would be few who would deny it. But in every country legislation had cost, and China must be prepared to pay the cost.

Value of Goodwill

To this it was answered that in the face of economic facts, goodwill mattered little. There was scarcely a Chinese cotton mill which had earned dividends during the past five years. Three had already gone out of existence within the past few months; one on the 25th of this month. When asked if this was due to the factory law, the reply was that obviously it was not; but if the industry was unable to stand up to competition under a system of no regulation, it would be manifestly impossible for it to do so when limitations were put upon its earning power. One opinion was expressed that there were certainly some cotton mills which had earned money last year: would they be able to meet the increased productions costs? Had any accurate figures yet been obtained? One manager stated that his mill was now running at a loss of Taels 15,000 to Taels 20,000 a month; it was goodwill toward the 4,600 workers involved that had not shut it down before; but it would certainly not be possible to add to this burden of loss.

A question was asked whether there was an inspectorate ready for the enforcement of this law: to this no answer was forthcoming. It was stated that two courses were open for the administration—through the present bureaucratic system of municipal governments, or through the establishment of special inspectorates. If the latter were not available, the former could, as an emergency measure, adhere to the National Government decree, and begin to put the law into effect as from the date proclaimed. Already groups of employers had been gathered by the Bureau of Social Affairs of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai, and discussion were proceeding as to the application of the law. How far the law will succeed, it was stated, depends upon the strength of the governmental organ and the goodwill of employers.

Place of Regulation

The statement was then made that the law was not built upon a framework of public opinion with regard to it. That the workers themselves would be the first to resent the limitations placed upon them in the matter of earnings at first. To this those in close touch with labour made the reply that for several years in the Party programme there had been proceeding education aimed at an understanding of what legal regulation meant. Workers in Shanghai, Tientsin, Canton, were fully aware of the place of regulation: it was believed that there would be welcome on the part of the more enlightened of them. Though Chinese labour was illiterate, it was not uninformed. The Government did not at any rate expect difficulty with workers, it was stated; and it was also sure of the goodwill of many employers. It was pointed out that at the present time there was a delegation in Nanking led by a prominent industrialist, pointing out to the government that the inability of industry to stand wholesale application would have its effect upon the whole programme of economic reconstruction for China; and incidentally upon the government's taxation.

Reverting to the question of output, it was stated that frequently there had been increase in output following reduction in hours. To this it was answered that it was upon the most carefully prepared plans, not with only five weeks notice. The point was made too that where output was largely controlled by the machine, and was automatic, shortening of hours did not produce such increased return.

A vital point in the discussion was reached when a lawyer asked whether, since from a practical standpoint application could only begin on February 1 and would take a long time to complete, the law would be applied in the courts if it were invoked. It was apparent that a real difficulty was here involved. It is one thing to have a set of regulations declared as governmental policy, and to set a Bureau to the task of educating a public to carrying them out—a long process evidently. It was quite another thing when this standard had legal status, and could be invoked in court. This was recognized even by those who believed that there was value in the declaration that the whole law was not in force, as being a difficulty.

It is obvious from the discussion that it is not expected by anyone that the impossible can happen: one sentiment favours however a gradual set application, clause by clause, will the whole is accomplished; another approach is that the whole law should be announced as in force, and within the succeeding years, little by little, factories should come to meet the ideal.

It is proposed to carry the discussion of the law and its problems further at a later date. The Forum is likely to be an interesting place for some time to come.

（签名：Rogers / Magoon / Mercer / ...）

《华北每日新闻》- 1931年1月31日。
（批注：档案 / J. 登记处 / 5492 / 6. - 2. - 31.）

讨论工厂法
劳工论坛辩论新法规之问题

上海劳工论坛昨日可谓名副其实。它成为就国民政府颁布将于2月1日生效的新《工厂法》这一主题进行最热烈讨论的场所。律师、工厂主、“包工头”、社会工作者、教授、以非官方身份出席的官员，以及虽对由此造成的局势没有特定责任、但因关心这一对社区至关重要的事项而来到论坛的“普通公众”，均出席了会议。意见交换的坦率证明了继续举办该论坛的必要性和价值。

主席将议题缩小为法律适用所涉及的问题：正如他所陈述的，并非法律本身的存在或其个别条款。然而，事实证明，在不考虑法律内容的情况下，不可能讨论执法所涉及的问题；因为内容显然造成了这些问题。

开场论点试图表明，仅从生产角度来看，且不涉及额外支出，立即全面实施该法律对工业界本身来说是不可能的。基于目前两班倒、每月休息两天的22小时工作制，并扣除目前的节假日损失时间，目前棉纺厂每台机器每年的总工作时间为7,216小时。在新的基础上，为了符合工时条款，妇女可轮班从上午6点工作至晚上10点，在六天工作周内，每台机器的工作时间为96小时。扣除最低年假和八个法定假日，每年有15天机器不运行其16个小时。因此，年总工作量将为4,772小时。这将导致每台机器每年减少2,444个工作小时；约为三分之一。哪家工业能承受这样的调整并生存下去？现状应该改变，且改变应从现在开始；但如何进行如此巨大的即时调整呢？

替换之困难

有人提出论点称，法律中任何地方都没有规定机器不能每天24小时运转：可以实行三班倒，而且正如天津一家棉纺厂引入三个八小时班次所证明的那样，这是成功的。辩论中假设，可以在棉纺厂引入由男工组成的第三班，因为禁止妇女在晚上10点至早上6点的第三班工作。一位在场的工厂主表示，这是不可能的：教导男性从事目前由女性完成的工作需要很长的培训期。

有人陈述道，相信国民政府在制定这项立法时并非没有充分考虑其后果。换言之，确信工业界有能力承受这一影响。事实上，早在1927年，政府就曾就工厂法的内容征求银行家和实业家的意见和咨询。小组中一名成员似乎认为协商不足；但其他人根据确切知识宣称，这种磋商确实发生过。据称，世界上没有任何地方的工业立法是在没有抗议的情况下产生的。有时抗议来自工人群体，如果他们不够开明，无法了解对其工作施加限制的价值；更多时候则来自利益攸关的雇主。此时重要的是雇主方面的善意态度。应当认识到，缺乏监管对工业界自身不利。据说，中国劳工的效率普遍低于世界其他一些地区的劳工；造成这种情况的原因之一很可能是长时间工作和低工资，这使得工人作为操作员时警觉性较低。拟议中的法律具有革命性；很少有人会否认这一点。但在每个国家，立法都有成本，中国必须准备好付出代价。

善意的价值

对此的回答是，面对经济事实，善意几乎无足轻重。在过去五年中，几乎没有一家中国棉纺厂赚取过红利。过去几个月内已有三家倒闭；其中一家于本月25日倒闭。当被问及这是否归因于工厂法时，回答是显然不是；但是，如果工业界在无监管体系下无法经受竞争，那么当其盈利能力受到限制时，显然更不可能做到。有一种观点认为，去年肯定有一些棉纺厂赚了钱：它们能否应对增加的生产成本？是否已经获得了准确的数据？一位经理表示，他的工厂目前每月亏损15,000至20,000两白银；正是出于对涉及的4,600名工人的善意，才没有在此之前关闭工厂；但肯定不可能再增加这一亏损负担。

有人提问，是否有现成的监察机构来执行这项法律：对此没有得到答复。据称，行政当局有两种途径可选——通过现有的市政府官僚体系，或通过建立专门的监察机构。如果后者不可用，前者可以作为紧急措施，遵循国民政府的法令，并从公布之日起开始实施该法律。大上海市政府社会局已经召集了雇主团体，正在就法律的适用进行讨论。据称，法律能在多大程度上成功，取决于政府机构的力度和雇主的善意。

监管的地位

随后有人陈述，该法律的建立并未基于针对它的公众舆论框架。工人们自己起初会对收入方面受到的限制感到不满。对此，与劳工密切接触的人士回答说，多年来，在党的纲领中一直进行着旨在理解法律监管含义的教育。上海、天津、广州的工人充分意识到监管的地位：据信，其中较开明的人会表示欢迎。虽然中国劳工是文盲，但并非无知。据称，政府无论如何不指望在工人方面遇到阻力；同时也确信许多雇主的善意。有人指出，目前有一个由著名实业家率领的代表团在南京，向政府指出，工业界无法承受全面适用将对中国整个经济重建计划产生影响；顺便也会影响政府的税收。

回到产量问题，有人指出，缩短工时后产量经常增加。对此的回答是，那是基于最精心准备的计划，而不是仅仅提前五周通知。还有人指出，在产量主要由机器控制且自动化的情况下，缩短工时并不会产生如此增加的回报。

当一名律师询问，既然从实际角度来看，适用只能从2月1日开始，并且需要很长时间才能完成，如果在法庭上援引该法律，法院是否会适用时，讨论达到了一个关键点。显然，这里涉及真正的困难。将一套规章宣布为政府政策，并设立一个局来教育公众去执行它们——这显然是一个漫长的过程——是一回事。而当这一标准具有法律地位，并可在法庭上援引时，则是完全不同的另一回事。即使是那些认为宣布整部法律尚未生效具有价值的人，也承认这是一个困难。

从讨论中可以明显看出，没有人期望不可能的事情发生：一种观点倾向于逐步逐项适用，直到整体完成；另一种方法是宣布整部法律生效，并在随后的几年里，工厂应逐渐达到理想状态。

提议在稍后日期进一步讨论该法律及其问题。在未来一段时间内，该论坛可能仍将是一个引人关注的场所。

（签名：Rogers / Magoon / Mercer / ...）

FACTORY LAWS DISCUSSED
Debate in Labour Forum Airs Problems
of New Regulations

Upon the new basis, when women may work from 6 a.m. till 10 p.m. in shifts to conform to the hours clauses, there are 96 working hours per machine per working week of six days. Allowing the minimum annual leave, and the eight statutory holidays, there are 15 days per year when the machine does not work its 16 hours. The total annual work will then be 4,772 hours. This would involve a reduction of 2,444 working hours per machine per year: approximately one third. What industry can stand such adjustment and live? The present situation should change, and change should begin now; but how can this so large immediate adjustment be made?

Difficulty of Replacement

The argument was put forward that nowhere in the law is it stated that the machines cannot work 24 hours a day: three shifts can be worked, and successfully, as has been shown by the introduction of three eight hour shifts by a Tientsin cotton mill, it was stated. It was assumed in argument that a third shift composed of men workers could be introduced into the cotton mills, since women are forbidden to work the third shift from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. A factory owner present stated that this was impossible: it would take a long period of training to teach men the work now performed by women.

The statement was made that it was believed the National Government had not gone into this legislation without due knowledge of the consequences. That it was assured, in other words, that there was ability on the part of industry to stand it. Indeed, as far back as 1927, the government had sought the advice and consultation of bankers and industrialists as to the content of a factory law. It seemed to be the opinion of one member of the group that there had been insufficient consultation: but it was declared upon accurate knowledge by others that this conferring had taken place. Nowhere in the world, it was stated, did industrial legislation come into being without protest. Sometimes it was from the workers group if they were not sufficiently enlightened to know the value of the limitations put upon their work: more often from employers whose self-interest was at stake. What was important at this time was an attitude of goodwill on the part of employers. It should be realized that lack of regulation worked against industries themselves. China's labour was generally said to be less effective than some other labour in the world: and one of the reasons for this might well be the long hours of work and poor wages which made the worker a less alert operative.

The law as proposed was revolutionary: there would be few who would deny it. But in every country legislation had cost, and China must be prepared to pay the cost.

Value of Goodwill

To this it was answered that in the face of economic facts, goodwill mattered little. There was scarcely a Chinese cotton mill which had earned dividends during the past five years. Three had already gone out of existence within the past few months: one on the 25th of this month. When asked if this was due to the factory law, the reply was that obviously it was not: but if the industry was unable to stand up to competition under a system of no regulation, it would be manifestly impossible for it to do so when limitations were put upon its earning power. One opinion was expressed that there were certainly some cotton mills which had earned money last year: would they be able to meet the increased production costs? Had any accurate figures yet been obtained? One manager

《字林西报》，1931年1月31日，星期六

讨论工厂法
劳工论坛的辩论揭示了新法规的问题

上海劳工论坛昨日可谓名副其实。这里成为了就国民政府颁布将于2月1日生效的新《工厂法》这一主题进行最热烈讨论的场所。律师、工厂主、“包工头”、社会工作者、教授、以非官方身份出席的官员，以及虽对由此造成的局势没有特定责任、但因关心这一对社区至关重要的事项而来到论坛的“普通公众”，均出席了会议。意见交换的坦率程度证明了继续举办该论坛的必要性和价值。

主席将议题缩小至法律适用所涉及的问题；正如他所陈述的，并非法律本身的存在或其个别条款。然而，事实证明，在不考虑内容的情况下讨论执法所涉及的问题是不可能的；因为内容显然造成了这些问题。

开场论点试图表明，仅从生产角度来看，且不涉及额外支出，立即全面实施该法律对工业界本身来说是不可能的。基于目前两班倒、每班工作22小时（注：此处原文逻辑似有误，通常指两班共22小时或类似排班，但译文依原文直译）、每月休息两天，并扣除目前的节假日损失时间，目前棉纺厂每台机器每年的总工作时间为7,216小时。在新的基础上，为了符合工时条款，妇女可分班从上午6点工作至晚上10点，在每周六个工作日的情况下，每台机器每周工作96小时。扣除最低年假和八个法定假日，每年有15天机器无法运行其16个小时。因此，年总工作量将为4,772小时。这将导致每台机器每年减少2,444个工作小时：约三分之一。哪家工业能承受这样的调整并生存下去？现状应该改变，而且现在就应该开始改变；但是如何进行如此巨大的即时调整呢？

替换的困难

有人提出论点称，法律中任何地方都没有规定机器不能每天24小时运转：可以实行三班倒，而且正如天津一家棉纺厂引入三个八小时班次所证明的那样，这是可以成功的。辩论中假设，可以在棉纺厂引入由男工组成的第三班次，因为禁止妇女在晚上10点至早上6点期间上第三班。一位在场的工厂主表示，这是不可能的：教导男性从事目前由女性完成的工作需要很长的培训期。

有人发表看法认为，相信国民政府在制定这项立法时并非没有充分考虑其后果。换言之，确信工业界有能力承受这一变化。事实上，早在1927年，政府就曾就工厂法的内容征求银行家和实业家的意见和咨询。小组中似乎有一位成员认为协商不足；但其他人根据确切知识宣称，这种磋商确实发生过。据说，世界上没有任何地方的工业立法是在没有抗议的情况下产生的。有时抗议来自工人群体，如果他们不够开明，无法了解对其工作施加限制的价值；更多时候则来自利益攸关的雇主。此时重要的是雇主方面持善意态度。应当认识到，缺乏监管对工业界自身不利。人们普遍认为，中国劳工的效率低于世界其他一些地区的劳工；造成这种情况的原因之一很可能是长时间工作和低工资，这使得工人成为反应较迟钝的操作者。

拟议中的法律具有革命性：对此否认的人寥寥无几。但在每个国家，立法都有代价，中国必须准备好付出这一代价。

善意的价值

对此，回应称面对经济事实，善意几乎无足轻重。在过去五年中，几乎没有一家中国棉纺厂赚取过红利。过去几个月内已有三家倒闭：其中一家就在本月25日倒闭。当被问及这是否归因于《工厂法》时，回答是显然不是；但是，如果工业界在无监管体系下都无法经受竞争，那么当其盈利能力受到限制时，显然更不可能做到。有一种观点认为，去年确实有一些棉纺厂赚了钱：它们能否应对增加的生产成本？是否已经获得了任何准确的数据？一位经理

stated that his mill was now run-
ning at a lost of Tae's 15,000 to
Tae's 20,000 a month; it was good-
will toward the 4,600 workers
involved that had not shut it down
before: but it would certainly not
be possible to add to this burden of
loss.
A question was asked, whether
there was an inspectorate ready for
the enforcement of this law; to this
no answer was forthcoming. It was
stated that two courses were open
for the administration—through the
present bureaucratic system of
municipal governments, or through
the establishment of special in-
spectorates. If the latter were not
available, the former could, as an
emergency measure, adhere to the
National Government decree, and
begin to put the law into effect as
from the date proclaimed. Already
groups of employers had been
gathered by the Bureau of Social
Affairs of the Municipality of
Greater Shanghai, and discussion
were proceeding as to the applica-
tion of the law. How far the law
will succeed, it was stated, depends
upon the strength of the govern-
mental organ and the goodwill of
employers.
Place of Regulation
The statement was then made
that the law was not built upon a
framework of public opinion with
regard to it. That the workers
themselves would be the first to
resent the limitations placed upon
them in the matter of earnings at
first. To this those in close touch
with labour made the reply that
for several years in the Party pro-
gramme there had been proceeding
education aimed at an understand-
ing of what legal regulation meant.
Workers in Shanghai, Tientsin,
Canton, were fully aware of the
place of regulation: it was believed
that there would be welcome on the
part of the more enlightened of
them. Though Chinese labour was
illiterate, it was not uninformed.
The Government did not at any rate
expect difficulty with workers, it
was stated; and it was also sure of
the goodwill of many employers. It
was pointed out that at the present
time there was a delegation in Nan-
king led by a prominent industrial-
ist, pointing out to the government
that the inability of industry to
stand wholesale application would
have its effect upon the whole pro-
gramme of economic reconstruction
for China; and incidentally upon
the government's taxation.
Reverting to the question of out-
put, it was stated that frequently
there had been increase in output
following reduction in hours. To
this it was answered that it was
upon the most carefully prepared
plans, not with only five weeks
notice. The point was made too
that where output was largely con-
trolled by the machine, and was
automatic, shortening of hours did
not produce such increased return.

A vital point in the discussion
was reached when a lawyer asked
whether, since from a practical
standpoint application could only
begin on February 1 and would take
a long time to complete, the law
would be applied in the courts if it
were invoked. It was apparent
that a real difficulty was here
involved. It is one thing to have a
set of regulations declared as
governmental policy, and to set a
Bureau to the task of educating a
public to carrying them out—a
long process evidently. It was quite
another thing when this standard
had legal status, and could be
invoked in court. This was re-
cognized even by those who believed
that there was value in the declara-
tion that the whole law was not in
force, as being a difficulty.
It is obvious from the discussion
that it is not expected by anyone
that the impossible can happen:
one sentiment favours however a
gradual set application, clause by
clause, till the whole is accom-
plished; another approach is that
the whole law should be announced
as in force, and within the succeed-
ing years, little by little, factories
should come to meet the ideal.
It is proposed to carry the dis-
cussion of the law and its problems
further at a later date. The Forum
is likely to be an interesting place
for some time to come.

表示，他的工厂目前每月亏损
15,000两至20,000两白银；正是
出于对涉及的4,600名工人的善
意，此前才没有关闭工厂；但肯
定不可能再增加这一亏损负担。
有人提问，是否有现成的检查
机构来执行这部法律；对此没有
得到答复。据说行政当局有两条
途径可选——通过现有的市政府
官僚体系，或通过建立专门的检
查机构。如果后者不可用，前者
可以作为紧急措施，遵循国民政
府的法令，并从宣布之日起开始
实施该法律。大上海市政府社会
局已经召集了多组雇主，正在就
法律的适用进行讨论。据说，法
律能在多大程度上成功，取决于
政府机构的力度和雇主的善意。
监管的地位
随后有人发表看法称，该法
律并非建立在公众舆论的基础之
上。工人们自己起初会首先对收
入方面受到的限制感到不满。对
此，与劳工阶层密切接触的人士
回答说，多年来，在党的纲领中
一直开展旨在理解法律监管含义
的教育。上海、天津、广州的工
人充分意识到监管的地位；人们
相信，其中较为开明的人会欢迎
这一法律。虽然中国劳工是文盲，
但他们并非无知。据说，政府至
少不指望在工人方面遇到困难；
同时也确信许多雇主持有善意。
有人指出，目前有一个由著名实
业家率领的代表团在南京，向政
府指出，工业界无法承受全面实
施的影响，这将波及中国经济重
建的整个计划；顺便也会影响政
府的税收。
回到产量问题，有人指出，
缩短工时后产量经常增加。对此
的回答是，那是基于最精心准备
的计划，而不是仅仅提前五周通
知。还有人指出，在产量主要由
机器控制且自动化的情况下，缩
短工时并不会产生如此增加的回
报。

当一位律师询问，既然从实
际角度来看，适用只能从2月1
日开始，并且需要很长时间才能
完成，那么如果援引该法律，法
院是否会予以适用时，讨论达到
了一个关键点。显然，这里涉及
一个真正的困难。将一套规章宣
布为政府政策，并设立一个局来
教育公众去执行它们——这显然
是一个漫长的过程——是一回事。
而当这一标准具有法律地位，并
可在法庭上援引时，则是完全另
一回事。即使是那些认为宣布整
部法律尚未生效具有价值的人，
也承认这是一个困难。

从讨论中可以明显看出，没
有人期望不可能的事情发生：一
种情绪倾向于逐步逐项适用，直
到全部完成；另一种方法是宣布
整部法律生效，并在随后的几年
里，工厂应逐步达到理想状态。
提议在稍后日期进一步讨论该法
律及其问题。在未来一段时间内，
该论坛可能仍将是一个引人关注
的地方。

Factory Law Postponed
The Chinese Government have
shown themselves reasonably ready
to listen to well-argued repre-
sentations, in their postponement of
the enforcement of the Factory
Law until August 1, instead of
February 1, as at first contemplat-
ed. The views of the Chinese mill-
owners, as put before the Ministry
of Industries at Nanking, have
thus been sympathetically consider-
ed. Readers of the articles and
comment which have appeared in
the columns of this journal will
understand that this period of six
months grace is in reality inade-
quate to create conditions for the
proper enforcement of the Law.
This view will have been reinforced
by study of the discussion which
took place on Friday evening at
the Chinese Y.M.C.A. Forum, where
various experts expressed very
definite opinions on the subject.
Nevertheless this period should be
used in trying to find a way in
which all Municipal authorities
could help to apply the law later.
Six months give little enough
time for the formulation of a sys-
tem; the authorities concerned
should not on that account favour
inaction.

中国政府表现出相当愿意听取
论证充分的陈情，将《工厂法》
的执行从最初考虑的2月1日推迟

周五晚上在中国青年会论坛举行

那里，各位专家就该主题表达了

有关当局不应因此倾向于不作为。

PEKING & TIENTSIN TIMES, FRIDAY, JANUARY 30, 1931.
C. I. O. R.
5492.
13 - 2 - 31

CHINA'S FACTORY LAW.
(To the Editor of the P. & T. Times.)

Sir,—I have read with great interest the article entitled "China's Factory Law" by Mr. H.G.W. Woodhead, reproduced in to-day's P. & T. Times.
I entirely agree with him that this law would be ignored as it would practically have the effect of stopping all work in the more or less primitive factories and workshops operated in the large cities of China. One would therefore have to proceed with the application of this law by gradual stages.
The first step; in my opinion, is the official registration of workers, or at least of the children working in these factories. It is inadmissible that, even in China, an employer can consider his labourers as beasts of burden which he may cast off when they are no longer able to serve his purpose, and that he is not held responsible to Society, when, after having squeezed from them all the energy which they were capable of rendering, he virtually throws them out into the street exhausted.
The foreign community of Tientsin does not know of the deplorable conditions of the local child labour. They cannot, however, form the slightest conception of prevailing conditions, for these children hardly ever leave the factories, where they are "boarding inmates". Apart from overcrowding, long working hours and general insanitary conditions, the insufficient nourishment of these children alone would cause one astonishment and disgust. This "nourishment" is given in the form of two meals a day of mantou—Chinese bread—and salted turnips. An employer of two hundred workers whom we asked whether he could not vary his workers' diet by substituting fresh cabbages for salted turnip, made the following calculation before us: "four dollars Mex. per day, i.e. two cents per person. And besides, the cabbage would stimulate their appetite and they would ask for some more

mantou". As a matter of fact, the outlay on the turnips, bought at a cheap price in season and then preserved in brine, is far below the price he would pay for a daily supply of fresh cabbages. Child labour is not paid; i.e. no wages are given them, who constitute nearly one hundred thousand unfortunates "living" on such a famine diet. They leave Oliver Twist far behind.
Who could admit that a human being, the more so a child who has yet to develop; is able to sustain itself on a diet which is certainly inferior to animal fodder without eventually succumbing to grave injuries to their general health? These Oliver Twists are, in fact, in extremely bad health, often contract tuberculosis and worse ... every year hundreds become blind owing to deficiency of vitamins. This blindness and its appalling frequency are undeniable, yet completely ignored, facts.
What remedy are we to offer for this truly deplorable situation? It would suffice to have an agreement between the Authorities of the different Municipalities of Tientsin to enforce the compulsory registration of child labour. The employer could no longer be able to deny his workers the necessary medical care, and specially ocular attention, and we would no longer witness the cruelty of the actual practice of ejecting these useless waifs after they have become incapacitated through blindness, contracted in the factory itself. He would be constrained to send the patients to a free clinic and would thereby free himself from further responsibility, if not, a fine or other legal enactment would punish the crime of which he is now daily guilty.
It must be understood, however, that there is no question of revolutionizing the diet of the Chinese workers. All that is needed is one egg a week in winter, or the equivalent in fresh vegetables, meat or liver—which contain the necessary vitamins. This would be sufficient to abolish the main cause of blindness which is afflicting the child labour in the great industrial centers of China. If necessary, the little patients would receive at the clinics dietetic treatment, such as is actually being dispensed by us, which protects from aggravation and cures the incipient stages of the disease.

Only after having taken this first step in the direction of Hygiene, will it be possible to envisage further reforms such as working and rest hours, minimum age of child workers, etc.
Apologising for the length of this letter,
I am, Sir,
Yours faithfully:
AN OLD RESIDENT,
(Member of the Board of the International League for the Prevention of Blindness in China).
Tien'sin, 26th January 1931.

SI, Please rule and pass
Wkpg. Wple.

1931年2月13日

中国的工厂法。
（致《京津泰晤士报》编辑。）

先生，——我饶有兴致地阅读了今日《京津泰晤士报》转载的H.G.W. 伍德黑德（H.G.W. Woodhead）先生题为“中国的工厂法”的文章。
我完全同意他的观点，即这部法律将被束之高阁，因为它实际上会导致中国大城市中那些或多或少处于原始状态的工厂和作坊全面停工。因此，实施这部法律必须分阶段逐步进行。
依我看，第一步是对工人，至少是在这些工厂工作的童工进行官方登记。即使在中国，雇主将劳工视为役畜，在其无法再为其目的服务时便将其抛弃，且在榨干他们所能提供的全部精力后，实质上将这些精疲力竭的人抛向街头，而无需对社会承担责任，这是不可接受的。
天津的外侨社区并不了解当地童工的悲惨状况。然而，他们根本无法对普遍存在的状况形成丝毫概念，因为这些孩子几乎从不离开工厂，他们是那里的“寄宿住客”。除了过度拥挤、长时间工作和总体卫生条件恶劣外，仅这些儿童营养不足这一点就足以令人震惊和厌恶。这种“营养”的形式是每天两餐馒头——中式面包——和咸萝卜。我们询问一位拥有两百名工人的雇主，是否不能用新鲜卷心菜代替咸萝卜来改善工人的饮食，他当着我们的面做了如下计算：“每天4墨西哥元，即每人2分。此外，卷心菜会刺激他们的食欲，他们会要求更多的

馒头”。事实上，他在当季以低价购买并腌制成咸菜的萝卜支出，远低于他每日供应新鲜卷心菜所需支付的价格。童工是没有报酬的；也就是说，不发工资，这构成了近十万不幸者靠这种饥荒般的饮食“生活”的基础。他们让奥利弗·特威斯特（Oliver Twist，狄更斯小说《雾都孤儿》主角）望尘莫及。
谁能承认，一个人，尤其是尚处于发育阶段的儿童，能够依靠肯定低于动物饲料的饮食维持生存，而不最终遭受对其整体健康的严重损害呢？这些“奥利弗·特威斯特”们实际上健康状况极差，经常患上结核病以及更严重的疾病……每年有数百人因缺乏维生素而失明。这种失明及其惊人的发生率是不可否认却完全被忽视的事实。
我们要为这种真正令人痛心的局面提供什么补救措施呢？只需天津各市政当局之间达成协议，强制执行童工强制登记制度即可。雇主将不能再拒绝为其工人提供必要的医疗护理，特别是眼部护理，我们也将不再目睹目前的残酷做法，即在这些人因在工厂本身染上的失明而丧失劳动能力后，将这些无用的弃儿驱逐出去。他将被迫将患者送往免费诊所，从而免除进一步的责任，否则，罚款或其他法律制裁将惩罚他目前每日都在犯下的罪行。
然而，必须理解，这里无意彻底改变中国工人的饮食结构。所需的只是冬季每周一个鸡蛋，或含有必要维生素的新鲜蔬菜、肉类或肝脏等量替代品。这足以消除困扰中国主要工业中心童工失明的主要原因。如有必要，这些小患者将在诊所接受饮食治疗，正如我们目前所提供的那样，以防止病情恶化并治愈疾病的初期阶段。

只有在朝着卫生方向迈出这第一步之后，才有可能考虑进一步的改革，如工作和休息时间、童工最低年龄等。
为此信的冗长致歉，
先生，
您忠实的：
一位老居民，
（中国防盲国际联盟董事会成员）。
天津，1931年1月26日。

Wkpg. Wple.
