得以执行。大上海市政府社会局官员曾表示，在涉及纠纷的问题中，标准的存在具有价值。当调解的责任落到他们身上时，由于每一起纠纷都各不相同，因此一个准则是必不可少的。

法律执行

但是，实施这项法律需要什么？一旦确定了日期，该法律即成为中国法典的一部分，如果有任何案件因违反其任何条款而被诉至法院，就必须予以适用。在英国和其他拥有现代工业法典的国家，虽然任何人或团体（例如工人或工会）都可以向法院提起诉讼，但由政府特别任命的官员负责确保法律的施行是他们的职责。这些官员被称为工厂视察员。他们与雇主的关系通常非常融洽，只有在频繁的友好警告未能达到目的时，才会采取法律行动追究违法行为。但是，如果违法行为持续发生，工厂视察员必须提起诉讼；通过这种方式，法院成为执法的工具。因此，对于研究工业法的学生来说，显而易见的是，除非同时具备视察机构这一工具，否则仅仅宣布法律在中国生效是无济于事的。目前尚不清楚是否已有一支视察员队伍准备就绪，尽管已知部里一直在考虑此事。条例中并未提及他们。主要法案提到了“主管当局”，但这并非指负责法律施行的责任。根据第二条，这在“市”是指市政府，在“县”是指县级当局。据推测，如果建立视察机构，它将隶属于各市的社会局。在西方国家，视察员需要接受专门培训，因为例如管辖安全状况的法案已经变得技术化且细节繁多。迄今为止，中国的原始法案形式相对简单，施行起来不需要长期的技术培训。坦率地说，这项法律能否得到执行，取决于是否拥有一支有效素质的视察队伍。

逐步施行是可取的

在其他国家，为受新立法影响的工业提供一段调整期是有历史先例的。在日本，继1919年国际联盟国际劳工组织华盛顿会议通过的标准之后，通过了一项废除妇女夜间工作的法案，并规定了三年的期限，以便相关工业进行必要的调整。尽管时间已充分利用，但最近与上海日本棉纺业同业公会的船津辰一郎先生（T. Funatsu）交谈显示，这段时间仍不足以通过增加纱锭数量来将所有女工吸收进白班。在这项新规定以及新法的许多其他深远条款中，都没有为逐步施行做出规定。

童工雇佣

接下来审查该法律的一些更重要方面。第二节专门处理童工和女工问题，尽管显然该法案的许多其他条款也涵盖了他们的雇佣问题。根据第五条：
“禁止在所有工厂雇佣十四岁以下的儿童”
“上述年龄以下但十二岁以上的儿童，若在本法颁布前已在工厂受雇，经主管当局同意，可允许继续受雇”。
本节中的其他条款将十四岁以上、十六岁以下的儿童称为“童工”，并定义了不得雇佣他们及女工从事的工序。
这一节代表了最深远的变革。目前，除了个别情况——例如怡和棉纺厂、一些日本棉纺厂和商务印书馆——对于从很小年龄开始使用童工没有任何限制。在大多数缫丝厂——除了那些采用中央煮茧室系统的工厂——儿童从大约七或八岁起就被雇佣。在棉纺厂，年幼的儿童从早上六点到晚上六点，或者在十二小时的夜班中工作。雇佣儿童的习惯既阻碍了机器工艺的引进，又减少了

page_data.en:
amount of a suitable employment for
adults. The writer has seen men
carrying food to children employed
in factories at lunch time, the men
the while being out of employment.
There is no question that this
state of affairs should be remedied,
and at once. But is the law wise in
setting at once a standard beyond
which few of the most advanced
industrial nations have yet been able
to move? It is a moot point. It
may be said that the only cure for
some social evils is surgical, and
that the provision for the continued
employment of children over the age
of twelve years who are already
employed represents the only neces-
sary concession.

How is Age Determined?

How, however, and upon what
basis shall age be determined?
There is no birth registration in
China. And is the age to be foreign
or Chinese count? The ordinances
take account of this difficulty and
provide that, when there is difficulty
in determining age
"Before promulgation of the law on
Census and Birth Place, in case age
of worker is called in question, it
shall be vouched for by the worker's
legal representative."
The new Civil Code, in the first
book on General Principles, states
in Article 24.
"Age is to be reckoned from the
day of birth; if it is not possible to
ascertain the month of birth of a
person he is presumed to have been
born on the first day of July. If the
month of birth is known and it is not
possible to ascertain the day, he is
presumed to have been born on the
fifteenth day of the month."
This would imply that from the
point of view of the Chinese Gov-
ernment, the old habit of reckoning
age by the Chinese New Year has
no recognition in law. Accordingly,
when "fourteen years" is mentioned,
it is presumed to be fourteen years'
"foreign count". This standard re-
presents a very high one for an
attempt at immediate attainment.
When, in 1924, the Child Labour
Commission of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council recommended the
drafting of a Child Labour Bye-Law,
it suggested that children under ten
years, rising to twelve years within
four years, should not be admitted
to employment. A famous phrase
accompanying this recommendation
stated that
"the evidence given before this com-
mission was such as to drive it to
the conclusion that, if the continued
existence of any industry in the
Settlement were dependent upon the
continuance of the employment of
children under ten, then the dis-
appearance of such industry from the
Settlement could be regarded with
equanimity."
With regard to proof of age, the
Commission recommended two me-
thods—the adoption of a standard
of height, or height and weight, or,
providing as in the case of the
Hongkong ordinances covering Child
Labour, that "in any prosecution,
until the contrary is proved, the
child, the subject-matter of the
charge, is to be assumed to be of the
particular age he or she appears to
be to the sitting magistrate." What
is now really involved in the fourth
article of the ordinances covering
the National Factory Law is not
quite clear; but it is assumed that
some certification by a "workers'
legal representative" will be requir-
ed.
The other clauses of this section
are reasonable and logical, prevent-
ing women and young workers from
being employed in relation to "in-
flammable or poisonous substances,
from working where they are ex-
posed to dust or fumes from noxious
fluids, from cleaning, oiling and re-
pairing machines in motion, and so
on. While they may involve adjust-
ment, there is no such large social
issue involved as in the question of
age. And even in the last named
matter, if the law proves possible
of enforcement at all, there are few
who would not rather see the diffi-
culties faced of achieving the age
limit set, than see the continued per-
petuation of so wrong a situation
as exists to-day.
Note.—The succeeding articles will
examine other significant clauses of the
Factory Law. The translation used is
the official translation of the Ministry,
which was issued in 1930. English texts
of the three National laws relating to
labour. They may be obtained from the
Bureau of Economic Information,
Fourth Floor Customs House, Nankow
Road.

成年人合适就业的机会。作者曾看到男人在午餐时间为在工厂工作的儿童送饭，而这些男人当时正处于失业状态。毫无疑问，这种状况应该立即得到纠正。但是，该法律立即设定一个连最先进的工业国家都尚未能完全达到的标准，是否明智？这是一个有争议的问题。可以说，某些社会弊病的唯一治愈方法是外科手术式的，而允许已受雇的十二岁以上儿童继续受雇的规定代表了唯一必要的让步。

如何确定年龄？

然而，如何以及依据什么基础来确定年龄？中国没有出生登记制度。年龄是按外国算法还是中国算法计算？条例考虑到了这一困难，并规定，在确定年龄有困难时：
“在户口及出生地法颁布之前，若工人的年龄受到质疑，应由工人的法定代理人担保。”
新《民法典》第一编总则第二十四条规定：
“年龄自出生之日起算；若无法查明某人的出生月份，推定其出生于七月一日。若已知出生月份但无法查明日期，推定其出生于该月十五日。”
这意味着，从中国政府的观点来看，按农历新年计算年龄的旧习惯在法律上不予承认。因此，当提到“十四岁”时，据推测是指十四岁的“外国算法”。这一标准对于试图立即实现的目标来说非常高。1924年，上海公共租界工部局童工委员会建议起草《童工附律》时，曾建议十岁以下儿童不得受雇，并在四年内将此年龄提高至十二岁。伴随这一建议的一句名言指出：
“向本委员会提供的证据使其得出如下结论：如果租界内任何行业的持续存在依赖于继续雇佣十岁以下儿童，那么此类行业从租界消失是可以坦然接受的。”
关于年龄证明，委员会推荐了两种方法——采用身高标准，或身高和体重标准，或者像涵盖童工的香港条例那样规定：“在任何起诉中，除非有相反证明，否则作为指控对象的儿童应被坐堂推事视为其外表所显示的特定年龄。”目前，《全国工厂法》条例第四条真正涉及的内容并不十分清楚；但据推测，将需要“工人法定代理人”的某种认证。
本节的其他条款合理且合乎逻辑，防止妇女和年轻工人受雇接触“易燃或有毒物质”，防止他们在暴露于粉尘或有害液体烟雾的环境中工作，防止他们清洁、加油和修理运转中的机器等。虽然这些规定可能涉及调整，但不像年龄问题那样涉及如此重大的社会问题。即使在最后提到的问题上，如果该法律证明有可能执行，很少有人不愿意面对实现既定年龄限制的困难，也不愿看到像今天这样错误的状况继续存在。
注：后续文章将审查《工厂法》的其他重要条款。所使用的译文是部里于1930年发布的官方译本。三部关于劳工的全国性法律的英文文本。可从南京路海关大楼四楼经济情报局获取。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C.I.D RECORDS
No. 1-O. 9139
Date... 18.6.29

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, JUNE 16, 1929

China Prepares
Advanced Code
Of Labor Laws
Discharge Indemnity, Pro-
fit Sharing Incorporated
Tentative Draft

Geneva, May 2.—According to the
text of a tentative legal code just
received here by the International
Labor Office the new China soon
will have a body of labor laws on a
level with those of the most “ad-
vanced” countries, and in some
instances even, more progressive.
This document, drafted by the
Ministry of Industry and Com-
merce, is based on the findings of
a committee of experts. It shortly
will be brought before the legisla-
tive council, with every prospect of
adoption.

Unlike most such codes, this one
deals with even the smaller factor-
ies, such as employ only thirty
workers. It forbids child labor
under the age of fourteen, admits
collective agreements approved by
the competent administration, and
provides workers with safeguards in
case of termination of service, in-
cluding indemnities on discharge.

EIGHT-HOUR DAY PROVIDED
The eight-hour day is provided,
although “exceptions up to the limit
of ten hours’ work a day may be al-
lowed, if required by special local
conditions, the special nature of the
factory and the seasonal character
of the work.”

No woman may be employed be-
tween 10 p.m. and 6 a.m., nor any
workers less than sixteen years old
between 7 p.m. and 6 a.m. There
must be one day’s rest in every
seven, a week’s holiday with pay
after six months’ continuous work
—two weeks after a year. Far from
avoiding the minimum wage issue,
the code declares that a minimum
wage must be fixed forthwith by the
competent administration.

Finally, there is devised a system
of profit sharing. Workers’ councils
are to be set up in every factory
employing more than thirty hands
for “the conciliation of disputes be-
tween workers, between different
departments of the factory and even
between employers and workers.”
Apprenticeship rules are suggested;
on the most liberal lines welfare
work is insisted upon and especial
emphasis laid on educational facili-
ties for workers.

GIVES ACCIDENT COMPENSA-
TION
compensation for accidents is pro-
vided and there is a set of rules
for factory inspection, with penal-
ties for infraction of the factory
laws, which would daunt many an
Occidental government.

Commenting on the code, Albert
Thomas, director in chief of the In-
ternational Labor Office said:
“Some surprise no doubt will be
felt at it but one must
remember that in the view of its
supporters the Chinese Nationalist
government is the workers to help
it in its national activity.” M.
Thomas has just returned from a
tour of the Orient, bringing a copy
of the code with him. He continu-
ed:
“Certain provisions which may
appear particularly advanced—such
as those relating to discharge in-
demnities, profit sharing, etc.—
merely correspond to the aspirations
of the new China or are based on
national traditional customs. Of
course, as I found in my talks with
officials, it is admitted that the
‘competent administrations,’ to
which so much is left, must be
trained for their task.
HAVE FOREIGN CONCESSIONS
TO CONSIDER
“Also, the inspection services are
still rudimentary. Nevertheless, the
government is enthusiastic over the
plan. If in the next few years it
can root out the few abuses still
existing in some industries it will
have done work of importance.
“It is especially necessary to act
with that prudence which alone
makes firmness possible, because the
Chinese government is faced with
delicate problems of foreign conces-
sions and colonies. So long as these
exist the problem will have the
same character as at the time of
the Washington Conference. The
Chinese Nationalist government will
be more anxious than any previous
government to enforce labor legisla-
tion in factories owned and man-
aged by foreigners.
“It cannot be admitted that there
should exist for such factories laws
inferior to those applying to Chin-
ese factories or that there should be
no special legislation of any kind.
Nevertheless, it must be admitted
that, for at present, both Chinese
and foreign employers are extreme-
ly uneasy at the far-reaching char-
acter of the draft code; they fear
lest it involve immediately an im-
mense expenditure.”

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事侦缉处档案
编号 1-O. 9139
日期... 1929年6月18日

《字林西报》，1929年6月16日，星期日

中国拟定
先进劳工法典
解雇赔偿金、利润
分享纳入
暂行草案

日内瓦，5月2日电。——根据国际劳工局刚刚在此收到的法律法典暂行文本，新中国很快将拥有一套与最“先进”国家水平相当的劳工法体系，在某些情况下甚至更为进步。这份由工商部起草的文件，是基于一个专家委员会的研究成果。它不久将被提交给立法院，极有可能获得通过。

与大多数此类法典不同，本法典甚至涉及仅雇佣三十名工人的小型工厂。它禁止雇佣十四岁以下的童工，承认经主管行政机关批准的集体协议，并为工人在终止服务时提供保障，包括解雇赔偿金。

规定八小时工作制

规定了八小时工作制，尽管“如果因当地特殊情况、工厂的特殊性质以及工作的季节性特征所必需，可允许例外情况，但每日工作上限为十小时。”

晚上10点至早上6点之间不得雇佣任何女性，晚上7点至早上6点之间不得雇佣任何十六岁以下的工人。每七天必须休息一天，连续工作六个月后享有一周带薪假期——一年后享有两周假期。该法典不仅没有回避最低工资问题，反而宣布必须由主管行政机关立即确定最低工资。

最后，还设计了一套利润分享制度。在雇佣超过三十名工人的每个工厂中，都将设立工人委员会，以“调解工人之间、工厂不同部门之间甚至雇主与工人之间的纠纷”。建议制定学徒规则；坚持在最宽泛的基础上开展福利工作，并特别强调为工人提供教育设施。

提供事故赔偿

规定了事故赔偿，并制定了一套工厂检查规则，对违反工厂法的行为处以惩罚，其严厉程度足以令许多西方政府望而却步。

国际劳工局局长阿尔伯特·托马斯（Albert Thomas）在评论该法典时说：“对此无疑会感到有些惊讶，但必须记住，在其支持者看来，中国国民政府是帮助其进行国家活动的工人。”托马斯先生刚刚结束东方之行归来，带回了一份法典副本。他继续说道：

“某些可能显得特别先进的条款——如有关解雇赔偿金、利润分享等的条款——仅仅符合新中国的愿望，或是基于民族传统习俗。当然，正如我在与官员的谈话中所发现的那样，人们承认，被赋予如此多权力的‘主管行政机关’必须为其任务接受培训。

需考虑外国租界

“此外，检查服务仍处于初级阶段。尽管如此，政府对该计划充满热情。如果在未来几年内它能根除某些行业中仍然存在的少数弊端，那它将完成一项重要的工作。

“尤其有必要采取那种唯有谨慎才能使坚定成为可能的审慎态度，因为中国政府面临着外国租界和殖民地的棘手问题。只要这些存在，这个问题就将具有华盛顿会议时期的相同性质。中国国民政府将比任何前任政府都更急于在外国人拥有和管理的工厂中执行劳工立法。

“不能承认这类工厂适用的法律低于适用于中国工厂的法律，或者没有任何形式的特别立法。然而，必须承认，目前中外雇主都对草案法典的深远性质感到极度不安；他们担心这会立即导致巨大的开支。”

（批注：刑事侦缉处登记）

Principles Are Defined
Of New Labor Union Law
By Legislative Yuan

Aim Is To Allay Industrial Unrest And Provide
Machinery For The Arbitration Of Industrial
Disputes Preventing Strikes

(Kuo Min News Agency)
Nanking, Sept. 2.—With a view to allaying industrial unrest consequent to labor strikes and in order to facilitate arbitration of industrial disputes, the Legislative Yuan, after lengthy and careful deliberations lasting over a period of two months, has finally laid down the General Principles governing the proposed Labor Union Law which is now being drafted by the Labor Law Committee of the Yuan. Following is a translation of the General Principles upon which the proposed Labor Union Law is based:—

1. The proposed Labor Union Law shall not be applicable to staff-members or other employees of Government administrative, communications, military and industrial organs; nor shall it be applicable to those in the employ of Government-managed, educational and public utility enterprises.
2. A labor union may be organized by industrial workers or employees of any other concern.
3. The object of all labor unions should be to promote the efficiency of the workers and improve their living and other labor conditions.
4. A labor union shall accept the highest local Party Headquarters as its advisory organ; and the Provincial, Municipal or District Government authorities concerned as its supervisory organ.
5. One and the same industry or concern shall have one labor union only. If no such labor union therefor has been established and if the local administrative authorities concerned consider it necessary to have such established, the highest local Party Headquarters may be requested to take charge of the organization thereof in accordance with the Labor Union Law.
6. A labor union shall submit a report to the responsible adminis-
(Continued on Page 2, Col. 2.)

Principles Are Defined
Of New Labor Union Law
By Legislative Yuan

(Continued from Page 1, Col. 3.)
rative authorities upon its establishment. A labor union which fails to report, or, though having reported, has not been approved and confirmed by the authorities con-
in the limits of the law and Government orders.
14. A labor union shall be responsible for any damage which may have been inflicted on a third party by its staff-members when performing their duties.
15. No employers shall demand of their employees that they must withdraw, or refrain from joining, a labor union.
16. A labor union shall be regarded as a juristic person; its dissolution, amalgamation and liquidation shall all conform to the provisions governing a juristic person defined in the Civil Code.
17. Labor unions of the same nature may unite to organize a General Labor Union; the requirements and procedure for its organization being similar to those for the organization of a labor union.
18. Unless with sanction from the Government, no labor union shall affiliate itself with any labor union of a foreign country.

立法院界定
新工会法原则

旨在平息工业动荡并提供仲裁机制
以防止罢工引发的劳资纠纷

（国民通讯社）
南京，9月2日电。——为了平息因劳工罢工而引起的工业动荡，并促进劳资纠纷的仲裁，立法院经过长达两个多月的 lengthy 和仔细审议，最终确定了拟议中的《工会法》总则，该法目前正由该院劳工法委员会起草。以下是拟议《工会法》所依据的总则译文：—

1. 拟议中的《工会法》不适用于政府行政、交通、军事和工业机关的职员或其他雇员；也不适用于政府经营的教育和公用事业企业的雇员。
2. 产业工人或任何其他商号的雇员可以组织工会。
3. 所有工会的目标应是提高工人的效率，改善他们的生活和其他劳动条件。
4. 工会应接受当地最高党部为其咨询机关；并接受相关的省、市或区政府当局为其监督机关。
5. 同一行业或商号只能有一个工会。如果尚未为此建立此类工会，且相关地方行政当局认为有必要建立，则可请求当地最高党部根据《工会法》负责组织建立。
6. 工会成立时应向负责行政当局提交报告。未提交报告的工会，或虽已提交报告但未获有关当局批准和确认的工会，
（续至第2栏第2页。）

在法律和政府命令的范围内。
14. 工会应对其工作人员在执行职务时对第三方造成的任何损害负责。
15. 任何雇主不得要求其雇员退出或拒绝加入工会。
16. 工会应被视为法人；其解散、合并和清算均应符合《民法》中关于法人的规定。
17. 性质相同的工会可以联合组织总工会；其组织要求和程序与组织工会类似。

立法院界定新工会法原则

旨在平息工业动荡并建立仲裁机制以预防罢工

（国民通讯社）
南京，9月2日电——为了平息因劳工罢工而引发的工业动荡，并便于对劳资纠纷进行仲裁，立法院经过长达两个多月的仔细审议，最终制定了正在由该院劳动法委员会起草的拟议《工会法》的总则。以下是作为拟议《工会法》基础的总则译文：—
1. 拟议的《工会法》不适用于政府行政、交通、军事和工业机关的职员或其他雇员；也不适用于受雇于政府经营的教育和公用事业企业的人员。
2. 产业工人或任何其他商号的雇员均可组织工会。
3. 所有工会的宗旨应是提高工人的效率，改善其生活及其他劳动条件。
4. 工会应接受当地最高党部为其指导机关；并接受相关的省、市或区政府当局为其监督机关。
5. 同一行业或同一商号只能有一个工会。如果尚未建立此类工会，且相关地方行政当局认为有必要建立，则可请求当地最高党部根据《工会法》负责组织事宜。
6. 工会成立后应向主管行政当局提交报告。未提交报告，或虽已报告但未获有关当局批准确认的工会，不得行使《工会法》规定的权利并享受其特权。
7. 同一行业的所有工人或同一商号的所有雇员均应加入同一个工会，该工会不得通过征收过高的入会费及年度或月度会费而歧视性地接纳他们。
8. 工会不得强迫工人加入，尤其不得阻止任何会员退会。
9. 工会可以组织合作社或分红社团、职业介绍所、托儿所，并设立偿债基金以救济失业者，以及其他合作企业。
10. 当工会尚未按其章程规定建立此类合作企业，且行政当局认为有必要建立时，当地最高党部可指派若干代表协助工会组织此类社团。
11. 所有劳资纠纷应由第三方调解或通过仲裁解决；工人不得违反法律和政府命令擅自宣布罢工。
12. 工会不得因未能获得高于标准工资等级的加薪要求而宣布罢工。
13. 工会在法律和政府命令允许的范围内享有言论和出版自由。
14. 工会应对其工作人员在执行职务时对第三方造成的任何损害负责。
Rev
15. 任何雇主不得要求其雇员退出或禁止其加入工会。
16. 工会应被视为法人；其解散、合并和清算均应符合《民法典》中关于法人的规定。
17. 性质相同的工会可以联合组织总工会；其组织要求和程序与组织工会类似。
18. 除非获得政府批准，任何工会不得与任何外国工会建立隶属关系。

C. P. O.

SHANGHAI, 29th May, 1931.

Dear Sirs,

As you are aware, the Employers' Federation has determined to make a study of the content of the Factory Act which the National Government has stated will be enforced as from 1st August, 1931. To do an effective piece of work it is necessary to study the effects of the application of every individual clause, both from their cost angle and as regards other possible results. Only so can the sum total effect of any effort to enforce the whole of the provisions be ascertained.

The Sub-Committee which has been appointed is of opinion that a scientific study, in which facts are readily made available by the members of the Federation, is the greatest safeguard which the situation offers. When authentic information is in the hands of the Committee of the Federation, definite recommendations can be made. Without such information it is likely that less effective results will follow.

Accordingly a detailed questionnaire has been prepared and is being sent to you herewith. The Sub-Committee to whom has been entrusted this study urges you to answer it as fully as possible. It is aware that in some few of its clauses it may not prove easy to provide the information asked for. But your Sub-Committee repeats that your co-operation is an essential factor in meeting the present situation, and a general answer is better than none.

For the sake of the records of the Federation we request that the usual forms be filled out in addition to the questionnaire.

It is probable that you will receive also a call for the purpose of having you express opinion upon some related points to be recorded along with the purely statistical data asked for in this questionnaire. It is assumed in advance that you will be glad to receive the call and to give your views.

In view of the urgency of this matter it is urged that your reply should be in the hands of the Sub-Committee not later than 15th June, 1931.

Yours faithfully,

C. D. PEARSON,
Chairman.

秘书：PECK & SWANN。

上海，1931年5月29日。

敬启者：

正如贵方所知，雇主联合会已决定对国民政府宣布将于1931年8月1日起实施的《工厂法》的内容进行研究。为了开展有效的工作，必须从成本角度以及其他可能产生的结果方面，研究每一条款实施的影响。只有这样，才能确定执行全部规定所产生的总体影响。

受任此职的小组委员会认为，由联合会成员提供现成事实进行的科学研究，是当前局势下最大的保障。当联合会委员会掌握确切信息时，便可提出明确的建议。若无此类信息，结果可能会大打折扣。

为此，我们准备了一份详细的问卷，随函附上。受托进行此项研究的小组委员会敦促贵方尽可能全面地回答。委员会意识到，在少数条款中，提供所要求的信息可能并非易事。但小组委员会重申，贵方的合作是应对当前局势的关键因素，即使是一般性的回答也胜于无。

为了联合会的记录起见，我们要求在填写问卷的同时，填写常规表格。

贵方可能还会接到拜访，目的是就一些相关问题征求贵方意见，这些意见将与本问卷中要求的纯统计数据一并记录。我们预先假定贵方乐意接受拜访并发表看法。

鉴于此事紧迫，敦促贵方最迟于1931年6月15日前将回复送交小组委员会。

此致
敬礼，

C. D. PEARSON,
主席。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 27, 1931
(12)
5494
29.10.31.

FACTORY ACT DISCUSSED
Institute Delegates Agree Education Must Precede Enforcement

Complete realisation of the benefits of the recently enacted Chinese Factory law, which created considerable local and international interest, cannot be attained until the general public has been educated to appreciate its advantages, according to the views expressed yesterday at the fourth session of the Institute of Pacific Relations Conference, which discussed that problem as well as the local labour situation, Chinese standards of living and the limitation of population.

Other obstacles to the successful enforcement of the Factory Act, it was pointed out at the "round table" debates, which comprise the conference, are the lack of sufficient capital by employers to effect the necessary improvements, the dire poverty to the majority of the workers and the general political instability of the nation at large. The discussion resulted in dividing the delegates into two groups, one of which adopted the "realist" opinion and the other the "idealist" viewpoint, inasmuch as the law, admittedly, sets a standard higher than can be enforced immediately in the majority of Chinese factories. The realists expressed the opinion that it is a mistake to set standards impossible to achieve when a more conservative law would produce immediate practical benefits. The idealists believed that more eventual good would come from a higher standard, even if its realization was only gradual.

Difference in Standards

A third viewpoint, however, was advanced by a member of the delegation from the International Labour Office who stated that he believed the difference at issue was not so much between "idealism" and "realism," but more a question of the difference in standards of law: in this instance between the British and European methods. According to the British standard, the delegate continued, a law is something that defines precisely what is to be done and expects that such regulations will be carried out to the letter. On the other hand, he explained, many European laws set up a standard to be attained and the machinery for attaining it, expecting the final results to be accomplished one step at a time. Accordingly, in enacting the Chinese factory regulations, its proponents may have had the continental standard in view, it was stated.

Coming to the educational problem in relation to this law, the delegates agreed that it is vital to enlist public sentiment and approval, holding the opinion that no law can be successfully enforced if lacking in this regard. Attention was drawn to the fact, however, that out of China's total population of over 400 million, only ten millions can be affected in any way by this act, while graver problems exist for larger percentages of the population than the one under discussion.

Discussion Academic

The next question taken up was that of emigration and immigration, although the chairman pointed out that the discussion would be purely academic, since there is a practical ban on immigration in all receiving countries, while in addition, there is an increasing recognition that mass emigration fails to solve the problem, even if there are no regulations against it. That emigration may help the emigrant himself and, within certain limits, such as relief of labour pressure, by remittances from abroad and by introduction of higher standards of living by returned nationals, may aid the country of departure, was agreed unanimously. When, however, emigration depopulates certain sections of industries, when it is so small as to be negligible, or when the gap in the population is automatically filled by an increase in the birth rate or decrease in the death rate, then it proves a hindrance to the solution of the question, it was declared.

As to immigration, the delegates agreed that it serves to assist the receiving nation by increasing production and consumption, but these benefits cease when the saturation point is reached. When that point is attained, however, is difficult to designate, they declared, inasmuch as the question of sentiment in the receiving country is largely to be considered. The mass emigration from Ireland to the United States, when America was under-populated, was the last example, perhaps, of a real solution of this problem in modern times, it was pointed out.

The chairmen in charge of "round table" discussions yesterday were Camille Pone, Mr. Paul Scharrenburg, Mr. K. Ayusawa and Mr. A. Benitez. To-day three of the "round tables" will discuss the question of "Diplomatic Machinery in the Pacific" and one "round table" "Dependencies and Native Peoples."

（批：Registry Attach to Factory Law file MR. 28/10）

《字林西报》，1931年10月27日，星期二
(12)
5494
1931年10月29日。

讨论工厂法
学会代表同意教育必须先行于执法

根据昨日在太平洋国际学会会议第四届会议上表达的观点，只有当公众普遍受教育并认识到其益处时，最近颁布的、引起当地和国际极大关注的中国工厂法的益处才能得到充分实现。该次会议讨论了这一问题，以及当地的劳工状况、中国人的生活水平和人口限制问题。

在构成此次会议的“圆桌”辩论中指出，成功实施《工厂法》的其他障碍包括：雇主缺乏进行必要改进所需的足够资金、大多数工人的极度贫困以及全国普遍的政治局势不稳。讨论导致代表们分为两组，一组采纳“现实主义”观点，另一组采纳“理想主义”观点，因为该法律公认地设定了一个高于目前中国大多数工厂能够立即执行的标准。现实主义者表示，当一部更为保守的法律能产生立竿见影的实际效益时，设定无法达到的标准是一个错误。理想主义者认为，即使其实现只是渐进的，更高的标准最终会带来更多的好处。

标准之差异

然而，国际劳工局代表团的一名成员提出了第三种观点，他表示，他认为争议中的分歧与其说是“理想主义”与“现实主义”之间的分歧，不如说是法律标准的差异问题：在本例中，即英国方法与欧洲方法之间的差异。该代表继续说道，按照英国标准，法律是精确定义应做之事的东西，并期望这些规定得到不折不扣的执行。另一方面，他解释说，许多欧洲法律设定了要达到的标准以及达到该标准的机制，期望最终结果一步步实现。因此，据称，在制定中国工厂法规时，其支持者心中可能存有欧洲大陆的标准。

谈到与该法相关的教育问题，代表们一致认为，争取公众舆论和支持至关重要，他们持有这样的观点：如果缺乏这一点，任何法律都无法成功实施。然而，人们注意到这样一个事实，在中国超过4亿的总人口中，只有1000万人能以某种方式受到该法案的影响，而对于更大比例的人口来说，存在着比正在讨论的问题更为严重的问题。

讨论纯属学术性质

接下来讨论的问题是移民和入境，尽管主席指出，这种讨论将纯粹是学术性的，因为所有接收国实际上都禁止移民，此外，人们越来越认识到，即使没有针对大规模移民的规定，它也无法解决问题。大家一致同意，移民可能有助于移民者本人，并且在一定限度内，例如通过缓解劳动力压力、通过来自海外的汇款以及通过回国国民引入更高的生活水平，可能有助于输出国。然而，有人宣称，当移民使某些行业部门人口减少时，当移民数量少到可以忽略不计时，或者当人口缺口通过出生率增加或死亡率降低而自动填补时，事实证明这会阻碍问题的解决。

关于入境，代表们同意，它通过增加生产和消费来帮助接收国，但当达到饱和点时，这些好处就会停止。然而，他们宣称，很难指明何时达到该点，因为在很大程度上要考虑接收国的情绪问题。有人指出，在美国人口稀少的时期，从爱尔兰到美国的大规模移民，也许是现代真正解决这一问题的最后一个例子。

昨天负责“圆桌”讨论的主席是卡米尔·波内（Camille Pone，音译）、保罗·沙伦伯格（Paul Scharrenburg，音译）先生、K. 绫泽（K. Ayusawa，音译）先生和A. 贝尼特斯（A. Benitez，音译）先生。今天，三个“圆桌”将讨论“太平洋地区的外交机制”问题，一个“圆桌”将讨论“属地与土著人民”问题。

Formation of Factory Management Examination Committee of
the Social Bureau of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai.

The China Times and other local newspapers publish
the following report:-

A Committee known as the "Factory Management Research
Committee" was formerly organized by the Social Bureau to
study ways and means to improve the management of factories.
Since the enforcement of the Factory Law, the Social Bureau
considers that there must be some urgent need for improve-
ment of the factory equipment and in this connection
proposes to extend the existing "Factory Management
Research Committee" by reorganizing it into the "Factory
Management Examination Committee of the Social Bureau of
the Municipality of Greater Shanghai'.

The following are the regulations governing the
"Factory Management Examination Committee of the Social
Bureau of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai":-

Article 1. This Committee has as its mission to
examine and devise ways to improve the equipment and
management of factories in the Municipality.

Article II. This Committee comprises 15 members to be
appointed by the Chief of the Social Bureau, one of whom
will act as chairman.

Article III. When necessary, this Committee will
convene a meeting of experts of the various industries
to be invited by the Social Bureau.

Article IV. The regular meetings will be held by
this Committee every month and provisional meetings will
be called for by the Chairman when necessary.

Article V. The resolutions passed by this Committee
have to be submitted to the Social Bureau for approval and
enforcement.

大上海市政府社会局工厂管理检查委员会之成立。

《时报》及其他本地报纸刊登如下报道：-

社会局此前组织了一个名为“工厂管理研究委员会”的委员会，以研究改善工厂管理的方法和手段。自从《工厂法》实施以来，社会局认为迫切需要对工厂设备进行改进，为此提议通过重组现有的“工厂管理研究委员会”，将其扩展为“大上海市政府社会局工厂管理检查委员会”。

以下是管辖“大上海市政府社会局工厂管理检查委员会”的规章：-

第一条. 本委员会的任务是审查并制定改善本市工厂设备和管理的方法。

第二条. 本委员会由社会局局长任命的15名委员组成，其中一人担任主席。

第三条. 必要时，本委员会将召开由各行业专家组成的会议，专家由社会局邀请。

第四条. 本委员会每月举行定期会议，必要时由主席召集临时会议。

第五条. 本委员会通过的决议须提交社会局批准并执行。

the Social Bureau to notify factory managers, engineers or
representatives of workers concerned to be present at this
Committee's meeting for the purpose of expressing their
opinions.

Article VII. This Committee may, when necessary, commissio
officers to conduct investigations in factories or other
places which have direct connection with matters already
examined and discussed.

Article VIII. The presence of two-thirds of the members
of this Committee is considered to constitute a quorum for
meetings. Decisions at meetings will be decided by the
majority of those present.

Article IX. Resolutions passed by this Committee are
not to be made public unless approved by the Social Bureau.

Article X. The affairs of the secretariat, etc. of this

Article XI. The affairs of this Committee may be
conducted by sections revised regulations governing which
will be enacted separately.

Article XII. The present regulations may be amended

Article XIII. The present regulations will come into
force on the date of their approval by the Municipality of
Greater Shanghai.

The Hsin Pao and other local newspapers publish the following report:-
At 1 p.m. yesterday the Bureau of Social Affairs of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai held a meeting to mediate the dispute between the printers and their employers over the enforcement of the new factory law. The representatives of the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang, of the Shanghai Printing Shopkeepers Association and the Printers Union were present. Representatives of both sides insisted on their own views and a heated debate ensued.
The Bureau advised them to peacefully resume work temporarily pending results of the Bureau's mediation. The Bureau assured the workers that should an nine hour working day prove indispensable for the benefit of their employers business, they would be paid extra for the one hour worked.

August 4, 1931.

The Min Pao and other local newspapers
publish the following reports:-
The local stereotype workers voluntarily
reduced their working time to 8 hours a day on August 1,
in accordance with the enforcement of factory law.
Following this occasion, the local Stereotype Trade
Association yesterday held a meeting at which they decided
to temporarily suspend business as the result of the
present hard times. They sent a representative to
the Bureau of Social Affairs and
also issued a circular notice to all members requesting
them to act together.
The Local Stereotype Workers Union also
met at 9 a.m. yesterday, and detailed a
representative to present the following demands to the
Bureau of Social Affairs:-
(1) That the employees of the concern be ordered
to resume work immediately.
(2) That the Stereotype Trade Association be punished
for instigating its members to suspend business.
(3) That the Bureau should mediate in this case
immediately.
On the other hand, the Stereotype Trade
Association yesterday submitted the following demands to
the Bureau:-
(1) That the unrestrained action of the Stereotype
workers union be strictly prohibited.
(2) That the Chinese workers may be restored in order
to maintain the business.
Both demands were accepted by the Bureau
of Social Affairs.
An emergency members meeting was held
yesterday afternoon by the Stereotype Trade Association at
which the following resolutions were passed:-
(1) That the business be permanently suspended
until the workers resume the Chinese working
day.
(2) That a second petition be submitted to the Bureau
of Social Affairs explaining the difficulties
they have encountered.
(3) That letters be sent to the local Chamber of
Commerce and various associations of the concern
urging them to render assistance.
(4) That a general meeting be held on August 4.

《民少报》及其他本地报纸刊登如下报道：—
鉴于国民政府决定工厂法应于8月1日施行，J.C.C.（注：可能指上海公共租界工部局或相关商会机构，原文缩写未展开，依惯例保留或视语境理解，此处依原文直译或保留缩写，但根据上下文“Council”及上海背景，通常指代某理事会或商会，此处暂按原文逻辑翻译为“理事会”或保留缩写，考虑到前文有Chamber of Commerce，此处J.C.C.极可能是Chinese Chamber of Commerce即上海总商会的误植或特定缩写，但为严谨起见，若无法确定则保留或译为通用称呼。结合历史背景，8月1日工厂法实施主要涉及中方机构，此处“J.C.C.”在当时的英文档案中常指“Junior Chamber of Commerce”或笔误。然而看下文“The Council”，更可能是指某个具体的委员会。鉴于不确定性，此处保留J.C.C.或译为“该会”。根据后文“The Council is of the opinion”，译为“理事会”较为稳妥，或者如果是指上海总商会，通常会写SCC。此处暂译为“该会”或保留J.C.C.。为了符合“能确定的用当时通行中文”，若J.C.C.确指上海总商会，应译为上海总商会。但在1931年语境下，有时J.C.C.指代不明。让我们看上下文，它是在讨论国家法律的实施。这里暂译为“该会（J.C.C.）”以保持准确，或者根据常见错误，可能是SCC (Shanghai Chinese Chamber)。但既然要求不确定保留原文，这里我将保留J.C.C.并在必要时加注，或者直接译为“该会”。再看要求3，“不确定的保留原文并加括号注明(音译)”。J.C.C.是缩写，不是人名地名。通常这类缩写如果是机构，最好查证。但在翻译任务中，若无法百分百确定，保留原文是安全的。不过，考虑到这是给警务处的报告，J.C.C.很可能是指 Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce (上海总商会) 的笔误或者是 Junior Chamber? 不，更有可能是 **S**hanghai **C**hinese **C**hamber of **C**ommerce 的误写，或者就是 **C**hinese **C**hamber of **C**ommerce。让我们看下一段 "The Council"。在很多档案中，CCF 或 SCC 常见。这里我选择保留 J.C.C. 并视其为机构名。
*修正思考*：根据历史档案习惯，J.C.C. 有时指 "Joint Consultative Committee" 或其他。但在此处语境下，讨论工厂法，最有影响力的是上海总商会。然而，为了严格遵守“不确定保留原文”，我将保留 J.C.C.。

鉴于国民政府决定工厂法应于8月1日施行，J.C.C. 于7月27日召开会议讨论此事。
理事会认为，作为实施工厂法的第一步，目前应解决下列问题：—
(1) 日班和夜班的工作时间。
(2) 对童工年龄的限制。
(3) 假期天数。
(4) 关于向在工作中受伤及患病劳工支付赔偿的事宜。
(5) 工资。
(6) 给予生育女工的抚恤金。
(7) 对学徒的限制。
(8) 建立旨在讨论雇员和雇主利益相关事项的机构。
(9) 工厂事务记录。

INTERNAL Information of Factory Law

According to officials of the Social Bureau of the
Municipality of Greater Shanghai, the new Factory Law
will become effective from August 1, 1931, in pursuance with
the order of the Nationalist Government, despite the
repeated petitions of local industrial concerns for a
further postponement of its enforcement. It is
reported that the Bureau has decided to apply the new law
to both foreign and Chinese concerns, and members of the
Inspection Section of the 3rd Department of the Bureau will
be detailed on dates to be fixed later to visit various
local factories for the purpose of ascertaining if the new
law is being obeyed. Provisions have been made by the
Bureau that small factories may not be restricted by the
conditions of the law.

It is reported that according to the investigation
conducted during past month by the Bureau in conjunction
with other organizations, there are in Shanghai 61 cotton
mills, employing 127,004 persons; 106 silk filatures employing
51,376 persons; 108 (cotton) weaving mills, employing 7,025
persons; 7 match factories employing 2,686 persons and
11 oil factories employing 1,981 persons.

The China Press and other local newspapers publish the following report:—

It was proposed, at first, to make the new law effective in the month of February this year. At the request of various parties and likewise with a view to arranging the whole matter in a satisfactory manner, the Minister of Industry postponed the date of its enforcement for six months, and now it is reported that a amendment from last month will be officially introduced.

Mr. Yü T'ang-ming, chief of the Labour Department of the Ministry of Industry, who arrived in Shanghai yesterday, was interviewed by a reporter of this paper regarding the details of the Factory Law and made the following statement:—

1. Article No. 11 of the Factory Law, governing the night work of female workers, will be suspended for two years; this resolution was discussed and passed by the Central Political Committee Meeting of the Nanking Government, held yesterday.
2. The enforcement of the article stipulating full pay on holidays has not yet been decided.
3. The problem as to whether representatives of factory proprietors are so qualified to attend factory conferences will be settled soon.

Lecture on Factory System

A lecture on the factory system was delivered by Hou
Dah-tsung (后大椿), former delegate representing local
labour unions to the People's Convention, between 4.15 and
5.0 p.m. June 24 under the auspices of and in the office
of the Chinese Y.W.C.A., 395 Nanking Road, before some
twenty women representatives of various local organisations.
The following is a resume of the suggestions aiming at the
improval of the factory system in China, outlined by him
in the course of his speech.

1. That the 8-hour working system should be adopted so
that labourers can rest and child workers have time
to receive education.

2. In the event of serious sickness or death of workers,
the factory management should assist.

3. When the factory management has proper cause to
dismiss workers, the latter should be given due notice
of such and should be paid a retiring gratuity
(to be determined by the Government), as it is not
easy for them to obtain fresh employment.

4. Female workers with children should be allowed to
suckle them two or three times a day.

5. Yearly profits should be distributed as follows:
40 to the shareholders, 40 to the workers and 20
to the management.

6. Special bonuses should be paid to good workers at
the end of each year.

In conclusion he advised the representatives present
to assist women workers, if possible, and warn them
not to do night work which impairs their health and
hinders them from looking after their families.

关于工厂制度的讲座

6月24日下午4时15分至5时，在南京路395号中华基督教女青年会办公室，由该会主办，前代表本地工会出席人民会议的代表后大椿（Hou Dah-tsung）向约二十名本地各组织的女性代表发表了关于工厂制度的演讲。以下是他在演讲中概述的旨在改善中国工厂制度的建议摘要。

1. 应采用八小时工作制，以便劳工休息，童工有时间接受教育。

2. 若工人患重病或死亡，厂方应提供协助。

3. 当厂方有正当理由解雇工人时，应给予适当通知，并支付退休金（由政府确定），因为他们很难找到新的工作。

4. 有子女的女工应被允许每天哺乳两到三次。

5. 年度利润分配如下：股东占40%，工人占40%，管理层占20%。

6. 每年年底应向优秀工人发放特别奖金。

最后，他建议在场的代表尽可能协助女工，并告诫她们不要从事损害健康且妨碍照顾家庭的夜班工作。

Bureau of Social Affairs to Settle Controversy
over Labour Working Hours.

The Shun Pao and other local newspapers publish
the following report:-

Since the enforcement of the Factory Law, the
question of working hours has been the object of frequent
dispute between the employers and employees. The former
favour lengthening the working day whereas the latter want
to reduce it as much as possible.

"With a view to alleviating the trouble, the
Bureau of Social Affairs submitted the following suggestion
to the Municipality of Greater Shanghai for consideration:-

"Any factory coming under the following five classifications
will be permitted to extend the working day to ten hours:-

1. Factories engaged in new industries.
2. Factories manufacturing dangerous articles.
3. Factories the productions of which are intended for
international competition.
4. Factories the productions of which do not affect the
health of workers.
5. Factories whose employers and employees both agree to
lengthen the daily working hours."

The Municipality of Greater Shanghai transmitted
the above suggestions to the Ministry of Industries and
received a reply stating that with the exception of categories
4 and 5 they can be considered adoptable. Category No. 4
should be slightly modified to read:- "Factories, the work of
which is easy and not injurious to the workers' health." The
5th category absolutely contradicts the spirit of the Factory
Law and is unsuitable.

社会局拟解决劳工工作时间争议。

《申报》及其他本地报纸刊登如下报道：

自《工厂法》实施以来，工作时间问题一直是雇主与雇员之间频繁争议的焦点。前者倾向于延长工作日，而后者则希望尽可能缩短工作时间。

“为缓解这一麻烦，社会局向大上海市政府提交了以下建议供考虑：

‘凡属于以下五类的工厂，允许将工作日延长至十小时：

1. 从事新兴行业的工厂。
2. 制造危险物品的工厂。
3. 产品旨在参与国际竞争的工厂。
4. 产品不影响工人健康的工厂。
5. 雇主和雇员双方均同意延长每日工作时间的工厂。’”

大上海市政府将上述建议转呈实业部，并收到回复称，除第4类和第5类外，其他类别可考虑采纳。第4类应稍作修改，改为：“工作轻松且不损害工人健康的工厂。”第5类完全违背《工厂法》的精神，是不合适的。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
C. I. D. REGIS.
No. A. O. 3492/11.
Date..4..-..6..-..31.

CHINA'S FACTORY LAW
...............

In formulating factory law many foreign countries have thus
far been guided ingeneral by the well-thought-out principle
of gradual application and eventual achievement of the law.
The legislators have, therefore, made a point not to dis-
locate living condition of the industrial workers, while
they have done everything they saw fit to promote the work-
ers' interests for instance legal provisions against the
mills so harmful to the health. The usual pratice of the
legislations was to furnish factory law with a certain margin
of years enough to allow the industrial circles of a country
to adjust itself to new order of thing, that they may be able
to come fully to appreciate the spirit of the law without any
abrupt changes detrimental to the legitimate continuation of
their business enterprises.
To quote an example from a foreign country legislative endea-
vour in Japan was first used in this direction in 1887, when
Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce drew up factory workers'
act with regulations in respect of apprenticeship consisting
of articles 46 and 31 respectively. Next came a factory law
in draft form provided with 35 articles, which was prepared
by Department of Public Works. Having had some revisions
page_data.zh:
上海公共租界
刑事侦缉处登记
编号：A. O. 3492/11。
日期：1931年6月4日。

中国的工厂法
...............

在制定工厂法方面，许多外国迄今为止大体上遵循着经过深思熟虑的原则，即逐步实施并最终实现该法律。因此，立法者特别注意不扰乱产业工人的生活状况，同时尽其认为适当之所能以促进工人的利益，例如制定针对严重损害健康的工厂的法律条款。立法的通常做法是为工厂法提供一定的年限缓冲期，足以让一个国家的工业界适应新的秩序，使其能够在不对企业的合法持续经营造成任何有害的突变的情况下，充分领会法律的精神。
举一个外国立法努力的例子，日本在此方向上的首次尝试是在1887年，当时农商务部起草了《工厂工人法》，其中关于学徒的规定分别由第46条和第31条组成。随后，工务局准备了一份包含35条的工厂法草案。经过一些修订

page_data.en:
- 2 -
effected and turned into a law the draft composing of 40 articles
was referred to various chambers of commerce for opinion in the
following year. On the other hand the government authorities
started to conduct a thorough investigation into conditions
then obtaining at mills, factories, and the like. In 1900 an
Imperial Edict called for the formation of Special Enquiry Comm-
ission into matters of several industrial plants. The Commission
duly nominated framed 14 outstanding items to be incorporated
into the factory law and be referred to different parties inte-
rested for consideration. This resulted into completion by the
Commission in 1909 of a factory law bill comprising 23 articles,
which was again made a subject of reference to the general public.
According to the bill, the women and the minors under 16 years of
age are prohibited from attending to work in the small hours of
night five years after the promulgation of the factory law, which
period of time was subsequently revised by Ministry of Home as to
ten years. It was in 1909 that the bill was submitted to the
Imperial Diet at Tokyo, but the Government had really to shelve
the bill due to the night work clause proving itself a veritable
stumbling block in the way of passing through the House.
Whereupon the Government sent out to numerous private quarters
a questionnaire made up of 23 items. The Investigation Committee
on Industrial and Allied Affairs, whose opinion had ultimately
been sought, suggested a few revisions in the factory law under
page_data.zh:
- 2 -
并转化为法律后，这份由40条组成的草案于次年提交给各商会征求意见。另一方面，政府当局开始对当时纱厂、工厂等处的状况进行彻底调查。1900年，一道敕令要求成立特别调查委员会，调查若干工业企业的相关事宜。该委员会适时提名并制定了14个突出事项，拟纳入工厂法，并提交给各方利益相关者审议。这导致委员会于1909年完成了一份包含23条的工厂法法案，该法案再次被提交给公众参考。根据该法案，妇女和16岁以下未成年人在工厂法颁布五年后，禁止在深夜时段工作，该期限后来被内务省修订为十年。该法案于1909年提交至东京帝国议会，但由于夜间工作条款成为通过议会的真正障碍，政府不得不将该法案束之高阁。于是，政府向众多私人机构发出了一份由23个项目组成的问卷。最终征询其意见的工业及相关事务调查委员会建议对正在考虑中的工厂法进行一些修订。

page_data.en:
- 3 -
contemplation. With the Government's concurrence given to the
revisions the draft law came at last to assume a more worthy
character. The most conspicuous of the revisions is an exten-
tion from 10 to 15 years necessary for preparation, before the
aforesaid night work may be prohibited.
The factory law bill was passed at the 27th session of the Im-
perial Diet in 1911 and made a law in March of the same year.
Thus it will be seen that the formulation of a factory law
containing not more than 25 articles took the Japanese Govern-
ment 30 long years since Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce
had started to carry out necessary investigation, indeed 25
years intervening between the first drafting and the final con-
summation of the law. Even then the law did not become opera-
tive until five years afterwards that is in September of the
year 1916.
Following on the outbreak of the Great War there took place in
Japan an industrial boom and a marked change in general trend
of thought so much so that keen necessity was soon felt of int-
roducing several amendments in the factory law. On the estab-
lishment of Social Affairs Bureau in Ministry of Home in 1922
the first thing the Bureau did was to see how such amendments
could best be effected. Five articles, which should constitute
essential points of the amendments were published and referred to
quite a great number of parties concerned for opinion. The Im-
page_data.zh:
- 3 -
在政府同意这些修订后，法律草案终于具备了更值得推崇的性质。其中最显著的修订是将上述禁止夜间工作所需的准备时间从10年延长至15年。
工厂法法案于1911年在帝国议会第27次会议上获得通过，并于同年3月成为法律。由此可见，制定一部不超过25条的工厂法，日本政府自农商务部开始进行必要调查以来，耗时长达30年之久；实际上，从初次起草到法律最终完成，中间间隔了25年。即便如此，该法律直到五年后，即1916年9月，才正式生效。
随着大战的爆发，日本出现了工业繁荣，总体思想趋势发生了显著变化，以至于人们很快感到有必要对工厂法引入几项修正案。1922年内务省设立社会局后，该局所做的第一件事就是研究如何最好地实施这些修正案。构成修正案要点的五条规定被公布，并提交给大量相关方征求意见。帝国

page_data.en:
- 4 -
perial Diet approved and passed the factory law amendment
bill with regulations stipulating 11 articles on Workers'
minimum age in February 1923. And due promulgation of both
of these was made just one month later. Because of the
appaling earthquake-conflagration at Tokyo the Japanese Govern-
ment put off until July 1926 the enactment of the new factory
law, which has remained in operation ever since.
The prohibition of child labour under 16 years of age and
female night workers originally intended to enforce in 1926,
that is after the lapse of 15 years as from the year 1911 was,
however, given another three years of grace, that the same
actually commenced to take effect as lately as July 1929.
Looking back on the legislative efforts over industrial plants
here in China regulations of a provisional nature was issued
first by Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce in 1923 but
failed to see enforcement. The regulations were intended for
application to mills, factories, and so forth with regular
workers more than 100 or wherever employees are asked to attend
to work of a dangerous or pds@nous nature. So they were very
much limited in scope, and in fact having none of provisions
on inspection, disciplinary measures.
In 1926 the Political Executive Council of Hupei Province issu-
ed a provisional factory law act composing of 23 articles to
be enforced in connection with mills, factories, and so forth
page_data.zh:
- 4 -
议会于1923年2月批准并通过了工厂法修正案法案，其中规定了关于工人最低年龄的11条条例。这两部法律均在一个月后正式颁布。由于东京发生了可怕的地震火灾，日本政府将新工厂法的施行推迟至1926年7月，该法自此一直有效。
原本打算在1926年实施的禁止16岁以下童工和女性夜间工作的规定，即从1911年起算15年后，又被给予了三年的宽限期，因此实际上直到1929年7月才真正开始生效。
回顾中国此处针对工业企业的立法努力，农商务部于1923年首先发布了一项临时性质的规章，但未能得到执行。该规章旨在适用于拥有100名以上正规工人的纱厂、工厂等，或雇员被要求从事危险或有毒性质工作的场所。因此，其适用范围非常有限，事实上没有任何关于检查和纪律措施的条款。
1926年，湖北省政治执行委员会发布了一项由23条组成的临时工厂法法案，拟在与拥有20名以上雇员的纱厂、工厂等，或处理危险材料的制造企业中强制执行。

page_data.en:
- 5 -

with over 20 workers in employ or manufacturing establishments handling dangerous materials. Provisions were set forth in the law over wage, working hour, child and female labour, and many other items. At the same time the provincial authorities prepared regulations necessary for organizations of Hupei Industrial Supervision Commission to deal with matters such as inspection of various manufacturing plants, settlement of labour dispute. It failed however to be materialized. The year 1927 saw the drafting of a factory law by Bureau of Agriculture and Industry at Canton. In the same year Ministry of Agriculture and Industry in Peking Government gave a new name of Peking Factory Law to a provisional factory act issued by its predecessor, Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce. Having had farther revisions made the law now embodying 27 articles mainly on factory inspections was quite ready for promulgation, but the political disturbances then prevailed, made the law never to see the light.
The Hopei provincial government published in 1929 a provisional factory law together with a set of regulations with special reference to factory inspection. In December 1929 the National Government at Nanking promulgated a factory law, which was to have been enacted throughout the Republic of China as from the first of February this year. This brings us back to the theme subject of the present paper.
page_data.zh:
- 5 -

该法律规定了工资、工作时间、童工和女工以及许多其他项目。同时，省级当局准备了组织湖北工业监督委员会所需的规章，以处理检查各类制造厂、解决劳资纠纷等事项。然而，这未能实现。1927年，广州农工局起草了一部工厂法。同年，北京政府的农工部将其前任农商务部发布的临时工厂法案重新命名为《北京工厂法》。经过进一步修订，该法现在包含主要关于工厂检查的27条，已准备好颁布，但当时的政治动荡使得该法从未问世。
河北省政府于1929年公布了一项临时工厂法及一套特别涉及工厂检查的规章。1929年12月，南京国民政府颁布了一部工厂法，原定于今年2月1日起在整个中华民国施行。这使我们回到了本文的主题。

page_data.en:
- 6 -

It is of no small interest to observe what conditions actually
obtained in recent years in the industrial circles here in
China. Those factories, mills and so on under native manage-
ment do not go very much higher in scale than old-fashioned
domestic enterprises excepting for spinning and weaving indus-
try. Ever since May 4th incident labour movement has, the
writer is prepared to admit, been much in evidence towards le-
gislative recognition of the workers' aspirations. The move-
ment has, however, never been backed by a self-awakening on
the part of workers as well as an urgent necessity in social
development. Behind the scene there lurks the Soviet Govern-
ment's machinations coupled with an anti-foreign feeling.
The National Government's action has, since they started to
devote themselves for abolition of all so-called "unequal
treaties" some time back, been marked with direct imitation
of things initiated in the far advanced foreign countries, no
matter whether or not such are unmistakably consistent with
special conditions in Chinese industrial and commercial cir-
cles. The fundamental idea of imitation is beyond doubt praise-
worthy, but in this case offers a good example of putting the
cart before the horse as we may observe in so many other ins-
tances in today's China. In reality nothing could be more reck-
lessly absurd than an attempt to put the factory law under dis-
cussion in effect when everybody is well aware that its enfor-
cement is next to impossible.
page_data.zh:
- 6 -

观察近年来中国工业界的实际状况是颇有趣味的。除了纺织业外，那些由华人管理的工厂、纱厂等的规模并不比老式的家庭企业高多少。自五四运动以来，笔者承认，劳工运动在争取立法认可工人诉求方面表现得十分明显。然而，这场运动从未得到工人自身觉醒以及社会发展迫切需求的支持。幕后潜伏着苏联政府的阴谋以及反外情绪。
自从国民政府前段时间致力于废除所有所谓的“不平等条约”以来，其行动特点是直接模仿先进国家发起的事物，无论这些事物是否与中国工商业界的特殊条件明显一致。模仿的基本理念无疑是值得称赞的，但在这种情况下，正如我们在当今中国的许多其他实例中所观察到的那样，这是一个本末倒置的好例子。实际上，当每个人都清楚其执行几乎不可能时，试图使正在讨论中的工厂法生效，没有什么比这更鲁莽荒谬的了。

page_data.en:
- 7 -

Let us now proceed to review the salient features in the new-
ly prepared factory law in the light of the conditions now-
adays obtaining here in China.
a) Working Hour:
Only at a few of the industrial plants under foreign manage-
ment work is limited to from nine hours to ten, and yet even
this limit is used as a facility more often in working out
wages than in safeguarding the employees' welfare, with
the result that they are generally obliged to remain on duty
somewhat longer against an extra pay. There is at Tientsin
a cotton mill, which adopted the eight hour day system.
It has met, we are told, with an indifferent success, since
their real aim was to make two shifts of workers into three
in order to dispense with the difficulty of discharging
so many workers all at once. The rest of the plants has
daily working hours of from 10 to 12, whereas those run by the
Chinese require workers' daily attendance of twelve hours in
general. The workers in the industries on a domestic scale
remain on duty more often than not for 13 to 14 hours.
Now the Chinese Government is about to curtail the working
hour so abruptly and put the eight hour day system into effect,
allowing an extension to ten hours in the case of condition,
local and commercial, justifying such a deviation. However in
view of absence of a concrete definition of the condition the
page_data.zh:
- 7 -

现在，让我们根据目前在中国存在的状况，来审视新制定的工厂法的主要特征。
a) 工作时间：
只有在少数由外国人管理的工业企业中，工作时间限制在九到十小时，而且即使这一限制也更多地被用作计算工资的手段，而非保障员工福利，结果是他们通常被迫稍微延长值班时间以换取额外报酬。天津有一家棉纺厂采用了八小时工作制。据称，其成效平平，因为其真实目的是将两班工人改为三班，以避免一次性解雇大量工人的困难。其余工厂的每日工作时间为10至12小时，而由中国人经营的工厂通常要求工人每日出勤12小时。家庭式工业中的工人往往值班13至14小时。
现在，中国政府正准备如此突然地缩短工作时间并实施八小时工作制，允许在地方和商业条件证明有此必要时延长至十小时。然而，鉴于对这些条件缺乏具体定义，

page_data.en:
- 8 -

eight hour day system is most likely to become order of the
day.
Putting aside the matter of female workers just for argument's
sake here the application of the new factory law would necessitate
a change of shifting arrangement of the workers from the pre-
sent two to three at the industrial plants, where make workers
only are employed. The Changed then would bring about two
alternatives - namely either the industrial plants bear the
payment of wages raised by fifty per cent as compared with
hitherto or the workers put up with a decrease in wages caused
by the loss of so many hours. Both of which are an utter im-
practicability. This very fact speaks most eloquently for the
wisdom of extending the working hour by degrees instead of all
at once.
The factory law also provides for an extension to 12 working
hours in order to meet special circumstances arising out of
disturbances, elemental, political or otherwise. Yet such pro-
vision should really be regarded as only an emergency measure
to be taken once in a long while. Besides one can not see the
reason why the working hour has to be extended in the case of
disturbances.
Mention must be made in this respect of the fact that the fac-
tory law in operation in Japan today specifies nothing at all
as to the working hour of adult employees.
b) Recreation and Holidays :
page_data.zh:
- 8 -

八小时工作制很可能会成为常态。
暂且不论女工问题，仅就论证而言，新工厂法的实施将 necessitate（需要）在仅雇佣男工的工业企业中，将工人的轮班安排从目前的两班改为三班。这种改变将带来两种选择——即要么工业企业承担比迄今高出百分之五十的工资支付，要么工人忍受因损失如此多工作时间而导致的工资减少。这两种情况都完全不可行。这一事实最有力地证明了逐步而非一次性延长工作时间的明智性。
工厂法还规定，为了应对因骚乱、自然灾害、政治或其他原因产生的特殊情况，工作时间可延长至12小时。然而，此类规定应被视为仅在极少数情况下采取的紧急措施。此外，人们看不出在骚乱情况下必须延长工作时间的理由。
在这方面必须提到的是，目前在日本施行的工厂法对成年雇员的工作时间根本没有任何规定。
b) 娱乐与假期：

page_data.en:
- 9 -

So far as the industrial establishments under foreign manage-
ment throughout China are concerned the workers are generally
given a certain amount of rest and recreation after a spell of
work every day and subsequent to a number of daily attendance.
The factory law under review however stipulates that the workers
be goven half-an-hour's rest after six hours' duty, one holiday
after seven days' attendance, and more than eight legal holi-
days each year, in addition to a vacation, the length of which
to be determined according to the years of service rendered -
all these days of absence with full wages paid.
To grant a few days of rest to the workers with full wages paid
does not mean any marked deviation from the present customs,
which makes it a rule to let the workers have a few days of
rest and an allowance as well at the beginning of new year.
Perhaps the worst feature we see under this item is the provi-
sion that the employees be granted a certain number of holidays
besides those legally fixed all with full wages paid, because
the same amounts to paying money to the "daily wage earners",
who do not attend to their daily work. The provision is so
wrong that one could hardly find anything like that in the fac-
tory law of other countries.
c) Child Labour :
In China due to the state of illiteracy and the universal custom
of early matrimony the workers, both male and female, are usually
page_data.zh:
- 9 -

就全中国由外国人管理的工业企业而言，工人在每日工作一段时间及连续出勤若干日后，通常会被给予一定的休息和娱乐时间。然而，正在审议的工厂法规定，工人每工作六小时后应给予半小时休息，每出勤七天给予一天休假，每年除根据服务年限确定长度的假期外，还应有八个以上的法定假日——所有这些缺勤日均全额支付工资。

给予工人几天带薪休息并不意味着与现行习俗有显著偏差，因为现行习俗规定在新年伊始让工人休息几天并发放津贴。也许在本项下我们看到的最糟糕之处是，规定雇员除了法定假日外还可享受一定数量的带薪假期，因为这等同于向那些未进行日常工作的“日薪劳动者”支付金钱。这一规定错误至极，在其他国家的工厂法中几乎找不到类似条款。

c) 童工：
在中国，由于文盲状态普遍以及早婚的习俗，工人，无论男女，通常都

page_data.en:
- 10 -

young, especially so in the case of apprenticeship. In fact at
silk filatures the operatives are almost entirely young girls.
According to the new factory law child labour under 16 years
of age is prohibited from working at night, while employment
is not permitted of the child less than 14 years. There is a
proviso to the effect that the child labour now in employ,
whose ages are over 12 may be allowed to retain its work. The
two years difference in age limit is, the writer thinks, too
small to be of legal merit. One can easily imagine what un-
welcome effect the prohibition of child labour would bring on
the industrial circles in China.
d) Female Worker :
The prohibition of female workers' night work like that of
child labour is certain to have a great deal of influence on
the industrial world. Should the female workers be prohibit-
ed in this way, it would lead either to throw one half of
their number out of employment or to divide them into two shifts
each of eight hours. The seriousness of the possible conse-
quences shows quite clearly how important the provision is to
allow a reasonable amount of time for preparation of the pro-
hibition.
As stated elsewhere in Japan the Government authorities fixed
first the time of 15 years for the preparation, and then added
another three years to make it 18 years in all, the prohibition
page_data.zh:
- 10 -

很年轻，学徒情况尤其如此。事实上，在缫丝厂中，操作工几乎全是年轻女孩。根据新工厂法，禁止16岁以下童工从事夜间工作，同时不得雇佣14岁以下儿童。但有一项附带规定，即目前受雇且年龄超过12岁的童工可被允许保留其工作。笔者认为，这两年的年龄限制差异太小，缺乏法律价值。人们不难想象，禁止童工将给中国工业界带来多么不受欢迎的影响。

d) 女工：
像禁止童工一样，禁止女工从事夜间工作肯定会对工业界产生巨大影响。如果以这种方式禁止女工工作，要么会导致半数女工失业，要么会将她们分为两班，每班八小时。可能产生的后果之严重，清楚地表明了为该禁令的实施预留合理准备时间的重要性。

如前文所述，在日本，政府当局首先确定了15年的准备期，后来又增加了三年，总共18年，该项性质的禁令实际上直到1929年7月才生效。这种鲁莽突兀的禁令，即使不与新工厂法中的其他破坏性因素相结合，也必然会给整个工业界带来无法挽回的灾难。

e) 工厂劳工委员会等：
鉴于中国目前的劳工状况，工厂法中关于工厂劳工委员会、工会参与合同签订及其他条款的规定均不合时宜。政府当局最好尝试制定提升劳工要素的方法和手段，至少暂时放弃制定工厂法的想法。

f) 福利工作等：
关于最低工资、福利工作等方面，相关规定的实施应根据有关各界的 prevailing conditions（现行条件）逐步进行。在此方面任何雄心勃勃的尝试，例如在极短时间内超越更先进的国家，对中国来说显然是不可取的。

在结束本文之际，笔者仅简要提及工厂法中某些规定的不切实际性质以及检查制度的不完善。首先，中国尚无准确的人口普查登记来证明一个人的年龄和其他具体情况。关于工资的规定措辞过于模糊，注定会成为

page_data.en:
- 11 -

of a nature in question came actually to take effect as lately
as in July 1929. The lecklessly abrupt prohibition, even if
not combined with other destructive elements in the new factory
law, would not fail to spell an unrecoverable disaster to the
industrial world at large.
e) Factory Labour Council etc.
Factory Labour council, union participation in contract and
other provisions in the factory law are all out of place in view
of the presnet stage of labour status here in China. The Govern-
ment authorities had better try to work out ways and means for
advancement of labour elements giving up the idea of factory
law at least for the time-being.
f) Welfare Work etc.
In respect of minimum wage, welfare work and so forth applica-
tion of provisions thereon should be made as by degrees subject
to conditions prevailing in the circles concerned. Any ambiti-
ous attempt in this connection such as to go ahead of the more
advanced countries in a very short space of time is certainly
unadvisable for China.
In concluding this paper the writer would refer just in brief
to the unpraticable nature of some provisions and the incomple-
teness of inspection system in the factory law. First of all
in China there is not yet accurate census registration to prove
one's age and other particulars. The provisions on wages are
set forth in term so vague that they are destined to become a
page_data.zh:
- 11 -

所涉性质的规定直至 1929 年 7 月才实际生效。这种轻率而突兀的禁令，即便不与新工厂法中的其他破坏性因素相结合，也必然会给整个工业界带来无法挽回的灾难。

dead letter. Practically nothing is mentioned in the way of
inspections, which is a most important element in the success-
ful institution of welfare work, safety accommodation, and

page_data.en:
June 3, 1931.

Comments on the new National Factory Law which have been
prepared by the Japanese Employers' Federation.

It is of no small interest to observe what conditions
actually obtained in recent years in the industrial circles
here in China. Those factories, mills and so on under na-
tive management do not go very much higher in scale than
old-fashioned domestic enterprises excepting for spinning
and weaving industry. Ever since May 4th incident labour
movement has, the writer is prepared to admit, been much
in evidence towards legislative recognition of the workers'
aspirations. The movement has, however, never been backed
by a self-awakening on the part of workers as well as an
urgent necessity in social development. Behind the scene
there lurks the Soviet Government's machinations coupled
with an anti-foreign feeling. The National Government's
action has, since they started to devote themselves for abo-
lition of all so-called "unequal treaties" some time back,
been marked with direct imitation of things initiated in
the far advanced foreign countries, no matter whether or
not such are unmistakably consistent with special condi-
tions in Chinese industrial and commercial circles. The
fundamental idea of imitation is beyond doubt praiseworthy,
but in this case offers a good example of putting the cart
before the horse as we may observe in so many other ins-
tances in today's China. In reality nothing could be more
recklessly absured than an attempt to put the factory law
under discussion in effect when everybody is well aware that
its enforcement is next to impossible.

Let us now proceed to review the salient features in the
newly prepared factory law in the light of the conditions
nowadays obtaining here in China.
page_data.zh:
1931年6月3日。

日本雇主联合会编制的关于新国家工厂法的评论意见。

观察近年来中国工业界的实际情况颇有趣味。除纺织业外，那些由中国人管理的工厂、纱厂等规模并不比旧式家庭企业大多少。自五四运动以来，笔者承认，劳工运动在争取立法认可工人诉求方面已十分显著。然而，这场运动从未得到工人自身觉醒以及社会发展迫切需求的支持。幕后潜伏着苏联政府的阴谋以及排外情绪。国民政府自从前段时间致力于废除所有所谓“不平等条约”以来，其行动特点便是直接模仿远较先进的外国事物，而不管这些事物是否明显符合中国工商业界的特殊条件。模仿的基本理念无疑值得称赞，但在本例中，正如我们在当今中国的许多其他实例中所见，这是一个本末倒置的好例子。实际上，当每个人都清楚其执行几乎不可能时，试图使正在讨论的工厂法生效，没有比这更鲁莽荒谬的了。

现在让我们根据目前中国的情况，回顾新制定的工厂法的主要特征。

a) Working Hour:
Only at a few of the industrial plants under foreign mana-
gement work is limited to from nine hours to ten, and yet
even this limit is used as a facility more often in working
out wages than in safeguarding the employees' welfare, with
the result that they are generally obliged to remain on
duty somewhat longer against an extra pay. There is at
Tientsin a cotton mill, which adopted the eight hour day
system. It has met, we are told, with an indifferent
success, since their real aim was to make two shifts of
workers into three in order to dispense with the difficulty
of discharging so many workers all at once. The rest of
the plants has daily working hours of from 10 to 12, whereas
those run by the Chinese require workers' daily attendance
of twelve hours in general. The workers in the industries
on a domestic scale remain on duty more often than not for
13 to 14 hours. Now the Chinese Government is about to
curtail the working hour so abruptly and put the eight hour
day system into effect, allowing an extension to ten hours
in the case of condition, local and commercial, justifying
such a deviation. However in view of absence of a concrete
definition of the condition the eight hour day system is
most likely to become order of the day.

Putting aside the matter of female workers just for
argument's sake here the application of the new factory law
would necessitate a change of shifting arrangement of the
workers from the present two to three at the industrial
plants, where male workers only are employed. The
change then would bring about two alternatives - namely
either the industrial plants bear the payment of wages
raised by fifty per cent as compared with hitherto or the
workers put up with a decrease in wages caused by the less

-5-

in the new factory law, would not fail to spell an unre-
coverable disaster to the industrial world at large.
e) Factory Labour Council etc.
Factory Labour council, union participation in contract and
other provisions in the factory law are all out of place in
view of the present stage of labour status here in China.
The Government authorities had better try to work out ways
and means for advancement of labour elements giving up the
idea of factory law at least for the time-being.
f) Welfare Work etc.
In respect of minimum wage, welfare work and so forth applica-
tion of provisions thereon should be made as by degrees subject
to conditions prevailing in the circles concerned. Any ambiti-
ous attempt in this connection such as to go ahead of the more
advance countries in a very short space of time is certainly
unadvisable for China.
    In concluding this paper the writer would refer just in
brief to the unpracticable nature of some provisions and the
incompleteness of inspection system in the factory law. First
of all in China there is not yet accurate census registration
to prove one's age and other particulars. The provisions on
wages are set forth in term so vague that they are destined
to become a dead letter. Practically nothing is mentioned
in the way of inspection, which is a most important element
in the successful institution of welfare work, safety accom-
modation, and sanitary arrangement, all of which we are
afraid will become a dead letter also.

...............

Shanghai, 7:3:31.
page_data.zh:
-5-

也必然会给整个工业界带来无法挽回的灾难。
e) 工厂劳工委员会等：
鉴于中国目前的劳工状况阶段，工厂法中关于工厂劳工委员会、工会参与合同签订及其他条款均不合时宜。政府当局最好设法制定提升劳工要素的途径和方法，至少暂时放弃制定工厂法的想法。
f) 福利工作等：
关于最低工资、福利工作等方面，相关规定的适用应根据有关各界的现行条件逐步进行。在此方面任何雄心勃勃的尝试，例如在极短时间内超越更先进的国家，对中国来说显然是不可取的。
在结束本文之际，笔者仅简要提及工厂法中某些条款的不切实际性以及检查制度的不完善。首先，中国尚无准确的人口普查登记来证明一个人的年龄及其他具体情况。关于工资的规定措辞过于模糊，注定会成为一纸空文。实际上，对于检查制度只字未提，而检查是成功实施福利工作、安全设施及卫生安排的最重要要素，我们担心这些也都将成为一纸空文。

...............

上海，1931年3月7日。

page_data.en:
June 3, 1931.

Comments on the new National Factory Law which have been
prepared by the Japanese Employers' Federation.

It is of no small interest to observe what conditions
actually obtained in recent years in the industrial circles
here in China. Those factories, mills and so on under na-
tive management do not go very much higher in scale than
old-fashioned domestic enterprises excepting for spinning
and weaving industry. Ever since May 4th incident labour
movement has, the writer is prepared to admit, been much
in evidence towards legislative recognition of the workers'
aspirations. The movement has, however, never been backed
by a self-awakening on the part of workers as well as an
urgent necessity in social development. Behind the scene
there lurks the Soviet Government's machinations coupled
with an anti-foreign feeling. The National Government's
action has, since they started to devote themselves for abo-
lition of all so-called "unequal treaties" some time back,
been marked with direct imitation of things initiated in
the far advanced foreign countries, no matter whether or
not such are unmistakably consistent with special condi-
tions in Chinese industrial and commercial circles. The
fundamental idea of imitation is beyond doubt praiseworthy,
but in this case offers a good example of putting the cart
before the horse as we may observe in so many other ins-
tances in today's China. In reality nothing could be more
recklessly absurd than an attempt to put the factory law
under discussion in effect when everybody is well aware that
its enforcement is next to impossible.

Let us now proceed to review the salient features in the
newly prepared factory law in the light of the conditions
nowadays obtaining here in China.
page_data.zh:
1931年6月3日。

日本雇主联合会编制的关于新国家工厂法的评论。

观察近年来中国工业界的实际状况颇有趣味。除纺织业外，那些由华人管理的工厂、纱厂等，其规模并不比旧式家庭企业高出多少。自五四运动以来，笔者承认，劳工运动在争取立法认可工人诉求方面已十分显著。然而，这场运动从未得到工人自身觉醒以及社会发展迫切需求的支持。幕后潜藏着苏联政府的阴谋策划以及排外情绪。国民政府自前段时间致力于废除所有所谓“不平等条约”以来，其行动特点在于直接模仿远较先进的外国举措，无论这些举措是否明显符合中国工商业界的特殊条件。模仿的基本理念无疑值得称赞，但在本例中，正如我们在当今中国许多其他场合所见，这是一个本末倒置的好例子。实际上，当所有人都清楚其执行几乎不可能时，试图使正在讨论的工厂法生效，没有比这更鲁莽荒谬的了。

现在，让我们根据目前中国的实际情况，回顾新制定的工厂法的主要特征。

page_data.en:
-2-

a) Working Hour:
Only at a few of the industrial plants under foreign mana-
gement work is limited to from nine hours to ten, and yet
even this limit is used as a facility more often in working
out wages than in safeguarding the employees' welfare, with
the result that they are generally obliged to remain on
duty somewhat longer against an extra pay. There is at
Tientsin a cotton mill, which adopted the eight hour day
system. It has met, we are told, with an indifferent
success, since their real aim was to make two shifts of
workers into three in order to dispense with the difficulty
of discharging so many workers all at once. The rest of
the plants has daily working hours of from 10 to 12, whereas
those run by the Chinese require workers' daily attendance
of twelve hours in general. The workers in the industries
on a domestic scale remain on duty more often than not for
13 to 14 hours. Now the Chinese Government is about to
curtail the working hour so abruptly and put the eight hour
day system into effect, allowing an extension to ten hours
in the case of condition, local and commercial, justifying
such a deviation. However in view of absence of a concrete
definition of the condition the eight hour day system is
most likely to become order of the day.

Putting aside the matter of female workers just for
argument's sake here the application of the new factory law
would necessitate a change of shifting arrangement of the
workers from the present two to three at the industrial
plants, where male workers only are employed. The
change then would bring about two alternatives - namely
either the industrial plants bear the payment of wages
raised by fifty per cent as compared with hitherto or the
workers put up with a decrease in wages caused by the loss
page_data.zh:
-2-

a) 工作时间：
只有在少数外资管理的工业企业中，工作时间限制在九至十小时，然而即使是这一限制，也更多地被用作计算工资的手段，而非保障员工福利，结果员工通常不得不稍微延长工作时间以换取额外报酬。天津有一家棉纺厂采用了八小时工作制。据称，其成效平平，因为其真正目的是将两班工人改为三班，以避免一次性解雇大量工人的困难。其余工厂的每日工作时间为10至12小时，而华资工厂通常要求工人每日出勤12小时。家庭式工业中的工人往往要工作13至14小时。现在，中国政府打算突然缩短工作时间并实施八小时工作制，允许在地方和商业条件证明有此必要时延长至十小时。然而，鉴于对这些条件缺乏具体定义，八小时工作制很可能成为常态。

暂且不论女工问题，仅就论证而言，新工厂法的实施将 necessitate（需要）在仅雇用男工的工业企业中，将工人的轮班安排从目前的两班改为三班。这种改变将带来两种选择——即要么工业企业承担比以往提高百分之五十的工资支付，要么工人忍受因损失

page_data.en:
-3-
of so many hours. Both of which are an utter impractic-
ability. This very fact speaks most eloquently for the
wisdom of extending the working hour by degrees instead of
all at once.
The factory law also provides for an extension to 12
working hours in order to meet special circumstances arising
out of disturbances, elemental, political or otherwise. Yet
such provision should really be regarded as only an emer-
gency measure to be taken once in a long while. Besides
one can not see the reason why the working hour has to be
extended in the case of disturbances.
Mention must be made in this respect of the fact that
the factory law in operation in Japan today specifies nothing
at all as to the working hour of adult employees.
b) Recreation and Holidays :
So far as the industrial establishments under foreign
management throughout China are concerned the workers are
generally given a certain amount of rest and recreation after
a spell of work every day and subsequent to a number of daily
attendance. The factory law under review however stipulates
that the workers be given half-an-hour's rest after six hours'
duty, one holiday after seven days' attendance, and more than
eight legal holidays each year, in addition to a vacation,
the length of which to be determined according to the years
of service rendered - all these days of absence with full
wages paid.
To grant a few days of rest to the workers with full wages
paid does not mean any marked deviation from the present
custom, which makes it a rule to let the workers have a
few days of rest and an allowance as well at the beginning of
new year. Perhaps the worst feature we see under this item
is the provision that the employees be granted a certain
number of holidays besides those legally fixed all with full
wages paid, because the same amounts to paying money to the
page_data.zh:
-3-
如此多工时而导致的工资减少。这两种情况都完全不可行。这一事实最有力地证明了逐步而非一次性延长工作时间的明智之举。
工厂法还规定，为了应对因骚乱、自然灾害、政治或其他原因引起的特殊情况，工作时间可延长至12小时。然而，此类规定应被视为仅在极少数情况下采取的紧急措施。此外，人们看不出在发生骚乱时为何必须延长工作时间。
在这方面必须提到的是，目前在日本实施的工厂法对成年雇员的工作时间根本没有任何规定。
b) 休息与假日：
就全中国外资管理的工业企业而言，工人通常在每天工作一段时间后以及连续出勤数日后，会获得一定的休息和娱乐时间。然而，正在审议的工厂法规定，工人每工作六小时后休息半小时，每出勤七天休假一天，每年另有八个以上的法定假日，此外还有假期，假期长度根据服务年限确定——所有这些缺勤日均支付全额工资。
给予工人几天带薪休息并不意味着与现行习俗有显著偏差，现行习俗规定在新年伊始让工人休息几天并发放津贴。也许本项中最糟糕的特征是规定雇员除法定假日外还可享受一定数量的带薪假日，因为这相当于向

page_data.en:
-4-
"daily wage earners", who do not attend to their daily work .
The provision is so wrong that one could hardly find anything
like that in the factory law of other countries.
c) Child labour :
In China due to the state of illiteracy and the universal
custom of early matrimony the workers, both male and female,
are usually young, especially so in the case of apprenticeship.
In fact at silk filatures the operatives are almost entirely
young girls. According to the new factory law child labour
under 16 years of age is prohibited from working at night,
while employment is not permitted of the child less than 14
years. There is a proviso to the effect that the child labour
now in employ, whose ages are over 12 may be allowed to retain
its work. The two years difference in age limit is, the writer
thinks, too small to be of legal merit. One can easily imagine
what unwelcome effect the prohibition of child labour would
bring on the industrial circles in China.
d) Female Worker :
The prohibition of female workers' night work like that of
child labour is certain to have a great deal of influence on
the industrial world. Should the female workers be prohibited
in this way, it would lead either to throw one half of
their number out of employment or to divide them into two shifts
each of eight hours. The seriousness of the possible consequences shows quite clearly how important the provision is to
allow a reasonable amount of time for preparation of the prohibition.
As stated elsewhere in Japan the Government authorities
fixed first the time of 15 years for the preparation, and then
added another three years to make it 18 years in all, the
prohibition of a nature in question came actually to take
effect as lately as in July 1929. The recklessly abrupt prohibition, even if not combined with other destructive elements
page_data.zh:
-4-
“按日计薪者”支付工资，而他们并未从事日常工作。此项规定谬误之深，在其他国家的工厂法中几乎找不到类似条款。
c) 童工：
在中国，由于文盲状态普遍以及早婚习俗盛行，工人无论男女通常都很年轻，学徒情况尤其如此。事实上，在缫丝厂中，操作工几乎全是年轻女孩。根据新工厂法，禁止16岁以下童工从事夜间工作，同时不得雇用14岁以下儿童。另有一项但书规定，目前受雇且年龄在12岁以上的童工可被允许保留其工作。笔者以为，年龄限制上这两年的差距太小，缺乏法律价值。人们不难想象，禁止童工将给中国工业界带来何种令人不快的影响。
d) 女工：
如同对童工的规定一样，禁止女工从事夜间工作肯定会对工业界产生巨大影响。若以此方式禁止女工夜班，要么会导致半数女工失业，要么需将其分为两班，每班八小时。可能产生的后果之严重，清楚地表明了为实施该禁令预留合理准备时间这一规定的重要性。
如前文所述，在日本，政府当局最初设定了15年的准备期，后又增加三年，共计18年，此类性质的禁令实际上直到1929年7月才生效。这种鲁莽仓促的禁令，即使不与其它破坏性因素相结合

page_data.en:
-5-
in the new factory law, would not fail to spell an unre-
coverable disaster to the industrial world at large.
e) Factory Labour Council etc.
Factory Labour council, union participation in contract and
other provisions in the factory law are all out of place in
view of the present stage of labour status here in China.
The Government authorities had better try to work out ways
and means for advancement of labour elements giving up the
idea of factory law at least for the time-being.
f) Welfare Work etc.
In respect of minimum wage, welfare work and so forth applica-
tion of provisions thereon should be made as by degrees subject
to conditions prevailing in the circles concerned. Any ambiti-
ous attempt in this connection such as to go ahead of the more
advance courses in a very short space of time is certainly
unadvisable for China.
    In concluding this paper the writer would refer just in
brief to the unpracticable nature of some provisions and the
incompleteness of inspection system in the factory law. First
of all in China there is not yet accurate census registration
to prove one's age and other particulars. The provisions on
wages are set forth in term so vague that they are destined
to become a dead letter. Practically nothing is mentioned
in the way of inspection, which is a most important element
in the successful institution of welfare work, safety accom-
modation, and sanitary arrangement, all of which we are
afraid will become a dead letter also.

.............

Shanghai, 7:3:31.
page_data.zh:
-5-
在新工厂法中，这必将给整个工业界带来无法挽回的灾难。
e) 工厂劳工委员会等
鉴于中国目前劳工状况所处的阶段，工厂劳工委员会、工会参与合同以及工厂法中的其他规定均不合时宜。政府当局最好设法谋求劳工阶层的进步，至少暂时放弃制定工厂法的念头。
f) 福利工作等
关于最低工资、福利工作等方面，其规定的实施应根据有关各界的 prevailing conditions（现行状况）逐步进行。在此方面任何雄心勃勃的尝试，例如在极短时间内超越更先进的做法，对中国来说肯定是不明智的。
    在结束本文之际，笔者谨简要提及工厂法中某些条款的不切实际性以及检查制度的不完善性。首先，中国尚无准确的人口普查登记来证明一个人的年龄和其他具体情况。关于工资的规定措辞过于模糊，注定将成为一纸空文。实际上，对于检查制度只字未提，而检查是成功实施福利工作、安全设施及卫生安排的最重要因素，我们担心这些也都将成为一纸空文。

.............

Chinese-American Daily News and National Herald :-

REGULATIONS GOVERNING FORMATION OF LABOUR FEDERATIONS
PROMULGATED BY THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL AFFAIRS

The following are the regulations governing
the formation of labour federations promulgated by the
Ministry of Social Affairs of the National Government to
Tangpus in various provinces and municipalities:-
(1) Workers of a certain trade in a district
failing to form a labour union may unite with workers
of other trades in the same condition to form a labour
federation of various trades.
(2) Workers of different trades in the various
sections of a certain enterprise in a district who fail
to form an industrial workers' union with a quorum may
join the labour unions of their respective trades or unite
with other labour unions, who have insufficient members
with which to form a quorum, to form a labour federation
of various trades.
(3) Sections of different trades may be formed
in a labour federation of various trades. These sections
should be formed according to the rules of formation of
sections and branches of labour unions. Measures for the
holding of meetings by the sections of a labour federation
of various trades should be drafted by the Tangpu of the
district according to conditions in the district concerned.
(4))When a labour federation of various trades
cannot hold a big meeting of more than 250 persons, a
meeting of representatives should be held. One out of
every five persons of the same trade will be elected as
a representative; the remainder in every section may be
put together to elect representatives among themselves.
(5) When the number of members of a section
of a labour federation reaches a quorum, this section
should retire from the labour federation of various trades
and form a labour union or an industrial workers' union
of its own trade.
(6) The title of labour federation of various
trades should include the name of the city or municipality
where the labour federation is located.
(7) A labour federation of various trades
should adopt the regulations governing labour unions and
its stipulations of enforcement.
(8) Rules of a labour federation of various
trades should be made with reference to the rules of
labour unions.
(9) A labour federation of various trades may
unite with other labour unions and industrial workers'
unions to form a general labour union of the city or
municipality concerned.
The above regulations are drafted by the
Ministry of Social Affairs and recorded by the Central
Executive Committee of the Kuomintang for enforcement.

《中美日报》及《国民新闻报》：

社会部颁布之组织职业工会条例

以下为国民政府社会部向各省市党部颁布之组织职业工会条例：
(1) 某地区内某一行业之工人若未能成立工会，可与处于相同情况之其他行业工人联合，组织跨行业之职业工会联合会。
(2) 某地区内某企业各部门之不同行业工人，若因人数不足法定定额而无法成立产业工会，可加入各自行业之工会，或与其他会员人数不足法定定额之工会联合，组织跨行业之职业工会联合会。
(3) 跨行业职业工会联合会内可设立各行业分部。这些分部应按照工会分部及支会之组建规则成立。跨行业职业工会联合会各分部召开会议之办法，应由该地区党部根据当地具体情况拟定。
(4) 当跨行业职业工会联合会无法召开超过250人参加之大会时，应召开代表会议。每五名同行业工人中选举一名代表；其余各部人员可合并在一起，从中互选代表。
(5) 当跨行业职业工会联合会之某一分部会员人数达到法定定额时，该分部应退出跨行业职业工会联合会，并自行组建本行业之工会或产业工会。
(6) 跨行业职业工会联合会之名称应包含其所在城市或市名。
(7) 跨行业职业工会联合会应采用工会条例及其施行细则。
(8) 跨行业职业工会联合会之章程应参照工会章程制定。
(9) 跨行业职业工会联合会可与其他工会及产业工会联合，组建有关城市或市之总工会。
上述条例由社会部起草，并经中国国民党中央执行委员会备案后施行。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, NOVEMBER 18, 1929.

NANKING TO PROBE
LABOUR UNIONS

Nation-Wide Investigation Will Start On
December 25

Nanking, Nov. 17.
December 25 has been set by the Ministry of Industry Commerce and Labour as the day for the beginning of a nation-wide investigation of the various labour unions in existence in this country.
The purpose of the investigation by the Ministry will be to ascertain the present conditions of the labour unions to be used as reference for the formulation and enforcement of various labour regulations in consequence of the adoption of the Labour Union Law by the Government.
Questionnaires in regard to the condition of each labour union, its past history, the system of organization, the number of officers and the estimated expenses have been sent to various local governments throughout the country. All reports must be submitted to the Ministry before the end of January 1930.—Kuo Min.

南京将调查
工会

全国性调查将于
12月25日开始

南京，11月17日电。
工商部已定12月25日为开始对全国现存各类工会进行全国性调查之日。
工商部此次调查之目的，在于查明工会现状，作为政府在通过《工会法》后制定和执行各项劳动法规之参考。
关于各工会状况、既往历史、组织体系、职员人数及预估经费之调查问卷，已发送至全国各地地方政府。所有报告必须于1930年1月底前提交至本部。——《国民新闻》
