Sir,

The Municipal Advocate was consulted
on May 25, 1940, regarding the legality of the
regulations mentioned in the attached translation.
Mr. Bryan stated that he was not able to
say whether or not the regulations had been duly
promulgated and instructed Mr. Ru to interview
Chief Judge Dzien. Later Mr. Ru informed me that
the Chief Judge had stated that no order had been
received by the Court from the Government regarding
these regulations and that in the absence of
instructions the Court would not recognize them.
The Chief Judge promised to inform the Legal Depart-
ment if and when instructions are received.

No. 1. October 1'29.
LABOUR
LAWS GOVERNING LABOUR UNIONS.
The Ming Kuo Pao published the following express
correspondence from Nanking on September 30:-
The Legislative Council of the National Government
some time ago drafted certain principles governing the
organization of labour unions which have been approved by
the Central Political Conference. On the basis of these
principles, regulations have been drafted by the
Legislative Council and were passed at the 51st session
of the Council held on the afternoon of September 28.
The regulations have been submitted to the National
Government for promulgation.
CHAPTER 1: Establishment.
Article 1. Male and female labourers in the same
industry or of the same profession in order to promote their
intelligence and skill, to extend their products, to maintain
and modify labour conditions and livelihood as their object,
may assemble more than 100 industrial workers above 16 years of age
or more than 50 workers of the same profession to organize
labour unions to which these regulations will be applicable.
The various kinds of industrial workers union and professional
workers union will be classified.
Article 2. Workers, with the exception of their
employers or representatives, who possess the following
qualifications, may become members of the labour unions
although they are not of the same profession or industry:-
a) Those who had been elected as a responsible
officer of the labour union.
b) Those who had been of the same industry
or profession.
Article 3. These regulations do not apply to the
organization of labour unions by employees or coolies of
administrative, communications, military or national enterprises,
educational or public utility organs of the government.
Article 4. The direct supervising organ of the labour
unions is the provincial government, the municipality or the City
Magistrate's Yamen of the district concerned.
Article 5. If a labour union is about to be organized,
a joint application for registration which has to be duly
endorsed by a number of persons as stipulated in Article 1 and
will be presented to the official organ concerned by five to nine
representatives together with two copies of the proposed regulations
and the biography of the representatives. Upon receipt of the
application, the official organ concerned will conduct an investi-
gation within two weeks and endorse its remarks. If any modifi-
cation or investigation by the subordinate organs be necessary,
the official organ, upon receiving the application, will adopt
similar measures at the completion of the modification or the
investigation made by its subordinate organs. After registration
has been approved, the labour union concerned will submit within
three weeks the date of its inauguration together with the biography
and addresses of the officers elected. Upon receipt of this report,
the official organ concerned will give publicity to this matter.
Labour Unions the registration of which has not been approved or
which is under progress cannot enjoy the privileges and pro-
tection provided by these regulations.

编号 1. 1929年10月1日。
劳工
工会管理法。
《民国报》刊登了以下来自南京的专讯，日期为9月30日：
国民政府立法院此前起草了若干关于工会组织之原则，并已获中央政治会议批准。基于这些原则，立法院起草了相关条例，并于9月28日下午举行的第51次会议上通过。该条例已提交国民政府颁布。
第一章：设立。
第一条. 同一行业或同一职业之男女劳工，以促进其智识与技能、推广其产品、维持及改善劳动条件与生活状况为目的，可集合100名以上年满16岁之产业工人，或50名以上同一职业之工人，组织适用本条例之工会。各类产业工会与职业工会将予以分类。
第二条. 除雇主或其代表外，具备下列资格之工人，虽非同一职业或行业，亦可成为工会会员：
a) 曾当选为工会负责职员者。
b) 曾从事同一行业或职业者。
第三条. 本条例不适用于政府行政、交通、军事或国营企业、教育或公用事业机构之雇员或苦力所组织之工会。
第四条. 工会之直接主管机关为省政府、市政府或所在地区之县公署。
第五条. 若拟组织工会，须由符合第一条规定人数之发起人联名申请注册，并由五至九名代表连同章程草案两份及代表简历一并呈交有关官方机关。有关官方机关收到申请后，将在两周内进行调查并签署意见。如需下级机关进行修改或调查，有关官方机关在收到申请后，将在下级机关完成修改或调查后采取相应措施。注册获批后，有关工会应在三周内提交成立日期以及当选职员之简历和地址。有关官方机关收到此报告后，将对此事予以公告。注册未获批准或正在办理中之工会，不得享受本条例规定之特权和保护。

No. 2. October 2'29.
Labour
LAWS GOVERNING LABOUR UNIONS
(Continued)

Article 6. Only one labour union shall be allowed
to be established in any district for a particular profession
or enterprise.

Article 7. When a labour union is organized, an
inauguration meeting is to be held and its regulations drafted,
such regulations must secure the approval of more than ¾ths
of its promoters.

Article 8. The regulations of a labour union must
stipulate the following:-
a) Name.
b) Object.
c) District and address of the Union.
d) Conditions governing the qualifications of
members together with their privileges and obligations.
e) Conditions governing the enrollment and
registration of members and expulsion from membership.
f) Conditions governing the staff.
g) Conditions governing meetings to be held.
h) Conditions governing membership fees and auditing.
i) Conditions governing affairs of mutual assistance.
j) Conditions governing alterations of the
regulations.

Article 9. Alterations to be effected to the regula-
tions will not be considered valid unless they have been approved
by the official organ concerned.

Article 10. A labour union is a judicial person and must
not engage in business transactions.

Article 11. A labour union must have a Committee elected
from among the members, but in case of necessity, non-members
of the union may serve on the Committee to deal with all the
affairs of the labour union and to represent the Union provided
the approval has been secured from the official organ concerned. The
placing of restrictions on the representative rights of the
committee must not interfere with a well-intentioned third party.

Article 12. When the Committee of a labour union or its
representative has done harm to another person while in the
execution of its duties, the labour union concerned will be jointly
responsible to make good the damage except in cases connected
with labour conditions in which event the members are jointly
responsible or in cases wherein restrictions have been imposed
upon the conduct of the members whereby employers will suffer
harm. The labour union may not be held responsible for the
individual conduct of its officers and members outside the union.

Article 13. The following matters must be decided by a
general meeting of members or a general meeting of representatives
a) Alterations to be made to the regulations of
the labour union.
b) Financial budget.
c) Acknowledgement of reports on activities as
well as budgets.
d) The maintenance or alteration of labour conditions.
e) The administration and disposal of reserve funds.
f) The undertaking of public enterprises in the union.
g) The organization of a federation of labour unions
as well as enrollment or resignation.
h) The dissolution, amalgamation or separate existence
of labour unions.

第2号。1929年10月2日。
劳工
管理工会之法律
（续）

第六条。任何地区内，就某一特定职业或企业而言，仅允许成立一个工会。

第七条。组建工会时，须召开成立大会并起草章程，该章程须获得发起人四分之三以上的批准。

第八条。工会章程必须规定以下事项：
a) 名称。
b) 宗旨。
c) 工会所在地区及地址。
d) 会员资格条件及其权利与义务。
e) 会员入会、登记及除名条件。
f) 职员管理条件。
g) 会议召开条件。
h) 会费及审计条件。
i) 互助事务条件。
j) 章程修订条件。

第九条。对章程所作的修订，除非经有关官方机构批准，否则视为无效。

第十条。工会为法人，不得从事商业交易。

第十一条。工会须设有由会员选举产生的委员会，但在必要时，非工会会员亦可担任委员会委员，以处理工会一切事务并代表工会，但须事先获得有关官方机构的批准。对委员会代表权的限制不得妨碍善意第三方。

第十二条。当工会委员会或其代表在执行职务过程中损害他人利益时，相关工会应共同承担赔偿责任，但与劳动条件有关的情况除外，在此情况下由会员共同承担责任；或因对会员行为施加限制而导致雇主遭受损害的情况除外。工会不对其职员和会员在工会之外的个人行为承担责任。

第十三条。下列事项必须由会员大会或代表大会议决：
a) 工会章程的修订。
b) 财务预算。
c) 对活动报告及预算的认可。
d) 劳动条件的维持或变更。
e) 储备金的管理与处置。
f) 工会内公共事业的兴办。
g) 工会联合会的组织以及加入或退出。
h) 工会的解散、合并或分立。

No. 3. October 2nd, 1929.

Article 14. A labour union may, in accordance
with its regulations or the decision of a general meeting,
organize a supervisory committee to handle the investigation
of all accounts and account books and various activities and
to supervise the work of the staff. The supervisory committee
must be elected from amongst the workers.

Chapter II. Duties.

Article 15. The duties of labour unions are as follows:-

A/ The drafting, amending or cancelling of agreements
made by public bodies cannot be regarded as valid
unless approval had first been secured from the
Government organizations concerned.
B/ To introduce (?recommend) members for employment
and to establish employment or recommendation offices.
C/ To establish savings offices, labour insurance
offices, hospitals and homes for children.
D/ To establish co-operative offices for the
development of industry and for dealing with
purchases, credit, residence, etc.
E/ To develop vocational education and other
labour educational works.
F/ To establish libraries and reading rooms.
G/ To publish printed matter.
H/ To establish clubs for the entertainment of
members and provide various kinds of amusements games.
I/ To mediate in disputes amongst labour unions
or labourers.
J/ To mediate in disputes between labourers and
capitalists.
K/ To express views relating to the amendment and
cancellation of any labour laws which might be
submitted to the administrative organizations, the
judical organs, and the legislative organs.
To send replies to the administrative organizations,
the judical organs and the legislative organs when
asked for.
L/ To investigate into the living and economic
conditions of the families of labourers and of those
persons newly employed as well as of those who are
unemployed. Lists showing the number of labourers
should also be complied.
M/ To deal with matters relating to the improvement
of working conditions and to enlarge the interests
of the members. If the labour union concerned fails
to deal with or carry out the foresaid mutual aid
enterprises although they are stipulated in the
regulations, officers might be appointed to render
assistance provided approval has been secured from
the authorities concerned and who are of the opinion
that this help ought to be given.
art. 16 —— N/ The labour unions formed by labourers in the
various industries have no right to draft agreements
for public bodies.
" 17 —— O/ The labour unions may collect membership fees
from their members. However the entrance fee should
not be more than $1 and the membership fees should
not be more than 2% of his income. These unions are
not allowed to raise special contributions or extra-
ordinary contributions unless permission has first
been secured from the Government organizations concerned.
" 18 —— P/ The labour unions should report to their members
every six months on the assets of the unions concerned,
Members who have secured the signature of over 10% of
the members, may elect representatives to check the
assets of the labour unions concerned.
page_data.zh:
第3号。1929年10月2日。

第十四条。工会可根据其章程或大会决议，组织监察委员会，负责调查所有账目、账簿及各项活动，并监督职员工作。监察委员会须从工人中选举产生。

第二章 职责。

第十五条。工会的职责如下：

A/ 起草、修改或取消由公共团体达成的协议，除非事先获得有关政府组织的批准，否则不得视为有效。
B/ 介绍会员就业，并设立就业或推荐机构。
C/ 设立储蓄所、劳工保险所、医院及儿童之家。
D/ 设立合作社，以发展工业并处理采购、信贷、居住等事宜。
E/ 发展职业教育及其他劳工教育工作。
F/ 设立图书馆及阅览室。
G/ 出版印刷品。
H/ 设立俱乐部以供会员娱乐，并提供各类游乐游戏。
I/ 调解工会之间或劳工之间的纠纷。
J/ 调解劳工与资本家之间的纠纷。
K/ 就可能提交给行政机构、司法机关和立法机构的任何劳工法律的修订和废止表达观点。
在被询问时，向行政机构、司法机关和立法机构作出答复。
L/ 调查劳工家庭、新受雇人员以及失业人员的生活和经济状况。还应编制显示劳工人数的清单。
M/ 处理改善工作条件及扩大会员利益的相关事宜。如果相关工会未能处理或执行章程中规定的上述互助事业，经有关当局批准并认为应当给予帮助的情况下，可指派官员提供协助。
第十六条 —— N/ 由各行业劳工组成的工会无权为公共团体起草协议。
" 第十七条 —— O/ 工会可向会员收取会费。然而，入会费不得超过1元，会费不得超过其收入的2%。除非事先获得有关政府组织的许可，否则这些工会不得募集特别捐款或额外捐款。
" 第十八条 —— P/ 工会应每六个月向会员报告相关工会的资产情况。获得超过10%会员签名的会员，可选举代表检查相关工会的资产。

No. 4. October 2, 1929.

Chapter III: Supervision.

Article 19. Labourers engaged in the same profession or industry may join the labour union.
Article 20. Labour Unions are prohibited from compelling labourers to join the unions nor are they permitted to prevent members from withdrawing their membership. Labour Unions are prohibited from rejecting applications made by those, who, from the legal point of view, are qualified for membership, nor are they permitted to allow those who, from the legal point of view, are not qualified to join them. Labour Unions are forbidden to obstruct the work of those labourers who have not joined any labour unions.
Article 21. Members may at any time withdraw their membership from a labour union but if the regulations of certain labour unions stipulate that members intending to withdraw their membership should send in a notice in advance, the period of this notice should not be more than one month,
Article 22. The amount of fines to be imposed on members by the labour unions should not be more than three days' wages of a member. Labour Unions are prohibited from striking off the names of members from the membership list unless proper reasons are quoted and the approval of two-thirds of the members has been secured.
Article 23. Disputes between labourers and ██████ ███████████ capitalists must undergo mediation and arbitration. Labour unions are not allowed to declare a strike unless approval has been secured by vote from more than two-thirds of the members. When a strike is called by a labour union, it should not menace the peace and good order of the locality nor should it endanger the lives and property of the employers. Labour unions are not allowed to ██████ declare a strike by demanding an increase of wages which is above the maximum. The labour unions formed by labourers engaged in the various kinds of trades specified in Article 3 are not permitted to declare a strike.
Article 24, No amendments to the labour union regulations or changes in its committee or staff may be made unless a report has been submitted to the Government organs concerned, which will, within two weeks, give publicity to this effect. Prior to this, no changes which are unfavourable to a third party may be made.
Article 25. After securing permission for registration, labour unions must submit two blank membership books and two account books to the Government organ concerned with a request that a stamp be affixed to these books. If new books be required in future, one membership book and one account book must be kept in the labour union concerned, whilst the other two books should be submitted to the Government organ concerned. The membership book must stipulate the names and the number of members, the date of their enrolment, the place of their occupation, changes in their occupation and details of death or injuries sustained. The account books must contain a record of all receipts and payments and separate numbered receipt books must be kept. In case of necessity, the Government organ concerned may order the auditor of the labour union concerned to compile a statement of account.
Article 26. The labour unions should submit the following lists and books to the Government organs concerned in June and December every year:-
A- The names and other particulars of the employees of the labour Unions.
B- The membership books.
C- The account books.
D- The business condition.
E- Detailed reports on disputes.
The Government organs concerned at any time may order the labour unions to submit the above books if necessary.
page_data.zh:
第4号。1929年10月2日。

第三章：监管。

第十九条。从事同一职业或行业的劳工可以加入工会。

第二十条。禁止工会强迫劳工加入工会，也不得阻止会员退会。工会不得拒绝在法律上具备会员资格者的申请，也不得允许在法律上不具备资格者加入。工会不得阻碍未加入任何工会的劳工的工作。

第二十一条。会员可随时退出工会，但如果某些工会的章程规定拟退会会员须提前发出通知，则该通知期不得超过一个月。

第二十二条。工会对会员处以的罚款金额不得超过会员三天的工资。除非引用正当理由并获得三分之二会员的批准，否则禁止工会将会员姓名从会员名单中除名。

第二十三条。劳工与 ██████ ███████████ 资本家之间的纠纷必须经过调解和仲裁。除非获得三分之二以上会员投票批准，否则工会不得宣布罢工。当工会号召罢工时，不得威胁当地的和平与良好秩序，也不得危及雇主的生命和财产。工会不得通过要求超过最高限度的加薪来 ██████ 宣布罢工。依据第三条规定的各类行业劳工组成的工会，不得宣布罢工。

第二十四条。除非已向有关政府机构提交报告，且该机构将在两周内予以公告，否则不得对工会章程进行修订，也不得变更其委员会或职员。在此之前，不得作出对第三方不利的任何变更。

第二十五条。获得注册许可后，工会须向有关政府机构提交两本空白会员名册和两本账簿，并请求在这些簿册上盖章。如果将来需要新簿册，相关工会须保留一本会员名册和一本账簿，而另外两本簿册应提交给有关政府机构。会员名册必须规定会员姓名及人数、入会日期、职业地点、职业变动以及死亡或受伤详情。账簿必须包含所有收支记录，并须保存单独编号的收据簿。如有必要，有关政府机构可命令相关工会的审计员编制财务报表。

第二十六条。工会应于每年六月和十二月向有关政府机构提交下列清单和簿册：
A- 工会职员的姓名及其他详情。
B- 会员名册。
C- 账簿。
D- 业务状况。
E- 纠纷详细报告。
如有必要，有关政府机构可随时命令工会提交上述簿册。

page_data.en:
No. 5. October 3, 1929.

Article 27. The employees and members of the labour unions must not commit the following acts:-
A- To seal up shops or mills.
B- To snatch or destroy goods or furniture belonging to shops or mills.
C- To arrest or assault labourers or employers.
D- To compel employers to take on labourers recommended by them.
E- To hold meetings or processions or to carry arms.
F- To commit extortion.
G- To order their members to stop work.
H- To receive commission or collect tax.

Article 28. If the elections held by the labour unions or if the decisions reached be in violation of law or regulations the same should be cancelled by the Government organs concerned,
Article 29. If the regulations of the labour unions violate the law, the government organs may order them to be amended.
Article 30. If a labour union be dissatisfied with the two preceding articles, it may make an appeal but the appeal must be submitted within 30 days,

Chapter IV: PROTECTION:
Article 31/ Employers or their representatives must not refuse to employ or dismiss labourers because they are either members or employees of labour unions, nor should the employers or their representatives ill-treat them.
Article 32. Employers or their representatives should not make labourers observe conditions such as refraining from working for labour unions or joining labour unions when the employers or their representatives employ new hands.
Article 33. Employers or their representatives must not dismiss labourers when a dispute is under mediation or arbitration.
Article 34. Labour unions are exempted from paying income tax, business tax and registration tax.
Article 35. Labour unions will be given priority of claim on the assets of a bankrupt.
Article 36. The following estates of the labour unions may not be confiscated:-
a/ Offices of labour unions, schools, libraries, reading rooms, clubs, hospitals, homes for children, movable and immovable property, etc.
b/ The reserve funds of labour unions and labour insurance funds.

CHAPTER V: DISSOLUTION:
Article 37. A labour union may be dissolved by the government organs concerned when any of the following defects has been found:-
a/ When important and fundamental articles are not complete
b/ In cases of violation of laws and regulations of a very grave nature.
c/ In cases of menace to the peace and good order of the locality.
Article 38. Apart from the preceding Article, labour unions may also dissolved in any of the following circumstances:-
a/ A resolution to dissolve is passed at a general meeting and approval has been secured from the government organs concerned,
b/ Dissolution in observance of regulations.
c/ Bankruptcy of labour unions.
d/ Insufficient number of members.
e/ The labour unions are to be amalgamated or separated.
Article 39. The amalgamation or separation of labour unions must not take place unless approval has been secured from over one-half of the members and from the government organs concerned,
page_data.zh:
第5号。1929年10月3日。

第二十七条。工会雇员及会员不得有下列行为：
甲、封闭商店或工厂。
乙、抢夺或毁坏属于商店或工厂的货物或家具。
丙、逮捕或殴打劳工或雇主。
丁、强迫雇主雇用由其推荐的劳工。
戊、举行集会、游行或携带武器。
己、进行勒索。
庚、命令其会员停工。
辛、收取佣金或征收税款。

第二十八条。如工会举行的选举或作出的决议违反法律法规，应由有关政府机关予以撤销。

第二十九条。如工会章程违反法律，政府机关可责令其修改。

第三十条。如工会对前两条规定不服，可提出申诉，但申诉必须在三十日内提交。

第四章：保护：

第三十一条。雇主或其代表不得因劳工是工会会员或雇员而拒绝雇用或将其解雇，雇主或其代表亦不得虐待他们。

第三十二条。雇主或其代表在雇用新工人时，不得要求工人遵守诸如不为工会工作或不得加入工会等条件。

第三十三条。在争议处于调解或仲裁期间，雇主或其代表不得解雇劳工。

第三十四条。工会免缴所得税、营业税及注册税。

第三十五条。工会对破产资产享有优先受偿权。

第三十六条。下列工会财产不得没收：
甲、工会办事处、学校、图书馆、阅览室、俱乐部、医院、儿童之家、动产及不动产等。
乙、工会储备金及劳工保险基金。

第五章：解散：

第三十七条。当发现有下列任何缺陷时，有关政府机关可解散工会：
甲、重要及基本条款不完备；
乙、严重违反法律法规；
丙、危害地方和平与良好秩序。

第三十八条。除前条规定外，工会在下列任何情况下亦可解散：
甲、在全体大会上通过解散决议，并获得有关政府机关批准；
乙、依章解散；
丙、工会破产；
丁、会员人数不足；
戊、工会合并或分立。

第三十九条。工会的合并或分立，除非获得过半数会员及有关政府机关的批准，否则不得进行。

No. 6. Continued.
Article 40. The labour unions which come into existence after amalgamation or which have been newly inaugurated, may continue to enjoy the privileges and to bear the obligations of labour unions which have ceased to exist after amalgamation because a labour union which is inaugurated through separation may continue to enjoy the privileges and bear the obligations in the same way as a labour union which has ceased to exist through separation or which continues to exist after separation. The proportion of the privileges to be enjoyed and obligations to be borne has to be decided at the time when the decision for separation is passed provided approval has been secured from the government organs concerned,
Article 41. Prior to the amalgamation or separation of labour unions, all creditors must be given more than one month's notice in which to express their opposition, but those who already know about the changes must be notified individually When it is within the period for creditors to lodge their opposition, the labour unions should first pay off the obligations or furnish adequate security before the amalgamation or separation is effected in accordance with the foregoing stipulations. The amalgamation or separation of labour unions must in no way be made in opposition to their creditors.
Article 42. When a labour union is about to be dissolved, it must submit to the government organ concerned the reasons for its action together with the state in full unless the labour union has been ordered to dissolve.
Article 43. When a labour union is about to be dissolved, with the exception in the cases of amalgamation, separation or bankruptcy, a clear account of its assets must be made by legal persons as stipulated in Civil Law.
Article 44. When a labour union is dissolved and its debts have been paid up, the ownership of the remaining property must be in accordance with the stipulations of its regulations or the decision of a general meeting without which the remaining property will go to the Federation of Labour Unions to which the said union belongs and if the Union is a non-member of the federation, the property will be taken over by the district self-governing organs in which the labour union is located.
CHAPTER VI. AMALGAMATION.
Article 45. Labour Unions of workers who belong to the same profession or industry in order to promote the intelligence and skill of members, to extend their products and to undertake affairs of mutual assistance, may submit a joint petition to the government organ concerned for permission to organize a federation of labour unions. After approval has been secured, a joint conference of labour unions of workers in official institutions must be held to draft the regulations which should be approved by the government organ concerned. With the exception of the foregoing two stipulations, these regulations may apply to any federation of labour unions.
Article 46. Labour unions must not amalgamate with any foreign labour union unless permission has first been secured the Government.
CHAPTER VII. PUNISHMENT.
Article 47. Employees or members of any labour union who commit any of the offences mentioned in Article 27 will be liable to a fine below $200 but if the offence is of a criminal nature, he will be subject to punishment according to to criminal law.
Article 48. Any employer or his representative who violates the stipulations of Articles 31 & 32 will be liable to a fine below $300.
Article 49. Any employer or his representative who violates the stipulations of Article 32 by dismissing his workers will be liable to a fine of over $10 or below $100 for each worker dismissed.

第6号。续。

第四十条。合并后成立的工会或新设立的工会，可继续享有因合并而终止存在的工会所享有的特权并承担其义务；同样，因分立而设立的工会，也可继续享有因分立而终止存在或分立后继续存在的工会所享有的特权并承担其义务。享有特权和承担义务的比例，须在作出分立决定时确定，并须获得有关政府机关的批准。

第四十一条。在工会合并或分立之前，必须给予所有债权人一个月以上的时间以表示反对，但对于已知晓变更情况的债权人，必须个别通知。在债权人提出异议的期限内，工会应按照前述规定，在进行合并或分立之前先清偿债务或提供充分担保。工会的合并或分立绝不得损害其债权人的利益。

第四十二条。工会拟解散时，除非是被责令解散，否则必须向有关政府机关提交解散理由及完整状况说明。

第四十三条。工会拟解散时，除合并、分立或破产情况外，必须由民法规定的法人对其资产进行清算。

第四十四条。工会解散并清偿债务后，剩余财产的所有权须依照其章程规定或全体大会的决定处理；若无此规定或决定，剩余财产将归该工会所属的工会联合会所有；若该工会非联合会成员，则财产由工会所在地的区自治机关接管。

第六章。合并。

第四十五条。同一职业或行业的工人工会，为促进会员的智识与技能、推广其产品以及办理互助事务，可向有关政府机关联合申请许可组织工会联合会。获得批准后，必须召开官方机构中工人工会的联席会议起草章程，该章程须经有关政府机关批准。除上述两项规定外，这些章程可适用于任何工会联合会。

第四十六条。工会未经政府事先许可，不得与任何外国工会合并。

第七章。处罚。

第四十七条。任何工会的雇员或会员犯有第二十七条所述任何罪行者，处以二百元以下罚款；但若该罪行具有刑事性质，则将依照刑法予以惩处。

第四十八条。任何雇主或其代表违反第三十一及三十二条规定者，处以三百元以下罚款。

第四十九条。任何雇主或其代表违反第三十二条规定解雇工人者，每解雇一名工人，处以十元以上一百元以下罚款。

Article 50. Any member of the committee of a
labour union who violates any of the following stipulations
will be liable to a fine below $100.
a/ Affairs relating to Art. 24, 26, 42 & 51
when a report is not submitted or when a false report is

b/ The stipulations of Article 25 and the orders

Article 51. Prior to the enforcement of these

Article 52. Prior to the enforcement of these

Article 53. An order giving the date of enforcement

第7号。续。

第五十条。工会委员会任何委员违反下列任何规定者，处以一百元以下罚款：
甲、涉及第二十四、二十六、四十二及五十一条事项，未提交报告或提交虚假报告者。
乙、违反第二十五条规定及第二十九条所规定的命令者。
丙、违反第四十一条第一及第二款，实施合并或分立者。

第八章。附则。

第五十一条。在本条例施行前已成立的工会，必须自本条例施行之日起两个月内，依照第五条规定重新注册。

第五十二条。在本条例施行前，某一特定区域内同一职业或行业的两个或更多工会，必须自本条例施行之日起两个月内合并。

第五十三条。将发布命令公布本条例的施行日期。

LAWS GOVERNING LABOUR UNIONS.

The Sing Pao published the following express correspondence from Nanking on September 28:-
The Legislative Council of the National Government some time ago drafted certain principles governing the organization of labour unions which have been approved by the Central Political Conference. On the basis of these principles, regulations have been drafted by the Legislative Council and were passed at the 1st session of the Council held on the afternoon of September 28. The regulations have been submitted to the National Government for promulgation.

CHAPTER 1: Establishment.

Article 1. Male and female labourers in the same industry or of the same profession in order to promote their intelligence and skill, to extend their products, to maintain and modify labour conditions and livelihood as their object, may assemble more than 100 industrial workers above 16 years of age or more than 50 workers of the same profession to organize labour unions to which these regulations will be applicable. The various kinds of industrial workers union and professional workers union will be classified.

Article 2. Workers, with the exception of their employers or representatives, who possess the following qualifications, may become members of the labour unions although they are not of the same profession or industry:-
a) Those who had been elected as a responsible officer of the labour union.
b) Those who had been in the same industry or profession.

Article 3. These regulations do not apply to the organization of labour unions by employees or coolies of administrative, communications, military or national enterprises, educational or public utility or any of the government.

Article 4. The direct supervising organ of the labour unions is the provincial government, the municipality or the City Magistrate's Yamen of the district concerned.

Article 5. If a labour union is about to be organized, a joint application for registration which has to be duly endorsed by a number of persons as stipulated in Article 1 and will be presented to the official organ concerned by five to nine representatives together with two copies of the proposed regulations and the biography of the representatives. Upon receipt of the application, the official organ concerned will conduct an investigation within two weeks and endorse its remarks. If any modification or investigation by the subordinate organs be necessary, the official organ, upon receiving the application, will adopt similar measures at the completion of the modification or the investigation made by its subordinate organs. After registration has been approved, the labour union concerned will submit within three weeks the date of its inauguration together with the biography and addresses of the officers elected. Upon receipt of this report the official organ concerned will give publicity to this matter. Labour Unions the registration of which has not been approved or which is under progress cannot enjoy the privileges and protection provided by these regulations.

工会管理法。

《申报》于9月28日刊登了以下来自南京的特急通讯：
国民政府立法院此前起草了一些关于工会组织的原则，这些原则已获中央政治会议批准。在此基础上，立法院起草了条例，并于9月28日下午举行的立法院第一届会议上通过。该条例已提交国民政府颁布。

第一章：设立。

第一条。同一行业或同一职业的男女劳工，以促进其智识与技能、推广其产品、维持及改善劳动条件与生活水平为目的，可召集一百名以上十六岁以上的产业工人或五十名以上同职业工人组织工会，适用本条例。各类产业工人工会和职业工人工会将进行分类。

第二条。除雇主或其代表外，具备下列资格的工人，即使不属于同一职业或行业，亦可成为工会会员：
甲）曾当选为工会负责人者。
乙）曾从事同一行业或职业者。

第三条。本条例不适用于行政、交通、军事或国营企业、教育或公用事业或任何政府部门的雇员或苦力组织的工会。

第四条。工会的直接主管机关为省政府、市政府或所在地区的县公署。

第五条。如拟组织工会，须由第一条规定人数的若干人正式背书，由五至九名代表连同章程草案两份及代表简历，向有关官方机关提交联合注册申请。有关官方机关收到申请后，将在两周内进行调查并签署意见。如需下级机关进行修改或调查，有关官方机关在收到申请后，将在其下级机关完成修改或调查后采取相应措施。注册获批后，有关工会须在三个月内提交成立日期以及当选职员的简历和地址。有关官方机关收到此报告后将对此事予以公告。注册未获批准或正在办理中的工会，不能享受本条例规定的特权和保护。

No. 2. October 2'29.
Labour
LAWS GOVERNING LABOUR UNIONS
(Continued)

Article 6. Only one labour union shall be allowed
to be established in any district for a particular profession
or enterprise.

Article 7. When a labour union is organized, an
inauguration meeting is to be held and its regulations drafted,
such regulations must secure the approval of more than ¾ths
of its promoters.

Article 8. The regulations of a labour union must
stipulate the following:-
a) Name.
b) Object.
c) District and address of the Union.
d) Conditions governing the qualifications of
members together with their privileges and obligations.
e) Conditions governing the enrollment and
registration of members and expulsion from membership.
f) Conditions governing the staff.
g) Conditions governing meetings to be held.
h) Conditions governing membership fees and auditing.
i) Conditions governing affairs of mutual assistance.
j) Conditions governing alterations of the
regulations.

Article 9. Alterations to be effected to the regula-
tions will not be considered valid unless they have been approved
by the official organ concerned.

Article 10. A labour union is a judicial person and must
not engage in business transactions.

Article 11. Labour union must have a Committee elected
from among the members, but in case of necessity, non-members
of the union may serve on the Committee to deal with all the
affairs of the labour union and to represent the Union provided
approval has been secured from the official organ concerned. The
placing of restrictions on the representative rights of the
committee must not interfere with a well-intentioned third party.

Article 12. When the Committee of a labour union or its
representative has done harm to another person while in the
execution of its duties, the labour union concerned will be jointly
responsible to make good the damage except in cases connected
with labour conditions in which event the members are jointly
responsible or in cases wherein restrictions have been imposed
upon the conduct of the members whereby employers will suffer
harm. The labour union may not be held responsible for the
individual conduct of its officers and members outside the union.

Article 13. The following matters must be decided by a
general meeting of members or a general meeting of representatives
a) Alterations to be made to the regulations of
the labour union.
b) Financial budget.
c) Acknowledgement of reports on activities as
well as budgets.
d) The maintenance or alteration of labour conditions.
e) The administration and disposal of reserve funds.
f) The undertaking of public enterprises in the union.
g) The organization of a federation of labour unions
as well as enrollment or resignation.
h) The dissolution, amalgamation or separate existence
of labour unions.

劳工
管理工会之法律
（续）

第六条。任何地区内，就某一特定职业或企业而言，仅准设立一个工会。

第七条。组织工会时，须召开成立大会并起草章程，该章程须获得发起人四分之三以上之批准。

第八条。工会章程须规定下列事项：
a) 名称。
b) 宗旨。
c) 工会所在地区及地址。
d) 会员资格条件及其权利与义务。
e) 会员入会、登记及除名之条件。
f) 职员管理之条件。
g) 会议召开之条件。
h) 会费及审计之条件。
i) 互助事务之条件。
j) 章程修改之条件。

第九条。对章程所作之修改，未经有关官方机关批准者，视为无效。

第十条。工会为法人，不得从事商业交易。

第十一条。工会须设有由会员中选出的委员会，但在必要时，经有关官方机关批准，非工会会员亦可担任委员，以处理工会一切事务并代表工会。对委员会代表权之限制，不得妨碍善意第三方。

第十二条。工会委员会或其代表在执行职务期间致他人损害者，有关工会应负连带赔偿责任；但与劳动条件有关之案件除外，在此情况下由会员负连带责任；或因对会员行为施加限制致使雇主受损之情况除外。工会对其职员及会员在工会以外之个人行为不承担责任。

第十三条。下列事项须经会员大会或代表大会决定：
a) 工会章程之修改。
b) 财务预算。
c) 对活动报告及预算之确认。
d) 劳动条件之维持或变更。
e) 公积金之管理与处置。
f) 工会内公共事业之承办。
g) 工会联合会之组织以及加入或退出。
h) 工会之解散、合并或分立。

No. 3. October 2nd, 1929.

Article 14. A labour union may, in accordance
with its regulations or the decision of a general meeting,
organize a supervisory committee to handle the investigation
of all accounts and account books and various activities and
to supervise the work of the staff. The supervisory committee
must be elected from amongst the workers.

Chapter II. Duties.

Article 15. The duties of labour unions are as follows:-

A/ The drafting, amending or cancelling of agreements
made by public bodies cannot be regarded as valid
unless approval had first been secured from the
Government organizations concerned.
B/ To introduce (recommend) members for employment
and to establish employment or recommendation offices.
C/ To establish savings offices, labour insurance
offices, hospitals and homes for children.
D/ To establish co-operative offices for the
development of industry and for dealing with
purchases, credit, residence, etc.
E/ To develop vocational education and other
labour educational works.
F/ To establish libraries and reading rooms.
G/ To publish printed matter.
H/ To establish clubs for the entertainment of
members and provide various kinds of amusements games.
I/ To mediate in disputes amongst labour unions
or labourers.
J/ To mediate in disputes between labourers and
capitalists.
K/ To express views relating to the amendment and
cancellation of any labour laws which might be
submitted to the administrative organizations, the
judical organs, and the legislative organs.
To send replies to the administrative organizations,
the judical organs and the legislative organs when
asked for.
L/ To investigate into the living and economic
conditions of the families of labourers and of those
persons newly employed as well as of those who are
unemployed. Lists showing the number of labourers
should also be compiled.
M/ To deal with matters relating to the improvement
of working conditions and to enlarge the interests
of the members. If the labour union concerned fails
to deal with or carry out the foresaid mutual aid
enterprises although they are stipulated in the
regulations, officers might be appointed to render
assistance provided approval has been secured from
the authorities concerned and who are of the opinion
that this help ought to be given.
N/ The labour unions formed by labourers in the
various industries have no right to draft agreements
for public bodies.
O/ The labour unions may collect membership fees
from their members. However the entrance fee should
not be more than $1 and the membership fees should
not be more than 2% of his income. These unions are
not allowed to raise special contributions or extra-
ordinary contributions unless permission has first
been secured from the Government organizations concerned.
P/ The labour unions should report to their members
every six months on the assets of the unions concerned,
Members who have secured the signature of over 10% of
the members, may elect representatives to check the
assets of the labour unions concerned.
page_data.zh:
第3号。1929年10月2日。

第十四条。工会可根据其章程或大会决议，组织监察委员会，负责调查所有账目、账册及各项活动，并监督职员工作。监察委员会须从工人中选举产生。

第二章 职责。

第十五条。工会之职责如下：

A/ 起草、修改或取消由公共团体订立之协议，未经有关政府机关批准，不得视为有效。
B/ 介绍会员就业，并设立就业或推荐机构。
C/ 设立储蓄所、劳工保险所、医院及儿童之家。
D/ 设立合作机构，以发展工业并处理采购、信贷、居住等事宜。
E/ 发展职业教育及其他劳工教育工作。
F/ 设立图书馆及阅览室。
G/ 出版印刷品。
H/ 设立俱乐部以供会员娱乐，并提供各类游乐游戏。
I/ 调解工会之间或劳工之间的纠纷。
J/ 调解劳工与资本家之间的纠纷。
K/ 就可能提交行政、司法及立法机关的任何劳动法之修改和废止发表意见。
应行政、司法及立法机关之要求予以答复。
L/ 调查劳工家庭、新受雇人员及失业人员的生活和经济状况。并应编制显示劳工人数之清单。
M/ 处理改善工作条件及扩大会员利益之相关事宜。如果有关工会虽在章程中规定了上述互助事业，却未能处理或实施，经有关当局批准并认为应当给予协助时，可指派官员提供协助。
N/ 由各业劳工组成的工会无权为公共团体起草协议。
O/ 工会可向会员收取会费。但入会费不得超过1元，会费不得超过其收入的2%。除非事先获得有关政府机关许可，否则这些工会不得征收特别捐或额外捐。
P/ 工会应每六个月向会员报告有关工会的资产情况。获得超过10%会员签名的会员，可选举代表检查有关工会的资产。

page_data.en:
No. 4. October 2, 1929.

Chapter III: Supervision.

Article 19. Labourers engaged in the same profession
or industry may join the labour union.
Article 20. Labour Unions are prohibited from compelling
labourers to join the unions nor are they permitted to prevent
members from withdrawing their membership. Labour Unions are
prohibited from rejecting applications made by those, who, from
the legal point of view, are qualified for membership, nor
are they permitted to allow those who, from the legal point of
view, are not qualified to join them. Labour Unions are
forbidden to obstruct the work of those labourers who have
not joined any labour unions.
Article 21. Members may at any time withdraw their
membership from a labour union but if the regulations of
certain labour unions stipulate that members intending to
withdraw their membership should send in a notice in advance,
the period of this notice should not be more than one month,
Article 22. The amount of fines to be imposed on
members by the labour unions should not be more than three
days' wages of a member. Labour Unions are prohibited from
striking off the names of members from the membership list
unless proper reasons are quoted and the approval of two-thirds
of the members has been secured.
Article 23. Disputes between labourers and capitalists
must undergo mediation and arbitration.
Labour unions are not allowed to declare a strike unless approval
has been secured by vote from more than two-thirds of the
members. When a strike is called by a labour union, it should not
menace the peace and good order of the locality nor should it
endanger the lives and property of the employers. Labour unions are
not allowed to declare a strike by demanding an increase of
wages which is above the maximum. The labour unions formed by
labourers engaged in the various kinds of trades specified in
Article 3 are not permitted to declare a strike.
Article 24. No amendments to the labour union regulations
or changes in its committee or staff may be made unless a report
has been submitted to the Government organs concerned, which will,
within two weeks, give publicity to this effect. Prior to this,
no changes which are unfavourable to a third party may be made.
Article 25. After securing permission for registration,
labour unions must submit two blank membership books and two
account books to the Government organ concerned with a request that
a stamp be affixed to these books. If new books be required in
the future, one membership book and one account book must be kept in the
labour union concerned, whilst the other two books should be submit-
ted to the Government organ concerned. The membership book must
stipulate the names and the number of members, the date of their
enrolment, the place of their occupation, changes in their
occupation and details of death or injuries sustained. The account
books must contain a record of all receipts and payments and
separate numbered receipt books must be kept. In case of necessity,
the Government organ concerned may order the auditor of the labour
union concerned to compile a statement of account.
Article 26. The labour unions should submit the
following lists and books to the Government organs concerned in
June and December every year:-
A- The names and other particulars of the
employees of the labour Unions.
B- The membership books.
C- The account books.
D- The business condition.
E- Detailed reports on disputes.
The Government organs concerned at any time may order
the labour unions to submit the above books if necessary.
page_data.zh:
第4号。1929年10月2日。

第三章：监督。

第十九条。从事同一职业或行业的劳工可加入工会。
第二十条。禁止工会强迫劳工加入工会，亦不得阻止会员退会。工会不得拒绝在法律上具备会员资格者之申请，亦不得允许在法律上不具备资格者加入。工会不得阻碍未加入任何工会之劳工的工作。
第二十一条。会员可随时退出工会，但若某些工会章程规定拟退会者须提前通知，则该通知期不得超过一个月。
第二十二条。工会对会员处以罚款之金额，不得超过会员三日工资。除非列举正当理由并获得三分之二会员批准，否则禁止工会将会员名字从会员名单中除名。
第二十三条。劳工与资本家之间的纠纷必须经过调解和仲裁。
除非获得三分之二以上会员投票批准，否则工会不得宣布罢工。工会发动罢工时，不得威胁当地和平与良好秩序，亦不得危及雇主的生命和财产。工会不得以要求超过最高限度的加薪为由宣布罢工。第三条所指各类行业之劳工所组成的工会，不得宣布罢工。
第二十四条。除非已向有关政府机关提交报告，且该机关在两周内对此予以公告，否则不得修改工会章程或变更其委员会及职员。在此之前，不得作出对第三方不利的任何变更。
第二十五条。获得注册许可后，工会须向有关政府机关提交两本空白会员名册和两本账簿，并请求在这些簿册上加盖印章。若日后需要新簿册，有关工会须保留一本会员名册和一本账簿，另两本则须提交给有关政府机关。会员名册须规定会员姓名及人数、入会日期、职业地点、职业变动以及死亡或受伤详情。账簿须记录所有收支款项，并须保存单独编号的收据簿。必要时，有关政府机关可命令有关工会的审计员编制财务报表。
第二十六条。工会应于每年六月和十二月向有关政府机关提交下列清单和簿册：
A- 工会职员的姓名及其他详情。
B- 会员名册。
C- 账簿。
D- 业务状况。
E- 纠纷详细报告。
如有必要，有关政府机关可随时命令工会提交上述簿册。

page_data.en:
No. 5. October 3, 1929.

Article 27. The employees and members of the labour unions must not commit the following acts:-
A- To seal up shops or mills.
B- To snatch or destroy goods or furniture belonging to shops or mills.
C- To arrest or assault labourers or employers.
D- To compel employers to take on labourers recommended by them.
E- To hold meetings or processions or to carry arms.
F- To commit extortion.
G- To order their members to stop work.
H- To receive commission or collect tax.

Article 28. If the elections held by the labour unions or if the decisions reached be in violation of law or regulations the same should be cancelled by the Government organs concerned.
Article 29. If the regulations of the labour unions violate the law, the government organs may order them to be amended.
Article 30. If a labour union be dissatisfied with the two preceding articles, it may make an appeal but the appeal must be submitted within 30 days,

Chapter IV: PROTECTION.
Article 31. Employers or their representatives must not refuse to employ or dismiss labourers because they are either members or employees of labour unions, nor should the employers or their representatives ill-treat them.
Article 32. Employers or their representatives should not make labourers observe conditions such as refraining from working for labour unions or joining labour unions when the employers or their representatives employ new hands.
Article 33. Employers or their representatives must not dismiss labourers when a dispute is under mediation or arbitration.
Article 34. Labour unions are exempted from paying income tax, business tax and registration tax.
Article 35. Labour unions will be given priority of claim on the assets of a bankrupt.
Article 36. The following estates of the labour unions may not be confiscated:-
a/ Offices of labour unions, schools, libraries, reading rooms, clubs, hospitals, homes for children, movable and immovable property, etc.
b/ The reserve funds of labour unions and labour insurance funds.

CHAPTER V: DISSOLUTION.
Article 37. A labour union may be dissolved by the government organs concerned when any of the following defects has been found:-
a/ When important and fundamental articles are not complete
b/ In cases of violation of laws and regulations of a very grave nature.
c/ In cases of menace to the peace and good order of the locality.
Article 38. Apart from the preceding Article, labour unions may also dissolve in any of the following circumstances:-
a/ A resolution to dissolve is passed at a general meeting and approval has been secured from the government organ concerned.
b/ Dissolution in observance of regulations.
c/ Bankruptcy of labour unions.
d/ Insufficient number of members.
e/ The labour unions are to be amalgamated or separated.
Article 39. The amalgamation or separation of labour unions must not take place unless approval has been secured from over one-half of the members and from the government organs concerned,
page_data.zh:
第5号。1929年10月3日。

第二十七条。工会之雇员及会员不得有下列行为：
甲、封闭商店或工厂。
乙、抢夺或毁坏属于商店或工厂之货物或家具。
丙、逮捕或殴打劳工或雇主。
丁、强迫雇主雇用由其推荐之劳工。
戊、举行会议、游行或携带武器。
己、实施勒索。
庚、命令其会员停工。
辛、收取佣金或征收税款。

第二十八条。如工会举行之选举或所作之决议违反法律法规，应由有关政府机关予以撤销。
第二十九条。如工会章程违反法律，政府机关可命令其修改。
第三十条。如工会对前两条规定不服，可提出上诉，但上诉须于三十日内提交，

第四章：保护。
第三十一条。雇主或其代表不得因劳工为工会会员或雇员而拒绝雇用或将其解雇，雇主或其代表亦不得虐待他们。
第三十二条。雇主或其代表在雇用新人时，不得要求劳工遵守诸如不为工会工作或不得加入工会等条件。
第三十三条。在争议处于调解或仲裁期间，雇主或其代表不得解雇劳工。
第三十四条。工会免缴所得税、营业税及注册税。
第三十五条。工会对破产资产享有优先求偿权。
第三十六条。下列工会财产不得没收：
子、工会办事处、学校、图书馆、阅览室、俱乐部、医院、儿童之家、动产及不动产等。
丑、工会储备金及劳工保险基金。

第五章：解散。
第三十七条。当发现有下列任何缺陷时，有关政府机关可解散工会：
子、重要及基本条款不完备时；
丑、违反法律法规情节极其严重时；
寅、危害地方和平与良好秩序时。
第三十八条。除前条规定外，工会在下列任何情况下亦可解散：
子、在全体大会上通过解散决议，并获得有关政府机关批准。
丑、依章程规定解散。
寅、工会破产。
卯、会员人数不足。
辰、工会拟合并或分立。
第三十九条。工会之合并或分立，除非获得过半数会员及有关政府机关之批准，否则不得进行，

page_data.en:
No. 6. Continued.
Article 40. The labour unions which come into existence after amalgamation or which have been newly inaugurated, may continue to enjoy the privileges and to bear the obligations of labour unions which have ceased to exist after amalgamation because a labour union which is inaugurated through separation may continue to enjoy the privileges and bear the obligations in the same way as a labour union which has ceased to exist through separation or which continues to exist after separation. The proportion of the privileges to be enjoyed and obligations to be borne has to be decided at the time when the decision for separation is passed provided approval has been secured from the government organs concerned.
Article 41. Prior to the amalgamation or separation of labour unions, all creditors must be given more than one month's notice in which to express their opposition, but those who already know about the changes must be notified individually When it is within the period for creditors to lodge their opposition, the labour unions should first pay off the obligations or furnish adequate security before the amalgamation or separation is effected in accordance with the foregoing stipulations. The amalgamation or separation of labour unions must in no way be made in opposition to their creditors.
Article 42. When a labour union is about to be dissolved, it must submit to the government organ concerned the reasons for its action together with the state in full unless the labour union has been ordered to dissolve.
Article 43. When a labour union is about to be dissolved, with the exception in the cases of amalgamation, separation or bankruptcy, a clear account of its assets must be made by legal persons as stipulated in Civil Law.
Article 44. When a labour union is dissolved and its debts have been paid up, the ownership of the remaining property must be in accordance with the stipulations of its regulations or the decision of a general meeting without which the remaining property will go to the Federation of Labour Unions to which the said union belongs and if the Union is a non-member of the federation, the property will be taken over by the district self-governing organs in which the labour union is located.
CHAPTER VI. AMALGAMATION.
Article 45. Labour Unions of workers who belong to the same profession or industry in order to promote the intelligence and skill of members, to extend their products and to undertake affairs of mutual assistance, may submit a joint petition to the government organ concerned for permission to organize a federation of labour unions. After approval has been secured, a joint conference of labour unions of workers in official institutions must be held to draft the regulations which should be approved by the government organ concerned. With the exception of the foregoing two stipulations, these regulations may apply to any federation of labour unions.
Article 46. Labour unions must not amalgamate with any foreign labour union unless permission has first been secured the Government.
CHAPTER VII. PUNISHMENT.
Article 47. Employees or members of any labour union who commit any of the offences mentioned in Article 27 will be liable to a fine below $200 but if the offence is of a criminal nature, he will be subject to punishment according to to criminal law.
Article 48. Any employer or his representative who violates the stipulations of Articles 31 & 32 will be liable to a fine below $300.
Article 49. Any employer or his representative who violates the stipulations of Article 32 by dismissing his workers will be liable to a fine of over $10 or below $100 for each worker dismissed.
page_data.zh:
第6号。续。
第四十条。合并后成立或新近 inaugurated（原文如此，意为成立/启动）之工会，可继续享有因合并而终止存在之工会之特权并承担其义务；同样，因分立而成立之工会，亦可继续享有因分立而终止存在或分立后继续存在之工会之特权并承担其义务。所享特权与所担义务之比例，须在通过分立决定时确定，惟须获得有关政府机关之批准。
第四十一条。在工会合并或分立之前，必须给予所有债权人一个月以上之期限以表示反对，但对于已知晓变更者，须个别通知。在债权人提出反对之期限内，工会应按照前述规定，在进行合并或分立之前先清偿债务或提供充分担保。工会之合并或分立绝不得损害其债权人利益。
第四十二条。工会即将解散时，除非系被命令解散，否则必须向有关政府机关提交行动理由及完整状况报告。
第四十三条。工会即将解散时，除合并、分立或破产情况外，必须由民法规定之法人对其资产进行清算。
第四十四条。工会解散并清偿债务后，剩余财产之所有权须依照其章程规定或全体大会之决定处理；若无此规定或决定，剩余财产将归该工会所属之工会联合会所有；若该工会非联合会会员，则财产由工会所在地之区自治机关接管。
第六章。合并。
第四十五条。同一职业或行业之工人工会，为促进会员之智识与技能、扩展其产品并承担互助事务，可向有关政府机关联合请愿，请求许可组织工会联合会。获得批准后，须召开官方机构中工人工会之联席会议，起草章程，该章程须经有关政府机关批准。除上述两项规定外，这些章程可适用于任何工会联合会。
第四十六条。工会未经政府事先许可，不得与任何外国工会合并。
第七章。处罚。
第四十七条。任何工会之雇员或会员犯第二十七条所述任何罪行，将被处以二百元以下罚款；但若该罪行具有刑事性质，则将依照刑法予以惩处。
第四十八条。任何雇主或其代表违反第三十一及三十二条之规定，将被处以三百元以下罚款。
第四十九条。任何雇主或其代表违反第三十二条之规定解雇工人，每解雇一名工人，将被处以十元以上一百元以下罚款。

page_data.en:
No 7. Continued,
Article 50. Any member of the committee of a
labour union who violates any of the following stipulations
will be liable to a fine below $100.
a/ Affairs relating to Art. 24, 26, 42 & 51
when a report is not submitted or when a false report is
submitted.
b/ The stipulations of Article 25 and the orders
stipulated in Article 29.
c/ Clauses 1 & 2 of Article 41 by effecting an
amalgamation or separation.

CHAPTER VIII. APPENDIX.

Article 51. Prior to the enforcement of these
regulations labour unions which have already been inaugurated
must register again in accordance with Article 5 within two
months commencing from the date of enforcement of these
regulations.
Article 52. Prior to the enforcement of these
regulations, two or more labour unions of the same profession
or industry in one particular district must be amalgamated
within two months commencing from the date of enforcement
of these regulations.
Article 53. An order giving the date of enforcement
of these regulations will be issued.

(THE END).
page_data.zh:
第7号。续，
第五十条。工会委员会任何成员违反下列任何规定，将被处以一百元以下罚款。
子、涉及第二十四、二十六、四十二及五十一条之事项，未提交报告或提交虚假报告时。
丑、违反第二十五条之规定及第二十九条所规定之命令时。
寅、违反第四十一条第一及第二款，实施合并或分立时。

第八章。附则。

第五十一条。在本条例施行前已成立之工会，须自本条例施行之日起两个月内，依照第五条规定重新注册。
第五十二条。在本条例施行前，某一特定区域内同一职业或行业之两个或多个工会，须自本条例施行之日起两个月内合并。
第五十三条。将发布命令，公布本条例之施行日期。

（完）。

LABOUR TREATIES. 


JAPAN’S BAD SHOWING IN 


RATIFICATION. 
MR. ALBERT THOMAS’S APPEAL. 
Mr. Albert Thomas, Director of the 


International Labour Bureau, spoke at a 
welcome meeting held in his honour 
under the auspices of the League of Na- 
tions Association on the 8th instant at 
the Gakushi Kaikwan at Kanda, Tokyo. 
Some 500 people were present, including 
Prince Tokugawa, Viscount Shibusawa, 
Baron Sakatani, Baron Matsui, Dr. 
Midzuno and Messrs. Abe and Suzuki, 
both members of the Shakai Minshuto. 
Mr. Albert Thomas spoke for about two 
hours, being interpreted by Mr. Ayuzawa, 
of the International Labour Bureau. 

In the course of his speech, he re- 
fretted that some people were _ still 
labouring under the false impression that 
the League of Nations and the Inter- 
national Labour Bureau constituted an 
encroachment on the sovereignty of the 
State. He strongly repudiated this idea 
and declared that all the signatories were! 
called upon to do was to co-operate within 
limits compatible with their respective 
sovereignty and according to their wishes. ! 
The function of these organs Were defined ! 
in the League of Nations Covenant and/ 
the Chapter on Labour in the Peace} 
Treaty, and the great principles laid! 
down in these instruments ought to be | 
constantly borne in ming by all the sig- 
natories. Japan had. been faithful in} 
acting up to these principles. She had} 
been perfectly represented at each of the; 
International Labour Conferences held: 
in the past. Her efforts hitherto made’ 
towards ratifying the labour treaties 
adopted at these Conference, however. j 
still left something to be desired. Of the 
twenty-five treaties adopted at the Con-! 
ference up to the present. Japan had 
ratified only nine, while Belgium had 
ratified 15, France 13, Britain 12 and 
Italy 11, This state of things was not 
quite up to the mark, considering that 
Japan was a big industrial Power in the 
Far East. The three treaties regarding 
juvenile labour had all been ratified by 
Japan, but an important treaty concern- 
ing night work for women was still left 
unratified. notwithstanding the fact that 
the Japanese Government delegate at the 
first International Labour Conference at 
Washington expressed approval, and that 
ten years had already passed since then. 
His present visit to Japan, Mr. Thomas 
declared, was for tae purpose of accelerat 
ing Japan's ratification of the treaties 
adopted at the International Labour Con. 
ference and urging on the Japanese Gov- 
ernment and people the necessity of 
social justice being established in a big 
industrial country. He felt sure that 
Japan with noble and excellent national 
characteristics would make earnest en- 
deavours to establish social justice and 
promote the spirit of the League of Na- 
tions. 


MR. THOMAS’S VIEWS. 


JAPAN’S PRIVY COUNCIL HINDERS 
RATIFICATION. 


The House of Representatives held a 
reception at the President’s official resi- 
dence on the 12th instant in honour of 
Mr. Albert Thomas, Director of the 
International Labour Bureau. Over fifty 
members of the Dfet of different party 
affiliations were present on the side of 
the hosts. Mr. Motoda, the President, 
made a welcomé speech, to whict Mr. 
Thomas replied. After thanking the 
hosts for their reception, Mr. Thomas 
Tepeated his earnest desire that Japan 
should make redonbied efforts to ratify 
the labour treaties adopted at the Inter- 


It appeared that there had been develop- 
ing a tendency in the world of late years

for social reconstruction to be effected 
through revolutionary methods, which 
were chiefly destructive, he said. The 
Chinese and Russian revolutions were 
cases in point. In his opinion, however, 
if a courtry had healthy parliamentary 
institutions, its social reconstruction 
could be achieved through the medium of 
its Legislature. and he believed that

cumstances disappointing to note that of 
the 29 treaties adopted at the Interna- 
tional Labour Conferences up to the pre- 
sent, Japan had ratified only nine. The 
main cause for this was presumably to 
be found in the fact that whereas in the 
case of most of the the countries within 
the International Labour Conference, the

ese Legislature had no voice in their 
ratification, the Privy Council being 
vested with the authority of recommend- 
ing ratification or non-ratification to the 
Throne. This was, of course, a matter 
of domestic politics, but if he could ven- 
ture his personal views on this opportu- 
nity. he would say that his past 
experience as a members of the Legisla- 
ture showed that the legislators had the 
right to express their views with a free- 
dom and courage which were denied other 
members of society. 

Messrs. Kiyose (Vice-President), Morita 
and Uehara (Parliamentary Councillor of 
the Foreign Office) also spoke explaining 
the peculiar circumstances of Japan and

Bureau for its activity. 

In conclusion, Mr. Motoda, the Presi- 
dent, assured Mr. Albert Thomas of the

in the efforts beng made in the direction 
of establishing social justice. and hoped 


for its redoubled endeavours in the 
future.

secial legislation, but the Nationalist Government is now

TO OUR READERS 


The Labour Research Association is an outgrowth of 
the visit of M. Albert Thomas, Director of the International 
Labour Office, to China. M. Thomas had at the time some 
long conversations with persons interested in labour con- 
ditions in China, and sympathetic with the work of the 
Office, who gave him full assistance and some brief reports 
upon the situation here. 


M. Thomas felt keenly the lack of definite information 
on conditions in this country, particularly in European 
languages. After his departure, therefore, several persons 
who had been in touch with him here decided to form an 
association and to supply the Labour Office with informa- 
tion on the subjects needed. This group included both 
Chinese and foreigners, and after discussion of the work 
before them decided that their investigations could be for 
the service both of the International Labour Office and of 
persons in China interested in labour conditions. With a 
government one of the most fundamental Principles of 


a 


which is its devotion to the people’s livelihood, such reports 
might be of particular value. Accordingly, it was consider- 
ed of value to publish reports in China of investigations 
made, having same printed in Chinese and in English 
{or French), and bringing them out in bulletin form so as 
to be available to all parties interested in such information. 


Most of our readers, we trust, have already some 
acquaintance with the nature of the International Labour 
Office created by the Versailles treaty. The I. L. O. is as 
organization separate and distinct from the League of 
Nations, and consists of representatives of government, 
labour, and capital of the nations affiliated,—now including 
most nations of the world. The organization was formed. 
upon the recognition, forced upon all in recent years, that 
lasting peace can be established and maintained only if 
based upon social justice, and that there exist widespread 
conditions which make for discontent and unrest. In the 
improvement of these conditions it is necessary to work 
on an international scale, so the I. L. O. drafts conventions 
and recommendations which are later brought before the 
governing bodies of the various nations for adoption and 
enforcement in their territory. Protection of workers in 
certain dangerous employments, protection of woman and 
child labour, investigations into compulsory labour, co- 
operation, trade union organization, etc., are taken up by 
the organization. Its work, broadly, falls into two 
divisions: scientific research,—the collection of informa- 
tion on all subjects related to conditions of labour and 
industrial life; and the preparation and adoption of 
conventions based upon such information. 


The work of the Labour Research Association of China 
is of the first category. We aim to gather information on 


a, ae 


the conditions of workers in mills and factories, on farms 
and in mines, in shops and in domestic service; information 
on the relations between employers and employees, 
whether regular wage labour, piece-work, contract labour, 
or slave labour; information on the legal position of work- 
ers and the protection accorded them by lav ; information 
on organizations formed by them to further their economic 
interests (co-operative associations, trade unions, mutual 
aid societies, etc.). Such information as we gather is to 
be put at the disposal of the International Labour Office, 
and is also to be published here in China. 


As regards this bulletin, we also hope to print, from 
time to time, information upon conditions in other coun- 
tries which may be of relevance in consideration of certain 
industries or occupations in China. We shall be grateful 
to any who will give us their assistance in our work. The 
Association, having no Government subsidy, is dependent 
upon the voluntary work and contributions of its members 
and of others sympathetic with its aims. Our first number 
is small in sizc, and contains but one report, but we expect 
to grow. 


The Labour Research Association is open to all, 
regardless of nationality, who agree with its aims as set 
forth in its preamble. We welcome all who wish to 
co-operate with us in this work. 


THE LABOUR RESEARCH ASSOCIATION OF CHINA. 


CONSTITUTION 
OF THE 
LABOUR RESEARCH ASSOCIATION OF ChitNA 


ARTICLE I (Purpose) 

Recognizing that peace, internally and internationally, 
can be maintained only if based upon social justice, and 
that in the realization of better and juster social conditions 
it is of fundamental importance to gather and to distribute 
information on all subjects relating to existing conditions 
of labour and industrial life; and for the purpose of 
gathering such information in China and putting same at 
the disposal of the International Labour Office created by 
the Treaty of Versailles in 1919; and further for the 
purpose of publishing such information, both with regard 
to China and other countries, in bulletin form at regular 
intervals here; we, the undersigned, form hereby the 
Labour Research Association of China. 


ARTICLE II (Membership) 


Section 1.—Anyone who subscribes to the aims of the 
Labour Research Association of China, as set forth in 
Article I of this Constitution, and who is proposed by a 
member in good standing of the Association, shall be 
eligible to membership upon payment of initiation fee. 


Section 2.—An entrance or initiation fee of Mex. $2.00 
shall be paid by each member of the Association, and 
regular dues of $6.00 yearly. The membership fee for 
workers and students of low income shall be $2.00 yearly, 
and no initiation fee shall be charged. 


Section 3.—In case any member of the Association is 
found to be working against the objects of the Association 


a S 


as set forth in Article I above, he may be expelled if the 
findings of the Organization Committee to that effect are 
confirmed and his expulsion decided upon by a regular 
meeting of the Association. 


Section 4.—Honorary members shall be selected as 
the Association may decide. 


ARTICLE III (Meetings) 


The Association’ shall hold regular meetings twice 
monthly, open to all members. Seven members shall con- 
stitute a quorum for a meeting. 


ARTICLE IV (Organization) 


Section 1.—The permanent officers of the Association 
shall consist of a Chinese Secretary, a Foreign Secretary, 
and a Treasurer. Officers shall be elected at the first 
regular meeting in January and the first regular meeting 
in July each year, and shall serve for six months. 


Section 2.—-Officers shall be subject to recall. The 
recall of any officer may be proposed by a regular meeting 
of the Association, but must be decided by a referendum 
of the membership. 


Section 3.—An Organization Committee may be 
selected as the need arises, to deal with matters concerning 
membership and organization. Permanent officers of the 
Association shall be ex-officio members of the Committee. 

Section 4.—An Editorial Committee of not less than 
five members, a majority of whom must be Chinese, shall 
be elected at the first general meeting in January and the 
first regular meeting in July each year. This committee 
shall be entrusted with the publication of all matter put 
out by the Association, as provided for in Article V. Its 


a mm 
members shall be subject to recall individually, as provided 
for officers in Section 2. Vacancies shall be filled by 
election at a regular meeting of the Association. 

Section 5.—The regular meetings of the Association 
shall select such committees as shall be necessary from time 
to time in the carrying out of the specific phases of its 
work. A chairman shall be elected for each meeting of 
the Association. 

Section 6.—Committees chosen, as provided in Section 5 
of this Article, for the investigation of specific subjects, 
may transmit their reports to the International Labour 
Offices. Such reports shall be signed by the members of 
the Committee making report, and by a permanent secre- 
tary of the Association. 

ARTICLE V (Publication) 

Section 1.—The Labour Research Association shall 
publish reports on subjects of labour and industrial life. 
For this purpose the Association shall put out a monthly 
bulletin. Reports on conditions in China or elsewhere 
shall be published in Chinese and/or English, and in such 
other languages as the Editorial Committee shall see fit 
from time to time. All reports prepared by the Association 
on conditions in China shall be published at least in Chinese 
and either English or French. 

Section 2.—The Editorial Committee shall have full 
charge of the monthly bulletin, and of any other publications 
that may be found necessary for the purposes of the 
Association. The Committee may select an editor or 
editors at their discretion. 

Section 3.—It shall be the aim to make the bulletin 
self-supporting. In the meantime, any deficit shall be 
made good by the Labour Research Association. 


ee 


—— 


Seetion 4.—The Editorial Committee shall receive 
reports from committees elected as provided for in 
Article IV, Section 5, for the study of specific subjects, and 
shall publish such reports at their discretion. Such reports 
shall be presented to the members of the Association at 
the first regular meeting following completion of reports. 


ARTICLE VI (Amendments and Changes) 


Section 1.—Amendments to the Constitution of the 
Labour Research Association of China may be made by 
any regular meeting of the Association, provided such 
amendments are in nature of additions or elucidations, 
and do not alter or nullify any existing section of the 
Constitution. 

Section 2.—Changes in the Constitution of the Associa- 
tion which involve alteration or nullification of existing 
sections may be made only by a referendum of the member- 
ship of the Association.
